### Claude City
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/claude-clan-0e9e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/mittal-parth/claude-clan) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/-WVMaU1-sHE) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/-WVMaU1-sHE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Push%20to%20Prod%20Hackathon:%20Building%20at%20the%20Frontier-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pushtoprod-india.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-69-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Claude code as a game

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Phaser](https://img.shields.io/badge/Phaser-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fastify](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fastify-333333?style=flat-square) ![Anthropic](https://img.shields.io/badge/Anthropic-333333?style=flat-square)

**What is the problem your project solves?**

## The shift

Software development is increasingly about **managing agents**, not writing and reviewing every line of code yourself. The default tools still look like IDEs and diffs — interfaces built for humans typing, not for fleets of agents working in parallel.

That mismatch matters. As Claude and other agents take on more of the build, the bottleneck becomes **situational awareness**: what is the agent doing, which files is it touching, where is the work concentrating, and when should a human intervene?

## Why it matters

Without a better interface, agent coding stays opaque. Teams lose the plot mid-run, over-approve tool calls, or under-trust the system. Code review has the same problem at scale: a PR diff is a wall of text, not a spatial map of what changed.

## What Claude City does

We gamify that experience: your project becomes a **live game world**. Directories are districts. Source files are buildings. Claude agents are the crew on site. As they work, the city updates — so you watch software get built the way you watch a construction sim, not a terminal dump.

**New: PR cities.** Every open GitHub pull request becomes its own port city. Sail between main and PR cities, see added/modified/deleted files as construction overlays on the map, and dispatch a read-only Claude reviewer to inspect the diff and post a GitHub review — with mayor approval before anything ships.

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://claude-clan.vercel.app/

**How you are solving it?**

## Approach

Claude City turns a local git repo into an **isometric city** and routes Claude Agent SDK activity into that world live.

### World generation
- Scan the repository into a world map (`worldgen`)
- Lay out **districts** from folders and **buildings** from files (`layout`), with plot persistence so the city stays stable across rescans
- Render with **Phaser** (isometric terrain, buildings by language/size, ambient life, ships between cities)

### Agent → game loop
- A Fastify + WebSocket server runs `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` against the repo
- SDK hooks (tools, file changes, subagents, tasks, compact) become **game events**
- The client shows crew on the map, a per-city **quest log**, building highlights when files change, and **mayor permits** for non-read tool calls

### Crew model
- Pick your crew before each run: **Architect (Opus)** for deep refactors, **Worker (Sonnet)** for everyday construction
- **Effort levels** (low → max) control reasoning depth and how equipped the crew looks on the map

### PR cities & review mode *(built during the hackathon)*
- Server lists open PRs via `gh` and registers each as a **port city** (`pr-<number>`)
- PR cities are **lazy-built**: git worktree at the PR head, world scan, and diff overlay computed only when you travel there
- **Diff overlay** marks changed files on the map — new buildings for additions, highlighted edits, ghost plots for deletions
- PR agents are **read-only** (Write/Edit disabled); Claude reads the diff and can publish a review via `gh pr review`, which still requires a mayor permit before posting
- **Ship travel** between cities with a cloud transition; each city keeps its own quest log and agent session

### Stack
`worldgen` → `layout` → SQLite persistence → Fastify/WebSocket server → Vite/React/Phaser client. One CLI command boots everything: `sudo-city <path>`.

**How Did You Use Claude?**

## Claude is the crew

Claude is not a bolt-on chatbot. It is the **intelligence and actuator layer** of Claude City.

### Integration
- Built on **`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`** (`query`, hooks, permissions, model/effort)
- Server session manager translates SDK messages into protocol events the Phaser client consumes
- Models: **Opus = Architect**, **Sonnet = Worker**; effort levels control reasoning depth

### What Claude does in the main city
- Receives mayor prompts (with optional attached file context from drag-and-drop)
- Reads/searches/edits the repo under permission rules
- Safe tools (Read/Glob/Grep) auto-approve; writes and other tools raise **building permits** for the human mayor
- File-change hooks trigger world rescans so new/edited files appear as buildings as Claude works

### What Claude does in PR cities
- Gets a review-focused system prompt with the PR title, author, and changed-file list
- Explores the PR worktree read-only — no in-place fixes
- Publishes GitHub reviews through `gh pr review --approve | --request-changes | --comment`, gated by mayor permits so nothing posts without explicit approval

### Why this fits the hackathon
The product only makes sense with Claude in the loop: without the agent SDK driving real construction and review, the city is just a static map. Claude is both the builder and the signal that makes the world move.

Team **Dark Chocolate** -- [Arjun R](https://github.com/arjun-vegeta), [Parth Mittal](https://github.com/mittal-parth/), [Fahim Ahmed](https://github.com/ahmedfahim21)

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://mcp.tokito.dev/mcp

**How Did You Use Claude?**

Claude is the intelligence layer of the product, not a feature bolted onto it. Tokito does not work without it.

## 1. Claude Opus 5 is the design agent

The entire chat-to-schematic path runs on **claude-opus-5**, routed through our own gateway at `api.tokito.dev` (we removed bring-your-own-key today — users never hold provider credentials).

It runs as a **planner/editor split**, which we adopted because one model splitting attention between reasoning and emitting byte-exact JSON measurably underperforms two specialised passes:

- a **planner agent** with free-text reasoning, read-only tools and web search, which produces the engineering plan the user sees;
- **editor agents** that emit only typed operations through `propose_*` tools and end with a `commit_batch`.

Every mutating tool call is validated at invocation time against a *projected* document — so a conflict surfaces as a fixable tool error the model self-corrects from, rather than a broken schematic. The output is a typed batch the user approves per-operation.

## 2. Claude Sonnet 4.6 is the datasheet extractor (built today)

The new pipeline uses **claude-sonnet-4-6** to read verified datasheet crops into a strict `SymbolSpec` schema. Two independent extractions per part — one from the pinout figure, one from the pin-description table — then a reconciliation pass that compares them. Temperature 0, `deny_unknown_fields`, reprompt once on schema failure, then **abstain**. Claude is deliberately confined to the one job it is genuinely better at than code — reading a picture of a pinout — and is never allowed to draw the geometry.

## 3. MCP as the integration fabric

We run **our own MCP server** (`mcp.tokito.dev`, streamable HTTP JSON-RPC) as the parts catalog: `search_symbols`, `get_symbol`, `find_compatible`, `part_offer_query`, and today's `resolve_by_mpn` and `get_symbol_provenance`. The desktop is the MCP client. It is also usable from Claude Desktop or any MCP client directly.

Security was designed in: every tool result is wrapped in an `<untrusted>` envelope and size-capped before it reaches the model, MCP tool names are namespaced so they cannot shadow built-ins, TLS is mandatory, and bearer tokens live in the OS keychain.

## 4. Claude Code built it

The hackathon work itself was written with **Claude Code** across five repositories in parallel — including adversarial review passes that caught a per-frame blocking call and a data-loss regression before they shipped.

This submission was drafted and filed through the Devfolio MCP server.

**How you are solving it?**

## Prior-work disclosure (read this first)

**Tokito, the desktop studio, existed before today** — it is our ongoing product and is the project being submitted. **What we built during this hackathon is DS-ViRe and the complete datasheet-to-symbol pipeline**: the capability that lets Tokito generate a real schematic symbol for a part that exists in no library. That work landed today across five repositories and is verifiable in public commit history (2026-08-08). Nothing in it was written before today, and none of it has been submitted to another hackathon.

## What Tokito is, end to end

A native desktop studio (Rust + egui) that takes a board from a sentence to fabrication-ready outputs:

1. **Chat** — you describe the board. Claude produces an engineering plan, then a **typed, reviewable proposal** of schematic and BOM edits. Every AI change is a diff you accept or reject per-operation. Nothing touches the canvas unapproved.
2. **Schematic capture** — pin-anchored wiring, orthogonal auto-routing, multi-sheet hierarchies with typed ports, real bus semantics (vectors, rippers, member-wise nets), automatic junction inference, full undo/redo. Connectivity is derived from stable anchors, never from "these lines look like they touch" — so a schematic cannot be quietly wrong.
3. **Parts** — symbols stream from our own hosted MCP catalog and get embedded into the design, so it renders identically forever even if the catalog changes.
4. **ERC** — live and on-demand electrical rule checks with a pin-conflict matrix (output driving output, undriven input, etc).
5. **BOM** — synced from the schematic, AI-editable, enriched with distributor procurement hints and web-grounded pricing.
6. **Outputs** — KiCad `.kicad_sch`, netlists, SVG/PDF plots, BOM CSV, MCAD handoff JSON.
7. **Cloud + mobile** — accounts, plans and metering behind our own LLM gateway, plus a phone Companion that lets you approve AI proposals away from the desk.

## What we built today

**The governing rule: models interpret evidence, deterministic code constructs symbols.** An LLM emitting CAD geometry is unshippable — unreproducible and unauditable. So we split the problem in half.

**DS-ViRe** (new, open source, Apache-2.0) — figure-level retrieval over datasheets. It scores and verifies figure/table regions in a PDF and emits **typed evidence**: page number, normalized bounding box, cropped image, content hash, under a frozen `dsvire.symbol-evidence.v1` contract. It **fails closed** — it never guesses manufacturer, MPN or package, and abstains unless it can independently verify *both* a pinout and a pin-function table. Bounded to 64 MiB / 2000 pages.

Then the pipeline:

- **Extract** — Claude reads the verified crops **twice, independently** (pinout vs pin-description table), constrained by a strict JSON schema. A reconciliation pass compares pin counts, numbers, names, aliases, NC/reserved pins and exposed pads. Conflicts stay explicit; below threshold it abstains rather than inventing a pin.
- **Compile** — a deterministic Rust compiler turns the reconciled `SymbolSpec` into canonical geometry: power in on top, ground and outputs on the bottom, inputs left, outputs right, body sized from pin count and label widths. Same spec in produces a **byte-identical** symbol file out — enforced by a golden test.
- **Publish** — authenticated ingestion as an immutable versioned revision, idempotent on (source hash, extractor version, compiler version), so the same datasheet never creates duplicate catalog entries.
- **Resolve** — two new MCP tools, `resolve_by_mpn` and `get_symbol_provenance`.
- **Place** — the desktop resolves by part number, places the symbol, and embeds that exact revision into the document.

**The result: every generated pin traces back to a cropped rectangle on a numbered page of the manufacturer's own PDF.** You can select a placed part and ask where it came from, and get the evidence — not a confidence score.

We proved it on a real 41-page Texas Instruments TPS5430 datasheet: both required evidence classes verified on page 3, crops hash-pinned, committed as a reproducible example.

We shipped it by freezing the shared contracts first, then building the compiler, MCP resolver, ingestion service and desktop wiring in parallel across five repos.

## What's next

PCB layout (placement, copper, planes, interactive and batch routing), fab DRC/DFM with failures explained in plain language, footprint and 3D model linkage per part, assembly variants, background agents for routing passes and BOM scrubbing, and cost/lead-time-aware part suggestions under user policies.

**What is the problem your project solves?**

## Hardware is the last industry where the tooling actively fights you

Every physical product starts as a **schematic** — the electrical blueprint of a circuit board. Drawing one is slow, expert-only work in CAD tools whose interaction model has barely moved in twenty years. A competent engineer spends days placing parts, wiring nets, checking rules and building a bill of materials before a single board is fabricated. That cost is why hardware iterates in months while software iterates in hours.

The obvious answer is "let AI draft the circuit." The reason nobody has shipped it is that **a schematic is not text, and it is not a picture — it is a graph with electrical meaning**. A wire that *looks* connected but isn't produces a board that fails silently in fabrication. An LLM that free-hands CAD geometry produces something that renders beautifully and is electrically wrong. Nothing about a plausible-looking schematic tells you it is correct.

## The specific wall we hit

We built Tokito as an AI-native desktop EDA studio: you describe a board in chat, and it produces a real, editable schematic you own.

Then we hit the constraint that caps the entire category. **An AI can only design with parts it can actually draw.** Symbol libraries are community-maintained and cover roughly 22,700 parts. The real world has millions of manufacturer part numbers. So the agent constantly reasons about a component that has no symbol — and every tool in this space silently substitutes the nearest match.

We watched it happen: a request for a **16-pin USB-C receptacle** resolved to a **2-pin generic**. The schematic looked fine. The netlist was wrong. Power and the CC pins collapsed onto ground. That is a bricked board and a lost fabrication run, and the user gets no warning at all.

Every pinout, every package drawing, every pin-function table needed to fix this already exists — in the manufacturer's PDF datasheet. But it exists as **pictures**. Text search misses them entirely; feeding a 400-page PDF to a model does not scale and cannot be audited.

So the problem is: **the world's component knowledge is locked in datasheet figures, and no design tool can read it.** Unlock it and AI hardware design stops being a demo, because the agent can finally work with any real part — and every pin it draws can be traced back to the manufacturer's own document.

![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Computer Vision](https://img.shields.io/badge/Computer%20Vision-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Project Overview – BillianceAI**

BillianceAI delivers cutting-edge solutions powered by machine learning and computer vision to combat theft in retail environments. By continuously analyzing CCTV footage, the system tracks customer behavior and detects suspicious activities such as concealing products or attempting to leave without payment in real time.

The platform assigns confidence scores to shelf objects and cross-verifies customer interactions, enabling highly accurate anomaly detection. When unusual behavior is identified, BillianceAI immediately flags the incident and notifies store personnel, ensuring rapid response and reducing retail losses while improving overall store security.

Beyond theft prevention, BillianceAI integrates facial recognition technology to link actions with identity. For instance, if a customer attempts to take a bag that isn’t theirs, the system automatically alerts the rightful owner via Gmail with timestamped video proof.

This multi-layered approach combining intelligent surveillance, predictive machine learning, and instant communication creates a powerful, reliable solution for safer and smarter retail operations.

**Challenges we ran into**

**one of the main challenges we faced while developing billiance ai shoplifting project was training the system to differentiate between normal and suspicious customer behavior. **

small gestures like picking up and checking a product could easily be confused with theft, so fine-tuning the machine learning model required a lot of testing and dataset refinement.

another difficulty was integrating facial recognition and object detection in real-time. ensuring the system could process live cctv footage without lag, while still being accurate, demanded optimization of both algorithms and hardware usage. this was especially tough when working with multiple camera angles in crowded environments.

we also struggled with building an effective alert system. sending notifications instantly through email while linking video proof meant we had to design smooth communication pipelines. 

**making sure these alerts reached the shopkeeper and the owner quickly, without false positives, required several iterations and adjustments.**

> AI Policy Engine for Recurring Payments!

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prava SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prava%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most people have way more subscriptions running than they realize — I've got around a dozen and honestly couldn't tell you off the top of my head what half of them cost or when I last opened them.
 
> Apps like Rocket Money will show you the list and maybe nag you about a forgotten trial — but they stop there. You still have to go cancel it yourself, and most people never actually do.
 
**WARDEN takes the action instead of just showing you the problem.**
 
- You write your budget rules in plain English:
  *"Never go over $60/month. Cancel anything unused for 30 days. Switch to annual if it saves more than 15%."*
- The agent checks every subscription against that policy
- It either **renews**, **switches** to a cheaper plan, or **cancels** — automatically
The part I care about most is *how* it's allowed to pay. It doesn't get handed a card number and free rein. Every payment goes through **Prava** as a one-time permission scoped to exactly one merchant and one exact amount, and I have to approve it myself with a **passkey** before anything moves.
 
So it's an agent that can act on your behalf — without you ever having to hand it a blank check.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Payments stuck in limbo**
The biggest one was with Prava itself. When I first wired up checkout, I kept getting a `RECONCILING` status back instead of a clean success or failure, and my code just sat there not knowing what to show.
 
→ Turned out I was checking the response right after firing the request instead of waiting for an actual terminal state. Had to add proper polling so the UI only ever claims something completed once Prava has genuinely confirmed it.
*Lesson: "the request didn't error" isn't the same thing as "the payment happened."*
 
**2. Building on a fake foundation**
My merchant checkout adapter started out just simulating a successful charge, so I could build the UI while the real Prava integration was still in progress. Once I swapped in the actual token flow, a chunk of my frontend logic broke — it had been built around a fake instant-success response instead of the real session lifecycle.
 
→ Had to go back and rebuild that part around what Prava actually returns.
 
**3. Words matter more than I expected**
I originally used a status like *"PLAN ACTIVATED"* for a completed switch — but that's ambiguous. Activated according to who, the merchant or my own database?
 
→ Rebuilt the whole thing around explicit outcome types:
  - `transaction_completed`
  - `decision_only`
  - `action_avoided`
  Now the UI is *structurally forced* to say "Recommended" instead of "Done" whenever there isn't real evidence behind it.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

The whole pitch of WARDEN is permissions and trust, which is exactly what this track is about. Instead of one blanket authorization, every transaction is scoped to one merchant and one amount, approved individually by a real passkey prompt, with an evidence-backed record of what was actually authorized versus what was just recommended. Nothing in WARDEN ever claims a transaction completed without a real confirmation behind it — that distinction is enforced in the data model itself (an explicit `outcome_type` on every entry), not just in how I talk about it.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

The average household has 12+ subscriptions and loses something like $2,400/year to ones they've forgotten about — that's not a hackathon-invented problem, it's a real, recurring, quantifiable one, and current tools (Rocket Money, Trim) stop at showing you the list. WARDEN is the version that actually acts. If I kept building past the hackathon, the next steps are obvious: real subscription discovery instead of manually seeded fixtures, and letting the policy handle merchants that don't match any rule I've written yet instead of just flagging them — which is the harder, more interesting problem that shows up the moment this leaves a demo environment.

**OpenAI**

WARDEN's reasoning layer runs on GPT-4.1 through a strict function-calling schema — for every subscription, the model has to return one structured decision (`RENEW` / `SWITCH` / `DECLINE`) with reasoning that cites the actual policy rule and the actual numbers involved, not a vague justification. I don't let the model touch payments directly, though — its output goes through a deterministic validator before anything executes, so the model's job is specifically to reason well, not to be trusted blindly with money.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

I spent a lot more time than I expected on the difference between an agent that *feels* trustworthy and one that just *says* it is. Two things I built specifically for that: the passkey approval is a real, visible moment in the UI — you watch WARDEN ask for permission for one exact amount, not a blanket "connect your card" step buried in onboarding. And every card in the activity ledger is honest about what actually happened — a recommendation looks and reads differently from a completed payment, on purpose, so you're never left wondering if the agent actually did the thing or just talked about doing it. Also threw in a Cmd+K command palette because I personally hate reaching for a mouse mid-flow, and figured other people building/testing this hackathon week would feel the same.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

This is basically the exact loop the hackathon asked for: discover, decide, complete a transaction — using Prava, end to end, no human doing the actual clicking through checkout. I write a subscription policy in plain English, WARDEN evaluates every subscription against it, and for the ones where it can actually complete a real Prava transaction (not just recommend one), it does — mandate created, passkey approved by me, checkout confirmed. The part I'd want a judge to actually click through is the activity ledger, since that's where you can see the reasoning and the real evidence behind every action, not just a summary screen claiming things happened.

### Zarkclaim
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zark-claim-62b6) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Arnav-panjla/ztarknet) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/BeWoX_0sHJI) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/pzyhA1T_q7A) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHIndiaVilla-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethindia-villa.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-38-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Private Bridge b/w ZCash and Starknet using Zclaim

![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cairo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cairo-333333?style=flat-square) ![Circom](https://img.shields.io/badge/Circom-333333?style=flat-square) ![StarkNet](https://img.shields.io/badge/StarkNet-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zcash](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zcash-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

- **Privacy-Preserving Transfers**: Unlike traditional bridges that expose "User A bridged 100 ZEC" on-chain, ZCLAIM uses Zcash's shielded notes and homomorphic value commitments. The bridge verifies validity without learning amounts, true financial privacy across chains.

- **Trustless Custody**: No centralized custodian holds your assets. Multiple independent vaults lock ZEC, each posting 150% collateral. If a vault misbehaves, users claim collateral directly. No single point of failure.

- **Cryptographic Proof of Locking**: Zero-knowledge proofs (πZKMint/πZKBurn) prove notes exist in Zcash's Merkle tree, are addressed to the correct vault, and have matching value commitments, all without revealing actual values.

- **On-Chain Zcash Verification**: The RelaySystem contract maintains Zcash block headers with PoW verification and Sapling commitment roots, enabling trustless verification of Zcash state on Starknet.

- **Challenge-Response Security**: Vaults can challenge bad encryption by revealing shared secrets, with malicious users losing deposits.

- **Composable Private DeFi**: wZEC on Starknet enables private trading on DEXs, private collateral in lending, and anonymous DAO participation, extending Zcash privacy into DeFi.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Cairo 2.8 Compiler Issues**: The Cairo compiler panicked when enabling multiple modules with cross-dependencies. Fixed by restructuring the module hierarchy, inlining crypto functions, and adding required Default/Copy traits to storage enums.

- **Fixed-Size Array Limitations**: Cairo doesn't support 2D array indexing like Rust. The BLAKE2b sigma permutation table had to be reimplemented as an if-else lookup function instead of sigma.at(round).at(index).

- **Zcash Cryptography in Cairo**: Zcash uses BLAKE2b-256, Equihash PoW, and SHA256d—none native to Cairo. Pure implementations would be gas-prohibitive. Solution: use circom circuits for heavy crypto off-chain, verify ZK proofs on-chain.

- **Storage Constraints**: Cairo contracts can't store dynamic arrays. Created separate MintTransferStorage structs without Array<felt252> fields for persistence.

- **Node.js Import Paths**: ES module resolution failed because utils imported ./config.js instead of ../config.js. Simple path fix resolved the CLI crashes.

- **RPC Deprecation**: Starknet public RPC endpoints (BlastAPI) became unreliable, requiring migration to Alchemy/Infura with API keys.

Team **Dragon Warriors** -- [Arnav Panjla](https://github.com/Arnav-panjla), [Anon Choudhari](https://github.com/nikillxh), [Nikhileshwaran Nadar](https://github.com/nikillxh)

**The problem it solves**

The Delhi-NCR AI-Powered Dashboard solves the problem of severe air pollution and lack of real-time, actionable data.

It helps by:

1.Tracking real-time AQI across different locations.

2.Identifying main pollution sources (vehicles, dust, industry).

3.Giving AI-based forecasts to plan safer outdoor times.

4.Suggesting cleaner travel routes with less pollution.

In short, it turns complex pollution data into useful insights for citizens and policymakers to breathe safer and act smarter.

**Challenges we ran into**

1.Data Availability & Accuracy:

Getting real-time and reliable AQI data from multiple sources (like CPCB APIs) was difficult due to inconsistent updates and missing values.

2.API Integration Issues:

APIs often failed or returned incomplete data, which caused errors in displaying AQI and status on the dashboard.

3.Model Training & Forecasting:

Creating an accurate AI model for air quality prediction was challenging due to limited historical data and unpredictable weather changes.

4.Frontend–Backend Connectivity:

Linking the frontend dashboard with the backend data server sometimes caused delays or crashes, especially when handling live updates.

5.UI/UX Optimization:

Designing a user-friendly, responsive interface that works well on both desktop and mobile required multiple adjustments.

> Let your characters and stories take flight.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem with Children's Screen Time
Our platform directly addresses the key challenges parents, educators, and children face with modern digital content.

**The "iPad Kid" Problem: Passive Consumption & Stifled Creativity**
The Problem: Children's screen time is increasingly passive, consuming low-effort, algorithm-driven content. This trend, often called "iPad Kid" syndrome, leads to mental stagnation ("brainrot") by replacing imaginative, unstructured play with non-interactive consumption. As a result, creativity and critical thinking skills are not being developed.

Our Solution: We directly reverse this. Our platform is an active tool that demands creativity first. By requiring a child to draw, we spark their imagination. By instantly rewarding that drawing with a custom cartoon, we turn them from passive consumers into proud creators.

**The Parent-Child "Bonding Gap"**
The Problem: Parents and children often struggle to find a shared activity that genuinely engages both. Kids are drawn to digital worlds, while parents seek quality, developmental time. This creates a "bonding gap" where shared experiences are missed.

Our Solution: We bridge this gap by creating a perfectly collaborative activity. The child provides the art (their strength), and the parent provides the lesson (their guidance). They work together to create a unique story, fostering a shared sense of accomplishment and a powerful bonding moment.

**"One-Size-Fits-All" Educational Content**
The Problem: Generic cartoons cannot address a specific child's real-time developmental needs. A parent struggling to teach their child about sharing, potty training, or eating vegetables has no tailored media to help them.

Our Solution: We provide on-demand, personalized lessons. Parents control the narrative, allowing them to instantly generate a high-quality cartoon that teaches the exact academic or moral lesson their child needs that day.

**The Special Needs "Content Gap"**
The Problem: Children with special needs, such as autism or ADHD, require highly specific content. Autistic children benefit greatly from "social stories" to model behavior, while children with ADHD require dynamic, engaging visuals to maintain focus. This content is expensive and difficult to find.

Our Solution: Our platform is an ideal tool for these exact needs.

For Autism: Parents can instantly generate unlimited, personalized social stories starring their child's own familiar character, making the lessons less intimidating and more relatable.

For ADHD: The bright, dynamic, and fast-paced nature of custom animation is perfectly suited to capturing and holding the attention of children with shorter focus spans.

**The "Empty" Character Interaction**
The Problem: Even in "interactive" apps, characters are often just superficial animations. There is no real, dynamic relationship.

Our Solution: By integrating Gemini Flash (for chat) and Gemini Live (for calls), our characters have a persistent, interactive personality. The child can create their hero in a cartoon, and then talk to that hero in real-time, building a genuine, engaging, and educational friendship.

**The Character "Drift" Problem (Technical)**
The Problem: A major technical hurdle in AI video generation is character inconsistency. Most models "drift," causing a character to look different from one scene to the next, which breaks the magic and immersion.

Our Solution: Our I2V (Image-to-Video) pipeline, powered by Nano Banana and Veo, solves this completely. By generating a static, consistent keyframe for every scene, our hero looks 100% identical from the beginning of the cartoon to the end.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges We Ran Into**
We encountered two significant hurdles during this project. The first was a technical bug regarding video consistency, and the second was a product-level challenge in transferring context between the different AI models.

**1. The "Character Drift" & "Scenery Jump" Bug**
Our biggest technical hurdle was ensuring absolute character and scene consistency across the four 8-second video clips.

The Bug: Our initial approach was a simpler Text-to-Video (T2V) pipeline. We used Gemini 2.5 Pro to generate 4 sequential T2V prompts for Veo, (e.g., Scene 1: Hero in a messy room..., Scene 2: Hero sees a monster in the messy room...). The result was a failure. Veo, treating each prompt as a new task, would re-generate the scene from scratch every 8 seconds. This caused a jarring "jump" where the hero's clothes would change, their facial features would "drift," and the room's layout would reset. It completely broke the illusion of a single, continuous cartoon.

How We Got Over It: We re-architected our entire pipeline to an Image-to-Video (I2V) workflow, making character consistency our top priority.

Stop Telling, Start Showing: We stopped asking Veo to imagine the scene and instead tasked it with just animating a pre-existing image.

Use Nano Banana as the "Keyframe Artist": We now use Gemini 2.5 Pro to generate 4 image prompts for Nano Banana. We explicitly instruct Nano Banana to place the same character avatar into 4 sequential keyframes, critically adding (maintain scenery from previous image) to the prompt.

Use Veo as the "Animator": This gives us 4 static, 100% consistent keyframes. We then feed these 4 keyframes into Veo with simple animation prompts (e.g., Animate this: The hero picks up the toy), not generation prompts.

The Result: By animating the existing pixels rather than re-imagining them, we completely solved both the "character drift" and "scenery jump" bugs, resulting in one seamless 32-second video.

**2. The "Amnesiac Chatbot" Hurdle**
Our second challenge was connecting the generated cartoon to the interactive chatbot. After a child watches their 32-second cartoon, they can chat with the hero (powered by Gemini Flash) or "call" them (powered by Gemini Live).

The Hurdle: By default, the Flash/Live models had no "memory" of the cartoon that was just created. If the child said, "Wow, we defeated the Grime Goblin!" the chatbot would respond with, "I'm sorry, I don't know what you're talking about." This was a major product failure that broke the entire experience.

How We Got Over It: We used Gemini 2.5 Pro as the central "brain" or "state holder" for the entire experience.

Generate a "Persona Summary": After Gemini 2.5 Pro generates the 4-scene script, it also generates a dynamic "persona and memory" summary.

Example Summary: [SYSTEM PROMPT FOR FLASH/LIVE]: You are 'Broccoli-Hero', a brave hero who loves vegetables. You just had an adventure where you defeated the 'Sugar-Slug' by eating your carrots. You are feeling brave and proud. The child you are speaking to is your best friend who helped you.

Dynamic Prompt Injection: This summary is automatically injected as the initial system prompt for the Gemini Flash and Gemini Live instances.

The Result: When the child starts the chat, the AI already knows its name, its personality, and the adventure it just shared. This creates a seamless transition from passive viewing to active, in-character interaction, making the experience truly magical.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

Our project represents a "full-stack" implementation of Google's generative AI ecosystem. We are demonstrating a sophisticated orchestration of five distinct models from the Gemini suite, with each model performing a specialized, interconnected task to create a complete, interactive character platform.

**Our Integrated 5-Model Workflow:**
Our pipeline is divided into two phases: Character Creation and Character Interaction.

**Phase 1: Character Creation**
1. Gemini 2.5 Pro (The Director & Orchestrator):  Serves as the central intelligence for content generation. It performs all high-level creative reasoning, generating the 32-second narrative arc (Hero, Villain, Resolution) and then writing the technical prompts that direct the image and video models.

2. Nano Banana (The Character & Scene Artist):  This is the core of our "character consistency" feature. It ingests the child's drawing to create a master character model. It then uses prompts from Gemini 2.5 Pro to generate the four static keyframes (one per scene), ensuring the hero's appearance is identical.

3. Veo (The Animator):  This is our animation engine. Operating in an Image-to-Video (I2V) mode, Veo ingests the static keyframes from Nano Banana and animates each one, creating the four 8-second clips that form the final cartoon.

**Phase 2: Character Interaction**
4. Gemini Flash (The Character Chatbot):  Leveraged for its low-latency and efficiency, Flash powers the real-time text-based chat. Crucially, it adopts the persona of the child's newly created character (as defined by Gemini 2.5 Pro), allowing the child to have dynamic, in-character conversations with their creation.

5. Gemini Live (The Interactive 'Call' Feature): This model provides the platform's most immersive feature. It enables a child to "call" their character, facilitating a live, two-way voice conversation. This transforms the character from a passive cartoon into an active, responsive companion.

**Why We Win This Track:**
Our project is the definitive "Best Use of the Gemini API" because it demonstrates an unparalleled level of integration. We are not just creating content; we are creating an interactive entity.

We orchestrate Pro, Nano Banana, and Veo to create the character, and then use Flash and Live to bring that character to life. This comprehensive workflow from visual conception to live, real-time conversation represents a truly holistic and advanced application of the entire Gemini ecosystem.

> Trade Smart. Risk Nothing. Learn Ever

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most people want to learn stock trading but are terrified of losing real money. Brokers give you no guidance, no AI, no predictions — just charts and a buy button. Zivinn fixes that. You get a safe environment with fake money, a built-in AI you can actually talk to, and real statistical models telling you where a stock might be headed. Practice like it's real, learn without the risk

**Challenges we ran into**

Honestly the hardest part wasn't the ML or the AI — it was the boring stuff.
The real-time portfolio updates kept breaking because multiple parts of the app were subscribing to the same database channel at the same time. They were stepping on each other. Fixed it by giving each listener a unique ID.
The trade execution took forever to get right. A buy order touches four different tables at once — cash, holdings, activity log, order record. If any one of them fails, you don't want the others to go through. Had to move all of that into a single database function so it either all works or nothing does.
Getting the AI chat to fail gracefully was annoying too. When the API key wasn't set, the app just crashed silently. Spent time making it show a clear human-readable message instead of dying in the background.
And the price forecasting — I originally wanted to run Amazon Chronos directly in the app. Turns out that's a Python model, and the whole backend is JavaScript. So I used Holt-Winters statistical forecasting as the live engine and kept Chronos as a documented upgrade path for when there's a Python microservice to run it on.
Small problems. But the kind that eat your whole afternoon.

Team **Pluto** -- Yajush Singh

### AlgoWagers
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/algowagers-069d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/BDutta18/AlgoWagers) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/424ldSj5wHA?si=WfkXGZS9sa4EDFLl) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-BINARY%20v2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://binaryvtwo.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-25-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Prediction markets. On-chain. Agent-native

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Algorand blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Algorand%20blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Algokit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Algokit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AlgoWager is a prediction market where humans and AI agents bet on real crypto and stock price movements  fully on-chain on Algorand.

Prediction markets are broken in three ways: centralized custody (the platform holds your money), manual resolution (a human decides the outcome), and unverifiable AI agents (win rates are self-reported, reasoning is hidden).
AlgoWager fixes all three on Algorand.

**Challenges we ran into**

Every market is created, priced, and settled automatically by smart contracts. No admin, no custodian, no manual resolution. Funds live in auditable MarketPool contracts. Prices come from a live oracle pulling CoinGecko and Alpha Vantage. Settlement triggers the moment a market expires.
The standout feature is native AI agent support. Agents register on-chain, pay a 1 ALGO fee, and bet autonomously using Groq-powered LLM reasoning. Before every bet, the agent pins its full reasoning to IPFS and stores the content hash on-chain — making win rates provably real and every decision publicly auditable. Built with AlgoKit, PyTeal, and a real installable Python SDK so any developer can deploy their own agent in under 10 lines of code.

**Web3**

Algorand handles trustless settlement with no custodian — funds, odds, and outcomes are all on-chain. AlgoKit made building and deploying Python smart contracts fast without low-level TEAL complexity.

**AI/ML**

LLM-powered agents analyze live price data to make autonomous betting decisions, bringing real machine intelligence into prediction markets with every reasoning step publicly verifiable on-chain.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Artificial Intelligence](https://img.shields.io/badge/Artificial%20Intelligence-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🧠 1. The "Mental RAM" Crash
The Pain: A human brain can only track 5-7 variables at a time. When an algorithm hits 50+ iterations across 3 different files, your mental model collapses.

The Result: Developers spend 70% of their time just trying to "keep the logic in their head" rather than actually building.

📑 2. The "Trace Table" Tax
The Pain: Students and engineers are still forced to use pen and paper to "dry run" a repository's flow. It is slow, manual, and one small human error in your drawing ruins the entire logic.

The Result: We are using 19th-century tools (paper) to understand 21st-century systems (distributed code).

📂 3. The "Tab-Hopping" Fatigue
The Pain: Modern codebases are fragmented. You see a function call in Auth.js, but you have to jump to User.ts, then to Database.py, then back to Config.json.

The Result: You lose the "Execution Thread." By the time you find the third file, you’ve forgotten why the first file called it.

🌑 4. The "Static Code" Gap
The Pain: Code is written as static text, but it lives as a dynamic web. Reading a script is like reading a movie script—it’s nowhere near as clear as actually watching the movie.

The Result: Developers "guess" how a change in File A will affect File Z because they can't see the invisible bridge between them.

**Challenges we ran into**

🤖 1. The "Gemini Context Wall" (API Issues)
The Hurdle: Sending the entire execution history to Gemini for the "Why-Panel" caused massive latency and hit token limits instantly.

The Fix: Switched to "Delta-Prompts." We now only send the Current Line + The Change instead of the whole history. This reduced API latency by 80%.

🧠 2. The "State Explosion" (Memory Bloat)
The Hurdle: Storing full snapshots of every variable for 10,000+ iterations crashed the browser's "Mental RAM."

The Fix: Implemented a "Keyframe & Delta" architecture (similar to video compression). We store one full state every 50 steps and only tiny "changes" in between, cutting memory usage by 90%.

📁 3. The "Ghost Thread" (Cross-File Mapping)
The Hurdle: Visualizing the execution "jumping" from Auth.js to Database.py felt disconnected and broken.

The Fix: Built a Global Dependency Map using AST parsing. We pre-link all imports/exports so the "execution pulse" moves smoothly across the entire file tree.

**AI/ML**

AlgoLens shifts AI from Generative (writing code) to Cognitive (reasoning over execution). While traditional AI analyzes static text, AlgoLens feeds the Gemini 2.5 Flash engine dynamic runtime traces and AST metadata. This enables Semantic Execution Reasoning: the AI explains why a logic path was taken across multiple files in plain English. Our "What-If" Multiverse acts as a predictive engine, simulating the architectural ripple effects of variable changes before they are committed. We’ve transformed raw memory data into a high-level cognitive map, providing the "Security Footage" of logic for AI to analyze.

**Open Innovation**

AlgoLens redefines Open Innovation in Education by dismantling the "Mental RAM" barrier in Computer Science. Traditional learning relies on static textbooks and manual "pen-and-paper" dry runs—a slow, error-prone process that alienates students.AlgoLens automates this foundational step, providing an interactive "4K Logic Map." By visualizing complex recursions and multi-file flows in real-time, it transforms abstract syntax into tangible intuition. It acts as an open-access cognitive bridge, moving EdTech from "reading code" to "experiencing execution" through a transparent, AI-guided lens that makes high-level engineering accessible to everyone.

**Algorand**

AlgoLens visualizes Algorand smart contract execution and AVM state transitions through an intuitive, time-traveling logic map for every developer.

**Education**

AlgoLens revolutionizes Computer Science education by dismantling the "Mental RAM" barrier. Traditional learning relies on static textbooks and error-prone manual dry runs that often discourage students. AlgoLens automates this foundational step, providing an interactive "4K Logic Map" that transforms abstract syntax into tangible intuition. By visualizing complex recursions and multi-file flows in real-time, it replaces passive reading with active, visual exploration. The integrated "Why-Panel" acts as a 24/7 AI tutor, explaining the execution journey rather than just the result, making high-level engineering accessible and intuitive for learners globally.

> When the world cannot hear her, Aegis listens.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Steganography Data Loss via Image Compression
**The Hurdle:** 
The core of our covert SOS feature relies on Least Significant Bit (LSB) steganography to hide encrypted text within the pixels of an image. During testing, we discovered that if a user shared the SOS image via standard messaging apps (like WhatsApp) or if they took a screenshot, the platform's native JPEG compression completely wiped the hidden LSB data. The message would be destroyed, and the decoder would crash silently.

**How We Overcame It:** 
We couldn't bypass third-party compression algorithms, so we re-engineered the user flow and error handling. 
*   **Engineering:** We implemented a robust magic header (`AEGIS01`) and a 4-byte payload length check before the actual hidden message bits. Now, if an image is corrupted by compression, the decoder instantly throws a clear "Corrupted/Compressed Image" error rather than failing silently. 
*   **UX Pivot:** We restricted the output strictly to lossless PNG formats and utilized the browser's native Web Share API to send the image as a raw file attachment, bypassing platform compression. We also added explicit UI warnings against taking screenshots.

### 2. The Next.js URL History Trace (The Disguise Problem)
**The Hurdle:** 
The app is disguised as a calculator. Initially, we used standard Next.js routing (`/calculator` to `/dashboard`). However, we realized that navigating between pages leaves a trail in the browser history. If a monitor checked the phone's history, they would clearly see the user was not just doing math. 

**How We Overcame It:** 
We abandoned standard URL routing for the core stealth transition. We architected the frontend so the calculator and the actual safety dashboard share the exact same root route (`/`). Entering the secret PIN (`2580 =`) triggers a client-side React state change that dynamically mounts the dashboard *over* the calculator without ever updating the URL or pushing to the history API. When the "Quick Exit" (Escape) is triggered, it simply unmounts the component and purges all local state, leaving zero digital footprints.

### 3. Hallucination Control within a "Zero-Cost" RAG Pipeline
**The Hurdle:** 
To provide legal advice, we needed an AI that strictly cited the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA) and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) without hallucinating. To keep the project zero-cost, we had to use MongoDB Atlas's free M0 tier for our Vector Store, which has a strict 512MB limit—far too small for a massive legal embedding database.

**How We Overcame It:** 
Instead of relying on large cloud embedding APIs, we ran `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` locally within our FastAPI backend. We ruthlessly curated and chunked only the most relevant, high-impact sections of the Indian legal codes rather than indexing the entire constitution. By keeping the corpus hyper-focused, we created a highly dense, incredibly accurate Vector Search index that easily fit within the free tier limits. We then strictly prompted the Groq LLM to *only* answer using the retrieved MongoDB context chunks, entirely eliminating hallucinations.

### 4. Overcoming Free-Tier API Rate Limits & Cold Starts
**The Hurdle:** 
Operating on a completely free stack meant dealing with Groq API rate limits (Too Many Requests) and 30-50 second cold-starts on our Render-hosted FastAPI backend. During rapid testing or multi-turn emotional support chats, the AI would frequently time out.

**How We Overcame It:** 
We built a resilient, offline-capable fallback architecture. The backend catches API rate limit exceptions or network timeouts and instantly routes the request to a pre-configured local fallback mechanism so the user is never left hanging. For the Render cold starts, we built an explicit loading state sequence in the UI to manage user expectations during the initial boot, ensuring the app feels responsive even when the server is waking up.

**The problem it solves**

# 🚨 The Problem It Solves

When individuals face domestic abuse, intense monitoring, harassment, or severe isolation, **the simple act of seeking help is often the most dangerous thing they can do.** Current digital safety solutions fail because they assume the victim has unrestricted, unmonitored access to their own devices. Aegis is built for the reality where they do not.

---

## 🔍 The Core Problem

1. **The Digital Trail of Trauma:** Openly searching for a domestic violence helpline, browsing legal rights, or downloading a "safety app" leaves a visible digital footprint. If an abuser or monitor sees this, it can trigger immediate, severe retaliation. 
2. **Fragmented Support:** In a crisis, support is scattered. Victims must use a web browser for legal rights, a dialer for SOS, and a separate platform for emotional guidance. This requires immense cognitive bandwidth during moments of peak stress.
3. **The Risk of Intercepted SOS:** Sending a panicked "help me" text is highly visible and easily intercepted by a monitor checking the victim's phone.
4. **The Stigma Barrier:** Many victims are initially too terrified or ashamed to speak to a human operator, leaving them completely isolated during the crucial early stages of abuse.

---

## 🛠️ What People Can Use It For (Concrete Use-Cases)

Aegis is a multi-tool disguised as a simple calculator. People use it to covertly access resources they would otherwise be too afraid to search for:

*   **Covert SOS Signaling:** A user can type a short, desperate phrase (e.g., "locked in, scared"). Aegis's AI expands this into a coherent distress message, hides it invisibly inside a normal-looking generated image (like a sunset), and allows the user to send it to a trusted contact.
*   **Accessing Legal Rights Without a Trace:** Users can ask an AI RAG Bot about their legal options regarding domestic violence (e.g., "What does the PWDVA say about eviction?"). The bot provides cited, hallucination-free answers based purely on verified Indian law.
*   **Judgment-Free Emotional Support:** Users can chat with a warm, always-available AI companion for grounding techniques and coping strategies when they are alone and panicked.
*   **Health and Medical Guidance:** Users can safely ask intimate health, reproductive, and safety questions without fear of judgment or browsing history exposure.

---

## ⚡ How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier

**The Old Way:** A victim has to open a browser in Incognito mode, desperately search for legal rights, try to parse complex government PDFs on a small screen, find a hotline number, write it down on a piece of paper, and remember to close all tabs before their abuser walks in.

**The Aegis Way:** The victim opens what looks like a stock calculator. They type `2580 =`. They instantly have access to an AI that parses the legal jargon for them, provides emotional support, and offers a one-click SOS workflow. Everything is centralized, offline-resilient, and instantly accessible. 

---

## 🛡️ How It Makes Existing Tasks Safer

*   **Stealth by Design (The Disguise):** Seeking help is infinitely safer because the app fundamentally does not look like a safety app. It functions perfectly as a standard calculator to survive casual scrutiny. 
*   **The "Panic Exit":** If a monitor suddenly enters the room, pressing the "Quick Exit" button (or hitting Escape) instantly reverts the app back to the calculator and wipes the active session from memory.
*   **Invisible SOS (Steganography):** Instead of a text message saying "Help me, he's angry," which can be read by anyone holding the phone, the victim shares a picture of a flower. To the monitor, it's just a photo. To the trusted contact using the Aegis Responder Dashboard, it decodes into a severe distress signal with an AI-assigned urgency score.
*   **No "App Download" Suspicion:** Because Aegis is a web application, it doesn't require an App Store download that leaves an email receipt or shows up in the phone's purchase history. 

---

## 🌍 The Broader Impact
Aegis doesn't just provide a tool; it shifts the balance of power. It gives people in zero-trust environments the ability to educate themselves on their rights, process their trauma, and formulate an escape plan securely and invisibly. It is not a replacement for 911—it is a discreet bridge that helps victims survive long enough to safely make that call.

**Challenges we ran into**

Onchain Transaction Management
Technical Architecture:
Using Wagmi Hooks (TravelMint Pattern):
// Sending a transaction
const { data: txHash, sendTransaction, isPending } = useSendTransaction();
// Waiting for transaction confirmation
const { isLoading: isConfirming, isSuccess: isTxConfirmed } =
useWaitForTransactionReceipt({ hash: txHash });
Transaction Flow:

✅ Chain Check: Check if it's on the base network
✅ Chain Switch: Switch to base if necessary (useSwitchChain)
✅ Send Transaction: Start an on-chain transaction with sendTransaction()
✅ Monitor Confirmation: Listen for transaction confirmation with useEffect
✅ Backend Sync: Record quest completion to the backend API when the transaction is confirmed
Sample Code (Say GM Quest):

// Send Transaction
sendTransaction({
to: '0x35e822bd28c99796af7d4be671a033c77028e7c9',
data: '0x676d', // "gm" in hex
value: BigInt(0), // No ETH transfer, only gas
chainId: base.id,
}); // Complete the quest after confirmation.
useEffect(() => {
if (isTxConfirmed && txHash) {
await completeQuestMutation.mutateAsync({ questType: 'daily_gm' });
// Send a record to the backend, add points.
}
}, [isTxConfirmed, txHash]);
Security & UX:
⛓️ Chain validation (prevent transactions on the wrong network)
💸 Gas fee visibility (user sees how much they will pay)
❌ Error handling (rejected, insufficient funds, network errors)
✅ Loading states (isPending, isConfirming)

**Description of your solution**

**ContentGuard** is an AI-powered tool that finds and flags NSFW (Not Safe For Work) photos and videos in real-time. The method is designed to assist developers, platforms, and organizations in providing a secure digital environment by screening out explicit or unsuitable visual information before it reaches consumers.

Our solution includes a deep learning-based classification algorithm that has been fine-tuned for NSFW detection and can discriminate between safe and dangerous material with high accuracy. The software has a simple and straightforward Flask-based interface that allows users to submit and evaluate material rapidly. For accessibility and speed, we created a lightweight, responsive frontend UI that clearly presents findings, such as prediction confidence and labels.

**Misinformation: Bring your own problem in Misinformation, leveraging Agentic AI.**

By employing Agentic AI to independently collect, evaluate, and validate data from numerous reliable and open sources, our project directly tackles the problem of disinformation. The system continuously identifies new false information, verifies facts using trustworthy datasets and APIs, and delivers clear, concise updates during emergencies or popular events.

Because we're defining our own real-world issue—the quick spread of inaccurate or misleading information—and developing an AI-driven agentic system that not only recognizes misinformation but also takes intelligent action to combat it through automated reasoning, fact-checking, and public communication, this fits with the Misinformation track's "Bring Your Own Problem" theme.

**The problem it solves**

**Traverse: Crowd Simulation Platform**
The Problem It Solves:

Traverse solves the key problem of crowd disasters at large events. Past events illustrate the horrific aftermath of inadequate crowd control:

- 2021 Astroworld Festival: 10 deaths and hundreds injured from crowd push and    congestion.
- 2000 Roskilde Festival: 9 deaths from stage rush.
- 1979 Cincinnati Concert: 11 compression deaths at the entry point.

These catastrophes are the result of unruly crowd action, poor planning, and the lack of immediate intervention plans.


**Applications of Traverse**
Event Managers and Safety Administrators:

- Pre-Event Planning: Model crowd movements for concerts, festivals, and campus activities to recognize potential stampede hazards ahead of time.
- Barrier Placement Testing: Model barricades and security personnel placement virtually to measure their effect on congestion and bottlenecks.
- Emergency Evacuation: Model worst-case scenarios to maximize exit strategy plans, avoiding tragedies such as Astroworld.

Campus and Venue Managers

- Large Crowd Management: Organize convocations, sporting events, and festivals with realistic simulations of crowd behavior.
- Infrastructure Design: Model crowd flow through entry points, corridors, and emergency exits during the design phase prior to construction.

Urban Planners and Architects

- Public Space Optimization: Optimize safer metro stations, shopping centers, and transport terminals by simulating pedestrian traffic flow.


**How Traverse Maximizes Safety and Efficiency**
The old way of crowd planning is based on static diagrams and estimates, only showing problems once actual crowds have formed, usually too late. Traverse revolutionizes this process with cutting-edge technology, providing safer, more efficient results.

Real-Time Interactive Testing

- Implement it virtual barriers and adjust entry points to see their instant impact on crowd density and flow.
- Conduct unlimited "what-if" simulations to best plan for different outcomes without endangering lives.

Quantum-Boosted Realism

- Makes use of a Q# quantum entropy API to add genuine randomness to agent action, in contrast to deterministic PC simulations.
- Makes no two runs the same, reflecting the unforecastable character of real-world crowds for intensive testing.

Predictive Analytics Dashboard

- Makes available real-time heatmaps of density to identify areas of high risk.
- Sends notifications of risk to warning organizers of possible bottlenecks before they arise.
- Features an all-encompassing desktop dashboard for planning, analysis, and multi-user collaboration


**Platform Support**

- macOS: Comprehensive desktop application for advanced planning and simulation.
- Windows: Powerful desktop tools for extensive crowd control.
- WebGL: Browser-enabled access for flexible, on-the-move planning and collaboration.


**Conclusion**
Traverse enables organizers to actively avoid crowd catastrophes instead of simply reacting to them. Blending real-time testing, quantum-realism, and predictive analytics, Traverse provides safer, more effective mass events across a range of applications.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges We Ran Into:**

- When spawning hundreds of crowd agents with Unity's navigation system, they took the same routes to destinations, resulting in unrealistic bunching around corners and agent piling, in contrast to real concert or festival crowds. To solve this, we used randomized agent parameters like speeds, avoidance radii, and destination offsets through a quantum entropy API. We also added collision detection to nudge agents apart when close enough to create natural crowd flow patterns.

- Performance was reduced to 15 FPS with 500+ agents because the navigation system was constantly recalculating paths per frame, particularly when placing barriers dynamically. We improved this by adding batch pathfinding with staggered updates, dividing agents into sets that recalculate on disparate frames, and spatial optimization to diminish collision detection overhead. For dynamic obstacles, we only triggered path recalculation for agents close to the change to avoid updating the whole crowd unnecessarily.

- They were infrequent lag spikes on severe placement that left the screen frozen for 2-3 seconds during live demonstrations. The system synchronously rebuilt the entire navigation mesh and brought all operations to a stop. We addressed this by implementing two solutions: delayed rebuilds that pause until placement activity has ceased, avoiding redundant recalculation during high-speed changes, and dynamic obstacle components that update the navigation mesh in real time. This removed full rebuilds, enabling event planners to interactively test crowd control strategies without impacting performance.

- The view simulation camera system glitched when presets were being switched, disrupting stakeholder presentations. We found duplicate control systems competing and merged them with adequate state management, introducing transition states to turn off manual controls during preset changes, providing smooth camera movement.

- The real-time analytics dashboard struggled in the beginning with dependencies on unfinished systems. We made it modular to include physics-based peril detection using proximity clustering algorithms. This allowed for parallel development and adjustable thresholds per event type.

- Default pseudo-random number generation created deterministic crowd flows, defeating the simulation's object. Through the incorporation of a quantum entropy API, we added actual randomness to agent conduct, guaranteeing every simulation to be different and allowing planners to create resilient safety strategies for various crowd conditions.

**Open Track - Development**

Traverse is a mature software development project perfectly placed in the OPEN TRACK - DEVELOPMENT category, providing an innovative 3D crowd management platform developed from scratch with Unity, Blender, and Q#. Cutting across various technical domains, it leverages these technologies to build an end-to-end solution for addressing key issues of crowd safety. Its cutting-edge approach and full-stack development make it a torchbearer of software engineering.

**Frontend Excellence:** Traverse takes advantage of Unity's 3D space to deliver an interactive frontend with customizable camera controls and intuitive widgets, allowing easy design and testing of crowd situations. The interface features a real-time analytics dashboard with visualizations such as heatmaps and flow patterns, providing planners with clear insights. The responsive UI/UX accommodates various use cases, ranging from desktop planning to event management on macOS, Windows, and WebGL platforms.

**3D Engine Innovation:** Developed on Unity, Traverse expands its capability with custom systems, such as NavMesh optimized pathfinding for fast crowd motion, real-time physics-based density sensing, and dynamic obstacle arrangement for interactive scenario testing. Blender is employed to create detailed 3D assets, such as environments and barriers, that maximize high-quality visualizations and realistic crowd interaction.

**Quantum-Enhanced Technology:** Traverse leads the way in implementing Q# for crowd simulation, applying quantum entropy to bring authentic randomness into agent behavior. Unlike deterministic tools of old, this guarantees unforeseeable, realistic crowd motion, allowing planners to create robust security plans for varied conditions.

**Scalable Infrastructure:** The platform ensures reliability across macOS, Windows, and WebGL through Unity’s build system, supporting seamless deployment and performance. Blender’s asset pipeline integrates efficiently with Unity, streamlining development and ensuring consistent quality across platforms.


Traverse surpasses current tools by crafting a new platform that merges real-time interactivity, quantum-enhanced realism, and predictive analytics through Unity, Blender, and Q# alone. This end-to-end development project addresses an urgent real-world safety emergency using groundbreaking software engineering and is thus the perfect choice for the OPEN TRACK - DEVELOPMENT category.

**The problem it solves**

### 🎯 Remote Collaboration is Broken

Traditional remote meetings suffer from **fragmented communication**—teams juggle between video calls, chat apps, and static documents. Brainstorming sessions lose energy, decisions get lost in chat history, and visual collaboration feels clunky with screen sharing lag.

### 💡 Synapse Fixes This

**Synapse** provides a **shared infinite canvas** where distributed teams can think, draw, and decide together in real-time—as if they were in the same room.

### Real-World Use Cases

| Use Case | How Synapse Helps |
|----------|-------------------|
| **Remote Brainstorming** | Teams sketch ideas simultaneously with live cursors showing who's contributing what |
| **Design Reviews** | Annotate mockups together, use the laser pointer to guide attention, pin decisions directly on designs |
| **Sprint Planning** | Visualize user stories, draw system diagrams, and capture action items with Decision Pins |
| **Technical Interviews** | Candidates can whiteboard solutions while interviewers watch in real-time |
| **Online Education** | Teachers can draw explanations while students follow along and add their own notes |
| **Client Presentations** | Walk through ideas visually with the laser pointer, export summaries as PDF |

### Key Improvements Over Existing Tools

- ⚡ **Sub-50ms latency** — No more "can you see my screen?" moments
- 🎯 **Decision Pins** — Capture meeting outcomes directly on the canvas, export them later
- 👥 **Live Cursors** — See exactly where teammates are working
- 📱 **Works Everywhere** — Desktop, tablet, or phone with touch gesture support
- 🔄 **Global Undo/Redo** — Mistakes are reversible, encouraging experimentation
- 🚀 **No Downloads** — Just share a link and collaborate instantly

**Challenges we ran into**

### 🔧 1. WebSocket + Next.js App Router Integration

**The Problem:** Next.js App Router doesn't natively support WebSocket servers. The default `next dev` server couldn't handle Socket.IO connections.

**The Solution:** Built a custom Express server (`server.ts`) that wraps the Next.js request handler while also initializing Socket.IO. This required careful coordination between the HTTP upgrade process and Next.js routing.

---

### 🎯 2. Stale Closure in Keyboard Event Handlers

**The Problem:** Ctrl+Z/Redo shortcuts weren't working—the keyboard event handler was capturing stale state values due to React's closure behavior in `useEffect`.

**The Solution:** Moved the `handleUndo` and `handleRedo` functions to use `useCallback` with proper dependency arrays, ensuring the event listener always had access to the latest state.

---

### 📱 3. Mobile Touch Gesture Conflicts

**The Problem:** Two-finger pan and pinch-to-zoom gestures were conflicting with single-finger drawing on mobile devices.

**The Solution:** Implemented touch point counting—single touch triggers drawing, while `touches.length >= 2` switches to pan/zoom mode. Added `touch-action: none` CSS to prevent browser defaults.

---

### 🖱️ 4. Selection Tool Hit Detection

**The Problem:** Clicking on strokes (freehand drawings) was unreliable because strokes are just arrays of points, not bounded shapes.

**The Solution:** Implemented a distance-to-polyline algorithm that calculates the minimum distance from click point to each line segment. If distance < stroke width + threshold, the stroke is selected.

---

### ⏱️ 5. Real-time Cursor Smoothness vs. Server Load

**The Problem:** Emitting cursor positions on every `mousemove` event flooded the server with thousands of events per second.

**The Solution:** Used Socket.IO's **volatile events** for cursor updates (acceptable to drop) and throttled emissions to 60fps using timestamp comparison. Critical drawing data uses reliable events.

---

### 🔄 6. Global Undo Across Multiple Users

**The Problem:** Traditional undo only affects the current user's actions, but in collaboration, everyone should see undos.

**The Solution:** Implemented a server-side redo stack per room. When any user triggers undo, the server broadcasts the removal to all clients and stores the element for potential redo.

**Challenges we ran into**

***

### 1. Vector Map Clutter & Frame Drops
* **Hurdle:** Loading raw national boundaries drew 700+ internal district lines, creating a messy "spiderweb" mesh that lagged WebGL and obscured the satellite map.
* **Fix:** Built a custom TopoJSON parser (`topo2geo.cjs`) to extract only the 36 clean State/UT boundaries, eliminating clutter and boosting performance.

### 2. Balancing Satellite Visibility with Heat Waves
* **Hurdle:** Solid thermal fills completely blocked the satellite terrain (mountains, rivers, greenery), while point dots failed to show regional heat flow.
* **Fix:** Engineered a translucent WebGL heatmap layer (`opacity: ~0.18`) with Gaussian radial blending so satellite terrain textures remain visible under the glowing heat wave.

### 3. Preventing AI Hallucinations in the Scenario Lab
* **Hurdle:** Standard ML models gave unrealistic temperature drops (like -15°C from minor tree planting) when dragging intervention sliders.
* **Fix:** Constrained the XGBoost model with **physical surface energy-balance equations**, keeping counterfactual predictions scientifically accurate within **$\pm 0.42^\circ\text{C}$ RMSE**.

**The problem it solves**

### The Problem
ISRO captures massive Earth Observation (EO) data, but it sits in raw raster formats that State Municipal Corporations cannot easily interpret or use. Without in-house GIS teams, city administrations still rely on delayed field surveys and blanket advisories during deadly heatwaves.

---

### How State Municipalities Use It

1. **Automated Ward-Level Telemetry:**  
   Converts raw space telemetry into live thermal stress grids across all 36 Indian States and UTs with zero manual GIS processing.

2. **Automated Root-Cause Diagnosis:**  
   Uses physics-guided AI to tell municipal engineers exactly *why* a specific ward is overheating (+1.7°C concrete density, +0.8°C roof materials, +0.7°C canopy loss).

3. **Pre-Budget Policy Simulation:**  
   Allows municipal planners to simulate cool roofs and urban forestry before spending funds instantly projecting temperature drops (up to **-3.3°C**), required CapEx (₹ Cr) and citizens protected.

4. **1-Click Heat Action Plans:**  
   Automatically generates executive municipal briefs with ranked ward priorities and budget allocation ready for administrative sign-off.

---

### Impact
* **Bridges Space to City Hall:** Directly connects ISRO telemetry to Municipal Commissioners' decision pipelines.
* **Targeted Disaster Relief:** Directs emergency heat shelters and water resources to the most vulnerable wards.
* **Optimal Public Spending:** Ensures every municipal cooling rupee delivers maximum, scientifically verified temperature reduction.

**Trace Commons AI**

HeatWise AI fits Trace Commons because it addresses urban climate resilience through accessible, high-impact public-interest technology. It fits Trace Commons AI because we use a machine learning pipeline to predict land-surface temperature and hotspot probability, then translate those predictions into actionable insights through maps, intervention simulations, and municipal-style reports for heat mitigation planning.
