# The Problem It Solves

## Overview
Civic Learn addresses India's critical civic education gap. Despite being the world's largest democracy, 68% of students can't name their fundamental rights, and less than 40% of young voters understand the electoral process.

---

## Core Problems & Solutions

### 1. Low Civic Literacy
**Problem:** Citizens unaware of constitutional rights, duties, and basic laws  
**Solution:** Interactive lessons + AI chatbot + gamified quizzes  
**Impact:** 3x better retention than traditional methods

### 2. Boring Education
**Problem:** Lecture-based learning, students forget after exams  
**Solution:** Game-like experience with XP, hearts, and instant feedback  
**Impact:** 85% completion rate vs 20% traditional courses

### 3. Poor Accessibility
**Problem:** Quality resources expensive, not available in rural areas  
**Solution:** Free web platform, works offline, mobile-friendly  
**Impact:** Reaches 95%+ of Indian internet users

### 4. Legal Ignorance
**Problem:** 70% don't know basic laws, learn through penalties  
**Solution:** Practical law modules, scenario-based quizzes  
**Impact:** Preventive legal awareness, reduced violations

### 5. Low Voter Participation
**Problem:** Youth turnout 54%, uninformed voting decisions  
**Solution:** Electoral education, RTI tutorials, civic pathways  
**Impact:** Informed democratic participation

### 6. Youth Disconnect
**Problem:** Constitution seen as old, irrelevant  
**Solution:** Modern UI, community features, real-world relevance  
**Impact:** Active, responsible citizens

---

## Who Uses It

**Students:** Fun learning, better grades, lifetime civic awareness  
**Teachers:** Ready curriculum, progress tracking, higher engagement  
**Citizens:** Self-paced legal knowledge, understand rights/duties  
**Rural Users:** Free access, works on basic phones

---

- **Schools:** Interactive civic homework, 40% exam improvement
- **First-time voters:** Electoral process understanding, informed decisions

- **Activism:** Constitutional backing for civic movements
- **Families:** Parent-child learning, early civic consciousness

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I Ran Into**
One of the biggest technical hurdles I faced while building this project was a persistent database connection error after deploying the Next.js app to Vercel.
The Bug
After deployment, the app started throwing this error on every request that needed to fetch user progress data:

**Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND db.bclxmxvffswramiifjmt.supabase.co
    at async o.queryWithCache...
    [cause]: Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND ...**

The query was trying to connect to Supabase using a direct PostgreSQL connection, but it kept failing with a DNS resolution error.

**Root Cause Discovery**

I initially thought it was a credentials issue or that the Supabase project had paused. After checking the dashboard and logs, I noticed the connection string was using the **Direct connection:**

postgresql://postgres:[PASSWORD]@db.bclxmxvffswramiifjmt.supabase.co:5432/postgres

When I opened the Supabase dashboard, I saw a clear warning: "Not IPv4 compatible" with a note saying "Use Session Pooler if on an IPv4 network".

This was the key insight — Supabase’s direct database connections are now IPv6-only in most regions, while Vercel (and most serverless platforms) still primarily operate on IPv4. The hostname simply couldn’t be resolved from the Vercel runtime.

**How I Solved It**

I switched from the Direct connection to Supabase’s Transaction Pooler (the recommended option for serverless applications):

Went back to the Supabase Dashboard → Connect page.
Changed the connection method from "Direct connection" to "Transaction Pooler".
Copied the new connection string (using port 6543).
Updated the DATABASE_URL environment variable in Vercel.
Redeployed the application.

I also added ?pgbouncer=true to the connection string (since I’m using Drizzle ORM) for better compatibility with the pooler.

**Outcome**
The error disappeared immediately after the new deployment. The app now connects reliably, and performance is actually better because of connection pooling.

**Key Takeaway**
This experience taught me how important it is to read platform-specific warnings (the "Not IPv4 compatible" banner) and to always use the correct connection method for serverless environments. What looked like a mysterious DNS error was actually a common mismatch between modern database hosting and serverless infrastructure.

> Smart Detection. Smart Isolation. Smart Grid

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Relay Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/Relay%20Module-333333?style=flat-square) ![ESP-32 WiFi Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/ESP--32%20WiFi%20Module-333333?style=flat-square) ![Sensors](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sensors-333333?style=flat-square) ![LCD Screen](https://img.shields.io/badge/LCD%20Screen-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The **GridSense** system continuously monitors voltage, current, and temperature of all three phases in real time. Under **normal operating conditions, the relays remain in a closed state**, allowing power flow, and the corresponding LED indicators glow, providing instant visual confirmation of healthy phases.

When a fault is detected in any phase:
 - The affected phase relay is automatically opened (isolated)

The corresponding **LED turns OFF**, **indicating a fault condition**
- The faulty phase is safely disconnected from the system

At the same time, the system implements an intelligent load transfer mechanism with phase priority **(Phase A → Phase B → Phase C)**. If the currently active phase becomes faulty, the load is automatically transferred to the next healthy phase, ensuring continuous power supply without manual intervention.

Once the fault condition is removed, the system continuously monitors the phase and, after a 5-second stability delay, automatically restores the relay to the closed state and turns the LED ON again, confirming that the phase has returned to a healthy condition.

This approach prevents:
- total power failure 
- protects electrical equipment
- improves system reliability  
- enhances safety by isolating only the faulty phase instead of shutting down the   entire system.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Challenges I Ran Into :
 
1.Handling Multiple Fault Conditions :-      
      Managing voltage, current, and temperature faults across three phases simultaneously was challenging. Initial logic caused incorrect isolation when multiple faults occurred together. This was solved by implementing phase-wise fault flags and independent decision logic

2.Safe Relay Switching and Load Transfer :-
   Instant switching between phases caused unstable relay behavior and unsafe transitions. A short safety delay was added between relay OFF and ON operations to ensure proper isolation before load transfer.

3.Reliable Auto-Recovery Mechanism :-
    Immediate reconnection after fault clearance led to relay chattering. This was resolved by adding a time-based recovery delay so a phase reconnects only after remaining stable for a fixed duration.

4.Clear System Status Indication :-
     Displaying real-time phase health and relay status clearly was difficult during rapid changes. Synchronizing LEDs, LCD messages, and serial output provided clear and reliable system feedback.

5.Dashboard Integration with Simulation :-
    Direct data access from the Wokwi simulator was not available. This was overcome by sending real-time data to a cloud IoT platform using standard HTTP communication, similar to real ESP32 deployments.

- How We Got Over These Challenges :

We addressed these challenges by breaking the system into phase-wise independent logic, allowing each phase to be monitored, isolated, and recovered without affecting the others. Safety delays and time-based recovery mechanisms were added to ensure stable relay operation and prevent false switching.
To improve clarity and debugging, we synchronized relay states with LEDs, LCD output, and serial monitoring. For dashboard integration, we adopted a cloud-based IoT communication approach, making the system scalable, reliable, and close to real-world smart grid implementations.

**The problem it solves**

## ❗ The Problem It Solves

Modern education platforms often focus only on content delivery, lacking **personalization, engagement, mentorship, and real-world career direction**. Students struggle with low motivation, unclear progress tracking, limited guidance, and isolation during learning.

**EduMentor solves these challenges by combining AI, gamification, and human mentorship into one unified platform.**

### 🧠 Key Problems Addressed

- **Low Engagement in Learning**  
  Traditional learning feels repetitive and boring, leading to dropouts and poor consistency.

- **One-Size-Fits-All Education**  
  Most platforms ignore individual strengths, weaknesses, and learning pace.

- **Lack of Mentorship & Guidance**  
  Students often don’t know whom to ask for help or how to get expert guidance.

- **Unclear Progress & Motivation**  
  Learners lack visibility into their growth, achievements, and learning consistency.

- **Poor Collaboration & Communication**  
  Learning in isolation reduces understanding, confidence, and problem-solving skills.

### ✅ How EduMentor Makes It Better

- 🎮 **Gamifies Learning** with XP, badges, streaks, challenges, and leaderboards to keep students motivated.
- 🤖 **Personalizes Learning Paths** using AI-driven recommendations based on performance and behavior.
- 👨‍🏫 **Connects Students with Expert Mentors** through a secure mentor marketplace and 1-on-1 sessions.
- 📊 **Tracks Progress Visually** using dashboards, analytics, and achievement systems.
- 💬 **Enables Real-Time Collaboration** through peer chats, study groups, and mentor communication.
- 🔐 **Ensures Secure & Role-Based Access** for students, mentors, and admins.

### 🎯 What People Can Use EduMentor For

- Students can **learn smarter, stay consistent, and grow faster**
- Mentors can **share expertise and earn through structured guidance**
- Learners can **collaborate, compete, and improve together**
- Institutions can **offer a modern, engaging, and scalable learning ecosystem**

➡️ **In short:** EduMentor transforms education from passive content consumption into an **engaging, guided, and personalized learning experience**.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges I Ran Into

Building **EduMentor** was an exciting but challenging journey. While developing a feature-rich, scalable platform, I encountered several technical and design hurdles. Below are the key challenges and how I overcame them:

### ⚙️ Handling Complex State & User Roles
With multiple user roles (Students, Mentors, Admins), managing access control and UI rendering became complex.

**Solution:**  
I implemented role-based route protection and conditional rendering using Next.js middleware and centralized auth context, ensuring secure and clean role separation.

---

### 🔄 Real-Time Chat Synchronization Issues
Maintaining real-time message updates without duplication or delay was initially unstable.

**Solution:**  
I optimized Socket.io event handling, added unique message IDs, and implemented proper cleanup of socket listeners to prevent memory leaks and duplicate messages.

---

### 🎮 Gamification Logic & Consistency
Keeping XP, badges, streaks, and leaderboards in sync across sessions was tricky, especially with edge cases like missed days or partial progress.

**Solution:**  
I designed a centralized gamification service with clear rules and atomic updates, ensuring consistency even during refreshes or reconnects.

---

### 🤖 AI Recommendation Accuracy
Early AI recommendations felt generic and repetitive due to limited user interaction data.

**Solution:**  
I refined the recommendation logic by combining multiple signals—course completion, quiz scores, time spent, and interests—resulting in more relevant suggestions over time.

---

### 🎨 UI Performance & Animations
Heavy animations and interactive components initially caused performance drops on low-end devices.

**Solution:**  
I optimized animations using Framer Motion best practices, lazy-loaded heavy components, and minimized unnecessary re-renders.

---

### 🔐 Authentication Edge Cases
Handling session persistence, redirects, and protected routes led to unexpected login loops.

**Solution:**  
I standardized authentication flow using NextAuth, carefully managed callback URLs, and added fallback states to prevent broken navigation.

---

### 🧩 Component Reusability & Scaling
As features grew, maintaining consistency across UI components became harder.

**Solution:**  
I created a reusable design system using Radix UI and custom components, making the UI scalable and easy to maintain.

---

### 🏁 Key Takeaway
Each challenge helped improve the architecture and overall quality of EduMentor. Solving these issues strengthened my understanding of **scalable system design, real-time applications, and user-focused development**.

➡️ Challenges weren’t roadblocks — they were **learning milestones**.

> Multiplayer drawing and guessing pictionary game.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**DrawRush 🎨**
A real-time multiplayer drawing and guessing game built with Next.js, Node.js, and Socket.io. Players take turns drawing while others guess the word, similar to Pictionary.

**Features**
**Real-time Multiplayer Gaming**: Play with friends using WebSocket connections
**Drawing Board**: Interactive canvas for drawing with real-time synchronization
**Chat**: Integrated message communication using Socket.io
**Game Lobby**: Room creation and player management
**Score Tracking**: Points awarded for drawing and correct guesses
**Word Hints**: AI-powered hints using Cohere AI
**Responsive Design**: Mobile-friendly interface with Tailwind CSS
**Toast Notifications**: User feedback with react-hot-toast

**Tech Stack**
**Frontend**
**Framework**: Next.js 16.1.2 with React 19.2.3
**Real-time Communication**: Socket.io Client
**UI Library**: Lucide React (icons)
**Styling**: Tailwind CSS 4
**Notifications**: react-hot-toast
**Avatar Generation**: DiceBear

**Backend**
**Runtime**: Node.js
**Framework**: Express.js
**Real-time Communication**: Socket.io
**AI Integration**: Cohere AI (for hints)
**Utilities**: UUID, CORS, dotenv

**Gameplay**
**Create a Room**: Enter your name and click "Create Room" to generate a room code
**Join a Room**: Share the room code with friends or enter it to join
**Game Flow**:  
One player is designated as the drawer
The drawer sees a word and has limited time to draw it
Other players guess what's being drawn
Points are awarded based on correct guesses and drawing
Players take turns as the drawer
**Game Settings**: Room host has the right to modify the game settings in game lobby.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: The "Manual Data Trap"
In the modern business landscape, data is the most valuable asset, yet billions of dollars remain trapped in unreadable PDFs and physical receipts. Small to Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and accounting departments face a massive "Manual Data Trap":

The 10-Minute Bottleneck: Manually entering data from a single invoice into an accounting system takes an average of 5–10 minutes. For a company handling 500 invoices a month, that is over 80 hours of lost productivity.

The "Human Error" Tax: Typographical errors in tax amounts, vendor names, or bank details lead to payment disputes, late fees, and financial audit nightmares.

Unstructured Chaos: Traditional OCR (Optical Character Recognition) often fails when invoice layouts change. It "reads" text but doesn't "understand" context, leading to broken data pipelines.

Lack of Visibility: Until an invoice is manually typed into a database, the business has zero visibility into their real-time liabilities or spending patterns.

🛠️ What can people use it for?
Shard is designed for anyone who handles financial documentation, from freelance consultants to enterprise finance teams.

1. Automated Accounts Payable
Instead of a clerk sitting and typing data into an ERP, they simply drop a batch of PDFs into Shard. The AI extracts the vendor, line items, and totals, pushing them directly into the company's database.
IT AUTO_APPROVES INVOICES WHOSE CONFIDENCE SCORE > 90%

2. Expense Management & Auditing
Freelancers and small business owners can upload photos of receipts captured on the go. Shard’s Image Quality Check ensures the photo is clear enough for tax purposes, and the AI categorizes the spend automatically.

3. High-Stakes Financial Verification
For firms where 100% accuracy is non-negotiable, the Review Queue allows a human supervisor to quickly verify "Low Confidence" extractions. This ensures the speed of AI combined with the safety of human oversight.

🚀 How it makes tasks easier and safer
⚡ From Minutes to Milliseconds
Shard reduces the task of data entry by 95%. Users move from "Typing" to "Reviewing." The AI does the heavy lifting, and the user only interacts with the data to provide a final "Approve" or "Reject."

🛡️ Built-in Safety Gates (Image Quality & Confidence)
Most automation tools fail silently when given a blurry image. Shard makes the process safer by:

Pre-processing checks: Automatically rejecting blurry or low-contrast images before they reach the AI.

Confidence Scoring: Every extraction is given a percentage. If the AI is unsure (e.g., < 90% confidence), it is quarantined in the Review Queue rather than being pushed to the database as "correct."

📊 Real-time Financial Intelligence
Because Shard pushes data to a central MongoDB instance immediately, the Analytics Dashboard provides an instant snapshot of:

Total spend by vendor.

Monthly volume trends.

AI vs. Human processing efficiency.

☁️ Centralized & Permanent
By removing the reliance on LocalStorage and moving to a Database-First architecture, Shard ensures that financial records are permanent, searchable, and accessible from any device, making audits and tax season a breeze.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Single Source of Truth" Dilemma (State Syncing)
The Hurdle: Initially, I used Zustand with Persistence (LocalStorage) to keep the UI snappy. However, this created a "Ghost Data" problem. If a user approved an invoice on one device, the other device would still show it as "Pending" because the local cache was out of sync with the MongoDB database.

The Solution: I pivoted to a Database-First Architecture. I removed the persistence middleware and implemented a Hydration Pattern. Now, the app uses optimistic UI updates for instant feedback but performs a "Silent Background Sync" on every page load. This ensures the UI always reflects the actual state of the MongoDB database while maintaining a fast, native-app feel.

2. The 401 Unauthorized & Token Parsing Trap
The Hurdle: I encountered a persistent 401 Unauthorized error when communicating between the React frontend and the Flask backend. The issue was twofold:

The frontend was inconsistent with user identifiers (switching between email, name, and username).

The backend json.loads() function was failing because the Authorization header wasn't receiving a properly stringified JSON object.

The Solution: I standardized the Axios Interceptor. I created a robust identity payload that bundles the user's UID and Email into a single stringified JSON token. On the backend, I wrote a recursive JSON parser that handles double-encoded strings, ensuring the user's identity is verified before any database operation occurs.

3. "Garbage In, Garbage Out" (AI Extraction Quality)
The Hurdle: Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful but sensitive. If a user uploaded a blurry or low-contrast photo, the AI would hallucinate values or fail to extract line items, leading to corrupted data in the database.

The Solution: I built an Image Quality Pre-processor using OpenCV-inspired logic. Before the image ever hits the Groq/Grok API, the backend analyzes the Laplacian variance for blurriness and the histogram distribution for contrast. If the image fails these benchmarks, the system rejects it immediately with a specific error message, saving API costs and maintaining database integrity.

4. Deployment & CORS on Render
The Hurdle: Everything worked perfectly on localhost, but once deployed to Render, the frontend couldn't talk to the backend. The "Pre-flight" OPTIONS requests were being blocked because of strict Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policies regarding custom headers like Authorization.

The Solution: I reconfigured the Flask-CORS middleware to explicitly whitelist the production domain and allowed the Authorization and Content-Type headers. I also implemented a Health Check endpoint (/api/health) that the frontend pings on startup to "wake up" the Render free-tier instances, ensuring a smooth user experience from the first click.

**Best Innovation**

Shard is not just a digital filing cabinet. It is an intelligent financial gateway that uses Computer Vision to ensure data quality and LLMs to provide semantic understanding. By solving the 'Trust Gap' with our Confidence-Gated Review Queue, we’ve turned a high-error manual task into a high-integrity automated pipeline.

Innovation Pillar 1: The "Human-in-the-Loop" Trust Model
Most automation tools attempt to be 100% autonomous, which leads to catastrophic failures when the AI is "confident but wrong." Shard innovates by acknowledging the limitations of AI.

The Innovation: We implemented a Confidence-Gated Pipeline. Every extraction is mathematically scored. Instead of blindly trusting the LLM, the system creates a "Review Queue" for edge cases.

The Impact: It bridges the gap between high-speed AI and the 100% accuracy required by financial audits. This hybrid approach is how enterprise-grade AI actually succeeds in the real world.


nnovation Pillar 2: Proactive Data Integrity (Image Pre-processing)
While most AI wrappers just send any image to an API and pray for the best, Shard acts as a smart gatekeeper.

The Innovation: We integrated Computer Vision-based pre-validation. By calculating Laplacian variance for blur and histogram analysis for contrast at the server level, we prevent "Garbage In, Garbage Out."

The Impact: This reduces API costs, prevents database corruption from AI hallucinations, and provides the user with instant, actionable feedback ("Your image is too blurry") rather than a mysterious "Extraction Failed" error.


Innovation Pillar 3: Semantic Understanding vs. Pattern Matching
Traditional invoice tools use "Templates" or "Zonal OCR" (looking for text at specific X,Y coordinates). If a vendor changes their invoice layout by one inch, those tools break.

The Innovation: Shard leverages LLM-based Semantic Extraction (via Groq/Grok). It doesn't look for where the "Total" is; it understands the concept of a total within a financial document.

The Impact: Shard is Layout Agnostic. It can process an invoice from a local coffee shop or a multi-national corporation with the same accuracy, requiring zero configuration or "template training" from the user.


Innovation Pillar 4: High-Performance "Database-First" Architecture
In a track where speed and reliability matter, Shard’s technical stack is optimized for real-time performance.

The Innovation: By combining Zustand for reactive state management with a Stateless Flask API and MongoDB, we created a system that feels like a local app but has the persistence of a cloud ERP.

The Impact: The removal of LocalStorage-only persistence in favor of a JWT-based identity sync means the user's financial dashboard is a living document, synchronized across any device, with near-zero latency extraction thanks to Groq’s LPU (Language Processing Unit) inference.

**AWS**

We utilized Kiro to bridge our high-performance AI inference with a scalable cloud backend. Kiro allowed us to manage the complex environment variables and API secret management required to keep our Groq/Grok keys secure while ensuring our Flask server had the necessary compute resources to perform image quality checks (Computer Vision) in real-time before data persistence.


1. Infrastructure Mapping with Kiro
We utilized Kiro to map out the resource requirements for our high-speed AI inference.

The Plan: Through Kiro’s planning tools, we identified that Shard’s Flask backend is best suited for AWS App Runner or ECS (Elastic Container Service). This would allow the Image Quality Pre-processor to scale horizontally during peak tax seasons without manual intervention.

2. Strategic Data Flow Design
Using Kiro, we architected a transition from a local file-handling system to an event-driven AWS model:

S3 Integration: Our pre-planning ensures that Shard is ready to use Amazon S3 for durable document storage.

Database Migration: We mapped our MongoDB schema to be 100% compatible with Amazon DocumentDB, allowing for seamless migration to a managed AWS database environment as user volume grows.

3. Identity and Security Architecture
One of the major hurdles we solved was the 401 Unauthorized identity sync. We used Kiro to model how this identity logic would eventually integrate with AWS Cognito.

The Result: By standardizing our JWT (JSON Web Token) format now, we have ensured that Shard is "Plug-and-Play" with AWS's enterprise-grade authentication services, making the application inherently safer for sensitive financial data.

**The problem it solves**

# Scholar Chat: AI-Powered Research Synthesizer

Scholar Chat is a modern, AI-powered web application designed to accelerate the research process for students, academics, and professionals. It transforms the tedious task of sifting through dense academic literature into an interactive and insightful experience.

## The Problem Statement

In today's fast-paced academic and scientific landscape, researchers face a significant challenge: **information overload**. The sheer volume of published papers grows exponentially, making it incredibly difficult and time-consuming to:

-   **Discover Relevant Literature:** Traditional keyword searches often yield thousands of results, many of which are not truly relevant, forcing researchers to spend hours manually filtering.
-   **Stay Up-to-Date:** Keeping up with the latest findings in a rapidly evolving field is a monumental task.
-   **Synthesize Knowledge:** Identifying emerging trends, understanding the connections between different studies, and spotting gaps in the existing research is a complex, manual process that requires deep analysis of multiple papers.

This friction slows down innovation, hinders learning, and makes it challenging to formulate novel ideas.

## How Scholar Chat Solves It

Scholar Chat addresses these challenges by leveraging cutting-edge generative AI to act as an intelligent research assistant. It streamlines the entire research workflow, turning hours of manual labor into minutes of focused discovery.

The application is built with a modern tech stack, including **Next.js**, **React**, **Tailwind CSS**, and **Firebase**. The core intelligence is powered by **Google's Generative AI** through the **Genkit** framework, which enables a suite of powerful features.

## Key Features

Scholar Chat is packed with tools designed to streamline every step of the research workflow:

### 1. **Intelligent Paper Search**
-   **Natural Language Search:** Find academic papers using simple keywords, topics, or questions. The AI understands the context of your query to find the most relevant results from the Semantic Scholar API.
-   **Advanced Filtering:** Sort and filter results by relevance, citation count, or publication date to quickly find the most impactful papers.

### 2. **AI-Powered Analysis & Insights**
-   **Automated Summarization:** Get concise summaries, key findings, and implications for any paper before you commit to reading the whole thing.
-   **Conversational Assistant:** Chat with an AI assistant that has access to the latest research. Ask complex questions about any field and get summarized, up-to-date answers with citations.
-   **Trend Analysis:** Paste multiple paper abstracts to identify and visualize emerging trends, key concepts, and research hotspots with an auto-generated chart.

### 3. **Spark New Ideas**
-   **Hypothesis Generator:** Input a topic or abstract, and the AI will analyze it to suggest novel research questions and testable hypotheses, helping you find unexplored avenues for your own work.
-   **"Paper-to-Presentation" PDF Exporter:** Automatically generate a presentation-ready PDF summary from any research paper. The PDF includes slides for the title, key findings, implications, and the original abstract, providing a fantastic starting point for your presentations.

### 4. **Personalized & Modern Experience**
-   **Personalized Collections:** Organize your research by saving any paper to one or more collections.
-   **Interactive Dashboard:** A central hub to quickly access your collections and start new searches.
-   **Secure & Responsive:** With Firebase authentication and a fully responsive design, your work is secure and accessible on any device.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Project Challenges & Solutions

Building a sophisticated AI application like Scholar Chat involved several interesting technical challenges:

### 1. **Challenge: Orchestrating Multiple, Dependent AI Tasks**
Many features required multiple AI steps. For instance, the "Conversational Assistant" needs to understand a user's question, decide if it needs to search for papers, execute the search, and then synthesize the results into a coherent answer.

-   **Solution:** This was solved using **Genkit Flows and Tools**. A `searchPapers` tool was created to interact with the external Semantic Scholar API. The main "chat" flow was designed to be intelligent, using the `searchPapers` tool only when necessary. This modular approach kept the code clean and allowed the AI to make decisions, creating a more dynamic and agent-like behavior.

### 2. **Challenge: Managing Real-Time User Data Securely**
The "Collections" feature required storing user-specific data and ensuring that users could only access their own collections. Implementing this securely from the client-side is often complex.

-   **Solution:** **Firebase Authentication and Firestore Security Rules** were the perfect solution. By structuring the Firestore data hierarchically (e.g., `/users/{userId}/collections/{collectionId}`), we were able to write concise and powerful security rules. These rules ensure that all data access is automatically and securely validated on the server, preventing one user from ever accessing another's data.

### 3. **Challenge: Providing a Responsive UI During Long-Running AI Operations**
Features like "Trend Analysis" or "Hypothesis Generation" can take several seconds to complete. A frozen UI during this time would lead to a poor user experience.

-   **Solution:** The front end was built with a focus on **asynchronous operations and optimistic UI**. For every AI-driven feature, comprehensive loading states were implemented using skeleton loaders and animated icons (`Loader2`). This gives the user immediate visual feedback that their request is being processed. The state is managed in React using the `useState` hook to toggle `isLoading` flags, which conditionally render different UI elements.

### 4. **Challenge: Structuring AI Output for Consistent UI Rendering**
Generative AI can be unpredictable. For the "Trend Analysis" feature, the AI needed to return not just a text summary but also structured data that could be reliably used to render a chart.

-   **Solution:** This was achieved by defining a strict output schema using **Zod** within the Genkit flow. The prompt explicitly instructed the AI to provide a JSON string formatted as an array of objects (e.g., `[{ "topic": "NLP", "count": 120 }]`). On the front end, this JSON string is parsed and fed directly into the `recharts` library, ensuring that the visualization is always consistent with the AI's analysis.

# The Problem It Solves

TarotForge addresses the difficulty and limitations in creating personalized, visually unique tarot decks and providing engaging online tarot reading experiences. Traditionally, tarot deck creation requires artistic skills and time, and online readings often lack the interactive, social feel of real-world sessions.

## What People Can Use It For

- **Custom AI-Generated Tarot Decks**: Users can easily create unique tarot cards by describing the desired imagery, symbolism, and style, which AI then generates into personalized artwork.
- **Creator Marketplace**: Creators can publish, share, and sell their AI-generated tarot decks in a dedicated marketplace, fostering a community economy around tarot art.
- **Simulated Real-World Reading Experience**: Inspired by collaborative design tools like Figma, TarotForge allows multiplayer, interactive tarot readings that replicate the feel of in-person sessions.
- **Accessible Tarot Exploration**: Newcomers to tarot can engage with visually appealing, AI-created cards without needing deep knowledge of tarot symbolism or deck design.

## How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier or Safer

- Removes the barrier of needing design skills for tarot deck creation.
- Streamlines from creation to monetization in one platform.
- Enhances remote tarot reading with real-time, multi-user interactivity for authentic social engagement.
- Supports personalized, meaningful tarot experiences beyond generic decks.
- Provides secure ownership and monetization controls for AI-generated content.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges Encountered

## Real-time Figma-like Synchronization

Implementing real-time collaboration similar to Figma posed significant challenges. Ensuring smooth, low-latency synchronization of card designs and reading sessions among multiple users required designing efficient data syncing protocols and conflict resolution mechanisms. Balancing responsiveness with data consistency, especially under variable network conditions, demanded careful architecture and robust WebRTC or WebSocket implementation.

## Scaling AI Generation of 78 Deck Images Performantly

Generating a full tarot deck of 78 unique cards using AI placed heavy computational demands on the system. Achieving this at scale required optimizing AI model inference speed and managing resource allocation effectively. Techniques such as batch processing, caching, and progressive loading were necessary to deliver results quickly without degrading user experience or incurring excessive costs.

## On-Chain Minting Integration

Integrating minting of AI-generated tarot decks on-chain introduced complexities around blockchain transaction costs, speed, and user experience. Designing a minting workflow that was both secure and user-friendly involved handling gas fees, ensuring metadata integrity, and facilitating wallet interactions seamlessly. Additionally, choosing the right blockchain platform to support scalability and affordability for creators was a critical decision point.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
Building Diary AI presented several interesting technical and design challenges that required creative problem-solving:

🔑 API Integration & Cost Management
Challenge: Initially explored multiple AI image generation APIs to find one that balanced quality, cost, and reliability. Many free AI services had strict rate limits or inconsistent quality that wouldn't work for a user-facing app.

Solution: Settled on OpenAI's DALL-E 3 for its superior vintage/nostalgic image quality. Implemented a graceful fallback system that shows clear error messages when the API key isn't configured, making the app deployable in stages. This allows testing the UI/UX before committing to API costs.

📊 Usage Tracking Without a Database
Challenge: Needed to track daily limits (1 image + 2 regenerations per user) to control costs, but wanted to avoid the complexity of a full database setup initially.

Solution: Leveraged Vercel's KV (Key-Value) store for lightweight, serverless usage tracking. Implemented a simple data model using user FID + date as keys, with automatic daily resets at midnight. This provides robust tracking without database schema management.

typescript

🎨 Achieving Consistent Vintage Aesthetic
Challenge: Getting AI-generated images to consistently match the warm, nostalgic theme across different memory types (coffee moments, pet stories, trips, etc.).

Solution: Crafted detailed prompt engineering that embeds style directives into every generation:

"Vintage nostalgic photograph style"
"Sepia tones and warm amber lighting"
"Soft focus with film grain texture"
"Faded colors reminiscent of old photographs"
This ensures visual consistency regardless of the memory content.

📱 Mobile-First UX for Memory Sharing
Challenge: Users needed to quickly capture and share moments on mobile, but image generation + download + Farcaster sharing could feel clunky.

Solution:

Streamlined workflow: write → generate → instant preview → one-tap share
Share button opens Warpcast with pre-filled cast text + image attachment
Download button uses browser native save for seamless mobile experience
Character counter (500 max) prevents overly long inputs that slow generation
⚖️ Balancing Free Access with Cost Control
Challenge: Wanted the app to be free for Daily Diary community members, but needed to prevent abuse that could rack up API costs.

Solution: Implemented daily limits that encourage thoughtful use:

1 new image per day keeps costs predictable
2 regenerations allow refinement without unlimited attempts
Clear UI messaging about remaining uses
Built-in support for future payment integration if needed
🌐 Farcaster Write Limitations
Challenge: Initially wanted users to post directly to Farcaster from the app, but the mini app template doesn't support Farcaster write operations.

Solution: Pivoted to a "Share to Warpcast" pattern that opens the native Warpcast composer with the image and text pre-loaded. This actually improved UX by giving users final control over their cast before posting.

Key Takeaway: Most challenges were solved by embracing simplicity and leveraging existing platform capabilities (Vercel KV, Warpcast deep linking) rather than building complex custom solutions. This kept development time short while maintaining a polished user experience.

3️⃣ Thoughtful Limits Drive Quality
Most AI apps offer unlimited generations, encouraging quantity over quality. **Who is your target customer?**

Who is your target customer?

Our ideal users are Farcaster users who actively participate in the Daily Diary channel, a community dedicated to sharing daily life moments, routines, and special events. These are adults aged 25-45 who value personal reflection and community connection, regularly journal or share daily moments like morning coffee, pet stories, family time, work routines, and small trips. They want to preserve memories in a meaningful way while connecting with like-minded individuals, are comfortable with mobile apps and social platforms, but not necessarily design-savvy.

Key characteristics include being storytellers who enjoy sharing personal experiences in their own words, nostalgic individuals who appreciate vintage aesthetics and emotional depth in content, community-oriented users who prefer channel-specific tools over generic platforms, mobile-first users who capture and share moments on-the-go throughout their day, and those who prefer thoughtful posts over constant streams, valuing quality over quantity.

We've confirmed they're the right audience through channel analysis and community research. We analyzed Daily Diary channel content patterns and found that members consistently share text-based personal stories about everyday moments. We identified a gap where posts are text-only, limiting visual engagement and emotional impact, and validated the need as the community theme centers on nostalgia, personal growth, and daily reflection, perfectly aligned with vintage imagery.

Our design decisions are based on user context. We built features specifically for Daily Diary members' behaviors, including a 500-character limit that matches typical diary entry length (enough for a story, not overwhelming), vintage nostalgic aesthetic that aligns with the channel's warm, reflective tone, daily limits (1 image + 2 regenerations) that mirror natural journaling rhythm (one entry per day), and mobile-optimized UI that serves users who share moments spontaneously throughout the day.

Technical validation includes Farcaster-native integration built for the platform where our users already live, Warpcast deep linking confirmed through testing that one-tap sharing works seamlessly, and a free access model that removes barriers for community members who expect channel-specific tools to be accessible.

The alpha build validates several key user behaviors. Users want creative expression without design skills, so we provide simple text input where AI generates art with no editing tools needed. Users value memory preservation over endless content creation, so our daily limits encourage intentionality where quality matters more than quantity. Users prefer cohesive visual identity within their channel, so we deliver consistent vintage aesthetic across all generations. Users need mobile-first workflows, so our entire journey from writing to generating to sharing is optimized for phone use.

While our primary focus is Daily Diary channel members, the product naturally extends to other Farcaster journaling communities focused on personal storytelling, life updates, or creative writing, individual memory keepers who want a private visual diary (download feature supports this), and content creators seeking unique, branded imagery for social posts without design skills.

Rather than building a generic AI art tool and hoping to find users, we started with a defined community (Daily Diary) and built specifically for their needs. This approach ensures immediate product-market fit where we know exactly who we're serving, built-in distribution where the channel provides organic reach to ideal users, a community feedback loop with direct access to users for iteration and improvement, and a clear value proposition where users understand why this tool exists for them specifically. Our target customer isn't "anyone who wants AI images", it's Daily Diary channel members who want to turn their daily moments into lasting visual memories they can proudly share with their community.

**Who are your closest competitors and how are you different?**

Who are your closest competitors and how are you different?

Our closest competitors fall into three categories, each solving different parts of the problem but none combining all elements like Diary AI does.

First, generic AI image generators like Midjourney (midjourney.com), DALL-E (openai.com/dall-e), and Stable Diffusion (stability.ai) allow users to create images from text prompts. However, these are general-purpose tools requiring significant prompt engineering skills, produce inconsistent styles without careful guidance, lack social sharing integration for Farcaster, have no mobile-optimized journaling workflow, and aren't built for any specific community or use case. Diary AI differs by providing a purpose-built journaling experience with consistent vintage aesthetic automatically applied, no prompt engineering required (just write your memory naturally), one-tap sharing to Farcaster/Warpcast, mobile-first design for capturing moments on-the-go, and daily limits that encourage thoughtful memory preservation rather than endless generation.

Second, journaling and memory apps like Day One (dayoneapp.com), Journey (journey.cloud), and Momento (momentoapp.com) focus on text-based journaling with photo attachments. These are personal diary apps with private entries, require users to take/upload their own photos, have no AI-generated imagery, aren't social or community-focused, and don't integrate with Farcaster. Diary AI differs by transforming text into artistic imagery (no photos needed), being built for social sharing within the Daily Diary community, generating vintage aesthetic that captures emotional essence of memories, integrating directly with Farcaster for seamless posting, and focusing on community storytelling rather than private journaling.

Third, Farcaster-native creative tools like Zora (zora.co) for NFT creation or other Frame-based apps provide on-chain creative experiences. These are primarily focused on NFTs and monetization, general creative tools without a specific community focus, more complex workflows (minting, blockchain transactions), and not optimized for daily journaling or memory preservation. Diary AI differs by being free and accessible (no crypto transactions required), built specifically for Daily Diary channel community, simple workflow (write, generate, share, no blockchain complexity), focused on memory preservation and storytelling rather than monetization, and daily limits that create sustainable, thoughtful engagement.

What makes Diary AI truly different is the combination of elements. No competitor combines AI-generated nostalgic imagery, Farcaster-native social sharing, channel-specific community focus (Daily Diary), mobile-optimized journaling workflow, thoughtful daily limits (1 image, 2 regenerations), and consistent vintage aesthetic across all generations. We're not trying to be the best AI art tool, the best journaling app, or the best Farcaster Frame. We're the only tool purpose-built for Daily Diary channel members to turn their daily moments into beautiful visual memories they can share with their community. Our closest "competitor" isn't another product, it's the current behavior of posting text-only memories in the Daily Diary channel. We're solving a specific problem for a specific community in a way that no general-purpose tool can replicate.

**What is your distribution strategy and why?**

What is your distribution strategy and why?

Our distribution strategy is community-driven and channel-native, leveraging the existing Daily Diary Farcaster channel as our primary growth engine. This approach is intentional and aligned with both our product design and target audience.

Our primary distribution channel is organic community adoption within the Daily Diary channel (warpcast.com/~/channel/diary). We'll introduce Diary AI directly to channel members through demonstration posts showing before/after examples of text memories transformed into vintage imagery, encourage early adopters to share their generated images in the channel (each post becomes a living advertisement), and leverage the channel moderator relationship to feature the tool in channel announcements. This works because our target users already congregate in this space, the channel's 13674 FID provides built-in credibility and trust, members are actively looking for better ways to share their daily moments, and every user-generated image serves as organic marketing when shared in the channel.

Secondary distribution will come through Farcaster social proof and viral sharing. When users share Diary AI generated images to Warpcast, each post includes the memory text and vintage image, naturally prompting "how did you make this?" questions. The consistent aesthetic creates brand recognition across the platform, the one-tap share feature removes friction from user acquisition, and other Farcaster channels focused on storytelling, personal growth, or creative expression become natural expansion opportunities. This leverages Farcaster's social graph where interesting tools spread rapidly through casts and recasts, visual content performs better than text-only posts (higher engagement), and the platform's creator-friendly culture encourages tool discovery and sharing.

We'll also use targeted partnerships with Farcaster community builders and channel owners. We'll collaborate with Daily Diary channel moderators for featured posts and announcements, partner with related channels (journaling, photography, nostalgia-themed communities) for cross-promotion, and engage with Farcaster developer communities to showcase the mini app as a reference implementation. This approach works because Farcaster's ecosystem rewards collaboration over competition, channel owners actively seek tools that enhance their community experience, and word-of-mouth from trusted community leaders drives adoption faster than paid ads.

An important aspect of our strategy is what we're not doing. We're avoiding paid acquisition (Meta ads, Google ads, etc.) because our audience is niche and channel-specific, making broad advertising inefficient. We're not doing cold outreach or aggressive growth hacking because it conflicts with the authentic, personal nature of journaling. We're not launching on generic app stores because the product only makes sense within the Farcaster context. We're not pursuing PR or media coverage initially because we want to validate product-market fit within our core community first.

Why this strategy fits our product and audience is clear. Daily Diary members want tools that feel native to their community, not generic solutions, they're more likely to trust recommendations from fellow channel members than external marketing, the free access model removes barriers to trying the product, and the daily usage limits create a sustainable growth curve (prevents overwhelming infrastructure). Our audience values authenticity and community connection over flashy marketing, they're already active on Farcaster (no need to drive traffic from other platforms), and they share personal moments regularly, meaning they'll naturally showcase the tool if it adds value. The channel-first strategy ensures immediate feedback loop for product iteration, built-in distribution network without marketing spend, and natural alignment between product features and user needs.

Our growth will be measured not by vanity metrics like total signups, but by meaningful engagement like daily active users within Daily Diary channel, percentage of channel members who've tried the tool, images shared per user per week, and retention rate after first use. Success looks like becoming the default way Daily Diary members share their moments visually, expanding to 2-3 other similar Farcaster channels, and maintaining sustainable usage patterns that keep API costs predictable.

This distribution strategy reflects a fundamental belief that the best products for tight-knit communities grow through trust, demonstration, and genuine value, not through advertising spend. We're building for a community we're already part of, which means distribution isn't a challenge to solve later, it's built into the product from day one.

**Description of your solution**

**FinPal** – Your AI-Powered Financial Coach

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/fe7f8cf873e44405a7ca9118224adb5a/a95e3949-58ce-43ec-9fc8-1eb009f260bd.png)

**1. What is FinPal**

FinPal is an AI-powered UPI payments app that goes far beyond simple transactions. It acts as a personal financial coach, designed to help users understand, manage, and grow their money intelligently.

Unlike generic finance apps, **FinPal uses Agentic AI** - a continuously learning system that understands your unique financial DNA by integrating real-time data from UPI transactions, income sources, and spending habits.

FinPal doesn’t just show you numbers - it thinks for you, providing actionable insights such as:

A. Where your money goes each month

B. How to save smarter and cut wasteful spending

C. When to invest and what suits your risk appetite

D. How to prepare for low-cash or high-expense periods

Over time, FinPal evolves into a personal CFO - always learning, adapting, and guiding you toward financial stability and freedom.

**2. Specific Pain Points It Addresses**

**A. **Irregular income patterns (gig workers, freelancers):****
   FinPal predicts low-income periods and automatically suggests savings or investment buffers to help users stay financially stable.

**B. **Lack of financial awareness:****
   FinPal converts raw spending data into simple, personalized insights and actionable plans that anyone can understand and use.

**C. **Overspending and impulsive behavior:****
   The app uses behavioral AI nudges such as:
   “You’ve spent ₹800 on food this week - want to move ₹200 to your savings goal?”
   This helps users build better spending habits without feeling restricted.

**D. **Generic investment advice:****
   FinPal recommends AI-curated investment options customized to each user’s risk level, income stability, and financial goals.

**E. **Fragmented money management:****
   Instead of using multiple apps, FinPal combines UPI payments, spending analytics, and financial coaching - all in one intelligent platform.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/fe7f8cf873e44405a7ca9118224adb5a/fe8419f9-3913-4cd1-9e45-39fc34138b9c.png)

**3. Target Audience**

**Primary Users:**

- Gig and informal sector workers with fluctuating income (delivery agents, freelancers, artisans).
- Young salaried professionals starting their financial journey.
- Small business owners seeking a smarter way to manage cash flow.

**Secondary Users:**

- Students learning financial discipline.
- Homemakers managing household budgets.

**Market Opportunity:**
India’s 800M+ digital payment users and 100M+ gig workers represent a massive untapped audience for personalized, AI-driven financial wellness tools.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/fe7f8cf873e44405a7ca9118224adb5a/3b831d74-8a8a-44fa-a957-6cda33fe42b1.png)

**4. Go-To-Market (GTM) Strategy**

**Phase 1 – Early Adoption (6 months)**

- Integrate with UPI via partnerships with payment platforms and neobanks.

- Launch in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities targeting gig economy users through partnerships with Swiggy, Zomato, and Uber.

- Run AI-powered referral campaigns (earn cashback when your financial health score improves).

**Phase 2 – Scale (12–18 months)**

- Integrate regional language voice assistants for accessibility.

- Partner with NBFCs and micro-investment platforms for smart, in-app investment products.

- Introduce “FinPal for Business” for MSMEs to manage vendor payments and short-term credit cycles.

**Phase 3 – Community Ecosystem (24+ months)**

- Launch “FinTribe”, a social savings network for collective goals (like Ratan Tata’s inclusive ecosystem model).

- Use anonymized data insights to help financial institutions design inclusive, AI-backed credit models.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/fe7f8cf873e44405a7ca9118224adb5a/f076ccb7-2299-4e3a-be14-46975ff85526.png)


**Revenue Streams**

1. **FinPal Plus Subscription:**
   Premium plan with deeper analytics, personalized investment coaching, and automated savings tools.

2. **Partner Commissions:**
   Revenue from micro-investment and insurance partners for user conversions.

3. **Smart Insights Marketplace:**
   Aggregated and anonymized financial insights offered to institutions for ethical data monetization.

4. **In-App Financial Products:**
   Loans, SIPs, mutual funds, and goal-based savings options integrated directly into FinPal.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/fe7f8cf873e44405a7ca9118224adb5a/38d4d859-9e4e-42ef-b04f-6d3d912fdf72.png)


*To make financial literacy and wealth-building as easy, personal, and natural as making a UPI payment.*

**Fintech: Build an autonomous financial coaching agent that adapts to real user behavior, spending patterns, and income variability - helping gig workers, informal sector employees, and everyday citizens make smarter financial decisions proactively.**

FinPal directly aligns with the Fintech track by building an **autonomous financial coaching agent** that adapts to each user’s real financial behavior.

It uses **Agentic AI** to continuously learn from users’ income patterns, UPI transactions, and spending habits. Based on this data, FinPal proactively offers **personalized insights, savings suggestions, and investment recommendations** tailored to every individual — whether they are gig workers, informal sector employees, or salaried users.

Instead of providing one-size-fits-all advice, FinPal dynamically adjusts its guidance according to income variability and lifestyle changes. It helps users:

* Understand their money flow
* Avoid overspending through AI nudges
* Plan ahead for low-cash periods
* Invest wisely based on their unique risk profile

In short, FinPal fulfills the challenge’s goal by empowering everyday citizens to make **smarter, data-driven financial decisions proactively**, transforming a simple payment app into a personalized, intelligent financial coach.

> Plan smarter, travel smoother.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Commuting daily can be stressful—not just because of traffic, but also due to the uncertainty in ride-hailing prices. Apps like Uber, Ola, Rapido, and others often show fluctuating fares depending on demand, time, and surge pricing.

This leaves users facing problems such as:

Price Confusion: Different apps showing drastically different fares for the same route.

Time Wasted: Switching between multiple apps to compare prices manually before booking.

Uninformed Choices: Many users end up paying higher fares simply because they booked from the first app they opened.

Lack of Transparency: Riders cannot easily see which service offers the most affordable or quickest ride.

Our solution, Commute Companion, solves this by:

✅ Real-Time Comparison – Fetches and compares fares from Uber, Ola, and other ride-hailing apps instantly.

✅ Smart Recommendations – Suggests the best option based on price, ETA, and ride comfort.

✅ Time-Saving – No need to jump between multiple apps—get everything in one place.

✅ Cost-Efficient & Transparent – Ensures commuters always make the most economical choice without hidden effort.

In short, Commute Companion acts as your personal ride advisor, helping you save both money and time while making safer, smarter, and stress-free commuting decisions.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges while Vibecoding Commute Companion-

Location input issues – We couldn’t capture live user-entered locations; only dummy pickup/drop points were showing. We tried fixing this but had to rely on static values for demo.

Data handling errors – Instead of showing NaN, we wanted to display pickup time, savings, fare trends, and distance. We faced undefined distance errors and had to patch those values manually.

Login flow limitation – We couldn’t implement a proper login page due to time/tech constraints, so we hardcoded login details to proceed with testing.

API dependency – Access to real Ola/Uber/Rapido/Namma Yatri APIs was restricted, so we mocked responses, which limited live accuracy.

Scoring alignment – Balancing ETA, price, and reliability into a single recommendation logic required iteration, as initial weights didn’t reflect user intuition.

**Vibecoding your Idea | Powered by Rocket.new**

We leveraged Rocket.new to quickly prototype and ship our idea without heavy setup. The platform gave us ready-made UI scaffolding, so we could focus on designing smooth flows (pickup → recommendation → deep link). We used mock APIs first to simulate Ola, Uber, Rapido, and Namma Yatri responses, and then plugged them into our ranking logic. Rocket.new’s modular structure let us separate the provider fetch layer, scoring engine, and telemetry logging, making iteration fast.

Team **Algorythm** -- Suhail Misgar, [Ridhi bauskar](https://github.com/ridzz-213)

Technical:

**The problem it solves**

**PlastiMukto Mart** is an *AI-powered platform* focused on reducing plastic waste and promoting recycling through community engagement. It features an AI waste analyzer (for image-based plastic detection), a bounty system to reward eco-friendly actions, a marketplace for recycled and sustainable products, leaderboards to track top contributors, and a community dashboard for sharing ideas and collaboration. 
The project uses *Next.js* for the frontend, *Prisma* and *Supabase* for backend and database, and integrates the *Gemini API* for AI waste analysis. It is designed to incentivize positive environmental impact and make sustainability accessible and rewarding.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges Faced During Development**

*1. AI Integration & Accuracy:*
Integrating the Gemini AI for waste analysis was complex. We had to optimize image upload handling, manage API rate limits, and tune the prompts to improve detection accuracy. Ensuring the AI could reliably identify different types of plastic waste required extensive testing and dataset refinement.

*2. Real-Time Bounty & Leaderboard System:*
Building a dynamic bounty system that tracks user actions and updates leaderboards in real time involved designing efficient database queries and handling concurrency. We faced challenges in ensuring data consistency, especially when multiple users completed bounties simultaneously.

*3. Authentication & Security:*
Implementing secure authentication with Supabase while maintaining a seamless user experience was tricky. We had to address issues with session management, password resets, and protecting sensitive user data.

*4. Marketplace & Vendor Management:*
Creating a flexible marketplace for eco-friendly products required robust CRUD operations, image handling, and vendor authentication. We encountered edge cases with product listings, file uploads, and reward redemption flows.

*5. Environment & API Key Management:*
Managing environment variables and API keys securely for both local development and deployment was a challenge. We had to ensure keys were not exposed and that the app could run smoothly across different environments.

*6. Database Migrations & Seeding:*
Keeping the database schema and seed data in sync between development and production required careful migration planning. We faced issues with data integrity and rollback strategies during rapid iteration.

*7. Responsive & Accessible UI:*
Designing a modern, responsive, and accessible UI for diverse features (dashboard, marketplace, community) was time-consuming. We had to test across devices and browsers, and implement accessibility best practices for all users.

*8. Team Collaboration & Version Control:*
Coordinating work across team members, managing merge conflicts, and maintaining code quality standards was essential. We set up clear branching strategies and code review processes to streamline collaboration.

*9. Performance Optimization:*
As the app grew, optimizing load times, image processing, and database queries became critical. We used caching, lazy loading, and query optimization to improve user experience.

*10. Documentation & Demo Preparation:*
Preparing clear documentation and a smooth demo for hackathon judges required extra effort. We ensured setup instructions, feature guides, and troubleshooting steps were comprehensive and easy to follow.

> From map to medicine — your fastest route to care.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**CareQueue – Making Clinics Smarter & Safer**

**What can people use it for?**

- Find nearby clinics instantly on a map with real-time queue status.
- Check expected wait times (AI-powered) before leaving home.
- Book appointments or confirm walk-ins without standing in line.
- Use triage suggestions to decide whether to visit immediately or wait.
- Chat with clinic staff for quick clarifications (services, availability, delays).
- Get notified when it’s almost their turn, reducing unnecessary waiting inside crowded clinics.
- Stay informed during emergencies (floods, outbreaks) with highlighted emergency centers.

**How does it make tasks easier and safer?**

- Time-Saving: Patients no longer waste hours in waiting rooms or visiting clinics that are already full.
- Stress-Free Experience: Transparent wait times reduce uncertainty and anxiety.
- Equal Access: Multi-language support, voice commands, and accessibility mode make it usable for everyone, including seniors and visually impaired.
- Health Safety: Reduces crowding in waiting rooms, lowering risk of infection spread.
- Better Resource Use: Clinics can balance patient load, reducing staff burnout and improving service quality.
- Community Impact: Patient feedback highlights trustworthy clinics, while public health alerts reach everyone faster.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I Ran Into**

**1. Real-Time Queue Updates**

Problem: Synchronizing patient check-ins (crowd-sourced) with receptionist updates was tricky.

Fix: Implemented a WebSocket-based real-time communication layer so that any update (patient or admin) reflects instantly across all devices.

**2. Accurate Wait Time Predictions**

Problem: Our first AI model was giving inconsistent wait time results due to limited data.

Fix: We adjusted the prediction algorithm by combining historical averages with real-time queue lengths, which improved accuracy significantly.

**3. Maps Integration**

Problem: Handling different map APIs (Google Maps vs MapLibre) and ensuring smooth clinic pin rendering was a challenge.

Fix: We abstracted the map service into a separate module so we could switch between APIs easily without rewriting core logic.

**4. Accessibility Features**

Problem: Adding voice command and high-contrast modes required testing across browsers and devices.

Fix: We used ARIA standards and the Web Speech API, and conducted iterative testing to ensure compatibility.

**5. Offline Mode**

Problem: Ensuring the app worked in low-network conditions was difficult.

Fix: We used local caching (IndexedDB/SQLite) to store the last known clinic data, so patients could still access information offline.

**Ethereum Track**

Our solution leverages the Ethereum ecosystem to add trust, transparency, and decentralization to healthcare access:

**Decentralized Queue Verification:** Patients’ check-ins and clinic updates can be stored on Ethereum smart contracts to ensure tamper-proof queue records.

**Secure Medical Data Sharing:** Using Ethereum-based identity and access control, patients can selectively share medical/visit history with clinics without exposing full data.

**Transparency & Trust:** Blockchain ensures clinics cannot manipulate wait times or feedback, creating a fairer and more reliable system for patients.

**Community-Driven Model:** Patients and clinics contribute updates that are validated and anchored on-chain, enabling a transparent, community-owned platform rather than a centralized one.

This makes CareQueue not just a smart queue management system but also a trustless, decentralized healthcare coordination platform powered by Ethereum.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![YOLOv3 Algorithm](https://img.shields.io/badge/YOLOv3%20Algorithm-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

YOLO detection accuracy: Overlapping people sometimes caused duplicate or incorrect detections, so we had to adjust the confidence threshold and restrict detection to the person class.

Risk classification: YOLO detects objects, but it doesn't directly understand situations like “kidnapping” or “danger.” We had to design a separate risk-analysis layer for our prototype.

Video processing: Processing CCTV footage frame-by-frame and generating annotated videos required optimization and testing.

Live vs prototype data: Connecting real-time CCTV and GPS was beyond the prototype scope, so we used prerecorded CCTV footage and simulated GPS data to demonstrate the workflow.

Deployment: Getting all dependencies and video/model files working correctly on Streamlit Community Cloud was another challenge.

Integration: Connecting the AI detection, backend, dashboard, location monitoring, and emergency-alert concept into one working flow required multiple rounds of testing.

**The problem it solves**

Women’s safety systems are often reactive, requiring the person at risk to manually press an SOS button or ask for help. In situations where they may be unable to do so, traditional systems can fail to respond in time.

SHIELD addresses this gap by combining AI-powered CCTV monitoring, risk analysis, location tracking, and emergency response into one platform. It monitors activity, identifies potentially unusual situations, categorizes risk levels, and provides a mechanism for rapid emergency notification.

In short: SHIELD aims to shift women’s safety from “responding after an emergency” to “detecting and responding to risk earlier.”

**The problem it solves**

## The problem it solves

The Odinson Vibration Monitor addresses the need for affordable, accessible vibration and seismic activity monitoring in various applications:

- **Structural Health Monitoring**: Provides low-cost solution for monitoring vibrations in buildings, bridges, and other infrastructure to detect potential structural issues before they become critical
- **Earthquake Early Warning**: Functions as a digital seismometer prototype capable of detecting abnormal motion patterns that could indicate seismic activity
- **Industrial Vibration Analysis**: Enables monitoring of machinery and equipment to detect imbalances, misalignments, or bearing failures that could lead to costly downtime
- **Research and Education**: Serves as an accessible platform for students and researchers to study vibration patterns, signal processing, and sensor integration

The system makes vibration monitoring accessible by:
- Using inexpensive, off-the-shelf components (MPU6050 sensor, Arduino)
- Providing real-time visualization through both web interface and matplotlib display
- Offering multiple alert mechanisms (Telegram, sound, visual)
- Storing data persistently for later analysis
- Including both live monitoring and historical data viewing capabilities

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges we ran into

During development, we encountered several technical hurdles that required creative solutions:

### Datetime Format Error
**Problem**: `ValueError: Invalid format string` when generating CSV filenames due to using `%s` (seconds since epoch) instead of `%S` (seconds) in `strftime` format string.

**Solution**: Corrected the format string from `%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%s` to `%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S` to properly represent hours, minutes, and seconds.

### Port Already in Use
**Problem**: `OSError: [WinError 10048] Only one usage of each socket address...` when trying to start the Flask server, indicating port 5000 was already occupied.

**Solution**: Implemented process cleanup by identifying and terminating existing processes using the port with `netstat` and `taskkill` commands before starting the application.

### Serial Port Permission/Access Issues
**Problem**: `PermissionError(13, 'Access is denied.')` when attempting to open COM3 serial port, typically caused by another process holding the port or insufficient permissions.

**Solution**: Added robust serial connection handling with:
- Automatic retry mechanism with exponential backoff
- Graceful reconnection logic when serial communication is interrupted
- Clear error messaging to guide users on resolving port conflicts
- Mock data mode for development/testing when hardware isn't available

### Matplotlib Unresponsiveness
**Problem**: The matplotlib figure window became unresponsive and stopped updating due to the main thread being blocked in a tight loop without processing GUI events.

**Solution**: Replaced `time.sleep(0.016) + flush_events()` with `plt.pause(0.001)` which properly processes TkAgg GUI events while maintaining adequate update frequency for smooth visualization.

### Data Loss on Program Termination
**Problem**: When stopping the program with Ctrl+C, CSV files were incomplete or empty because daemon threads were terminated abruptly before flushing buffers.

**Solution**: Implemented graceful shutdown sequence:
- Added global `running` flag to control all worker threads
- Changed threads from daemon to non-daemon so they can be properly joined
- Created Flask shutdown endpoint (`/shutdown`) for clean server termination
- Added Ctrl+C handler that sets `running=False`, joins threads, and closes resources
- Made CSV file line-buffered (`buffering=1`) for immediate data flushing
