> AI-Powered Planetary Defense.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**
StellarOrbit bridges the critical gap between raw satellite data and actionable intelligence. Currently, analyzing satellite imagery is a slow, manual process prone to human error and centralized data manipulation. StellarOrbit automates this workflow to provide Real-Time Planetary Defense & Environmental Accountability.
 1. Accelerating Disaster Response (AI Analysis)
The Problem: During forest fires or floods, every second counts. Traditional analysis relies on human experts manually reviewing satellite feeds, which creates a dangerous latency between an event occurring and rescuers being deployed. The Solution: StellarOrbit’s Computer Vision Engine instantly processes incoming satellite telemetry.

Fire Detection: Uses Deep Learning (CNNs) to identify thermal hotspots and wildfires instantly, enabling faster evacuation orders.

Flood Mapping: Automatically segments water bodies to track flood progression in real-time.

2. Censorship-Resistant Environmental Data (Web3)
The Problem: Centralized databases containing environmental records (like oil spills, illegal deforestation, or emission violations) can be altered, hidden, or deleted by corrupt actors or governments. The Solution: Immutable Mission Logs.

Every critical hazard detected by our AI is hashed and logged onto the Ethereum Blockchain.

This creates a permanent, tamper-proof "Proof of Hazard" that ensures transparency and accountability for future generations.

3. Precision Agriculture & Food Security
The Problem: Farmers lack accessible tools to monitor crop health over vast areas, leading to resource waste and lower yields. The Solution: Our NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) module analyzes crop density and health from orbit. This allows farmers to target water and fertilizer exactly where needed, reducing waste and increasing food security.

4. Planetary Defense & Situational Awareness
The Problem: Space debris and Near-Earth Objects (Asteroids) pose an existential threat to satellites and Earth, yet tracking data is often fragmented across different agencies. The Solution: The Live Ops Dashboard aggregates real-time data from NASA and local radar arrays into a single "Glass Cockpit."

Collision Avoidance: Local tactical radar scans for orbital debris.

Asteroid Tracking: Live integration with NASA's NEO API monitors potentially hazardous asteroids passing Earth today.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into
Building a full-stack AI application for space tech came with significant hurdles, particularly when moving from a local environment to the cloud.

1. The "Out of Memory" Crash (TensorFlow on Cloud)
The Hurdle: Our deep learning models for fire detection are computationally heavy. When we attempted to deploy them on a standard AWS EC2 free-tier instance (t2.micro), the server repeatedly crashed with Killed messages or No space left on device errors during installation. The Solution: We had to think like DevOps engineers.

Storage: We dynamically expanded the AWS EBS volume from 8GB to 15GB and resized the Linux partitions on the fly using growpart and resize2fs.

Memory: We created a 2GB Swap File (virtual RAM) to give the server just enough breathing room to load the TensorFlow weights without crashing the kernel.

2. The "JSON Serialization" Trap
The Hurdle: Our computer vision algorithms use NumPy for high-speed pixel counting. However, when sending these statistics to the frontend, the app would silently fail. We discovered that Flask’s JSON serializer cannot handle numpy.int64 or numpy.float32 data types. The Solution: We implemented a strict type-casting layer in our backend logic, explicitly converting every AI-derived metric into standard Python int() or float() types before the JSON response is constructed.

3. Securing the NASA Feed (Backend Proxy)
The Hurdle: To track asteroids for the "Planetary Defense" module, we integrated NASA's NeoWS API. Initially, we called this directly from the frontend JavaScript, which exposed our private API Key to anyone inspecting the browser network tab. The Solution: We re-architected the data flow using a Proxy Pattern. We built a dedicated Flask route (/api/asteroids) that reads the API key securely from a server-side .env file. The frontend now asks our server for the data, and our server talks to NASA, keeping the credentials completely hidden from the public.

4. The "Localhost" Disconnect
The Hurdle: Everything worked perfectly on our laptops, but when we tried to open the "Live Ops" dashboard on a mobile phone to test responsiveness, it failed to connect. The API was hardcoded to 127.0.0.1 (localhost), which meant the phone was trying to find the server inside itself! The Solution: We configured our Flask application to listen on 0.0.0.0 (all public interfaces) and updated our frontend logic to dynamically target the AWS Public IP. This enabled a true cross-device experience where the dashboard could be monitored from anywhere in the world.

**Best AWS Hack**

**How We Used Amazon Web Services (AWS)**
StellarOrbit is a computation-heavy application that processes high-resolution satellite imagery using Deep Learning models. A simple static hosting solution would not suffice; we required the robust, scalable infrastructure of AWS to handle the processing load.

1. High-Performance Compute (Amazon EC2)
The Core Engine: We deployed our Flask backend and TensorFlow AI models on an Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) instance.

Why it fits: Processing satellite data requires significant RAM and CPU power. By utilizing EC2, we moved the heavy inference workload off the user's device and onto the cloud. This ensures that a farmer with a low-end mobile phone can still access sophisticated crop analysis instantly.

2. Scalable Storage Architecture (Amazon EBS)
Handling Big Data: Satellite imagery datasets are massive. During development, we encountered storage bottlenecks where the AI libraries and image buffers filled our initial disk allocation.

The AWS Advantage: We leveraged Amazon EBS (Elastic Block Store) to dynamically modify and expand our storage volume on the fly (growing partitions from 8GB to 15GB) without server downtime. This elasticity is crucial for a platform intended to archive historical planetary data.

3. Global Accessibility & Networking
Mission Control Anywhere: A key feature of StellarOrbit is the "Live Ops" dashboard, which must be accessible to field teams worldwide.

Security & Access: We configured AWS Security Groups to strictly manage traffic, opening specific ports (5000) for the API while securing administrative access (SSH) to our IP. This turned a local Python script into a globally accessible, secure web application.

4. Future Integration (Roadmap)
The Next Step: While our current architecture relies on EC2/EBS, the project is architected to scale into the wider AWS ecosystem:

Amazon S3: For long-term archival of "Immutable Mission Logs" images.

AWS Bedrock: To replace our rule-based chatbot with a GenAI agent capable of answering complex geological questions.

**The problem it solves**

# **The Problem It Solves**
(First Time Builder)
AtmosHealthAI addresses a widespread but often unnoticed problem: **people frequently fall sick because of sudden changes in air quality and weather without knowing the exact cause.**

Most individuals rely on AQI or weather apps that only display numbers, not explanations. These apps don’t tell you how PM2.5, pollen, humidity, or temperature shifts specifically affect *your* body. As a result:

### **Common Real-Life Problems**

* People keep getting asthma attacks, allergy flare-ups, sinus infections, or migraines **without understanding the trigger**.
* There is **no system that combines environmental data with personal health history**.
* Existing health apps only track symptoms, while weather apps only track climate **nothing connects both**.
* Users react to illnesses *after* they happen instead of preventing them.

AtmosHealthAI fills this critical gap by acting as a **personal health guardian** that understands both your body and your environment. It intelligently correlates **your past health patterns** with **current air and weather conditions** to warn you *before* problems start.

---

# **How People Can Use It**

## **1. Get Daily Personalized Health Predictions**

Instead of raw AQI numbers, users receive **simple, human-friendly predictions** about how the day’s environmental conditions may affect them.

Example:

> “High particulate matter today asthma and sinus issues are more likely.”

---

## **2. Discover Their Unique Triggers**

Every person’s body reacts differently.
AtmosHealthAI learns whether you are sensitive to:

* Dust levels
* Humidity changes
* Temperature drops
* Pollen spikes
* Pollution peaks

It then explains **your personal vulnerabilities**, not generic ones.

---

## **3. Receive Smart Preventive Alerts**

Users get proactive alerts *before* symptoms appear, such as:

* *“PM2.5 levels are rising  carry a mask today.”*
* *“High humidity expected this evening. You may experience sinus pressure.”*

This transforms healthcare from reactive to **preventive**.

---

## **4. Plan Their Day with Confidence**

With better predictions, users can decide:

* The best time to go outdoors
* Whether to carry inhalers, allergy meds, or masks
* How to plan workouts, travel, or children’s outdoor activities
* When to avoid highly polluted areas

Users gain **control over their daily routine**.

---

## **5. Build Long-Term Health Awareness**

As users record their symptoms and provide feedback, the system adjusts itself.

Over time, AtmosHealthAI becomes:

* More personalized
* More accurate
* More predictive

This creates a **self-learning health assistant** unique to each user.

---

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

Building **AtmosHealthAI** came with several interesting and sometimes complex challenges. Solving each one helped strengthen the system and deepened my understanding of how environmental intelligence and health analytics work together.

---

## 1. **Translating Environmental Data Into Meaningful Health Insights**

One of the hardest parts was figuring out how to turn raw AQI and weather parameters such as PM2.5, PM10, humidity, temperature, and wind speed into understandable health warnings for users.

**What made it challenging:**
The data is technical, varies a lot throughout the day, and doesn’t directly say *“you might get a headache today.”*

**How I solved it:**

* I researched medical studies that show how specific pollutants and weather changes affect breathing issues, allergies, migraines, etc.
* Instead of training a custom model, I used a **pretrained LLM** and designed a structured prompt system that gives the LLM clear rules for how to interpret environmental patterns.
* Through repeated testing and refinement, I tuned the prompts and scoring system so the predictions became more consistent and meaningful.

---

## 2. **Unstable or Delayed API Responses**

Weather and AQI APIs sometimes returned incomplete, delayed, or inconsistent data, which could break the prediction flow.

**How I solved it:**

* Added **fallback APIs** and a **retry mechanism** so a single failure didn’t stop the system.
* Introduced **response caching** to use the last valid data if APIs were down.
* Implemented **timeouts** to keep the UI responsive even when API calls lagged.

---

## 3. **Designing for Highly Personalized Health Sensitivities**

Every user reacts differently to pollution and weather changes, so a one-size-fits-all model wasn’t possible.

**How I solved it:**

* Built a dynamic feedback loop where the **pretrained LLM adapts via prompts** based on user-submitted symptoms and triggers.
* Allowed users to manually mark factors that affect them such as dust, cold winds, or humidity so the system learns their risk profile progressively without retraining the model.

---

## 4. **Making Predictions Trustworthy and Easy to Understand**

Early versions of the system produced predictions that felt either too generic or too technical for everyday users.

**How I solved it:**

* Improved the message format to focus on **clarity, prevention, and real-world actions**.
* Added simple suggestions like using a mask, avoiding running outdoors, or increasing hydration so the insights became more practical and helpful.

---

## 5. **Synchronizing Data Across Frontend, Backend, and AI Engine**

Managing the flow between user data, environmental data, and the AI prediction logic required careful orchestration.

**How I solved it:**

* Built a clean workflow pipeline ensuring that all data reaches the LLM in the correct order.
* Used proper state management and queues to maintain smooth, real-time interaction between components.
* Ensured predictions remain accurate even when user or environmental data updates happen quickly.

> The first trustless Zcash relay on Starknet

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cairo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cairo-333333?style=flat-square) ![StarkNet](https://img.shields.io/badge/StarkNet-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zcash RPC](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zcash%20RPC-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Z.U.L.U. (Zcash Unified Ledger on Starknet) - a trustless Zcash relay on Starknet

[1] the trust problem with bridges
right now, if you want to bridge Zcash to any chain, you have to trust some centralized entity (multisig, MPC, whatever). they hold your funds and you just... hope they don't rug.

solution: i built a relay that cryptographically verifies Zcash block headers directly on Starknet. no trust needed - the math proves the block is valid.

[2] zcash → starknet interoperability didn't exist
there was literally no way for a Starknet contract to know what's happening on Zcash. zero connection between these two ecosystems.

solution: now any Starknet contract can query verified Zcash blocks. this opens up:
- trustless bridges (verify a tx was included in a block via merkle proof)
- cross-chain dApps that react to Zcash events
- SPV-style payment verification

[3] equihash verification was "impossible" on-chain
verifying Zcash's proof-of-work (Equihash) on-chain is too expensive. 512 blake2b hashes per block

solution: heavily optimized the blake2b and equihash implementation in Cairo to make it actually feasible. ~15 STRK per block, ~3 minutes, fully on-chain verification.

tldr: i built the infrastructure to connect Zcash's privacy chain to Starknet's scaling chain - trustlessly.

**Challenges we ran into**

[1] the blake2b bottleneck [biggest hurdle & thanks to Starkware ecosystem team to guide and help me out]

problem : equihash requires verifying 512 indices, each needing blake2b hash & standard implementation was far too expensive (gas wise) and slow

solution :
i optimized blake2b and equihash 
a. unrolls all 12 rounds of compression function to eliminate loop overhead

b. precomputes the equihash init state constants to skips param block construction 

c. first -block caching : [biggest optimization] the first 128 bytes of the header are identical for all 512 hashes, i made a the verifier to compress this chunk once , cache the state and then reuse it.
this cut compression calls by ~50%

[2] the endian-ness : little and big endian conversion
this was the most annoying problem, the internal state of the block is in little endian but my program was for big endian 
and since there were many functions with different endian-ness expectation - it was really exhausting but i finally made all of it consistent

[3] frontend synchronization : so to showcase the inner working of this project , i had to show the backend's step by step logs of the multi-tx 

solution : i used websockets to the frontend, giving users real time visibility to the 11 tx

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

Z.U.L.U. bridges zcash and starknet trustlessly - no oracles, no multisigs

the relay verifies zcash's equihash proof-of-work on-chain and stores block headers. users can then submit merkle proofs to prove any tx happened on zcash

this enables private cross-chain interactions - a user can make a shielded payment on zcash and trigger an action on starknet by proving that tx inclusion

this exactly matches , the cross-chain privacy solution track

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

Z.U.L.U is the first trustless zcash relay on starknet - verifies equihash PoW fully on-chain in cairo

and for this I made some privacy infra & tools/libraries :

built open source cairo libraries for zcash verification:
blake2b_ultra.cairo
 - optimized blake2b with unrolled rounds and state caching

equihash.cairo - full equihash (200,9) verification with batch processing
also built python scripts for generating merkle proofs from zcash rpc in the exact format the contract expects

these tools make it easy for other devs to build zcash-verifying apps on starknet

**General Bounty**

Z.U.L.U. is the first trustless zcash relay on starknet - verifies equihash PoW fully on-chain in cairo

built optimized blake2b and equihash verification libraries that cut gas costs by ~50% through first-block caching and unrolled compression rounds

the relay stores verified block headers and enables merkle proof verification for any tx 

this is the foundational infra needed for ztarknet and cross-chain privacy apps between zcash and starknet

**The problem it solves**

Jobmarket is a crypto-native job marketplace that connects employers with talent (both humans and AI agents) using blockchain-based payments.

🔧 Problems It Solves
1. Salary Privacy
Traditional job platforms expose salary information publicly. Jobmarket uses Zcash shielded transactions to keep compensation private between employer and talent.

2. Slow & Expensive Payments
Freelancers and contractors often wait weeks for bank transfers and lose money to fees. Jobmarket uses:

X402 Micropayments (Coinbase) for instant settlement
Crypto payments (SOL, ETH, ZEC) with minimal fees
3. No Infrastructure for AI Agents
As AI agents become capable workers, there's no marketplace for them. Jobmarket has a dedicated AI Agent marketplace where:

Developers can list their AI agents for hire
Employers can pay per-task or hourly for agent work
Agents have their own wallets for machine-to-machine payments
4. Identity & Trust Without Centralization
Instead of relying on centralized KYC, Jobmarket uses:

Wallet-based authentication (Privy - supports MetaMask, Phantom, social logins)
On-chain reputation based on completed work and reviews
Verification levels (basic → verified → premium)
🌟 Key Features
Private Payments	Zcash z-addresses hide transaction amounts
Instant Settlement	X402 protocol for micropayments
AI Agent Marketplace	Hire AI workers or list your agents
Multi-Chain Support	Solana, Ethereum, Zcash
Wallet Auth	No passwords, just connect your wallet
Escrow System	Secure funds until work is delivered

💡 Target Users
Web3/Crypto Developers seeking privacy-first employment
Companies hiring remote talent globally without banking friction
AI Agent Developers monetizing their agents
Freelancers wanting instant crypto payments

**The problem it solves**

## The problem Arcsilence solves

On Solana today, every meaningful trade is a **public signal**:

- Large swaps, treasury rebalances, and hedging moves are fully visible on-chain.
- MEV bots can **front-run, back-run, or sandwich** those trades.
- Competitors can **infer strategies** (what you rotate into, when, and in what size).

For DAOs, funds, and POL managers this leads to:

- Worse execution (higher slippage, worse prices).
- Long-term **alpha leakage** (strategies become predictable).
- Friction for more “institutional” DeFi use cases that expect dark-pool style execution.

Arcsilence removes that “transparency tax” without sacrificing on-chain settlement.

---

## What people can use Arcsilence for

Arcsilence is a **private dark pool and rebalancer for Solana**, powered by Arcium’s encrypted compute. It can be used to:

- **Rebalance DAO treasuries privately**
  - Rotate between stables, LSTs, LRTs, and governance tokens.
  - Avoid pre-signalling “the DAO is exiting X and entering Y” before trades complete.

- **Run fund / market-maker strategies without leaking alpha**
  - Execute systematic hedging, arbitrage, or rotation strategies.
  - Hide order sizes, routing preferences, timing, and thresholds from bots and competitors.

- **Adjust protocol-owned liquidity (POL) quietly**
  - Move liquidity across pools/venues to optimize yield and depth.
  - Prevent markets from trading ahead of POL changes.

- **Batch larger trades without becoming MEV bait**
  - Use Arcsilence as a private execution backend on top of existing DEXs/aggregators.
  - Keep trades verifiable on Solana, but **intent invisible** while execution is in flight.

---

## How it makes existing tasks easier and safer

Arcsilence changes DeFi execution in three key ways:

- **Safer from MEV and manipulation**
  - Orders are fetched from Solana, encrypted, and matched via **Arcium MPC**.
  - There is no clean, public pre-trade signal for MEV bots to target.

- **Better protection of strategy and IP**
  - Matching, sizing, and routing logic run inside **encrypted compute**.
  - Observers see only final settlements on-chain, not the internal decision process.

- **DeFi-native and composable**
  - Settlement still uses Solana programs, SPL token vaults, and DEX integrations.
  - Protocols can plug Arcsilence in as a **private execution layer**, not a separate silo.

In short: **Arcsilence lets serious Solana users keep public settlement and composability, while hiding the sensitive part – their intent and strategy – during execution.**

**General Bounty**

Arcsilence is a privacy-preserving dark-pool and rebalancing engine that tackles a core primitive needed by any privacy-first ecosystem: **confidential capital movement with verifiable settlement**.

Our system uses encrypted compute (via Arcium) to privately match orders and rebalance portfolios, while only revealing final settlements on-chain. This lets DAOs, funds, and protocol treasuries move capital without exposing intent, strategy, or sensitive portfolio information to the wider network.

Although our MVP focuses on trading, the same architecture can support zk-Passport / zk-Census style use cases: DAOs or digital communities can prove aggregate economic activity or treasury health **without doxxing individual members or positions**. In that sense, Arcsilence contributes a reusable building block for privacy-preserving coordination and measurement.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

Arcsilence is a private dark-pool and rebalancing engine on Solana built directly on **Arcium’s encrypted compute** for the Private DeFi & Trading track.

We integrate Arcium MXE end-to-end: a TypeScript solver fetches OPEN orders from our Solana darkpool program, encrypts the order fields (x25519 + RescueCipher), and submits them to the Arcium MPC network for matching. Only the attested MPC result is then used to call `batchSettle()` on-chain, moving funds between SPL token vaults and updating order state.

This means **orders, positions, and strategies remain confidential**, while **settlement stays fully verifiable on Solana**. DAOs, funds, and POL managers can execute large swaps and treasury rebalances without leaking intent to MEV bots or competitors. The project is therefore a concrete implementation of Arcium-powered **private DeFi trading infrastructure**.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

Arcsilence is a private dark-pool and rebalancing engine that can be **directly extended to a Zcash-backed, privacy-first stablecoin design**.

Today, Arcsilence uses encrypted compute (via Arcium) to privately match orders and rebalance portfolios, while settling transparently on-chain. The same architecture can be adapted so that:

- A **ZEC-backed stablecoin on Aztec** is treated as a core collateral/quote asset inside the dark pool.  
- Users privately deposit ZEC (or a wrapped ZEC representation) as collateral, earn yield via protocol-defined strategies, and receive a stablecoin whose minting, transfers, and redemptions are modeled as **private orders** in Arcsilence.  
- Yield generation and risk parameters (LTV, liquidation bands, rebalancing rules) run inside encrypted compute, while Zcash/ Aztec provide the **shielded settlement layer**.

In other words, Arcsilence already solves the **private matching, rebalancing, and risk-engine** side; plugging in a ZEC-backed collateral model and Aztec settlement turns it into a full **privacy-first stablecoin and capital-management stack**.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

Arcsilence is a private dark-pool and rebalancing engine that can also function as **privacy infrastructure** for Zcash developers.

Our architecture cleanly separates:
- **Intents** (orders/strategies),
- **Encrypted compute** (Arcium MPC),
- **Settlement layer** (pluggable, currently Solana).

This makes it straightforward to add a Zcash leg plus a small **TypeScript SDK** that:
- Takes funds from **transparent-only Zcash users**,
- Uses the **PCZT API** to construct shielded outputs,
- Routes those shielded funds into private Arcsilence strategies or dark-pool execution.

In this way, Arcsilence can be extended into a **bridge tool** that helps transparent Zcash users and developers seamlessly move into shielded, privacy-preserving DeFi flows.

**Private Payments & Transactions**

Arcsilence is a private execution layer that can be extended from trading into **private payments and transaction routing**.

Today, Arcsilence uses encrypted compute (Arcium MPC) to privately match and settle orders on Solana, hiding intent, sizing, and routing logic while keeping settlement verifiable. The same mechanism can be used to:

- Route **large or recurring payments** (treasury payouts, vesting streams, DAO grants) through a private matching layer instead of broadcasting them as obvious on-chain transfers.
- Enable **confidential remittance flows** where only the final settlement is visible, but path, batching, and counterparties are shielded during execution.
- Power **merchant/point-of-sale style payouts** that aggregate and route funds privately before final settlement to recipients.

In short, Arcsilence provides the core primitive this track asks for: a **privacy-preserving transaction system** that sits between users and public settlement, making high-value payments and transfers significantly more private and harder to exploit.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

Arcsilence is an **unstoppable private DeFi execution layer**: a dark-pool and rebalancing engine that hides intent while keeping settlement censorship-resistant and on-chain.

- **User privacy & security**
  - Orders and strategy parameters are processed in **encrypted compute** (via Arcium), not exposed to mempools or public order books.
  - Only final settlements are written on-chain, significantly reducing MEV, copy-trading, and exploit surfaces.

- **Innovative DeFi protocol**
  - Separates **intent → private matching → on-chain settlement** into clean layers.
  - Acts as a shared **private execution backend** that DAOs, funds, and protocols can plug into, rather than a closed silo.
  - Can be extended to leverage Zcash-style shielded legs for capital movement and profit withdrawal.

Arcsilence therefore delivers exactly what this bounty calls for: a practical, composable **private DeFi trading platform** that prioritizes user privacy and security while remaining credibly neutral and on-chain.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

Arcsilence is a modular private execution layer that can be extended into **developer tooling around Zcash core**.

Our architecture already separates:
- **Intents** (orders/strategies),
- **Private compute** (encrypted matching),
- **Settlement backends** (currently Solana, designed to be pluggable).

This makes it straightforward to ship Zcash-focused developer tools such as:

- A **TypeScript SDK** that abstracts moving value from Zcash (transparent or shielded) into private execution flows and back.
- Reusable **adapters around Zcash core** (e.g., PCZT-based constructors, shielded payout helpers, proof/attestation verifiers) that plug directly into existing wallets or services.
- A simple **“privacy router” library** that lets other apps send value into Zcash-backed, strategy-driven flows without hand-rolling transaction logic.

In this way, Arcsilence becomes not just an app, but a piece of **privacy infrastructure** that makes it easier for developers to integrate Zcash-based privacy into their own DeFi and payment applications.

**Self-Custody & Wallet Innovation**

Arcsilence can power **next-generation self-custody wallets** by acting as a “private execution mode” behind a familiar wallet UX.

Instead of users sending large swaps or treasury operations directly from a wallet to public DEXs (and leaking intent), the wallet can:

- Expose a **“Private Trade / Private Rebalance”** button that routes orders to Arcsilence.
- Keep users **in full self-custody**: funds remain in user-controlled accounts or program vaults with explicit approvals.
- Use Arcsilence’s encrypted compute layer to handle routing, sizing, and matching privately, then return verifiable settlement back to the wallet.

This enables:

- Wallets with built-in **MEV-safe execution** and strategy protection.
- Improved **private asset management UX**: users manage portfolios, not raw transactions.
- A clean path to integrating shielded/Zcash legs later, while keeping the core wallet experience simple and mobile-first.

Arcsilence therefore complements this track as a **backend privacy engine** that next-gen wallets can plug into to offer true private, self-custodial DeFi interactions.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

Arcsilence is a **private execution layer for swaps and rebalancing**, making it a natural fit for this prize.

- **Private swaps**  
  Arcsilence already treats swaps as **encrypted intents** that are matched off-chain (via Arcium) and then settled on-chain. This keeps **route, size, and counterparties private** while preserving verifiable settlement.

- **Privacy-preserving analytics**  
  Order flow and routing logic live inside the encrypted compute layer, enabling aggregate analytics (e.g., volumes, utilization, venue preference) to be derived **without exposing individual strategies or positions**.

- **Integration into existing swap flows**  
  Arcsilence is designed as a **pluggable backend**: it can sit behind existing Solana DEX aggregators or cross-chain routers, acting as a **private swap engine** for high-value or sensitive flows, while the front-end UX and liquidity sources remain unchanged.

In short, Arcsilence extends existing swap flows with a **native private swap model**: encrypted matching, minimal on-chain disclosure, and a clear path to Zcash-style privacy legs for capital movement.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

Arcsilence is a modular **private execution layer** that can double as privacy infrastructure for other builders, not just a standalone app.

Because we cleanly separate:

- **Intents** (orders / strategies),
- **Private compute** (encrypted matching via Arcium),
- **Settlement backends** (pluggable chains, currently Solana),

we can expose Arcsilence as a **developer-facing framework** for privacy-preserving financial logic:

- A **TypeScript SDK** and set of “privacy adapters” that let other dApps send intents into encrypted execution and receive verifiable settlements back, without handling crypto details themselves.
- Reusable primitives for **private coordination** (e.g., DAOs or contributor groups coordinating capital flows or rewards) where only aggregates are visible, but individual contributions remain hidden.
- A simple set of **interfaces and examples** that show how to bolt encrypted matching + private routing onto existing open-source protocols, turning Arcsilence into a base layer for privacy-focused DeFi and collaboration tools.

In short, Arcsilence can be packaged as a **privacy execution framework + SDK**, making it easier for developers to integrate strong privacy into their own applications.

**General Bounty**

Arcsilence is a privacy-preserving dark-pool and rebalance engine that aligns directly with the goals of the General Bounty: building stronger private finance infrastructure.

While our MVP focuses on encrypted matching (via Arcium) and transparent settlement on Solana, the same architecture naturally extends to **Zcash as a shielded leg** – for example, routing profits, treasury allocations, or fees into Zcash shielded addresses for long-term private holding or cross-domain settlement.

By solving MEV and information-leakage problems for large DeFi flows and designing with a Zcash-compatible privacy model in mind, Arcsilence contributes to the broader ecosystem of **privacy-first financial tools**

**Private Payments & Transactions**

Arcsilence is a private execution layer that can be extended into an **innovative Zcash-based payment router**.

Today, Arcsilence privately matches and settles high-value swaps and rebalances using encrypted compute, while only revealing final settlements on-chain. The same engine can be adapted so:

- **ZEC (or shielded ZEC addresses)** become the core settlement rail for payouts, salaries, DAO grants, and remittances.
- Users or DAOs submit **payment batches as private intents** (who to pay, in what currency/amount), which Arcsilence routes and nets out in encrypted compute.
- Final settlements are executed via **shielded Zcash transactions**, so recipients get funds with strong privacy, while senders benefit from efficient, netted execution.

This turns Arcsilence into a **Zcash-native private payouts and remittance layer**: a system where treasuries, employers, and DAOs can schedule and route complex payment flows, but counterparties, amounts, and routing logic stay shielded—aligned with the “Private Payments & Transactions” bounty and compelling as a live pitch for The Shot.

**The problem it solves**

## Privacy in On-Chain Gaming

Traditional on-chain games face a fundamental privacy problem: **all game state is publicly visible on the blockchain**. This eliminates strategic gameplay, makes games predictable, and prevents classic game mechanics like hidden cards, secret moves, or private information.

**Liars Proof** solves this by enabling **privacy-preserving on-chain games** where players can:
- Keep their cards completely hidden from opponents
- Make verifiable claims about hidden information
- Prove statements without revealing underlying data
- Play strategically without information leakage

----

## Zero-Knowledge Proofs for Gaming

### The Challenge
How do you verify that a player has a specific card (e.g., "a Heart card with value ≥ 10") without revealing:
- Which exact card they have
- Their entire hand
- Any other private information

### Our Solution
Using **Zero-Knowledge Proofs**, players can:
1. **Commit** to their hand privately (cryptographic hash)
2. **Claim** they fulfill conditions (e.g., "I have a Heart ≥ 10")
3. **Prove** their claim with a ZK proof that verifies:
   - The claim is true
   - The proof matches their committed hand
   - Without revealing the actual cards

----
### Problems Solved:
- ✅ **No Cheating**: Cryptographic proofs prevent players from lying about their cards
- ✅ **No Information Leakage**: Opponents learn nothing beyond what you claim
- ✅ **Verifiable Fairness**: All game logic is on-chain and auditable
- ✅ **Trustless**: No need for trusted intermediaries or servers

---
### Making On-Chain Games Practical

**Before Liars Proof:**
- ❌ All game state visible → No strategy possible
- ❌ No hidden information → Can't implement classic game mechanics

**With Liars Proof:**
- ✅ Private game state → Strategic gameplay possible
- ✅ Verifiable claims → Fair and secure with ZK
- ✅ Hidden information → Classic game mechanics work on-chain

**Challenges we ran into**

## Network Instability & Transaction Failures

### The Problem
Working with **ZStarknet** (a testnet) presented significant challenges:
- **Frequent transaction rejections**: Transactions would fail unpredictably

### The Solution
We implemented **robust retry logic** and **transaction verification**:

**Key improvements:**
- ✅ Automatic retry with up to 20 attempts
- ✅ Transaction verification
- ✅ Better error handling and user feedback

-----
## Wallet Integration Challenges

### The Problem
Integrating wallets (Ready/Braavos/Controller) with **ZStarknet** was difficult:
- **Network configuration**: Users had to manually configure custom RPC endpoints
- **Poor UX**: Required technical knowledge to set up correctly

### The Solution
We built a **Guest Wallet** that eliminates the need for manual wallet setup:

**Features:**
- ✅ **Auto-generated wallets**: Create a Ready wallet with one click
- ✅ **Automatic funding**: Wallet is funded from an owner account (0.1 Ztf)
- ✅ **Auto-deployment**: Account contract deployed automatically on first use
- ✅ **Persistent storage**: Wallet saved in localStorage for returning players
- ✅ **Seamless experience**: Users can start playing immediately

**Impact:**
-  **Zero setup time**: Users can play in seconds, not minutes
-  **Better conversion**: No technical barriers to entry
-  **Fallback option**: Even experienced users prefer guest mode for quick testing

# 🎯 The Problem It Solves
**The project can be used by both founders as well as investors**

Startup founders often face an opaque, high-stakes environment where feedback is scarce, and finding the right capital feels like searching for a needle in a haystack. **Founders Fuel** eliminates the guesswork by democratizing access to venture capital insights.

### 1. 🔍 The "Black Box" of Investor Feedback
* **The Struggle:** Most founders only get rejection emails without explanation. They rarely receive honest, detailed feedback on their pitch decks until it's too late.
* **The Solution:** The **AI Pitch Deck Analyzer** acts as an always-available Venture Capitalist. It doesn't just "read" slides; it critiques them from multiple personas (e.g., *The Skeptic*, *The Visionary*).
    * **Benefit:** Founders can iterate and "debug" their pitch narrative *before* burning bridges with real investors.

### 2. ⏳ The "Spray and Pray" Fundraising Approach
* **The Struggle:** Founders waste hundreds of hours researching investors or spamming firms that simply don't invest in their sector or stage.
* **The Solution:** Our **Intelligent Matching Engine** instantly aligns startups with investors based on specific investment theses (Sector, Stage, Ticket Size).
    * **Benefit:** Drastic reduction in research time and a higher response rate by targeting only relevant capital sources.

### 3. 📉 Building Without Market Validation
* **The Struggle:** Many startups fail because they build solutions for problems that don't exist or enter markets that are too small (TAM/SAM/SOM issues).
* **The Solution:** The **7-Domain Evaluation Module** performs a brutal, data-backed audit of the startup idea against real-time market conditions using expert frameworks.
    * **Benefit:** Validates problem-solution fit early, preventing years of wasted development effort.

### 4. 💬 The Need for Interactive Strategy
* **The Struggle:** Static reports provide data, but founders often have specific follow-up questions or need to stress-test assumptions against *live* market changes (e.g., "What did Competitor X release yesterday?").
* **The Solution:** The **RAG Research Chatbot (Research Lab)** offers an interactive "war room" where founders can chat with an AI that has real-time web access and deep domain knowledge.
    * **Benefit:** Turns a one-way report into a dynamic strategy session, simulating a conversation with a human expert who has instant access to the entire internet.

### 5. 🎲 Uncertainty in Fundraising Success
* **The Struggle:** Launching a crowdfunding or fundraising campaign is often a gamble with no visibility into potential outcomes.
* **The Solution:** The **ML Success Predictor** analyzes campaign parameters (goal, description, category) to predict the statistical probability of success.
    * **Benefit:** Allows founders to adjust their financial goals or marketing messaging to maximize their chances of funding.

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🚧 Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. 🏋️‍♂️ The Weight of AI: Deploying a "Heavy" Platform
**The Hurdle:**
Building a platform that runs multiple local ML models (BERT for embeddings, RoBERTa for sentiment, and custom classifiers) alongside a FastAPI server was a resource nightmare. Initially, the server would crash or time out because it tried to reload these heavy models for every single API request, leading to massive memory spikes and slow response times.

**The Solution:**
I restructured the backend architecture using **FastAPI's `lifespan` events**. Instead of loading models on-demand, I implemented a global model loader that initializes all heavy ML models (Sentiment, NER, and BERT) exactly *once* when the application starts.
* **Result:** This drastically reduced inference latency and stabilized memory usage, allowing the deployment to handle concurrent requests without crashing.

### 2. ⚡ Balancing RAG Speed vs. Quality Retrieval
**The Hurdle:**
The "Research Lab" needed to be smart enough to validate ideas against real-time market data but fast enough to feel like a conversation. A major bottleneck was the latency introduced by embedding generation and the sheer volume of data needed for the 7-domain analysis.

**The Solution:**
I implemented a three-pronged optimization strategy:
* **LRU Caching:** I used `@functools.lru_cache` for the embedding function. This allows the system to instantly recall vector embeddings for repeated text chunks without re-computing them, significantly speeding up the retrieval process.
* **Single-Shot "Mega-Prompting":** Instead of chaining 7 separate LLM calls for each domain (which would take minutes), I engineered a single, structured prompt that forces the LLM to output all 7 domains (Idea, Tech Stack, Competitors, etc.) in one go. This cut generation time by ~80%.
* **Hybrid Retrieval:** To ensure "good" retrieval, I didn't rely solely on static vectors. I built a hybrid system that combines **Pinecone** (for fast, indexed knowledge) with **SerpApi** (for live, fresh web data), giving the user the best of both worlds: speed and accuracy.

**Best Use of GitHub**

1. Robust Version Control: .gitignore files are employed at every level (root, backend, frontend) to maintain a clean and secure repository history by excluding sensitive or unnecessary files.

2. Clear Documentation: A root README.md file serves as the essential entry point, allowing developers to quickly understand the project's purpose and installation procedures.
 
3. Modular Architecture: The codebase is organized into distinct, logical directories (vc-copilot-backend and founders-fuel-ui), promoting clear separation of concerns and easier navigation.
 
4. Deployment Readiness: Configuration files such as vercel.json and Dockerfile demonstrate preparation for modern CI/CD pipelines, facilitating automated deployments and containerization.

**The problem it solves**

HIVEMIND is an intelligent, real-time anomaly detection system that monitors continuously changing data across multiple domains such as cryptocurrency markets, derivatives activity, weather metrics, and GitHub repository activity. Instead of relying on a single method, it uses **five specialized AI agents** (Statistical, Temporal, Correlation, Context, and OI Derivatives) to analyze data from different perspectives. Their combined findings are processed through a **consensus mechanism** that determines anomaly severity and confidence.

The system also generates **clear, human-readable explanations** using large language models and presents results through an **interactive dashboard** featuring real-time anomaly feeds, a knowledge graph of correlated events, system health displays, derivatives insights, and long-term statistical trends. Its asynchronous backend, WebSocket-based updates, and modular architecture make it **scalable, extensible, and adaptable** to new data sources and rule sets.

**Challenges we ran into**

## **Challenges Faced**

Developing HIVEMIND required solving several key challenges. The team needed to balance **sensitivity vs. false positives**, ensuring meaningful anomalies were detected without excessive noise. Handling **multiple real-time external APIs** demanded careful rate limiting, error tolerance, and asynchronous design for performance. Another major challenge was converting complex statistical outputs into **clear explanatory narratives**, requiring a reliable LLM fallback chain. Finally, designing a **coordinated multi-agent consensus** model and aligning different data domains into comparable structures required significant architectural iteration and testing.

### GitGenius

> From code chaos to clarity

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![axios](https://img.shields.io/badge/axios-333333?style=flat-square) ![Stripe API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Stripe%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Developers and teams often face a huge challenge when trying to make sense of large or unfamiliar GitHub repositories. Diving into a new repo can feel like navigating a labyrinth. Manually checking commits, tracing file changes, or deciphering what’s actually happening is:

⏳**Extremely time-consuming** — hours can slip away just trying to piece things together
🧠 **Mentally exhausting** — understanding the flow of changes and code logic is tough
🤯 **Overwhelming with multiple contributors** — when dozens of people are involved, it’s easy to get lost

And yet, there’s still no simple way to ask:

*"What exactly did this commit change?”*
*“Who’s been the most active contributor to this repo?”*
*“Give me a clear, bird’s-eye view of this entire repository.”*

It’s like trying to read an entire book by glancing at random pages.

So we developed, **Git-Genius** which is an AI-powered platform that helps you **analyze any GitHub repository instantly**.  
It gives you commit insights, summaries, and allows you to **chat with the repository** using natural language.

### 🔍 What it Does  
- 🧠 **Analyzes commits** — generates human-readable summaries of each commit.  
- 💬 **Chat with any repo** — ask questions like *“Explain this PR?”*, *“How does authentication work?”*, or *“Show files related to login flow.”*  
- 📊 **Commit insights** — visualize who contributed, when, and what changed the most.  
- 🪄 **AI-generated summaries** — get concise overviews of repos before cloning or contributing.  

Perfect for developers, reviewers, and hackathon teams who want to **understand codebases faster.**

---

## ⚙️ Key Features  

✅ **GitHub Repo Analysis**  
Just paste any GitHub repo URL — Git-Genius fetches commits, authors, and key metrics automatically.  

✅ **AI-Generated Commit Summaries**  
Each commit is summarized using LLMs for quick understanding.  

✅ **Chat with Repo**  
Ask natural language questions about the repository’s content and history.  

✅ **Interactive Dashboard**  
View commits, contributors, and repository activity in a clean UI.  

✅ **Seamless GitHub Integration**  
Works with public GitHub APIs — no extra configuration required.  

---

## 🧠 Example Use Cases  

- 🧩 **Developers** — Quickly grasp unfamiliar codebases before contributing.  
- 💼 **Project managers** — Track team contributions and project evolution.  
- 🧑‍🏫 **Educators** — Help students understand open-source repositories.  
- ⚡ **Hackathons** — Analyze project repos and showcase team activity transparently.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building **Git-Genius**, our team faced a few challenges along the way:  

### ⚙️ 1. Getting Data from GitHub  
GitHub limits how much data we can pull at once.  
For big repositories, it was tricky to fetch all commits and details without hitting those limits.  
We solved this by using smart request handling and caching using **Octokit**.  

### 🧠 2. Handling Big Repositories  
Large projects have thousands of files and commits.  
Creating AI embeddings for everything takes time and processing power.  
We fixed this by analyzing only the most important commits and storing results for reuse.  

### 💬 3. Making AI Understand Context  
When users ask questions like “How does login work?”, the AI needs to find the right code parts.  
We used **Gemini embeddings** to understand meaning and match questions with the correct code sections.  

### 🖥️ 4. Smooth and Fast Dashboard  
Showing lots of data, charts, and commits can slow down the app.  
We used **Next.js optimization**, lazy loading, and efficient components to make the UI fast.  

### 🔒 5. Security  
We didn’t want users to need tokens or logins for basic features.  
So Git-Genius works using **public GitHub APIs** without storing any private data.  

### 🧾 6. AI Summaries Changing  
AI can sometimes give slightly different answers for the same input.  
We used consistent prompts and templates to make summaries stable and clear.  

---

## 💡 Future Improvements  

- 📈 Add live visualizations for repo activity over time.  
- 🧠 Train better AI models for detailed code explanations.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

## 🔮 How We Use Gemini  

**Gemini** is the brain behind Git-Genius.  
It helps our app *understand* code and commits — not just read them.  

Here’s how we use it:  

- 🧠 **Embeddings:** Gemini turns code, commits, and text into special “vectors” — basically, numerical fingerprints that help the AI find meaning and connections.  
- 🔍 **Search & Chat:** When you ask a question like “How does authentication work?”, Gemini finds the most relevant parts of the code and explains them.  
- ⚡ **Context Understanding:** Instead of keyword matching, it understands what you *mean*, so you can chat naturally with any repository.  

In short — **Gemini makes Git-Genius smart.**  
It helps the platform turn complex codebases into clear, human-readable insights.

**The problem it solves**

# Sparrow — Your Voice Health Companion

**Sparrow** is designed to make health checking and voice care **simple, quick, and accessible** for everyone.

---

## 🌿 The Problem

Many people ignore early signs of throat or voice problems — such as **hoarseness**, **roughness**, or **strain** — because getting a medical check-up takes **time, money, and effort**.  
Visiting a specialist or doing regular tests isn’t always possible, especially for:

- People living in small towns  
- Individuals with busy schedules  

---

## 💡 The Solution

**Sparrow** solves this by allowing users to **record their voice** directly from their phone or computer.  
The system uses **artificial intelligence** to analyze the audio and check for signs of **possible voice or throat-related issues**.

✨ It’s completely **non-invasive** — no hospital visit or equipment required.

---

## 🤖 AI-Powered Assistant

Sparrow comes with a **friendly AI assistant** that:

- Explains diagnosis results in **clear, simple language**  
- Suggests **precautions** and **vocal care tips**  
- Guides users on **when to see a doctor** if needed  

---

## 🧘 Daily Care & Motivation

To encourage regular care, Sparrow includes:

- **Breathing and vocal exercises** for lung strength and voice clarity  
- **Daily progress tracking** and **streaks**  
- **Reward points** for consistency  

This makes health care **interactive, fun, and motivating** instead of purely medical.

---

## 💬 In Short

Sparrow turns a **complex and often ignored medical process** into a  
**friendly, engaging, and accessible experience** — helping people monitor and maintain their **voice health with ease**.

**Challenges we ran into**

# ⚙️ Challenges Faced During Sparrow’s Development

---

## 🎙️ Different Voice Qualities and Background Noise

Every user records their voice in a **different environment** — some in quiet places, others with **background noise or echoes**.  
Making the AI correctly analyze all these varied voice types was challenging.  

✅ **Solution:**  
We applied multiple **audio-cleaning** and **preprocessing techniques** to ensure that the voice analysis stayed **accurate and consistent**, regardless of recording conditions.

---

## 📊 Lack of Enough Data for Diseased Voices

We had many **normal voice samples** but very few with **actual vocal or throat diseases**.  
This imbalance made it hard for the model to learn effectively.  

✅ **Solution:**  
We used **SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique)** to create **synthetic diseased voice samples**, balancing the dataset and improving model performance.

---

## 💬 Designing Natural and Friendly Conversations

We wanted Sparrow’s AI assistant to sound **natural, clear, and kind**, not robotic or confusing.  

✅ **Solution:**  
We carefully designed the **conversation flow**, enabling the AI to:
- Understand user queries  
- Respond politely  
- Provide **simple and easy-to-understand** explanations about diagnoses and exercises  

---

## 📞 Implementing One-to-One AI Call Assistant

One of the most exciting yet complex features was the **real-time voice call assistant**.  

✅ **Implementation Details:**
- Used **Vapi API** for live call connections and user–assistant communication  
- Integrated **Groq’s LLaMA model** for transcript generation and real-time response processing  

⚠️ **Challenges:**
- Maintaining **low latency** for instant conversation feel  
- Ensuring **accurate transcription** and **response timing**  
- Managing **API costs**, since Vapi charges per call  

---

## 🔗 Integrating Multiple Systems Together

Sparrow includes many components:
- Voice Analysis Model (**VGGish + LSM**)  
- **Flask Backend**  
- **AI Chat Assistant**  
- **Exercise & Reward Tracker**  

✅ **Challenge:**  
Ensuring all these systems worked **seamlessly together** without lag or data mismatch required **extensive debugging and testing**.

---

## 🧘 Adding the Breathing Exercise and Reward System

We aimed to help users build **healthy vocal habits** through **daily breathing and vocal exercises**.  

✅ **Challenge:**  
Developing a smooth system where users can:
- Maintain **streaks**  
- Earn **points**  
- Track **daily progress**

We ensured accurate **data storage**, **streak logic**, and **reward distribution** for a motivating user experience.

---

## 🩺 Maintaining Accurate and Safe Responses

Since Sparrow deals with **health-related information**, accuracy and safety were critical.  

✅ **Solution:**  
We ensured that:
- The AI gives **useful, reliable suggestions**
- It always **reminds users to consult real doctors** for medical concerns  
This helps keep the system **ethical, safe, and user-trusted**.

---

**In summary**, each challenge made Sparrow stronger — transforming it into a reliable, empathetic, and intelligent voice health companion.

**Best Agentic AI**

# 🤖 Why We’re the Best Fit for AI Agentic

## 1. Personalized Learning Agent
Sparrow acts as an **AI communication coach** that adapts to each user’s tone, speech pattern, and confidence level — offering *human-like feedback* in real time.

## 2. Action-Oriented AI
Unlike passive chatbots, Sparrow **initiates tasks, tracks progress, and guides daily improvement**, making it an active agent, not just a responder.

## 3. Multimodal Intelligence
Integrating **voice analysis, text understanding, and progress analytics** allows Sparrow to function as a complete, context-aware AI companion.

## 4. Continuous Adaptation
Our AI learns with every conversation — evolving its guidance style and recommendations, much like a real human coach.

## 5. Emotional Intelligence
By focusing on *confidence, clarity,* and *self-expression,* Sparrow stands out as an agent that nurtures *emotional growth*, not just linguistic accuracy.

---

> “Sparrow isn’t just an AI — it’s an adaptive communication coach that learns, guides, and grows with you.”

**The problem it solves**

PROBLEM STATEMENT : The internet is full of information, but users face information overload and task inefficiency while performing multi-step online processes like software setup, form filling, or learning. Existing browsers and assistants fail to provide automated, context-aware, and goal-oriented support.

PROBLEM SOLVED :
1. Information Overload: Users waste time searching and verifying data.
2. Multi-step Tasks: Manual execution of repetitive tasks (e.g., installation).
3. Time Consumption: Each step (like searching, downloading, verifying) takes 
     effort.
4. Lack of Context: Normal browsers don’t provide related or prerequisite info
     automatically.
5. User Confusion: Beginners don’t know the correct sequence of steps (e.g., 
    installing compilers).
6. Distraction: Users get lost between irrelevant ads, blogs, and videos.
7. Fragmented Learning: No continuity between related information.
8. Error-Prone Actions: Users often install wrong versions or incomplete setups.
9. Manual Navigation Fatigue: Clicking through endless pages reduces 
    productivity.
10. Poor Knowledge Retention: Users learn tasks but forget supporting 
    information later.

SOLUTION :

1. Understands your goal/task.
2. Automatically executes or suggests the correct sequence of actions.
3. Displays a contextual sidebar with relevant explanations, tools, and updates.
4. Uses AI to predict the next logical step and prepare resources in advance.
5. Provides one-click automation for common web tasks like:
   # Installing software.
   #Opening correct documentation.
   # Fetching tutorials or videos.
   # Managing downloads or dependencies.

FUTURE SCOPE :

1. Plugin Ecosystem: Let developers publish “AI Workflows” or “Task Packs.”
2. AI Personal Assistant Mode: Works as a digital guide for installation, learning, 
    or job preparation.
3. Cross-browser Extension: Build as a Chrome/Edge plugin before a full 
    standalone browser.
4. Collaborative Mode: Multiple users can share automated workflows in real-time.
5. Offline Mode: Cache AI-generated info for offline use.
6. AI Workflow Training: Train AI on your browsing patterns for better  
    personalization.
7. Education Integration: Partner with learning platforms (Coursera, edX) to auto-
    setup environments.
8. Enterprise Version: For companies that want pre-configured setups for 
    employees.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Speed Optimization Issues

Challenge: The system’s speed dropped significantly due to multiple NLP and search engine calls running concurrently, causing performance lags.

Solution: We implemented progressive task loading — allowing subtasks to load in the browser immediately after completion instead of waiting for the entire process to finish.

Impact: This approach greatly improved response time and user experience by parallelizing data handling and reducing idle waiting.

2. API Timeout Problems

Challenge: Frequent API timeouts occurred when handling heavy data sessions, interrupting workflow and delaying execution.

Solution: We deployed dual Lambda containers — one dedicated to session creation and another focused on database population with the actual data.

Impact: This distributed approach enhanced reliability, prevented timeout failures, and ensured seamless system operation even under high loads.

**Best AWS Hack**

1. AWS Lambda (Serverless Compute):
We implemented a dual Lambda architecture to handle high-performance backend operations:

Lambda 1: Manages session creation and initialization.

Lambda 2: Handles data processing and database population.
This modular design provides auto-scaling, fault tolerance, and minimal latency.

2. Amazon Bedrock (Generative AI Integration):
To power the project’s AI reasoning, NLP processing, and content generation, we integrated Amazon Bedrock.

Provides secure access to foundation models (FMs) for NLP and text-based reasoning.

Enables custom model fine-tuning for domain-specific queries.

Reduces dependency on external APIs by keeping inference within AWS boundaries, ensuring low latency and data privacy.
This makes Bedrock the core intelligence layer of our system.

3. Amazon API Gateway:
Acts as the entry point for client requests, managing authentication, throttling, and timeout protection. It ensures smooth communication between the frontend, Lambda functions, and Bedrock APIs.

4. Amazon DynamoDB :
We use AWS-managed databases to store structured and semi-structured information.

DynamoDB: For real-time data retrieval.

RDS: For long-term relational data management.
This ensures data integrity, fast response, and automatic scaling.

5. AWS CloudWatch & IAM:

CloudWatch: Tracks the health and performance of Bedrock calls, Lambda execution times, and API metrics.

IAM: Manages fine-grained permissions, ensuring secure communication between all AWS components.

6. SQS service:

It allowed to communicate between both lambda containers securely and safely and only invoke second container when required letting us save compute time and cost

**Best Agentic AI**

Our project exemplifies Agentic AI principles by combining autonomous decision-making, intelligent task handling, and adaptive learning within a cloud-based system.

1. Autonomous Task Management:
The system independently handles multiple NLP and search tasks, deciding when to fetch data, process subtasks, and update the database without manual intervention.

2. Intelligent Workflow Orchestration:
By using a dual Lambda architecture and Amazon Bedrock, the AI agent prioritizes tasks, handles API timeouts, and manages data pipelines, ensuring smooth and self-regulated operations.

3. Context-Aware Reasoning:
Bedrock enables the AI to understand context, generate responses, and adapt to user queries, reflecting autonomous problem-solving abilities typical of agentic AI systems.

4. Scalable Decision Execution:
The integration of API Gateway and DynamoDB/RDS allows the agent to scale decisions, store knowledge, and maintain consistency across multiple sessions.

5. Monitoring & Self-Optimization:
With CloudWatch, the AI continuously monitors its performance, detects bottlenecks, and ensures self-improvement over time, a key feature of agentic AI.

**Open Innovation**

How Our Project Fits into Open Innovation

Our project aligns with the principles of Open Innovation by leveraging external resources, cloud-based AI services, and collaborative technologies to accelerate development and enhance capabilities.

1. Leveraging Cloud AI Services:
By integrating Amazon Bedrock, we use pre-built foundation models for natural language understanding and reasoning, allowing us to focus on innovation rather than building AI from scratch.

2. Modular and Extensible Architecture:
Using AWS Lambda, API Gateway, and DynamoDB, our system is highly modular, making it easy for external contributors or future teams to extend functionality or integrate new tools.

3. Collaboration and Knowledge Sharing:
Our approach enables multiple teams or developers to collaborate, test new features, and share improvements without disrupting the core system, reflecting the open innovation ethos.

4. Rapid Experimentation:
Cloud-based deployment allows us to quickly test ideas, iterate, and optimize workflows, accelerating the innovation cycle while maintaining scalability and reliability.

**What is your product’s unique value proposition?**

BORC’s unique value lies in its real-time, squad-based multiplayer system built entirely on decentralized wallet identities, removing traditional logins while ensuring secure, seamless play.
The alpha build validates this by demonstrating instant wallet-linked(will be basenames soon) matchmaking, synchronized gameplay, and peer-to-peer interaction through Colyseus networking.

**Who is your target customer?**

Our target customers are gamers on the BaseApp looking for fun, social experiences they can share with friends.

**Who are your closest competitors and how are you different?**

Closest Competitor: Slay by Farverse( https://slay.farverse.games/ ): a Web3 “slay-to-earn” game focused on individual performance and token-based rewards.

How We’re Different:
Our mini app focuses on team-based multiplayer gameplay inside the Base app, not just solo earning. Players squad up, complete missions, and compete on leaderboards for shared rewards; making it more social, cooperative, and replayable. Unlike Slay, which prioritizes token incentives, our approach builds community, retention, and fun-first experiences native to Base’s ecosystem.

To be frank the co-op multiplayer scene on the Base App is none existent and what we're building is in many ways incomparable with the existing apps.

**What is your distribution strategy and why?**

We’ll launch natively in the Base app, targeting active Base users through community channels like Farcaster and X. Leaderboards, rewards, and cross-project missions will drive viral, squad-based growth. This works because Base users already share and discover new mini apps socially; we’re building the one they’ll actually play together.

Trust through transparency as all commissions tracked and paid onchain

Before MarketBase: "I can tip creators and buy subscriptions, but I still shop on Amazon with my credit card"

With MarketBase: "I can buy those headphones directly with USDC from a Base App vendor, using Base Pay".

Why This Matters Now:

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges Encountered & Solutions
1. Deep Linking & Affiliate Attribution in Mini Apps
Challenge: Creating shareable affiliate links that work seamlessly within the Farcaster social graph proved complex. Standard web URLs don't maintain context when shared via compose casts, and we needed to attribute conversions back to specific Farcaster users (FIDs). 

Solution: Developed a dual approach system:

Created anonymous click tracking links that capture the referrer's FID from Farcaster context.

Built a database schema to track affiliate clicks → product views → conversions
Used Farcaste & The Base App compose cast action to pre-populate share links with affiliate parameters that link directly to the product in the miniapp.

Implemented a commission system that automatically attributes conversions when users with registered FIDs make purchases.

Learning: Mini app distribution requires rethinking traditional web analytics. Social graph attribution is more powerful than cookie-based tracking. The examples from the Base GitHub really helped with getting this to work. 

2. Database Architecture for Social Commerce

Challenge: Traditional e-commerce databases aren't designed for Farcaster-native affiliate systems. We needed to track:

Affiliate clicks from compose casts
FID-to-wallet associations
Commission calculations and payouts
Click to conversion attribution across sessions

Solution: Built a custom Supabase schema with four core tables:

affiliate_clicks: Captures FID, product, timestamp
affiliate_conversions: Links orders to original click events
orders: Includes farcaster_fid field for cross-referencing
Real-time 45-second polling for order updates to trigger affiliate attribution

Learning: Onchain-native commerce needs identity tied to wallets AND social identities (FIDs) to enable viral growth mechanics.

3. Testing Mini Apps Without Production Context
Challenge: The base.dev preview mode doesn't inject Farcaster context (FID, username, etc.), making it impossible to test core features like:

Affiliate link generation
User-specific recommendations
FID-based authentication flows
Social sharing functionality

Solution:

Used base.dev console input extensively for debugging context data structures
Built conditional rendering to detect when running in preview vs. production
Implemented robust fallbacks for missing context data
Heavy reliance on console logging for affiliate flow debugging

Workaround Needed: Eventually had to test many features directly in The Base App rather than preview, slowing iteration cycles.

Learning: Mini app development requires different testing strategies than traditional web apps. We need better local development tools that simulate full Base App context. That said, it is really useful to have console output in base.dev.

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem Parrot Solves**

You can go viral on social media, reach hundreds of thousands of people, and still make nothing. Ten thousand likes, a million impressions, and not a single cent in your pocket. That’s the strange truth of the internet today - ***attention doesn’t equal ownership.***

When you post on traditional social networks(X, Insta or Tiktok), your content lives on someone else’s platform, under their algorithm, inside their walls. Every time you go viral, the platform makes money from your reach, not you. You build their audience, feed their ads, and hope a small fraction of it trickles back your way. Your distribution isn’t yours. It’s rented.

**The Web3 Shift**

Web3 changes that by turning distribution into a market. Onchain platforms like Farcaster, Baseapp, and Zora make it possible to actually earn from your content.

- People can tip you directly, 
- Collect your post as an NFT, 
- or even trade a coin linked to it. 

Each post becomes its own little economy, something that can *live, move, and grow beyond one feed.*

In this new model, attention becomes an asset. You still create the same content, but instead of giving it away to a platform, you own it. You decide where it goes, how it’s monetized, and how it connects with your community.

**How Parrot Helps**

Parrot makes it effortless to earn from what you already post on traditional platforms while helping build the Internet’s Distribution Market.

- You simply **pick and cast** your favorite posts - Parrot sends them to Zora, Farcaster, or Baseapp instantly.
- Turn on **YOLO mode** to let it automatically post your new tweets or Instagram posts across web3 socials while you stay focused on creating.
- With **micropayments**, every post works on a pay-per-post model - you only pay for what you use. Post less, pay less. Post more, pay more.

Parrot quietly automates your distribution and helps your content start earning, wherever it flies.

**Challenges we ran into**

**API Costs and Workarounds**

At first, we planned to use X’s official API, but the paid plans were way too expensive for long-term use. We switched to a more affordable option on RapidAPI, which gave us access to tweets but didn’t support webhooks. That meant we couldn’t detect new tweets in real time.
To solve it, we built a cron job that runs every 10 minutes, fetching each user’s latest tweets and automatically cross-posting them to Farcaster and Baseapp.

**Formatting Tweets for Farcaster**

Tweets don’t map perfectly to Farcaster. Mentions, hashtags, and URLs all behave differently. So we built a reverse lookup system that checks whether a Twitter username is linked to a Farcaster account and automatically tags the right person.
For big accounts like Base, Coinbase, or Farcaster itself , which weren’t linked, we created a small local directory inside Parrot that keeps brand handles correctly mapped.

**Scaling Background Jobs**

As more users joined, our single cron job couldn’t keep up. It started hitting rate limits, timing out, and occasionally skipping users. We rebuilt the system into a batched and queued architecture, each user’s sync task now runs in smaller, parallel batches. This made syncing faster, safer, and scalable as we grew.

**Reconstructing Tweet Threads**

Thread handling turned out to be one of the hardest parts. The RapidAPI endpoint doesn’t return full threads, so Parrot reconstructs them manually. It follows each tweet’s ***in_reply_to_status_id*** backward until it finds the root, sorts everything in order, and then posts it cleanly to Farcaster.

**What is your product’s unique value proposition?**

Parrot stands out because it makes cross-posting and earning across web3 socials effortless and accessible to everyone.

First, the user experience is incredibly seamless. We built a mini-app directly on Farcaster and Baseapp where users can simply pick a post and share it or, if they prefer a fully hands-off experience, enable **YOLO mode**. YOLO mode automatically shares new posts across platforms without the need to manually select anything. The idea is to make distribution so simple that creators can focus purely on creating on their preferred social media like X or Instagram.

Second, Parrot uses a micropayments model instead of monthly subscriptions. Users pay only when they post - a true **pay-per-post** system. If you post five times, you might pay fifty cents, and that’s it. There are no flat $10 or $20 monthly fees, which makes it affordable, fair, and usage-based.

Finally, Parrot isn’t just about distribution - it’s about earning. Every post that travels through Parrot can generate rewards across web3 platforms. Whether it’s **tips, collectibles, or tokenized engagement**, users can actually make money while sharing content, not just generate impressions.

**Who is your target customer?**

Parrot is built for creators, anyone who regularly shares content online, from individual storytellers to brands building communities.

Our ideal users are people who already post on **Twitter, Instagram, TikTok, or Medium**, and want to extend their reach into web3 social platforms like **Farcaster, Zora, Paragraph or Baseapp** - without needing to learn new tools or workflows.

This includes:

- Individual creators who want to own their distribution and start earning directly from their content.
- Small and mid-sized creators who are priced out of expensive creator tools but still want professional-level reach.
- Communities and projects that already use social platforms to grow and want to plug into the onchain creator economy.

Through our testing on Farcaster, we’ve already seen strong engagement from this audience. Many early users are active on both traditional and onchain socials, they want a simple bridge that lets them keep creating where they’re comfortable while exploring new monetization opportunities in web3.

**Who are your closest competitors and how are you different?**

Yup.io is one of the closest competitor to us. While Yup.io tries to be an all-in-one platform with feeds, rewards, and analytics, Parrot focuses on one thing - seamless cross-posting from X to Farcaster or Baseapp

**Create Where You Are**
Most platforms make you leave your usual apps to post. With Parrot, you keep creating on Twitter, Instagram, or TikTok, and it automatically brings your content into web3, no new workflow needed.

**Native Experience**
Parrot reformats every post to look natural on Farcaster or Baseapp, cleaning up X links, tagging verified users, mapping brand accounts like Base or Coinbase, and preserving threads and media.

**Built Inside Farcaster**
Parrot runs natively in the Farcaster mini-app, detects linked Twitter accounts, fetches tweets, and auto-casts them through YOLO mode - no setup required.

Parrot gives creators the smoothest, most native, and effortless cross-posting experience on Farcaster or Baseapp.

**What is your distribution strategy and why?**

Parrot’s growth so far has been organic and community-driven. We’ve onboarded 100+ users primarily through word of mouth - creators discovering the product, using it, and sharing it with others. That organic momentum has validated that people see real value in what we’re building.

Going forward, our distribution strategy focuses on reward-driven virality and in-product growth loops:

**Weekly Engagement Pool**
Each week, top-performing posts shared through Parrot will earn rewards. These rewards will be funded through Parrot’s usage fees and, later, our native token. This creates a direct incentive for creators to use Parrot more often and make their content perform better.

**Referral and Share-to-Earn Credits**
Users who share about Parrot on social platforms will earn credits they can use to post for free. This encourages creators to spread the word while giving them tangible value in return.

**Built-In Product Discovery**
Every post shared through Parrot on Farcaster automatically includes a small “from parrotapp” tag. Anyone can click it to learn more and start using Parrot themselves - turning every user’s post into a lightweight marketing channel.

Together, these loops make Parrot’s distribution self-sustaining. As more creators use Parrot to earn, they naturally help bring in new users, driving growth from within the product itself.
