> Teach what you know. Learn what you want

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Modern learning platforms are largely passive and content-driven, focusing more on watching courses than applying skills. Learners often study in isolation, struggle to find collaborators for real-world projects, and lack reliable ways to prove their practical abilities beyond generic certificates.

### Key Challenges
- Limited **hands-on and project-based learning**
- Poor **peer-to-peer knowledge sharing**
- Difficulty in **finding skilled collaborators**
- Weak **skill validation** beyond certificates
- Lack of **instant guidance** when learners get stuck
- Fragmented tools for learning, collaboration, and progress tracking

---

## How SkillDOM Is Used

SkillDOM is a peer-to-peer learning and collaboration platform where users actively learn, teach, and build together. It brings courses, projects, and community interaction into a single space.

Users can:
- Enroll in community-created courses or teach their own skills
- Collaborate with peers on real-world projects through a collaboration hub
- Find project partners based on complementary skills
- Interact directly with creators and learners without institutional gatekeeping

An integrated AI assistant (Skill SOS) provides instant, context-aware help whenever users are stuck, acting as a 24/7 learning companion.

---

## How SkillDOM Makes Learning Easier and More Effective

SkillDOM focuses on **learning by doing**, reducing friction and increasing engagement.

### What Makes It Effective
- Combines **courses + projects**, so skills are applied immediately
- Provides **AI-powered, on-demand support** instead of delayed forums or emails
- Uses **skill-based profiles and recommendations** to personalize learning paths
- Encourages collaboration instead of isolated learning

To promote active participation, SkillDOM introduces **Skill Value Coins (SVC)**. Users earn SVC by completing courses, contributing to projects, and engaging with the community, and can use them to unlock or trade courses—shifting value from payment to participation.

Course quality is reinforced through **surge-based pricing**, where popular and high-impact courses naturally gain more value, rewarding quality creators and relevant content.

---

## What Makes SkillDOM Different

SkillDOM stands apart by integrating learning, collaboration, incentives, and intelligence into one ecosystem.

### Core Differentiators
- **AI-powered learning assistance (Skill SOS)** for instant, personalized help
- **Collaboration hub** for real-world, skill-based project work
- **Peer-driven education** where anyone can teach or learn
- **AI-based skill verification** through project contributions and activity
- **Incentive-driven ecosystem** using SVC instead of purely paywalled access

SkillDOM transforms passive, fragmented learning into a **collaborative, credible, and outcome-driven experience**, where skills are built, validated, and shared through real participation.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

### Balancing Scope in Limited Time
We wanted to build AI assistance, peer-to-peer courses, collaboration, and messaging within a short hackathon window. The challenge was prioritization. We solved this by focusing on the core value—**learning through collaboration with AI support**—and deferring non-essential features.

### Integrating Multiple Services
SkillDOM uses Firebase, Supabase, and Gemini AI together. Each service has its own APIs and data models, which made integration challenging. We overcame this through iterative testing and clear separation of responsibilities between services.

### Authentication Flow Complexity
Managing a **dual authentication setup** was one of the biggest hurdles:
- Firebase Auth for user authentication  
- Supabase for user profiles and application data  

Keeping sessions in sync and avoiding duplicated user data required careful mapping, with Firebase acting as the source of truth.

---

## What We Learned

- Prioritizing core features is crucial in a hackathon.
- Early integration testing saves time later.
- AI features need iteration to feel truly useful.
- Clear team coordination helps manage complexity under pressure.

### LunarVision

> Spotting Moon Boulders with Smart Eyes

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Computer Vision](https://img.shields.io/badge/Computer%20Vision-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🌓 What Problem LunarVision Solves

LunarVision is an AI-powered tool built to automatically detect and analyze geological hazards on the Moon — like landslides and scattered boulders — using high-resolution images from India’s Chandrayaan-1 and Chandrayaan-2 missions.

🧠 The Core Challenge

Planetary scientists and mission planners often need to study lunar surface images to understand terrain risks (e.g., steep slopes, large rocks, unstable regions). Traditionally, this is:

manual or semi-manual, meaning experts have to look through tons of images with the naked eye or simple tools, or

slow and subjective, because it depends on human interpretation.

That’s tedious and not very scalable — especially when dealing with huge datasets from orbiters or planning future landings. LunarVision changes that.

💡 How LunarVision Helps

LunarVision makes lunar terrain analysis faster, easier, and more reliable by applying smart computer vision and AI.

🚀 Key Benefits
🛰️ 1. Instant Automated Detection

Instead of a researcher staring at hundreds of raw images, LunarVision’s AI quickly finds:
- landslides
- boulders
- possibly other terrain anomalies
…with bounding boxes and measurements, saving hours of manual work.

🧭 2. Better Risk Awareness

It doesn’t just find objects — it helps understand where the terrain might be dangerous or unstable by analyzing patterns, slopes, and spatial features. That’s huge for:
- mission safety planning (e.g., rover routes)
- deciding landing zones
- future lunar base scouting

📊 3. Quantitative Insight

Rather than just marking a picture, LunarVision gives real numbers like:
- counts of rocks per region
- average sizes of boulders
- rough risk or slope metrics
- So scientists don’t just see where things are — they see what’s going on.

🔁 4. Scalable and Repeatable

This system can run on any new lunar image set — polar regions, crater floors, or highlands — making it useful at scale rather than one photo at a time.

🧑‍🔬 Who Can Use It

LunarVision isn’t just for scientists — it opens up ways for a bunch of folks to use space data:

✨ Planetary geologists — quickly study patterns of landslides and rock fields.
✨ Space mission planners — make safer choices for landers/rovers.
✨ Educators and students — explore moon data with AI tools.
✨ Developers and researchers — build on top of an open pipeline for other celestial bodies too.

🧠 In a Nutshell

Without LunarVision:
Researchers spend days manually scanning images → prone to error → slow insight.

With LunarVision:
AI does the heavy lifting → fast detection, deep analysis, numbers you can trust → safer, smarter lunar exploration.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building LunarVision was exciting, but definitely not smooth sailing. A few key challenges pushed me to think harder and learn more deeply.

🛰️ 1. Low Contrast & Noisy Lunar Images

The problem:

1. Lunar surface images don’t behave like normal photos.
2. Very low contrast 
3. Extreme lighting conditions
4. Shadows that look like craters or landslides

This confused the model — it sometimes detected nothing or flagged shadows as objects.

How we fixed it:

- Applied image preprocessing (contrast enhancement, normalization)
- Experimented with different filters to make edges and terrain features clearer
- Carefully chose image samples that represented different lighting conditions

✅ Result: The model became far more stable and consistent.

🧠 2. False Positives in Boulder Detection

The problem:
Small craters and rough textures often got misclassified as boulders.
The model basically said: “rock… rock everywhere.”

How we fixed it:
- Tuned confidence thresholds to reduce over-detection
- Adjusted bounding-box filtering based on size and shape
- Manually reviewed outputs to understand where the model was getting confused

✅ Result: Cleaner detections with fewer “ghost rocks.”

🧪 3. Limited Labeled Data

The problem:
High-quality, labeled lunar datasets are rare. Training data was limited and uneven.

How we fixed it:
- Used data augmentation (rotation, flipping, scaling)
- Reused pretrained weights instead of training from scratch
- Focused on learning patterns rather than brute-forcing accuracy

✅ Result: Better generalization without needing massive datasets.

⚙️ 4. Balancing Accuracy vs Performance

The problem:
Higher accuracy models were slow and heavy.
Lighter models were fast but less reliable.

How we fixed it:
- Tested multiple configurations
- Chose a balanced setup that gives reasonable accuracy without killing performance
- Optimized inference rather than chasing perfect scores

✅ Result: A practical model that works well in real scenarios.

🧩 5. Debugging “Why Is This Not Working?” Moments

The problem:
Some detections just… didn’t make sense.
No errors. No crashes. Just wrong results.

How we fixed it:
- Visualized intermediate outputs (feature maps, predictions)
- Printed logs instead of guessing
- Stepped back and re-read my own code (painful but effective 😅)

✅ Result: Fewer silent bugs and a much better understanding of the pipeline.

🌱 What I Learned

This project taught me that:

- Real-world data is messy
- AI models need guidance, not just training
- Debugging is a skill, not a failure
- Every hurdle made LunarVision stronger — and made me a better developer.

**Duality AI — Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation**

LunarVision focuses on detecting hazardous lunar surface features such as boulders and landslides from Chandrayaan imagery. To strengthen this capability, I explored and proposed the integration of off-road semantic segmentation techniques inspired by Duality AI.

🔍 Why Off-Road Semantic Segmentation?

The Moon is essentially the ultimate off-road environment:

- No roads or structured paths
- Highly unstructured terrain
- Extreme lighting, shadows, and slopes

Duality AI’s off-road segmentation approach is designed to classify terrain types in harsh, unstructured environments, making it a strong conceptual fit for lunar surface analysis.

⚙️ How I Used / Proposed It in My Project
🧪 Conceptual Integration

While LunarVision currently focuses on object detection, I proposed extending the pipeline with semantic segmentation to classify each pixel of the lunar surface into categories such as:

- Stable terrain
- Boulder-dense regions
- Landslide-prone slopes
- Rough vs smooth surface areas

This shifts the system from “what objects exist?” to “what kind of terrain is this?”

🛰️ Synthetic Data Inspiration

One major challenge in lunar AI projects is the lack of labeled data. Duality AI’s approach of using synthetic environments inspired a future extension where:

- Simulated lunar terrains could be generated
- Controlled lighting, slope, and surface roughness could be varied
- Segmentation models could be trained safely before real deployment

This would dramatically reduce dependence on scarce real lunar annotations.

🚀 Future Use in LunarVision
🌕 Safer Landing Zone Identification

Semantic segmentation could label:

- Flat, stable regions → safe for landing
- Rocky or sloped regions → high risk

This makes LunarVision useful not just for analysis, but for mission planning.

🤖 Autonomous Rover Navigation

By combining:

- Object detection (boulders, hazards)
- Semantic segmentation (terrain type)

LunarVision could guide rover path planning by avoiding:

- Loose regolith
- Steep slopes
- Boulder clusters

This directly improves autonomy and safety.

🔁 Generalization to Other Planets

The same off-road segmentation logic can be reused for:

- Mars
- Asteroids
- Other planetary bodies

Making LunarVision a scalable planetary vision framework, not just a Moon-specific tool.

🌱 In Simple Words

Before: LunarVision sees objects

With Duality-inspired segmentation: LunarVision understands the terrain itself

That’s the difference between looking at the Moon and understanding how to move on it.

> Remedies at home

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Spring Boot](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spring%20Boot-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

People today don’t think twice before taking medicines for fever, headache, stomach pain, cold, cough, acidity, or body pain. They go to a medical store, describe symptoms, and consume whatever is given. Most of these medicines are strong chemical drugs that are meant to be taken only under medical supervision. Over time this damages the liver and kidneys, weakens natural immunity, increases antibiotic resistance, and hides serious diseases until they become dangerous.

At the same time, India has one of the richest traditional medical systems in the world, but it is slowly being forgotten. Simple and safe remedies from Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, and Sowa-Rigpa that were once used for everyday health problems are now replaced by quick chemical solutions. People no longer know what is safe, what to avoid, or when a condition is actually serious.

This project solves that gap.
It gives people a responsible and safe way to handle common health problems by:

Encouraging traditional and preventive care for mild conditions

Educating users about precautions and lifestyle habits

Warning against unnecessary use of strong medicines

Helping people understand when a doctor is truly needed

It is not trying to cure diseases or replace hospitals.
It is trying to stop careless medicine use, revive forgotten traditional knowledge, and make people think before consuming harmful drugs for small problems.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was finding reliable and structured traditional medicine data. Most knowledge from Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, and Sowa-Rigpa exists in books, ancient texts, or unorganized sources, not in clean digital datasets. Converting this into a usable and consistent format was difficult and time-consuming.

Integrating multiple medical systems was challenging. Each system has different terminology, treatment philosophy, and diagnostic approach. Presenting them in a single structured format required careful design.

**The problem it solves**

Our proposed academic search engine solves this problem by providing a single, centralized platform where all college-related academic resources are collected, indexed, and updated in real time. Instead of searching through multiple portals, emails, or messaging groups, students and faculty can access notes, syllabi, announcements, and recently published research papers through one powerful search interface.

The system uses intelligent indexing and filtering to organize content by course, department, document type, and date, making information retrieval fast and precise. Real-time updates ensure that users always receive the latest academic materials without delay. Faculty and administrators can easily upload or approve resources, maintaining content authenticity and relevance. By reducing information fragmentation and manual effort, the platform saves time, improves academic collaboration, and enhances research visibility within the institution. Overall, it creates a more efficient, accessible, and digitally connected academic ecosystem for the college.

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/d4e3bbcc91554e00a8e66b85fd94c6ae/05a633c8-e6ce-478c-83f2-eff64e44647d.png)

(1) **The Problem It Solves:**

Students entering 11th standard often struggle to choose the right academic group such as Bio-Maths , Computer Science , Commerce, or Arts .At this stage 

1. - Many students select a group **based on marks , peer pressure** or parental expectations.

2. - They lack clarity about their interests , aptitude and strengths

3. - They do  not understand how a chosen group affects future career opportunities
 
4. - Wrong group selection leads to stress, poor performance and limited options in 12th and beyond.

(2) **What People Can Use It For**

This project acts a a guided decision making platform for students in **11th and 12th standard**

(1) **- For 11th Standard Students**

1.  Take an interest -and **aptitude based quiz**
2.  Get personalized group recommendations (Bio-Maths, Computer-science, Commerce, Arts)
3.  Understand why a particular group suits them 
4.  **Make a confident** and informed group selection

(2)**- For 12th Standard Students**

1.  Explore career opportunities available from their chosen group**(Through career road map)**
2.  Learn about degree courses ,entrance exams and skill paths 
3.  Discover non-traditional and emerging career options
4.  **Plan their next steps after school**


(3) **Easier & Safer**

*Easier:*

- Simplifies group selection and degree selection using a structured quiz and career road map instead of guesswork
- Saves time compared to random internet searches 
- Also **get notifiedr** about their selected group and selected degree **through notifications it help them knowing current trends of their career.**

*Safer:*

- Reduces the risk of choosing an unsuitable academic group
- Helps students **make decisions before it's too late to change**

**Challenges we ran into**

******Collecting the right Quiz Data:******

       One of the biggest challenges in this project was collecting accurate and meaningful data for the quiz , since the quiz plays crucial role in deciding a student's academic group and future career direction

**Designing Questions that truly reflect a student's:**

1.  Interests
2.  Aptitude
3.  Strengths

Without being biased toward that truly marks or popular choices was difficult.

**Why this was Challenging?**

1. Career decisions cannot be based on random or generic questions
2. Poorly framed questions can lead to **wrong group recommendations**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/d4e3bbcc91554e00a8e66b85fd94c6ae/610a30c4-9dd9-43c0-a523-bcb7bb4a66bc.png)

**How I Overcame It?**

- Researching *existing aptitude tests and career guidance models*
- Studied school subjects requirements for Bio-Maths , Computer Sceince , Commerce and Arts
- Designed questions based on real  life preferences and problem-solving scenarios instead of direct career questions
- Iteratively tested the quiz with sample student responses and refined unclera quetions
- Balanced the quiz to measure interest ,logical thinking ,creativity and analytical ability

**This process helped me create a quiz is more reliable , student-friendly , and aligned with real career pathways.**

**AOPS**

This project fits into the AOPS track by helping students make informed academic and career decisions using a structured, quiz-based approach.

It analyzes students’ interests and aptitude to guide 11th standard students in choosing the right academic group, and helps 12th standard students explore clear career pathways from their chosen group.

The solution focuses on problem-solving, decision support, and improving outcomes in education through a simple and accessible platform.

Guess The Number is an interactive web-based game built using Python and Streamlit. The player selects a difficulty level (Easy, Medium, or Hard) and tries to guess a randomly generated number within a limited number of attempts.

The game provides instant feedback (higher or lower hints), tracks remaining attempts, and includes a fun car race animation and score system when the player wins. Session state is used to manage game progress smoothly.

### SignFlow
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/signflow-82c4) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/KDsyd7BzeiA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> translating hands into voices

![Visual Studio Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Visual%20Studio%20Code-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Unity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Unity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kivy](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kivy-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

There are many deaf people around the **world** who find it hard to **understand or talk to others**, especially when it comes to things like TV shows, speeches, or normal conversations. Most people don’t know sign language, which makes communication even harder.

To help with this, I made **an app that can change spoken language into sign language and also sign language into text**. This makes it easy for deaf and hearing people to talk and understand each other without needing anyone in between.

The app makes communication **simple and clear**. It helps deaf people understand what others are saying and also helps others learn how to communicate with them. The main aim is to make talking and understanding easier for everyone using technology.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was understanding sign language itself. Sign language is not the same everywhere and Indian Sign Language has its own rules and signs. Finding correct and trusted learning resources took a lot of time.

Another major challenge was training the machine learning model. At first the model was not accurate. It confused similar hand signs especially when lighting was bad or the camera angle was wrong. I had to adjust the dataset and test the model again and again to improve accuracy.

Camera detection issues were also a problem. Sometimes the hand was not detected properly because of background noise skin color variations or fast hand movements. Using MediaPipe and OpenCV helped but tuning them correctly was difficult.

Creating sign animations in Unity was another challenge. Making the hand movements look natural and matching them correctly with words required patience and multiple corrections.

There were also technical issues like bugs errors crashes and performance problems when combining Python and Unity. Making both parts work smoothly together took a lot of debugging and testing.

Lastly lack of real-world testing was a challenge. Since not many people around me use sign language daily it was difficult to test the app with real deaf users at every stage. Visiting Sanjay School was helpful, but more testing is still needed.

**AOPS**

My project fits the AOPS track because it uses AI technology to assist deaf and mute individuals by breaking communication barriers. It is accessible affordable and designed for real social impact benefiting millions of people.

### Neural Architect
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/neural-architect-29e1) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Out%20Of%20Context'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://out-of-context-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The Blueprint of Brilliance

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Neural Architect solves the problem of "Cognitive Fragmentation" faced by engineering students, where scattered notes, deadlines, and resources lead to overwhelm and burnout. It replaces disconnected apps (like generic to-do lists and folder systems) with a unified "Second Brain" designed specifically for the academic lifecycle.
Instead of just listing tasks, it uses a Priority Engine to calculate exactly what to study next based on difficulty and urgency, eliminating decision paralysis. It organizes content by "Nodes" (concepts) rather than just dates, turning static notes into an interconnected lattice of knowledge. Ultimately, it transforms the chaos of engineering education into a structured, navigable system, allowing students to architect their intellect rather than just survive the semester.

**Challenges we ran into**

Our biggest technical hurdle was synchronizing the complex logic of the backend Priority Engine with the frontend's interactive visualization. We faced significant data mismatches where the calculated 'urgency' scores failed to update the visual lattice nodes in real-time, causing the graph to break. Debugging these asynchronous API calls was difficult, as we had to restructure our response schemas to ensure the 'Second Brain' state remained consistent across the user interface."

Team **Error:404** -- Darshil Shah, Varshil Patel, Roshan Shinde, Dhyan Patel

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sara-the-ai-scheduling-agent-3475) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/promathe/devfest-sara-scheduler) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Wv-pZYkqq2I) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Devfest%205.0%20Goa-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devfest5goa.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Your time, optimized.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OAuth](https://img.shields.io/badge/OAuth-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Calendar API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Calendar%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Lang graph](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lang%20graph-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1)Turns plain English requests into real calendar actions (schedule, search, delete, shift).

2)Finds free slots and books events without overlaps.

3)Saves you from manual calendar juggling by doing the planning automatically.

4)Handles quick changes (like shifting the rest of today) instead of you moving things one by one.

5)Gives you a single chat-style way to work with Google Calendar.

**Challenges we ran into**

1)CORS headaches between the frontend and FastAPI (browser blocks calls unless CORS is set up right).

2)Parsing issues: pulling clean tool-call JSON from the model output and handling malformed/partial args.

3)Missing details in user requests (duration, deadline, flexibility), so we need safe defaults or quick clarifying questions.

4)OAuth/token failures (Google access token missing/expired) → Calendar API calls fail.

5)Time zone + datetime formatting bugs (ISO formatting, local vs UTC, offsets).

6)Duplicate events / partial writes if the agent retries or the user reruns the same request without idempotency.

7)Calendar race conditions (free slot changes between “check availability” and “book event”).

8)Tool-call brittleness (wrong tool name/params) causing the agent to do nothing or fail scheduling.

9)OAuth redirect failures.

**AI**

This project is a take on the AI-Powered Personal Planning & Scheduling Agent. 
This project leverages a LLM within a ReAct architecture, transforming natural language into executable actions. Instead of static scripts, the AI autonomously analyzes user intent, manages context history, and decides which Python functions to trigger for real-time scheduling. 
By using tool calling, the system bridges the gap between generative text and the Google Calendar API, allowing it to read schedules and write events. 
Furthermore, embedded AI guardrails dynamically enforce human-centric constraints, such as burnout prevention limits, ensuring the agent acts as a considerate partner rather than just a command executor.

> A Collaborative Whiteboard

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Working together visually is still harder than it should be. Most teams either rely on heavy whiteboard tools packed with features they never use, or fall back to screen sharing and chat, which kills real collaboration. Lag, sync issues, confusing permissions, and cluttered interfaces slow people down when they just want to think together.

Notate exists to remove that friction.

---

## What People Can Use Notate For

### Brainstorming Without Friction
Notate lets teams sketch ideas, draw flows, and write notes together in real time. Everyone sees changes instantly, so conversations stay natural instead of turning into “wait, can you see this now?” moments.

### Remote Meetings With a Shared Visual Space
Instead of juggling screen sharing and slides, teams can use Notate as a shared canvas during meetings. It works well for explaining concepts, planning tasks, or walking through ideas visually.

### Collaborative Note-Taking
Multiple people can add notes, annotations, and quick sketches in the same space. This makes it easier to capture ideas collectively rather than relying on one person to write everything down.

### Quick Planning and Problem Solving
Notate is useful for rough planning, system diagrams, flowcharts, and early-stage designs where speed matters more than polish. You open a room, start drawing, and get to work.

### Teaching and Peer Learning
Students, mentors, and study groups can use Notate to explain problems visually. Drawing alongside text helps clarify ideas that are hard to explain with words alone.

---

## Why It Makes Things Easier

- No heavy setup or complex permissions
- Everyone stays in sync with a single shared state
- Real-time updates with low latency
- Clean interface that stays out of the way
- Focused on collaboration, not feature overload

Notate is meant to feel simple and reliable. You spend your time thinking, explaining, and collaborating.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

Building Notate wasn’t smooth sailing the whole way. A few problems looked small on the surface but turned out to be tough nuts to crack.

---

### Real-Time Performance Under Concurrent Drawing

Freehand drawing generates a lot of updates very quickly. Sending every tiny movement without care caused performance drops and visible lag when multiple users drew at once.

**What went wrong:**  
High-frequency updates flooded the network and caused unnecessary re-renders.

**How I fixed it:**  
I optimized how drawing data is batched and transmitted, reducing update frequency without sacrificing visual smoothness. This significantly improved performance while keeping the drawing experience responsive.

---

### Text Rendering and Resizing Issues

Handling text inside a resizable canvas turned out to be trickier than expected.

**What went wrong:**  
Text would overflow, resize unpredictably, or feel constrained when users tried to expand the text box.

**How I fixed it:**  
I decoupled text rendering from automatic size constraints and allowed the container to grow freely while keeping font scaling predictable. This gave users more control and made text behave in an intuitive way.

---

### Authentication vs Collaboration Flow

Balancing authentication with quick collaboration was another hurdle.

**What went wrong:**  
Strict auth checks initially interrupted the flow when users tried to join rooms quickly.

**How I fixed it:**  
I simplified the entry flow while still keeping authentication intact, making sure users could join sessions smoothly without unnecessary redirects or blocking states.

---

### Debugging Real-Time Bugs

Real-time bugs are hard to reproduce because they depend on timing, order, and multiple users acting at once.

**What went wrong:**  
Some issues only appeared when testing with multiple browsers or devices simultaneously.

**How I fixed it:**  
I tested aggressively using multiple sessions, logged state transitions carefully, and fixed issues at the data-model level instead of applying surface-level patches.

---

## What I Learned

- Real-time collaboration exposes problems that don’t show up in single-user apps
- Performance issues often come from “small” details repeated many times, like in the textbox problem I have listed above.
- Simple tools require more discipline, not less. Like it took really long time to set up the sign-in screen because a very simple bug caused it to not show up on the browser.

These challenges shaped Notate into a more stable and reliable collaborative tool.

**Software Development**

## How This Project Fits the Software Development Track

Notate fits naturally into the software development track because it focuses on solving a real, practical problem using solid engineering principles.

It reflects full-stack development in practice, combining frontend design, backend logic, real-time communication, and authentication into a working system. The decisions made while building Notate mirror the kind of trade-offs developers face in real-world applications, making it a strong representation of applied software engineering.

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem InkSync Solves**

*Real-World Use Cases*

Collaborative Teams & Brainstorming
Teams can draw and work together on a shared whiteboard in real-time, no matter where they're located. No more lost ideas on physical whiteboards that get erased at the end of the meeting.

Real-Time Chat with Collaborators
Alongside the shared canvas, participants can communicate using a built-in real-time chat. This allows teams to discuss ideas, clarify drawings, and coordinate actions without switching tools, keeping all collaboration—visual and conversational—in one place.

Documentation & Record Keeping
Whiteboard sessions are automatically captured and can be downloaded as PDF/Image files. Keep permanent records of your brainstorming sessions, technical designs, and planning discussions without manual transcription.

Knowledge Transfer & Onboarding
New team members can review previous whiteboard sessions to understand past decisions, architectures, and project evolution. Visual explanations are preserved and searchable.

Design & Architecture Planning
Designers and engineers can sketch diagrams, flowcharts, and system architectures on a digital whiteboard. The system automatically extracts and describes what was drawn, making it easy to reference later.

Meeting Notes Without the Hassle
Instead of someone furiously typing notes while others draw, the entire session is automatically captured. Meeting participants can focus on collaboration, not documentation.

Remote-First Teams
Eliminates the whiteboard gap for distributed teams. Everyone gets a digital equivalent that's shareable, searchable, and permanent—not locked on a physical board in one office.

Quick Problem-Solving Sessions
Sketch out ideas, workflows, or solutions instantly and get structured documentation automatically. Share solutions with team members who couldn't attend the session.

Accessibility & Searchability
Drawing content is automatically analyzed and extracted, making whiteboard sessions discoverable and shareable across your organization.

The Bottom Line: InkSync turns fleeting whiteboard moments into permanent, shareable, and searchable collaborative assets.

**Software Development**

What we built

InkSync is a real-time collaborative whiteboard that allows multiple users to draw, write, and brainstorm together inside shared rooms. A user creates a room, shares the link, and everyone joins the same live canvas instantly — no setup, no reloads, no friction.

The core goal was to build a fast, reliable, and distraction-free collaboration tool that feels instant and intuitive.

How it works

Each whiteboard session runs inside a room identified by a unique ID.
When users join a room, they connect via WebSockets and subscribe to a single shared canvas state.

Every action — drawing a stroke, adding text, or erasing — is transmitted in real time to all connected clients, ensuring everyone always sees the same board.

Key features

- Real-time room creation and joining via shareable links

- Live drawing, text, and erasing with instant synchronization

- Optional live cursor visibility for better collaboration awareness

- Host and participant roles to keep sessions structured

- Automatic state sync for late joiners (no blank canvas)

- Clean, modern, and fully responsive UI


Technical highlights

- Built using WebSockets (Socket.io) for true real-time communication
- Centralized backend room manager maintaining consistent canvas state
- Efficient stroke batching to reduce network overhead
- Client-side canvas rendering for immediate visual feedback
- Low-latency updates tested with multiple concurrent users

Why this fits the Software Development track

- InkSync demonstrates strong software engineering fundamentals:
- Real-time system design
- State synchronization across multiple clients
- Scalable frontend–backend architecture
- Clean, modular, and maintainable code
- The project prioritizes correctness, performance, and simplicity over feature bloat.
- 

What makes it stand out

- InkSync removes friction from collaboration:
- One room, one shared canvas
- Instant join through a link
- Predictable roles
- Real-time sync that simply works
- Instead of adding complexity, the focus was on making collaboration feel natural and immediate.

## The Problem It Solves
Citizens deal with fragmented, confusing civic systems. Safety, reporting issues, accessing schemes, avoiding scams, managing documents, and paying utilities all live in separate portals, leading to time loss, confusion, and missed benefits.

This app brings these together into a **single, agentic, citizen-first platform** that actively guides users instead of making them figure things out.

---

## What People Can Use It For

### Smart Civic Issue Reporting
- Camera-first reporting for civic issues such as potholes, garbage, and streetlights  
- Automatic capture of location and time  
- Heatmaps to visualize issue hotspots and recurring problem areas  
- Duplicate detection and transparent issue status tracking  

---

### Personal and Child Safety
- Safety Check-In that alerts trusted contacts only if the user does not check in on time  
- Child safety support with guardian notifications  
- Safe shelter locator for emergencies  
- No continuous tracking or invasive monitoring  

---

### Agentic AI (Natural-Language Task Automation)
- Users can **simply describe what they want to do in natural language**
  - e.g., “Report a pothole near my house”
  - “Find schemes I’m eligible for after retirement”
  - “Help me stay safe until I reach home”
- The agent **automatically navigates the app**, fills steps, and completes flows on the user’s behalf  
- Eliminates the need to understand menus, forms, or app structure  
- Especially useful for elderly, first-time, and non-tech users  

---

### Government Schemes and Benefits
- Eligibility-based scheme discovery  
- Life-event-based scheme recommendations (education, childbirth, retirement, job loss, etc.)  
- Step-by-step application guidance, document checklists, and status tracking  

---

### Secure Document Storage and Smart Recommendations
- Safe storage for important personal documents  
- Context-aware recommendations on:
  - which documents are required for a scheme or service  
  - what documents are missing or expiring  
- Reduces failed applications and repeat office visits  

---

### Digital Safety Tools for Modern Scams
- Tools to understand and respond to modern digital scams such as OTP fraud, fake links, and impersonation  
- Clear guidance on what to do immediately after a scam  

---

### Everyday Civic Utilities
- Centralized access to utility bill and local tax payments (demo/conceptual)  
- Reduced need to navigate multiple disconnected portals  

---

## In One Line

A citizen-first civic platform that combines reporting, safety, and agentic AI to help people complete government-related tasks using simple natural language.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

### Blockchain-Based Decentralized Reporting (Partially Implemented)
We explored integrating a **blockchain-based, decentralized layer** for civic issue reports to ensure immutability and prevent tampering. The idea was to anchor reports on-chain so that once submitted, they could not be silently altered or deleted.

While we successfully implemented a working prototype of this system, we could not integrate it into the deployed version due to **time constraints and deployment complexity**. We consciously chose to prioritize a stable, usable core platform over shipping an incomplete or fragile integration.

---

### Enhancing Child Safety with Automatic Audio Recording
We also planned to enhance the **child safety feature** by automatically triggering **audio recording** when a safety alert was raised, providing additional context during emergencies.

However, we ran into **browser permission and privacy constraints**, especially in a web environment. Automatically starting audio recording without explicit, continuous user consent is restricted by modern browsers, and we decided not to compromise on user privacy or platform compliance.

As a result, we deferred this feature and kept safety tools **explicit, opt-in, and privacy-first**, aligning with the overall design philosophy of the app.

> Care that listens, answers, acts

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twilio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twilio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![FAST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/FAST%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

- *Problem it solves*: Critical services (healthcare, emergency, government schemes, legal aid) are hard to access for visually impaired, elderly, and semi-literate users who struggle with text-heavy apps, navigation, and language barriers.

*What people can use it for:*
- Speak to book a doctor, pick a time, and get confirmations read aloud.
- Call emergency services hands-free (police/ambulance/fire/women helpline).
- Discover government schemes and eligibility via voice Q&A.
- Get guided steps for legal aid or filing complaints.

*How it makes tasks easier/safer:*
- Voice-first flow: options are read aloud; the mic auto-listens, reducing taps and navigation friction.
- Bilingual (English/Malayalam) speech-to-text and text-to-speech, covering local terms and accents.
- Clear confirmations and error prompts reduce mis-selections; hands-free emergency access improves response speed.
- Accessible UI (large touch targets, simple states) paired with audio guidance lowers cognitive load.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Voice auto-listen loop: The mic stopped after the first answer because the STT session never fully stopped before TTS restarted. We fixed it by explicitly stopping recognition on final transcripts and re-starting listening in the TTS onEnd callback, with a guard ref to keep the flow alive through every question.
- Dual-language STT/TTS quirks: Malayalam + English recognition needed the browser Web Speech API, but an earlier hook pointed to a local Whisper server that wasn’t always running. Switching back to the native useVoiceRecognition with dynamic lang fixed reliability for both languages.
- JSX tag mismatch in Government screen: A stray closing token inside a mapped section broke the render. We removed the misplaced block and closed the layout properly. Build errors vanished afterward.
- Speaking back results accessibly: The schemes flow initially only showed results visually. We added spoken summaries (count + top schemes) so visually impaired users get the outcome read aloud.
- Session-safe backend agent: The appointment agent was stateful in a single global context. We refactored it into per-session contexts with FastAPI endpoints so multiple conversations can run safely in parallel.

> “From preparation to presence.”

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem Protocall Solves

Interview preparation today is largely **one-dimensional**. Most platforms focus on *what* a candidate says, but real interviews evaluate *how* a candidate communicates , their confidence, clarity, tone, and non-verbal presence. Access to realistic mock interviews with immediate, objective feedback is limited, expensive, or inconsistent, leaving candidates underprepared despite strong technical skills.

## How Protocall Makes Interview Preparation Better

Protocall transforms interview practice into a **realistic, AI-driven simulation** using Google Studio AI, making preparation smarter, safer, and more effective.

# 🎯 What People Use Protocall For
- Practicing **real-time, voice-to-voice mock interviews**
- Improving **communication, confidence, and clarity**
- Preparing for **role-specific interviews** (Frontend, Backend, Leadership, System Design)
- Receiving **objective, unbiased feedback** without human pressure
- Tracking personal growth across multiple interview sessions

# 🧠 How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer
- **Instant feedback** instead of delayed or subjective reviews  
- **24/7 availability** without scheduling peers or mentors  
- **Privacy-first practice** with no persistent data storage  
- **Reduced anxiety** through judgment-free AI coaching  
- **Consistent evaluation** using standardized AI metrics  

### 🚀 What Makes It Different
Powered by **Google Studio AI**, Protocall uses multimodal intelligence to:
- Analyze **spoken responses** in real time  
- Interpret **non-verbal cues** like eye contact and posture  
- Adapt interview difficulty dynamically  
- Deliver actionable insights immediately after the session  

# Impact
Protocall bridges the gap between preparation and performance by turning interview practice into **measurable intelligence**, helping candidates walk into real interviews with confidence, clarity, and control.
## 🛠 Tech Stack Used

# Frontend
- **React 19** – Leveraging concurrent rendering and modern hooks for a smooth, responsive UI.
- **TypeScript** – Strong typing for managing complex AI interaction states, audio streams, and UI logic.
- **Tailwind CSS** – Utility-first styling with a custom professional palette and Glassmorphism design.

# Artificial Intelligence & AI Orchestration
- **Genkit (Google AI Studio)** – Used to orchestrate agent-based reasoning and manage multimodal AI workflows.
- **Gemini 2.5 Flash (Native Audio)** – Powers low-latency, real-time voice-to-voice interview conversations.
- **Gemini APIs** – Enables live transcription, reasoning, evaluation, and function calling.
- **Function Calling** – Allows the AI agent to update visual feedback in real time without interrupting the interview flow.

# Multimedia & Web APIs
- **Web Audio API** – Real-time audio capture, PCM encoding/decoding, and streaming.
- **MediaDevices API** – Camera and microphone access for multimodal interaction.
- **Canvas API** – Video frame extraction for visual cue analysis.

#Data Visualization
- **Recharts** – Interactive radar and bar charts for post-interview performance analytics.

# Infrastructure & Delivery
- **ESM.sh** – Zero-install ES module CDN for fast, serverless dependency delivery.
- **HTML5 / CSS3** – Modern web standards for performance and accessibility.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Through

Building **Protocall** required solving several technical and design challenges to deliver a realistic, low-latency, and privacy-first interview experience.

#🔊 Real-Time Audio Latency
Creating natural, voice-to-voice conversations was challenging due to strict latency requirements. We had to carefully manage raw PCM audio streaming and buffering to ensure smooth, uninterrupted dialogue using the Gemini Live API.

# 🎥 Multimodal Synchronization
Coordinating live audio, video frames, transcription, and AI reasoning in parallel was complex. Ensuring that visual cue analysis aligned accurately with spoken responses required precise timing and frame extraction logic.

#🧠 Agent-Based Reasoning Design
Designing an AI agent that could **perceive, reason, and act** in real time,without interrupting the interview flow,was a key challenge. This involved implementing function calling so the agent could update UI feedback dynamically while maintaining conversational continuity.

# 🖥 UI Feedback Without Distraction
Delivering real-time behavioral feedback (confidence, eye contact, posture) without overwhelming or distracting the user required multiple UI iterations. We balanced visibility and subtlety to maintain interview realism.

# 📊 Meaningful Evaluation Metrics
Translating subjective interview qualities like confidence and clarity into structured, measurable scores and radar charts was non-trivial. We refined scoring weights and feedback logic to ensure fairness and interpretability.

# 🛡 Privacy & Security Constraints
We deliberately avoided persistent data storage to protect user privacy. This required careful session handling and real-time-only processing, which added complexity to analytics generation.

#⚙️ Browser & Device Constraints
Working with Web Audio, MediaDevices, and Canvas APIs across browsers introduced compatibility and performance challenges, especially for camera and microphone handling.


Despite these challenges, overcoming them allowed us to build a **robust, scalable, and immersive AI interview coaching platform** that closely mirrors real-world interview dynamics.

> Prescribe Smarter.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This project addresses the critical challenge of physician burnout and medication safety caused by the overwhelming administrative burden of manual documentation and illegible handwriting. By acting as an intelligent digital scribe, our system leverages Generative AI to automatically convert unstructured doctor-patient conversations into precise, structured medical records in real-time. Instead of a doctor spending valuable consultation time typing notes, the AI filters out small talk, extracts key clinical details like diagnoses and medication dosages, and instantly generates a professional, error-free PDF prescription. This transforms a tedious administrative task into an automated workflow, minimizing medical errors and allowing doctors to reclaim their time to focus entirely on patient care.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the most significant technical hurdles was ensuring the determinism and structure of the AI model's output. Since LLMs are naturally conversational, getting Gemini to consistently return strict, parsable JSON without markdown formatting or hallucinatory filler required rigorous prompt engineering and backend sanitation logic. We also faced latency and resource quotas (specifically 429 Resource Exhausted errors) when processing high-resolution audio, which we resolved by implementing optimized wait-retry mechanisms and managing file states effectively. Finally, bridging the gap between a mobile frontend and a local backend introduced networking complexities regarding CORS, Windows Firewall restrictions, and dynamic IP resolution, forcing us to move beyond standard localhost configurations to a robust, network-exposed server setup.

**Best Innovation**

This project stands out in the Best Innovation track because it fundamentally redefines the clinical workflow, moving from "Digitization" (typing into a computer) to "Ambient Intelligence" (the computer listening and understanding). Unlike traditional health-tech solutions that merely shift paperwork from paper to screen, our system leverages the cutting-edge multimodal capabilities of Gemini 2.5 Flash to process raw, unstructured audio and autonomously synthesize it into a legally compliant, structured prescription. By architecting a sophisticated hybrid microservices framework—combining Python for deep reasoning with Node.js for high-speed document rendering—we have created a seamless, stateless solution that solves the complex problem of "unstructured data to actionable document" in real-time. This is a leap forward in reducing physician burnout and eliminating medication errors, demonstrating how Generative AI can be practically, safely, and invisibly integrated into critical infrastructure.

> VITA-LINK: Care, Connected

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dialogflow](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dialogflow-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twilio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twilio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem Statement: Healthcare systems today are largely reactive, fragmented, and slow to respond during critical situations. Patients-especially seniors and high-risk individuals-lack real-time monitoring, timely emergency alerts, and a unified platform to manage health data. This leads to delayed medical intervention, missed warning signs, and increased risk during emergencies.

Solution:

VITA-LINK is a smart health connectivity platform that enables real-time monitoring, instant emergency alerts, and centralized health data access, ensuring faster response and safer healthcare outcomes.

Use Cases:

Real-time tracking of vital health parameters
Automatic emergency alerts to caregivers and responders
Centralized and secure health data management
Remote monitoring for seniors and chronically ill users
Seamless communication between patients, families, and healthcare providers

Impact: VITA-LINK transforms healthcare from reactive to preventive, reducing response time, improving safety, and providing peace of mind through intelligent, connected care.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building VITA-LINK, one of the biggest challenges was handling real-time health data in a reliable way. Initially, the system either generated false emergency alerts due to noisy or incomplete inputs or delayed alerts because different modules were not properly synchronized. This was critical, as accuracy and response time are essential in healthcare applications. I overcame this by adding data validation and adaptive threshold checks before triggering alerts, and by decoupling the monitoring and alerting logic to reduce latency and simplify debugging. Another hurdle was keeping patient, caregiver, and dashboard views in sync, which I resolved by improving API response handling and using event-based updates. These challenges helped me learn the importance of modular architecture, clean data flow, and user-focused design when building safety-critical systems.

**Best Innovation**

VITA-LINK stands out through its innovative approach to healthcare by combining real-time health monitoring, intelligent alerting, and a unified care ecosystem into a single platform. Instead of reacting only after emergencies occur, it enables proactive and preventive care, ensuring faster response, better coordination between patients and caregivers, and improved safety—especially for seniors and high-risk users.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Embedded Javascript (EJS)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Embedded%20Javascript%20(EJS)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem Finpilot Solves:

Small businesses generate a large amount of financial data every day—through invoices, expenses, taxes, and investments.
However, this data is usually spread across multiple tools and formats, making it difficult to understand the overall financial health of the business.

Most existing financial tools focus on recording transactions, not on helping business owners interpret the data or make decisions.
As a result, businesses operate reactively, identify cash-flow problems too late, and make financial decisions without clear insights.

 What Finpilot Is Used For:
Finpilot is used as a central financial command center for small businesses.

People can use Finpilot to:

- Monitor real-time cash inflow, outflow, and net cash flow
- Track paid and unpaid invoices to avoid receivable delays
- Understand where their money is being spent through visual charts
- Manage multiple types of taxes without mixing them with revenue
- Track digital asset investments alongside operational finances
- Simulate financial scenarios safely using demo accounts
- Ask questions and receive AI-generated financial insights

 How Finpilot Makes Financial Tasks Easier:

-  Simplifies Complex Financial Data

Finpilot converts raw financial numbers into clear summaries, charts, and explanations, removing the need for financial expertise.

- Replaces Multiple Tools with One Platform

Instead of switching between spreadsheets, accounting tools, and investment apps, Finpilot brings everything into a single unified interface.

- Improves Decision-Making Speed

Visual insights like pie charts and AI-generated recommendations allow users to understand their financial position at a glance.

- Reduces Manual Errors

Automated cash-flow calculations and tax separation reduce mistakes that often occur with manual tracking.

 How Finpilot Makes Finance Safer:

- Supports demo accounts so users can explore and test scenarios without using real financial data
- Separates tax liabilities from actual revenue, reducing compliance risks
- Provides clear visibility into investment exposure, reducing over-risking
- Offers explainable AI insights rather than opaque calculations

Overall Impact:

Finpilot bridges the gap between financial data and financial decisions.
It helps small businesses move from reactive financial management to proactive, informed, and confident decision-making.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into

One of the main challenges was designing a unified financial data model that could support invoices, transactions, taxes, and investments without creating confusion or conflicts. Each feature required different data structures, and combining them into a single backend required careful separation of concerns. This was resolved by designing modular components and connecting them through a central cash flow engine.

Another challenge was keeping cash flow calculations accurate while introducing taxes and investment tracking. There was a risk of counting tax amounts or investments as operational revenue, which could distort financial insights. This issue was solved by clearly separating operational cash flow, tax liabilities, and investment capital within the backend logic.

Making the AI insights meaningful instead of generic was also a challenge. Early responses lacked context and did not reflect the actual financial state of the business. This was overcome by sending structured financial summaries to the AI layer, which resulted in more relevant, explainable, and actionable insights.

Implementing the demo account feature introduced complexity in managing multiple data states. Switching between example data and user-defined demo data risked breaking calculations and visual consistency. This was handled by isolating data sources and ensuring all calculations, charts, and AI responses updated dynamically when the data source changed.

Balancing feature depth with hackathon time constraints was another hurdle. There was a constant trade-off between adding more features and maintaining system stability. This was addressed by prioritizing core business problems and implementing features incrementally.

Presenting complex financial information in a simple and understandable way was also challenging. Displaying too many metrics reduced clarity for users. This was solved by focusing on high-level summaries and visual elements such as pie charts instead of raw tables.

Finally, ensuring the project felt realistic and production-ready without real banking integrations was difficult. This was solved by using mock and sandbox data while designing the system architecture in a way that can easily support real-world integrations in the future.

**Best Innovation**

Finpilot fits the Best Innovation track by transforming financial management from simple data tracking into intelligent decision-making. Instead of using separate tools for invoices, expenses, taxes, and investments, Finpilot unifies all financial activities into a single platform and layers AI-driven insights on top.

Its key innovation lies in the AI Finance Copilot, which converts complex financial data into clear, actionable recommendations that do not require financial expertise. Additionally, the demo account and data-switching feature enables safe financial simulation and experimentation without using real data. By combining embedded finance, visual intelligence, and explainable AI, Finpilot introduces a new, decision-focused approach to managing business finance.

> For A Smarter City

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Urban flooding in cities like Kolkata is highly localized, yet most existing alert systems operate at a broad city or district level. This makes it difficult for citizens and authorities to understand real flood risk at a specific location, leading to delayed responses and ineffective preparedness.
Kolkata Flood Risk Analyzer addresses this by providing grid-level flood risk prediction using machine learning and real environmental data. The system combines historical rainfall (2014–2024), short-term rainfall accumulation, elevation, and hydrological features to classify flood risk as No, Low, Medium, or High for precise locations.
By allowing users to simply enter a location and instantly view risk levels on an interactive map, the platform enables early, actionable insights. This supports better decision-making for citizens, emergency responders, and urban planners, shifting flood management from reactive alerts to proactive risk intelligence.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a reliable flood prediction system was challenging due to the lack of clean, labeled flood risk data at a fine spatial scale. There was no ready-made dataset with ground-truth flood labels, so we had to design a rule-based risk scoring framework using rainfall intensity, accumulation windows, elevation, and hydrological factors to generate meaningful labels.
Another major challenge was ensuring the model generalized spatially, not just temporally. Flood patterns vary significantly across different parts of the city, so we validated the model using time-based splits and spatial holdout testing to avoid overfitting to specific regions and ensure robust performance for unseen locations.
Finally, integrating the machine learning pipeline with a real-time, location-based web interface required careful coordination between backend prediction logic and frontend visualization. This was addressed by modularizing the API, optimizing inference latency, and progressively building an interactive map-based UI that remains responsive and intuitive.

**The problem it solves**

***The Problem It Solves***

Modern public spaces rely heavily on traditional CCTV surveillance systems that require continuous human monitoring. This approach is not only inefficient but also prone to human fatigue, delayed reactions, and missed threats.

- Security teams are often overwhelmed by:
- Hundreds of camera feeds to monitor simultaneously
- Delayed identification of unattended or suspicious objects
- Lack of intelligent prioritization of potential threats
- Reactive responses instead of proactive prevention

As a result, critical security incidents are often detected too late, reducing the effectiveness of existing safety infrastructure.

***How This Project Helps***

- The Smart Threat Detection & Alert System transforms passive surveillance into an intelligent, proactive safety solution.

*What people can use it for:*
- Monitoring airports, railway stations, campuses, malls, and public events
- Automatically detecting unattended or suspicious objects
- Receiving real-time alerts instead of manually watching camera feeds
- Improving response time during potential security threats

*How it makes tasks easier & safer:*
- Reduces human workload by automating surveillance
- Minimizes human error and fatigue
- Detects threats early, enabling faster intervention
- Filters false alarms using contextual analysis
- Operates in a privacy-first, non-intrusive manner (no facial recognition)

***Key Impact***
- By combining AI, computer vision, and real-time alerts, this system:
- Enhances public safety
- Improves situational awareness
- Enables faster, smarter decision-making
- Makes existing security infrastructure more effective
The result is a safer, smarter, and more reliable threat detection system suitable for real-world deployment.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I Ran Into**

Building an AI-powered, full-stack threat detection system within a limited hackathon timeframe presented several real-world engineering challenges. The project required seamless coordination between AI models, backend services, and frontend interfaces, all while ensuring real-time performance, reliability, and ethical constraints.

1. ***Integrating AI Detection with Real-Time Backend Systems***
*Challenge:*
The AI model was capable of detecting unattended or suspicious objects, but integrating its output with the backend for real-time analysis and alert generation was initially unreliable. Detection data sometimes arrived late, in inconsistent formats, or caused processing delays—making real-time alerting difficult.

**How It Was Overcome:**
Detection outputs were standardized into well-defined API response structures
Clear data contracts were established between the AI module and backend
Continuous log monitoring was used to trace data flow end-to-end
This ensured reliable, low-latency communication between detection and analysis layers, enabling accurate real-time alerts.

2.***Frontend–Backend Communication & API Stability***
*Challenge:*
The frontend dashboard occasionally failed to fetch data or trigger alerts correctly due to issues such as:
CORS misconfigurations
Incorrect API endpoints
Payload mismatches between frontend requests and backend expectations
These issues caused broken UI states and delayed responses.

**How It Was Overcome:**
Real-time debugging and network inspection were used to trace failed requests
API configurations were centralized to avoid inconsistencies
Backend validation and error handling were improved
This resulted in a stable and responsive frontend experience.

3. ***Managing Multiple Services Under Hackathon Pressure***
*Challenge:*
Running and coordinating multiple services simultaneously—AI model, backend server, and frontend application—under tight deadlines was challenging. Context switching between tools and terminals slowed down debugging and testing.

**How KIRO IDE Helped:**
Provided a single unified workspace for all components
Allowed running multiple services side-by-side using integrated terminals
Made it easy to monitor logs, restart services, and debug issues instantly
KIRO IDE significantly reduced setup overhead and saved valuable hackathon time.

4. ***Debugging Configuration & Environment Issues***
*Challenge:*
Environment variables, database connections, and runtime configurations caused unexpected failures during development, especially when switching between local and test environments.

**How KIRO IDE Helped:**
Centralized project structure made configuration issues easier to spot
Real-time logs exposed misconfigured variables and connection errors
Faster debugging cycles helped resolve issues without disrupting progress
This ensured smoother development despite time constraints.

5. ***Reducing False Positives in Threat Detection***
*Challenge:*
Initial AI detection results triggered alerts for non-threatening scenarios, leading to false positives that could reduce system trust in real-world deployment.

**How It Was Overcome:**
Introduced object persistence duration checks
Applied context-based rules instead of raw detection outputs
Tuned thresholds through rapid testing and iteration
KIRO IDE’s live reload and fast debugging enabled quick experimentation and fine-tuning during the hackathon.

***Overall Impact of Using KIRO IDE***
*KIRO IDE played a critical role throughout the project by:*
Accelerating development cycles
Reducing debugging and integration time
Enabling efficient multi-service management
Allowing the team to focus on problem-solving rather than tooling

*KIRO IDE acted as a silent teammate, empowering rapid innovation, smooth integration, and efficient execution under hackathon pressure.*

**Best Innovation**

Our project strongly embodies the ***Best Innovation*** track by reimagining how public safety systems operate. Instead of treating CCTV as a passive recording tool, we transform it into an ***intelligent, proactive threat detection system*** powered by AI.

Unlike conventional surveillance solutions that depend on constant human monitoring, our system uses ***computer vision, contextual intelligence, and real-time decision-making*** to automatically identify unattended or suspicious objects and trigger instant alerts. This not only improves response times but also significantly reduces human workload and operational fatigue.

What makes our solution truly innovative is its ***privacy-first and ethical design***. By deliberately avoiding facial recognition and biometric data, the system focuses on object behavior rather than personal identity, making it suitable for real-world deployment in sensitive public spaces.

By seamlessly combining ***AI intelligence, real-time processing, and a scalable cloud-ready architecture***, our project delivers a practical yet forward-looking solution that modernizes existing security infrastructure and demonstrates how AI can be responsibly used to enhance public safety.

**AWS**

Our project aligns strongly with the ***AWS*** track by leveraging cloud-native architecture to deliver a scalable, reliable, and real-time AI-powered threat detection system.

The system is designed to run seamlessly on ***AWS infrastructure***, where:

- AI detection services can be deployed using scalable compute (e.g., EC2 / containers)
- Backend APIs can be hosted using AWS-managed services for high availability
- Real-time alerts and notifications can be handled through cloud-based messaging and event-driven workflows
- Data storage and logs can be securely managed using cloud databases and monitoring tools

By using AWS, the system achieves ***elastic scalability***, allowing it to handle multiple camera feeds and increasing workloads without performance degradation. AWS’s reliability and security features further ensure that sensitive surveillance data is processed safely and efficiently.

Overall, AWS enables our project to move from a hackathon prototype to a ***production-ready, cloud-deployable solution***, making it suitable for large-scale public safety deployments such as airports, campuses, and smart cities.
