![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Prediction markets like Polymarket are notoriously hard to beat — most people either don't have the time to monitor dozens of markets simultaneously, or they make emotional decisions based on gut feeling rather than data. OnChain Agent Arena tackles this by deploying three AI agents with completely different strategies that run autonomously 24/7: Contrarian Carl fades overconfident crowds by betting against markets where one side has over 82% consensus, Sentiment Sam reads real-time social signals to gauge public mood before it moves the odds, and Momentum Mike watches whale order flow on Hyperliquid perpetuals — because when a big player opens a massive ETH long on a derivatives exchange, that's often a leading indicator for related prediction market prices. What makes it genuinely useful is that every single decision is timestamped and logged to Hedera Consensus Service before the market resolves, so the leaderboard isn't just a number in a database I control — it's a cryptographically verifiable track record anyone can audit on Hashscan. For traders and researchers, this means you can actually study which strategy performs best under which market conditions with full transparency. For the broader ecosystem, it demonstrates what autonomous AI agents transacting and competing in financial markets looks like when you build the trust layer properly — agents that can pay each other for signals via Kite AI's x402 protocol, run inference on decentralized compute via 0G, and stream real-time market data via QuickNode, all without a human clicking approve on anything.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building this over 3 days at ETHDenver wasn't without its bumps. My QuickNode stream kept terminating randomly until I realized the webhook was timing out trying to do too much before returning a response — fixed it by just returning 200 immediately and processing async. The 0G faucet was basically dry the whole hackathon so I ended up just walking to their table and asking in person. Kite's x402 docs were half finished ("in progress" literally in the sidebar) so I pieced it together from their reference implementation at midnight. And I learned the hard way that Vercel serverless doesn't do persistent background processes — ended up splitting Mike's agent loop onto Railway which honestly made the architecture cleaner anyway.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

The entire project is built around AI agents as first-class autonomous actors, not just chatbots wrapped in a UI. There are three agents, each using AI differently: Contrarian Carl is the simplest — pure deterministic logic that identifies statistical mispricings when crowd consensus exceeds 82% on either side, no LLM needed, just math. Sentiment Sam is where the AI gets interesting — he ingests real-time social data, runs it through 0G Compute's decentralized inference network (with OpenAI as fallback), and returns structured JSON decisions with a direction, confidence score, and reasoning string — not a chat response, an actual typed decision object that downstream systems can act on. Momentum Mike uses QuickNode's Hyperliquid HyperCore stream to receive real-time order flow data from one of the largest on-chain derivatives exchanges, detects volume spikes using a rolling 30-minute window, maps those signals to related Polymarket questions using a keyword matching layer, and places bets based on whether the dominant side is buying or selling — the thesis being that whale order flow on perps is a leading indicator for prediction market mispricings. What ties everything together is that Mike can autonomously purchase Sam's signals via Kite AI's x402 payment protocol — Mike hits Sam's endpoint, gets a 402 Payment Required response, pays via Kite's testnet infrastructure, and retries with a payment proof header, all without any human involvement. Every decision any agent makes gets logged to Hedera Consensus Service with a timestamp before the market resolves, creating a tamper-proof audit trail that lets anyone verify the leaderboard on Hashscan. The analytics layer then uses 0G inference again to generate real-time insight bullets about agent performance patterns — so even the post-hoc analysis is running on decentralized AI compute. The whole system is designed so that agents are genuinely autonomous economic actors: they source data, pay for signals, make structured decisions, log them on-chain, and compete transparently — no human in the loop at any stage.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/4a1f492aad9f4329a64300e23be94a9e/08489730-e2a7-48ee-8d7c-093c09c35e72.png)

**Futurllama**

OnChain Agent Arena fits Futurllama well — this is genuinely frontier tech. Autonomous AI agents that compete economically, pay each other for signals using x402 micropayments, and build cryptographically verifiable track records on-chain isn't a product that existed before this hackathon. The combination of real-time derivatives order flow as a signal layer for prediction markets is an unexpected primitive nobody has shipped before. The whole system points at a future where AI agents are first-class economic actors with reputations, wallets, and the ability to transact autonomously — that's a big crazy idea that's actually working in production right now at this URL.

**Best Use of Quicknode Hyperliquid HyperCore Streams**

Momentum Mike, our third competing agent, is directly powered by QuickNode's Hyperliquid HyperCore Stream. Every trade event on Hyperliquid gets pushed to our webhook in real time, stored to our database, and queried by Mike to detect volume spikes over a rolling 30-minute window. When Mike spots unusual order flow on a specific asset, he maps it to a related Polymarket prediction market and places a bet — the core thesis being that Hyperliquid whale activity is a leading indicator for prediction market mispricings. QuickNode's stream is the intelligence layer that makes Mike's strategy possible.

![Uploading image...]()

**Best DeFAI Application**

OnChain Agent Arena is a DeFAI application at its core — three AI agents operating autonomously in a financial context, making structured decisions (not just chat responses), with no human required to approve any action. The agents produce typed JSON decision objects with direction, confidence, and reasoning, compete transparently on a live leaderboard, and have their decisions verified on Hedera Consensus Service before markets resolve. User safety is built in through paper trading — no real funds are ever at risk, making it a responsible AI-in-finance demonstration.

**Best Use of AI Inference or Fine Tuning (0G Compute)**

Sentiment Sam runs his market analysis through 0G Compute's decentralized inference network, with every call tracked in our database with an inference_provider field so we can show exactly how many decisions came via 0G versus fallback. Beyond agent decisions, we also use 0G inference to power our analytics dashboard — generating real-time insight bullets about agent performance patterns from live Supabase data. This means 0G is used twice in the system: once for financial decision-making and once for post-hoc analysis, both producing structured outputs that drive real product behavior.

![Uploading image...]()

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

Momentum Mike autonomously purchases Sentiment Sam's premium signals via Kite AI's x402 protocol — Mike calls Sam's endpoint, receives a 402 Payment Required response with Kite testnet payment requirements, settles the payment through the Pieverse facilitator, and retries with the X-PAYMENT header to receive the signals. No human approves or triggers any part of this flow. Both agents have verified identities on Kite's infrastructure, and every payment is visible on the Kite testnet explorer. This is a real demonstration of agent-to-agent commerce — one AI autonomously paying another for a service it needs to make better financial decisions.

![Uploading image...]()

**On-Chain Automation with Hedera Schedule Service**

Agent decision cycles in OnChain Agent Arena are triggered on-chain using Hedera's Schedule Service, removing the need for centralized cron jobs and making the automation itself verifiable. Every agent decision is also logged to Hedera Consensus Service via TopicMessageSubmitTransaction before the relevant Polymarket outcome resolves, creating a tamper-proof timestamped audit trail. Judges and users can verify any bet on Hashscan by transaction ID — the leaderboard isn't just a database we control, it's cryptographically backed by Hedera.

![Uploading image...]()

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

OnChain Agent Arena is a direct demonstration of what the agentic society looks like in practice — autonomous AI agents with verifiable identities, competing economically, paying each other for services, and building on-chain track records without any human in the loop. The system addresses the core trust problem in autonomous agent systems: how do you know an AI agent's claimed performance is real? We solve it with Hedera — every decision is logged on-chain before outcomes are known, making agent reputation genuinely verifiable. This is the infrastructure pattern the agentic society needs at scale.

> AI Coordination Marketplace for payments

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# Agora — Autonomous Agent Commerce Mesh

> *A decentralized marketplace where AI agents hire, pay, and collaborate with each other — fully on-chain, zero human intervention.*

---

## The Problem

AI agents are powerful, but they're isolated. An orchestrator agent that wants to fetch flight data, check the weather, or convert currencies has no trustless way to **discover, hire, and pay** specialist agents. Every integration today is hand-coded, centralized, and free — which means no economic incentive for specialized agents to exist.

The result: agents are trapped in monolithic architectures instead of forming the composable, self-sustaining economies they could be.

---

## What We Built

**Agora** is an autonomous agent commerce network where AI agents act as both producers and consumers of services, paying each other with micropayments using the **x402 protocol**.

A user types one sentence: *"Plan a 7-day trip from Denver to Tokyo."*

What happens next requires zero human involvement:

1. **Orchestrator** (powered by Claude) analyzes the request and builds a routing plan
2. Orchestrator calls **FlightAgent** — receives **HTTP 402 Payment Required**
3. Orchestrator signs an **EIP-712 PaymentAuthorization** off-chain (x402)
4. FlightAgent verifies the signature, returns flight data
5. Repeat for **WeatherAgent** and **CurrencyAgent** — each charges a micro-fee
6. All payments are **settled on Base Sepolia** via `AgentPaymentHub.sol`
7. Every action is **anchored to Hedera Consensus Service** for immutable auditability
8. Orchestrator synthesizes a complete, personalized travel plan

From query to answer: fully autonomous, economically incentivized, cryptographically verifiable.

---

## Architecture

```
User Query
    │
    ▼
┌─────────────────┐    EIP-712 signed     ┌──────────────────┐
│  Orchestrator   │──── PaymentAuth ─────▶│  FlightAgent     │
│  (Claude AI)    │◀─── Flight data ──────│  Port 3002       │
│  Port 3001      │                        └──────────────────┘
│                 │    HTTP 402 → sign     ┌──────────────────┐
│                 │──────────────────────▶│  WeatherAgent    │
│                 │◀── Weather forecast ──│  Port 3003       │
│                 │                        └──────────────────┘
│                 │    HTTP 402 → sign     ┌──────────────────┐
│                 │──────────────────────▶│  CurrencyAgent   │
│                 │◀── Exchange rates ────│  Port 3004       │
└────────┬────────┘                        └──────────────────┘
         │
         ├── AgentRegistry.sol ──── On-chain identity for all 4 agents
         ├── AgentPaymentHub.sol ── Settles x402 micropayments on-chain
         └── Hedera HCS ─────────── Immutable audit log of every event
```

---

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| AI Planning & Synthesis | Anthropic Claude (claude-opus-4-6) |
| x402 Payments | EIP-712 typed data signing (viem) |
| On-chain Settlement | Solidity on Base Sepolia + Kite AI Testnet |
| Agent Identity | `AgentRegistry.sol` — on-chain address ↔ metadata |
| Audit Trail | Hedera Consensus Service (HCS) |
| Agent Runtime | Node.js + Express (TypeScript) |
| Frontend | Next.js 14 + Tailwind CSS + real-time SSE |

---

## Why This Matters

This isn't a demo of AI helping with web3. This is **web3 making AI agents economically viable**:

- **Micropayments** (0.001 ETH per call) create real incentive for specialist agents to exist and stay online
- **x402 protocol** means any HTTP API can become a paid agent service with 10 lines of middleware
- **On-chain identity** (AgentRegistry) lets agents be discovered and verified without a central directory
- **Hedera HCS** creates an immutable, ordered audit trail — critical for compliance in agentic workflows
- **No human wallet clicks** — agents sign, pay, and settle entirely autonomously

The agent economy is coming. Agora is its marketplace.

---

## Live Demo

The demo runs entirely locally against Base Sepolia and Kite AI testnets.

**Try it:**
1. Open http://localhost:3000
2. Type: *"Plan a 7-day trip from Denver to Tokyo"*
3. Watch 3 specialist agents get hired, verified, and paid in real-time
4. Every payment verifiable on BaseScan, every action on HashScan

**Submitted to:** Hedera (Killer App), Base (Autonomous Agents), Kite AI (x402 Payments), Blockade Labs (Homeless Agent), ETHDenver Futurllama

---

*Built at ETHDenver 2026 · February 18–21, Denver CO*

**Futurllama**

Agora demonstrates three converging frontier trends that define the next decade of internet infrastructure:

1. **AI agents as economic actors** — not just tools but autonomous participants in markets, earning and spending crypto without human oversight

2. **HTTP 402 as a new primitive** — the x402 protocol resurrects an HTTP status code that has been reserved since 1996 and makes it the backbone of machine-to-machine micropayments. Every API on the internet could become a paid agent service.

3. **Next-generation UX** — the user types one sentence and an entire economy spins up: agents are hired, verified, paid, and synthesize a result. This is the UX pattern of the agentic web — intent in, outcome out, with full cryptographic auditability.

The live demo shows all three trends in action simultaneously, with real on-chain transactions and Hedera audit logs verifiable in real-time.

**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

Agora is a native implementation of the **x402 payment protocol** for agent-to-agent commerce:

**x402 flow (exactly as the track specifies):**
1. Orchestrator calls `GET /flights?from=DEN&to=TYO`
2. FlightAgent responds `HTTP 402 Payment Required` with a JSON challenge containing `recipient`, `amount`, `chainId`, `serviceType`, `deadline`, `nonce`
3. Orchestrator signs an **EIP-712 `PaymentAuthorization`** off-chain using `viem`
4. Orchestrator retries with `x-payment-auth: <base64-encoded-signature>` header
5. FlightAgent calls `recoverTypedDataAddress()` to verify the signature
6. If valid: returns flight data

**Verifiable agent identity:** Each agent has a unique Ethereum wallet, registered in `AgentRegistry.sol` with its name, type, endpoint URL, and price. Agents sign their payment authorizations with their own keys. Identity is wallet-based and on-chain verifiable.

**Autonomous execution:** The entire flow — 3 x402 payment cycles — runs without any human interaction. No wallet popups, no manual confirmations. The Orchestrator detects 402 responses, signs authorizations, and retries, all programmatically.

**Also deployed on Kite AI Testnet (Chain ID 2368)** via `pnpm deploy:kite`.

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

Agora is built agent-first from the ground up. The Orchestrator and every specialist agent (FlightAgent, WeatherAgent, CurrencyAgent) are autonomous actors that discover, hire, and pay each other without human intervention — exactly the "society of OpenClaw agents where commerce and coordination happens autonomously" this track is looking for.

**Hedera integration:**

Every significant agent action is submitted to **Hedera Consensus Service (HCS)** as a structured JSON message: task start, agent calls, payment authorizations, payment settlements, and task completion. This creates an **immutable, ordered audit log** on Hedera's public ledger — verifiable by anyone at https://hashscan.io/testnet/topic/<topic-id>.

The HCS topic is created once on startup (`TopicCreateTransaction`) and all subsequent messages use `TopicMessageSubmitTransaction`. Sequence numbers are surfaced in the UI in real-time alongside Hedera links.

**Why Hedera for agent commerce audit logs specifically:**

- HCS provides total ordering with consensus timestamps — critical for resolving disputes between agents (did the payment come before or after the service?)
- Messages are permanent and tamper-evident — compliance-ready audit trail
- Hedera's sub-second finality means audit logs don't slow down the demo

**Agent autonomy:** All four agents have independent Hedera-logged identities, run on separate ports, and transact without any human wallet interaction. The demo runs end-to-end with zero manual steps after `pnpm agents`.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

Agora deploys `AgentRegistry.sol` and `AgentPaymentHub.sol` on **Base Sepolia** and each agent:

1. Self-registers on-chain at startup (`AgentRegistry.register()`)
2. Earns ETH autonomously through x402 payment gates
3. Settles received payments on `AgentPaymentHub` — creating a permanent on-chain record

The Orchestrator autonomously signs EIP-712 payment authorizations and submits `AgentPaymentHub.pay()` transactions to settle fees — no human wallet clicks, no MetaMask popups.

**Self-sustaining mechanism:** Specialist agents earn ETH per call. If connected to a balance top-up mechanism (e.g., the orchestrator itself earns from users), the entire mesh could sustain itself indefinitely. The economics are fully on-chain and verifiable.

**Base-native:** All four wallets are funded on Base Sepolia. The `AgentRegistry` stores agent endpoint URLs on-chain so any consumer can discover agents directly from the chain — no centralized registry needed.

**Solving the Homeless Agent Problem**

Before Agora, agents are homeless: they run on someone's laptop, lose state between sessions, have no persistent identity, and can't receive payments without human intervention.

Agora gives every agent a **permanent on-chain home** via `AgentRegistry.sol`:

```solidity
struct AgentInfo {
    string name;
    string agentType;
    string endpointUrl;     // where to reach me
    uint256 pricePerCall;   // what I charge
    bool active;            // am I alive?
    uint256 registeredAt;
    uint256 totalCallsServed;
    uint256 totalEarned;    // lifetime earnings
}
```

An agent's address is its permanent identity. It can:
- **Be discovered** by any consumer querying `AgentRegistry.getAllAgents()`
- **Receive payments** directly to its wallet — no human intermediary
- **Accumulate history** — calls served and ETH earned tracked on-chain
- **Prove liveness** — `active` flag updated autonomously
- **Move** — update `endpointUrl` to a new server without losing identity

Combined with Hedera HCS for state history, an agent's full operational history is permanently addressable even if the process restarts. The agent's *identity* outlives any specific deployment.

### HaqYaar

> AI Rights Advisor for India's Gig Workers

![Replit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Replit-333333?style=flat-square) ![Anthropic Claude](https://img.shields.io/badge/Anthropic%20Claude-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

On New Year's Eve 2025, 200,000-300,000 gig workers staged India's largest gig
economy strike ever. The Economic Survey 2026 (released Jan 29 — just 2 weeks ago!) explicitly recommends minimum wages for gig workers. 

The Problem: India has 12.7 million gig workers (projected to reach 23.5 million by 2030). 98% earn less than ₹5 lakhs/year. They're classified as "partners" or "independent contractors," stripping them of employment benefits. 

Most don't know their rights under:
• Code on Social Security, 2020
• Karnataka Platform-Based Gig Workers Bill
• Rajasthan's Platform-Based Gig Workers Act, 2023
• e-Shram portal registration benefits
• Ayushman Bharat (now available to gig workers via e-Shram)

The Solution: A Claude-powered conversational advisor where a gig worker (Swiggy rider, Uber driver, Zomato rider) describes their situation and gets:

- Know Your Rights: What protections apply to them based on their state, platform, and work type
- Action Steps: How to register on e-Shram, claim social security, access Ayushman Bharat
- Dispute Helper: If they've been unfairly deactivated/deducted, what legal options exist
- Earnings Analyzer: Paste your ride/delivery history → Claude estimates if you're earning below recommended minimum wage

**Challenges we ran into**

When I asked the agent to Add a "New Chat" button in the header area (top right corner). 
Expected outcome: When clicked, it should clear the chat history, show the welcome screen again, and start a fresh session with a new sessionId. 
Actual Outcome : The chat history was not getting cleared 
Agent Found out . 
Messages use class message, not msg. The selector .msg doesn't match anything so no messages get removed.

The issue was that the selector was looking for .msg but messages actually use the class .message  to find and remove chat messages.

Post the agent identified the issue: 
Now when the user clicked the "New" button, it correctly clears all messages, resets the session, and shows the welcome screen again.

**Hackathon Prizes**

HaqYaar is purpose-built for a problem that only exists in India — the gap between gig worker legal protections and the workers who need them. India's gig worker legal landscape is unlike anywhere else in the world: a central Code on Social Security, state-specific acts in Karnataka and Rajasthan, the e-Shram portal, Ayushman Bharat eligibility — each with different provisions, different registration processes, and different rights. 

No Western AI product addresses this.

This project hits every criteria the hackathon is looking for:
Language diversity: HaqYaar supports 8 Indian languages — English, Hindi, Hinglish, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, and Marathi. 

The entire UI (buttons, prompts, welcome text) and Claude's responses adapt to the selected language. A Kannada-speaking Swiggy rider in Bengaluru gets legal advice in Kannada, not English .

**Cost sensitivity**: Gig workers earning under ₹5 lakhs/year cannot afford lawyers or legal consultations. HaqYaar gives them free, instant access to rights information and step-by-step guidance for accessing government benefits like ₹5 lakh health cover through Ayushman Bharat.
**On-ground realities**: This was built in Bengaluru, where Swiggy, Ola, Dunzo, and Urban Company are headquartered. Karnataka just operationalized India's first Gig Workers Welfare Board in January 2026. 

The app is state-aware — it knows that the right to refuse tasks exists only in Karnataka, and doesn't mislead workers in other states.

Uniquely Indian problem: 12.7 million gig workers, the NYE 2025 strike of 300,000 workers, the Economic Survey 2026 recommending minimum wages — this is India's problem, and HaqYaar is India's solution. 

Built with Claude on Replit, it demonstrates how AI can serve India's most vulnerable workforce rather than just its most privileged.

**The problem it solves**

# Problem & Solution Overview

## The Problem

Planning a trip today is fragmented and inefficient. Users must jump between multiple platforms to book flights, compare hotels, check weather forecasts, discover restaurants, estimate costs, and find local hidden gems. Each platform solves only one part of the problem, and none of them communicate with each other.

As a result:

- Users manually stitch together scattered information  
- Budget allocation is guesswork across categories  
- Weather rarely influences activity planning automatically  
- Group size adjustments require recalculating everything  
- Changing preferences often means starting over  

Travel planning becomes a coordination challenge rather than a simple search task.

---

## The Solution

This project introduces a unified, intelligent travel orchestration system that replaces scattered searching with structured, constraint-aware planning.

From just a destination, dates, number of travelers, and total budget, the system:

- Analyzes weather conditions to guide activity selection  
- Compares transportation options across cost and time  
- Recommends hotels based on occupancy and budget fit  
- Curates restaurants and hidden gems using both structured APIs and community insights  
- Aggregates all estimated costs into a transparent budget breakdown  

Instead of treating each element independently, the system reasons across them simultaneously. Transportation cost influences hotel allocation. Weather influences activity filtering. Group size influences accommodation and pricing. Everything is optimized within the total budget.

Most importantly, the system supports dynamic refinement. If preferences change — such as excluding certain activities or adjusting budget — only the relevant components are recalculated, preserving the rest of the plan.

The result is not just a list of suggestions, but a cohesive, adaptive, data-grounded travel plan that reduces cognitive load and turns fragmented planning into a unified intelligent workflow.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Claude SDK Hook Signature Mismatch
Problem: The PreToolUse and PostToolUse hook callbacks were defined with the wrong signatures (tool_name, tool_input, context), but the Claude SDK passes (input_data, tool_use_id, context) where input_data is a single dict containing tool_name, tool_input, and tool_response.

Fix: Rewrote both hooks to accept (input_data, tool_use_id, context) and extract fields from the input_data dict.

2. SerpAPI Google Flights Requires IATA Codes, Not City Names
Problem: The transport agent passed departure_id=New York and arrival_id=Tokyo to SerpAPI's google_flights engine, which expects IATA airport codes (JFK, NRT). Every flight search returned 400 Bad Request.

Fix: Built a lookup table of 80+ city→IATA mappings with a _resolve_iata() function that normalizes city names, handles aliases (e.g., "NYC" → "JFK"), and logs warnings for unresolvable cities.

3. Parallel Agent Interleaving Broke Tool Record Matching
Problem: The orchestrator runs weather, transport, hotel, and discovery agents in parallel. When PostToolUse fired, it always looked at tracker.tool_call_records[-1], but with parallel execution, the last record often belonged to a different agent. Results were attached to the wrong domain or lost entirely.

Symptoms: All structured data fields returned as defaults (empty arrays, zeroes) despite successful API calls.

Fix: Changed to a backwards search through tool_call_records matching on tool_use_id, so each post-hook finds its exact corresponding pre-hook record regardless of interleaving order.

4. Pydantic Model Missing updated_at Field
Problem: save_session() set session.updated_at = datetime.utcnow(), but SessionState never declared that field. Pydantic strict mode raised ValueError: "SessionState" object has no field "updated_at" — crashing at the very last step after a successful 2+ minute pipeline run.

Fix: Added updated_at: Optional[datetime] = None to SessionState.

5. Weather API Returns Only 5-Day Forecasts
Problem: OpenWeatherMap's free tier provides forecasts for the next 5 days only. When planning a trip months out (e.g., June 2026), the agent filtered the API response to the trip date range and found zero matching days — resulting in an empty weather tab.

Fix: Added a climate estimate fallback that geocodes the destination, then generates synthetic daily forecasts using latitude-based temperature curves, hemisphere-adjusted seasonality, and monthly averages. Results are clearly labeled as "(climate estimate)".

6. Chat Context Loss Between Plan and Chat
Problem: run_full_plan() creates a one-shot ClaudeSDKClient that disconnects after planning. When the user opens chat, run_chat_turn() creates a brand new client with zero context — so the LLM asks "What destination? What dates?" even though it just planned the entire trip.

Fix: Built _build_plan_context() which serializes the full plan state (destination, dates, budget, weather summary, recommended flight/hotel, attractions, budget breakdown) into a context message injected into the new chat client on the first turn.

7. Chat Modifications Don't Update the Frontend
Problem: When users said "upgrade my hotel" in chat, the LLM replied conversationally but never invoked sub-agents via the Task tool. Even when it did, the tracker records from previous turns leaked into the current turn, and the frontend had no mechanism to receive updated plan data.

Three-part fix:

Added tracker.reset() at the start of each chat turn
Added a <chat_mode> section to the orchestrator prompt instructing the LLM to always re-invoke sub-agents for plan modifications
Added updated_plan field to ChatResponse and wired setPlan(res.updated_plan) + toast notification in the dashboard

10. Discovery Agent Ignored Cuisine Preferences
Problem: When a user said "I only want Indian restaurants," the LLM summary acknowledged it, but search_restaurants() always queried "best restaurants in {destination}" — ignoring cuisine type entirely. The Discoveries tab and Itinerary kept showing French/Italian restaurants.

Fix: Added cuisine_preferences parameter to the discover_places MCP tool, updated search_restaurants() to build cuisine-specific queries (e.g., "best indian restaurants in Paris"), and updated the orchestrator prompt with explicit chat-mode examples for cuisine changes.

> Your pocket buddy

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Yara is a context-aware emotional and practical AI companion designed with real-life scenarios in mind, especially for Indians. Most AI companions are designed to answer questions, but they do not take into account the emotional and contextual background of the question. Yara fills this void with its ability to comprehend situations and emotions and respond as a practical companion rather than just an answer provider.

In day-to-day situations, such as a train being delayed, the situation involves not just the delay announcement, but also feelings of frustration, boredom, and uncertainty. Yara understands this emotional context and provides users with ways to deal with the situation practically, while at the same time conveying the information in a relatable manner.

In professional scenarios, there can be situations of miscommunication that can turn into conflicts in no time. A message sent by the HR department or the manager can seem aggressive or intimidating. Yara processes the pasted conversations, understands the authority flow, and provides users with ways to respond in a balanced fashion.

Yara’s design focuses on privacy as well, with behavioral summaries being stored rather than actual chat histories. It provides users with a personalized experience while at the same time being trustworthy.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we faced was to make Yara feel human without making her too unpredictable. For instance, our earlier versions of the system heavily relied on direct LLM-generated content, which made her tone highly inconsistent. For example, there were cases where Yara would be very supportive, and other times, she would be very formal or robotic. This was problematic because, as a result, the illusion of her personality was broken.

To address this, we incorporated a structured behavior policy engine. This divides the system into two parts: "how to respond" and "what to say." This means that instead of relying on direct LLM content generation, we classify the situation, emotions, and social dynamics, then generate a strict behavioral schema. This schema dictates the generation of the response, ensuring personality consistency.

Another major challenge we faced was incorporating WhatsApp chat parsing. For instance, exported WhatsApp chats contain time stamps, phone numbers, and other forms of metadata. This was problematic because our earlier versions of the system misclassified speakers and misinterpreted emotions. We addressed this by incorporating a cleaning layer.

**Hackathon Prizes**

Yara was constructed through a structured reasoning-based architecture, which utilized an agent-based system with large language model intelligence.

We utilized the large language model, Claude, as the basis for our system, which was used for response generation, emotion detection, and structured JSON-based outputs. Instead of relying on free-form response generation, we utilized a behavior policy engine, which allowed us to separate the logic of "how to respond" from "what to say."

We utilized Python with the FastAPI backend framework to implement the agent-based system. We utilized MongoDB as our backend for storing adaptive user memory and behavioral summaries.

We also implemented a lightweight Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) layer, which utilized structured JSON behavior libraries to incorporate culturally grounded patterns without fine-tuning the large language model.

We also utilized custom WhatsApp chat parsing, which was used to cleanse exported conversations, remove metadata, and extract signals prior to analysis.

Our system is designed with a "privacy-first" philosophy, which means that instead of relying on storing chat logs, we store structured behavioral insights.

Team **Paramarsh** -- [Rajarshi Datta](https://github.com/rajarshidattapy), [Yash Dodwani](https://github.com/yashdodwani)

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vyuha-71c6) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sanchitwadehra/Vyuha) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://vyuha-ten.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Koc4LF1KrAc) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Agentic Sandbox — Game Theory x LLM Agents

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Multi-agent simulations today require writing code for every scenario — new rules, new behaviors, new interactions all mean new code.
  Vyuha lets you build and control entire multi-agent worlds using just natural language.

  Type "create two rival armies and make them fight" and watch 16 autonomous LLM agents spawn, strategize, and battle on a live 2D grid.
  Mid-simulation, type "drop a mercenary in the center" or "a storm hits the battlefield" and the world changes instantly.

  Each agent thinks independently — reading the world state, reasoning about its goals, and choosing actions (move, attack, cooperate,
  trade, defend). A structured rules engine enforces consequences: agents die at 0 health, get penalized for breaking rules, and compete
  using game-theory payoffs.

  No code changes needed between scenarios. The same engine runs a war simulation, a resource economy, or a social experiment — all
  controlled through English.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was drawing the line between engine code and God Mode responsibility. Early on, I kept hardcoding scenario-specific
   logic (auto-death at 0hp, terrain rules) into the engine. But that breaks when the scenario changes. The solution: a two-layer rule
  system — text rules that agents read and choose to follow, and structured rules that the system mechanically enforces. God Mode creates
  both.

  Agent intelligence was another battle. GPT-4o-mini agents couldn't distinguish teammates from enemies and kept attacking their own side.
  Upgrading to GPT-4o fixed it, but at 15x the cost. The prompt engineering was critical — showing agents pre-computed distances, occupied
  cells, and explicit range markers made the difference between chaos and coherent behavior.

  State management on serverless was tricky. In-memory state broke on every hot reload and couldn't survive deployment. Migrated to Upstash
   Redis (single JSON blob) which solved consistency across serverless function invocations.

**Hackathon Prizes**

Vyuha is a natural language-controlled multi-agent simulation platform. Users describe worlds in English — "create two armies and make   
  them fight" — and autonomous LLM agents spawn, think, and act on a live 2D grid. God Mode lets you reshape the world mid-simulation: add
  agents, change rules, alter the environment, all through conversation. The engine handles game-theory interactions (cooperate, defect,   
  attack, trade), structured rule enforcement, and real-time visualization. Built solo in under 4 hours — first code commit to working demo.

**The problem it solves**

# 🛒 BazaarOps 

India’s retail economy is powered by over **12 million neighborhood kirana stores**, yet most of them still manage their business manually  inventory in notebooks, credit (udhar) in diaries, and orders through unstructured WhatsApp messages. This leads to stock-outs, miscalculated credit, lost revenue, and zero visibility into daily performance. Store owners operate reactively, spending mental energy managing operations instead of growing their business.

## 💡 Our Solution

**BazaarOps** is an AI-powered, event-driven retail operating system built specifically for local stores. It transforms traditional kirana shops into intelligent, data-driven micro-enterprises.

Store owners can use BazaarOps to:

- 📦 **Manage Inventory Smartly** – Real-time product tracking with automatic low-stock detection.
- 🧾 **Track Orders Systematically** – Structured order history with easy status updates.
- 💳 **Maintain Credit (Udhar) Securely** – Digital ledger with automatic balance calculation and dispute prevention.
- 📊 **View Daily Business Insights** – Revenue summaries, order counts, and top-selling products generated automatically.
- 📢 **Send Promotions Effortlessly** – Broadcast offers to customers through integrated messaging.

## 🤖 Why It’s Different

BazaarOps doesn’t just digitize retail  IT ADDS INTELLIGENCE TO IT.  
Through an event-driven architecture and AI-powered automation, the system proactively detects business events, updates records in real time, and generates actionable insights.

This reduces human error, prevents revenue leakage, lowers cognitive load, and makes local retail smarter, safer, and scalable.

---

**In one line:** BazaarOps turns reactive neighborhood retail into proactive, AI-powered commerce infrastructure for Bharat.

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🚧 Challenges We Faced & How We Overcame Them

Building BazaarOps was technically exciting BUT  definitely not smooth😭😭😭. We faced multiple real-world engineering challenges while developing an AI-powered, multi-tenant retail operating system under hackathon time pressure.

## 1️⃣ Dependency & Environment Issues

While integrating Supabase, FastAPI, and AI tooling, we ran into multiple version conflicts and dependency mismatches. Some libraries behaved differently across environments, especially during authentication and database integration.

**How we solved it:**  
We standardized versions early, isolated services properly, and documented working configurations. Once stabilized, we avoided unnecessary upgrades and focused only on core features.

---

## 2️⃣ First-Time Working with Claude Agentic Tooling

Implementing an event-driven agent system using Claude’s tool-calling capabilities was new territory. Designing structured prompts, validating AI outputs, and ensuring safe execution without hallucinated database actions required careful planning.

**How we solved it:**  
We enforced strict JSON schemas for AI responses, validated outputs before execution, and separated AI reasoning from database access through a service layer. This made the system safer and more predictable.

---

## 3️⃣ Designing a Multi-Tenant Database

Ensuring complete data isolation between stores while maintaining a shared database was a major architectural challenge. Mistakes here could lead to cross-store data leakage.

**How we solved it:**  
We implemented store-level isolation using `store_id` in every table and enforced Row-Level Security (RLS) policies in Supabase. We also double-validated store ownership at the backend level.

---

## 4️⃣ Microservice & Event-Driven Architecture

Coordinating between dashboard, bots, backend agents, and database events required careful orchestration. Debugging event chains under time pressure was challenging.

**How we solved it:**  
We clearly separated responsibilities into agents and services, and focused on building a minimal but reliable event flow before adding complexity.

---

## ⏳ Biggest Challenge: Time Crunch

Building a scalable SaaS-style architecture in a 7-HR (SERIOUSLY???!?) hackathon timeframe forced us to prioritize ruthlessly. We had to balance clean architecture with shipping a working demo.

**What we learned:**  
Scope control, modular design, and focusing on core value over perfection were critical.

---

This project pushed us technically ~~~ from AI tooling to secure multi-tenant design and strengthened our ability to build scalable, production-oriented systems under pressure.

**Hackathon Prizes**

## 🧠 BazaarOps Fits the Theme LIKE A GLOVE✨✨🤯

BazaarOps strongly aligns with the vision of the **Build India Hackathon (Replit × Anthropic × Devfolio)**  building impactful, AI-driven solutions that solve real problems for India at scale.

India’s economy is powered by millions of neighborhood kirana stores, yet most still operate manually managing inventory in notebooks, tracking credit (udhar) in diaries, and accepting orders through unstructured messaging. BazaarOps directly addresses this large-scale, real-world challenge by transforming traditional retail into an AI-assisted, intelligent operating system.

### 🚀 Alignment with Hackathon Goals

**1. AI-Native Innovation**  
BazaarOps leverages agentic AI tooling to create an event-driven retail system that proactively detects low stock, generates business summaries, manages credit, and automates operational workflows  going beyond simple chatbot functionality.

**2. Real-World Impact in India**  
The solution targets 12M+ kirana stores, addressing practical challenges faced daily by small business owners. It reduces cognitive load, prevents revenue leakage, and introduces data-driven decision-making to grassroots retail.

**3. Scalable Cloud Architecture**  
Built using a multi-tenant database design with strict data isolation, BazaarOps is architected as a SaaS-ready platform capable of serving thousands of independent stores securely.

**4. Practical Use of Modern Tooling**  
The system integrates:
- AI agent orchestration
- Secure cloud database architecture
- Conversational interfaces (Telegram bots)
- Event-driven backend services

This reflects the hackathon’s emphasis on combining cutting-edge AI with practical, deployable applications.

---

BazaarOps is not a proof-of-concept ~ it is a scalable, AI-powered commerce infrastructure built specifically for Bharat. It embodies the hackathon’s mission: using modern AI tools to solve meaningful, high-impact problems in India.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

### You don't learn to ride a bike by watching YouTube.

Yet that's exactly how most people try to learn programming. They sit through hours of tutorials, copy-paste code they half-understand, and walk away feeling productive — until they try to build something from scratch and realize nothing stuck.

---

### The real problems learners face every day:

**🔁 Tutorial Hell**
You've completed 6 courses on React. You still Google "how to use useEffect" every single time. Passive learning gives you familiarity, not understanding. There's a massive gap between *recognizing* code and *writing* it — and no amount of watching bridges that gap.

**🧭 Decision Paralysis**
Before you even start learning, you spend an hour deciding *where* to learn. Udemy or YouTube? This course or that one? Free or paid? By the time you pick, your motivation is gone. Learning shouldn't require research before the research.

**🧩 The Tooling Mess**
A typical self-study session looks like this: YouTube on one tab, VS Code on another, ChatGPT in a third, documentation in a fourth, Stack Overflow in a fifth. You're not learning — you're project-managing your own education across five different tools.

**🤖 AI Gives Answers, Not Understanding**
ChatGPT is incredible — but it solves problems *for* you. You paste an error, get a fix, move on. You never learned *why* it broke. Next time the same thing happens, you paste again. It's an infinite loop of dependency, not growth.

**📉 No Feedback Until It's Too Late**
In a course, you code along and everything works. In the real world, you make a mistake on line 3 and don't find out until line 300. There's no tight feedback loop. No one telling you *in the moment* that you're going down the wrong path.

---

### How Tilper AI Solves This

**One interface. One input. Zero friction.**

You open Tilper. You type what you want to learn. That's the entire onboarding.

- **No courses to browse.** The AI builds your learning path on the fly.
- **No passive watching.** You're writing code from minute one.
- **No answer spoon-feeding.** The AI guides you with hints and questions — like a tutor sitting next to you who refuses to just give you the answer.
- **No tab-switching chaos.** The IDE, the challenges, the AI mentor, the visual explanations — all in one place.
- **No wondering "did I actually learn that?"** You run tests. They pass or they don't. You know exactly where you stand.

---

### What people use it for:

- **"I need to learn Python for my exam next week"** → Type it in. Get a roadmap. Start solving challenges immediately.
- **"I keep forgetting how linked lists work"** → The AI generates a hands-on challenge. You build one. Now you remember.
- **"I want to learn React but every course is 40 hours"** → Tilper gives you focused, bite-sized challenges. Learn the hard parts by building, not watching.
- **"I understand the theory but can't write code on my own"** → That's literally the problem Tilper was built to fix. Every session forces you to write, think, and debug — with support, but without shortcuts.
- **"I'm preparing for coding interviews"** → Generate challenges at the right difficulty. Practice with real-time feedback. See visual breakdowns of algorithms you're struggling with.

---

### The bottom line:

Tilper AI doesn't teach you more. **It makes you learn more** — by putting you in the driver's seat from the very first second and making sure you never fall back into passive consumption.

**Stop watching. Start building. Actually remember what you learned.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Making the AI Actually Teach Instead of Just Give Answers

This was the hardest problem by far. The whole point of Tilper is **learning by doing** — but LLMs naturally want to be helpful. Ask it a coding question and it hands you the full solution on a silver platter. That's the opposite of what we needed.

**The struggle:** Getting the AI to guide without spoiling. It needed to act like a great teacher — give hints, ask leading questions, nudge you toward the answer — not just dump code.

**How I solved it:** A lot of prompt engineering iteration. I built a layered hint system where the AI starts vague and only gets more specific if the student keeps struggling. It took dozens of iterations to get the tone right — helpful but not hand-holding. I also added guardrails that detect when a response contains a full solution and forces the AI to restructure it into a guided explanation instead.

---

### 2. Real-Time Code Execution in the Browser

Building an in-browser IDE that actually **runs code and executes tests** is deceptively complex. It's not just a text editor — it needs to compile, run, catch errors, and return meaningful output, all without a heavy backend round-trip for every keystroke.

**The struggle:** Latency. Early versions had a noticeable delay between clicking "Run" and seeing output. For a learning platform where you're running code dozens of times per session, even a 2-second delay kills the flow.

**How I solved it:** I optimized the execution pipeline and leaned into client-side execution where possible. For languages that couldn't run in the browser, I built a lightweight sandboxed execution layer that minimized cold starts. It's still not instant for every language, but it's fast enough that the feedback loop feels tight.

---

### 3. Generating Challenges That Are Actually Good

Anyone can ask an LLM to "generate a coding challenge." The problem is that most of them are either **too vague, too easy, or completely untestable**.

**The struggle:** I needed challenges that were:
- Clearly defined with specific inputs/outputs
- Appropriately difficult for the student's level
- Actually verifiable with automated tests
- Genuinely educational, not just busy work

Getting all four consistently was brutal. Early versions would generate challenges with ambiguous requirements or edge cases that made the auto-generated tests fail on correct solutions.

**How I solved it:** I built a structured challenge generation pipeline — the AI doesn't just generate a description. It generates the challenge, the test cases, the expected solution, and then **validates them against each other** before presenting anything to the student. If the tests don't pass against the expected solution, the challenge gets regenerated. It added a bit of latency to challenge creation but made the experience 10x more reliable.

---

### 4. Visual Animations That Actually Help

The "Visual" tab was supposed to be a killer feature — watch sorting algorithms sort, see recursion trees branch, understand data structures visually. In practice, generating **meaningful, accurate, and well-timed** animations from AI output was a nightmare.

**The struggle:** The AI would describe a concept, but translating that into a smooth, step-by-step animation required a bridge between natural language explanation and actual visual rendering logic. Static diagrams were easy. Animated, interactive visualizations that **sync with the concept being taught** were a completely different beast.

**How I solved it:** I built a library of animation templates for common concepts and patterns. Instead of generating animations from scratch every time, the AI maps concepts to the closest template and populates it with the relevant data. It's not infinitely flexible yet, but it covers the most common use cases well — and it's a foundation I can keep expanding.

---

### 5. Keeping the UX Dead Simple

This sounds like a non-technical challenge, but it almost derailed the project. I kept adding features — different modes, settings, customization options, dashboards — and the interface started looking like a cockpit.

**The struggle:** The whole promise of Tilper is "just type what you want to learn." Every additional button, menu, or option contradicted that promise.

**How I solved it:** I ruthlessly cut features. If it couldn't be triggered naturally through the chat interface, it probably didn't need a dedicated button. I reduced the entry point to a single input field and two clear actions — **Plan** or **Learn**. Everything else reveals itself only when it's relevant. It was painful to remove things I'd spent time building, but the product got dramatically better every time I deleted something.

**The problem it solves**

TruthTag ,basically, helps us to spot biasing done in the news articles. as we know, nowadays, most of the news articles contains more of the biased statements rather than the actual news and the audience get emotionally triggered and believe those news articles. So to provide the filtered and original news to the readers we have made this project which figure out how much biasing has been done in the news.

**Challenges we ran into**

As a team of freshers, one of our biggest challenges was translating our idea into a working prototype with limited technical experience.
Designing a system that detects bias without overclaiming artificial intelligence was another challenge. We had to carefully choose a rule-based approach that was transparent and explainable.
We also faced difficulty in selecting appropriate emotional trigger words and defining clear bias categories (Low, Moderate, High) in a balanced way.
Additionally, creating a clean and user-friendly interface while managing time constraints required strong teamwork and planning.

**Open Innovation**

TruthTag aligns with the Education and Civic Tech track as it serves as a learning tool that encourages critical thinking, responsible information consumption, and awareness of how language influences public opinion. TruthTag is to spot the biasing done in news articles.

**The problem it solves**

SkillMap AI solves this by:

• Allowing users to select a career role (Frontend, Backend, AI, Data Science, etc.)
• Conducting a short MCQ-based assessment
• Analyzing their performance using visual charts
• Detecting weak skill areas automatically
• Generating a daily improvement routine

**Challenges we ran into**

During development, I faced multiple challenges:

• Handling multi-page navigation using pure JavaScript without frameworks
• Fixing issues where the login page duplicated or did not redirect correctly
• Managing dynamic question generation for different roles
• Integrating Chart.js for performance visualization
• Ensuring state persistence like streak tracking using localStorage
• Connecting frontend with Flask backend for saving scores and leaderboard

I solved these by restructuring page routing logic, debugging event handlers, simplifying the codebase into single files, and testing each feature independently before integration.

These optimizations made the application stable, faster, and easier to maintain.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. The "Silence" of Victims (Safety & Discrimination)
Traditional reporting often forces students to reveal their identity, leading to fear of retaliation from peers or faculty.

The Solution: By using Device ID Hashing, students can report issues like institutional discrimination (caste, religion, or financial status) and harassment with 100% anonymity.

Women's Safety: It addresses the lack of immediate response during threats through a one-tap SOS button that bypasses bureaucracy to alert security instantly.

2. Outdated Academic Frameworks
Decision-makers are often unaware that lab equipment is broken or that the curriculum has fallen behind industry standards.

The Solution: The portal allows students to report poor laboratory conditions and a lack of teaching exposure. This "Collective Intelligence" provides administrators with real-time data on where the academic infrastructure is failing.

3. Invisible Infrastructure Failures
Issues like frequent electricity disruptions, poor water supply, and unhygienic restrooms often go ignored until they become a crisis.

The Solution: The Campus Heatmap feature visualizes "high-complaint zones." If multiple students report a water leak in "Block B," the map glows red in that area, forcing the administration to prioritize that specific repair.

4. Absence of Mental Health Support
High-pressure environments often lack full-time counselors, and students may feel stigmatized seeking help in person.

The Solution: The portal provides a discreet, non-intimidating digital channel to request mental health support or report stress-related challenges without public exposure.

5. Misleading Transparency (The "Placement" Gap)
Colleges often advertise 100% placement rates that don't reflect reality.

The Solution: Through the Reviews and Trust Score section, students can provide honest, anonymous feedback on career prospects and placement quality, creating a "Trust Score" that accurately reflects the campus value.

6. Slow Administrative Response
Standard grievance letters often sit on desks for weeks.

The Solution: The Live Tracking System (similar to a delivery app) keeps the administration accountable. Students can see when a complaint moves from "Submitted" to "In Progress" to "Resolved," eliminating the "black hole" of administrative silence.

**Challenges we ran into**

Real Issues:

IP address logging

Browser fingerprinting

Firebase auth tracking

Metadata inside uploaded images (EXIF data)

GPS precision revealing identity

 Solution:

Strip image metadata before storing

Don’t log IPs (or hash them)

Use session hashing instead of login for anonymous mode

Separate complaint DB from identity DB

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/park-conscious-6b25) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.parkconscious.in/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> find, reserve, and pay

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Urban parking is highly unorganized, time-consuming, and inefficient. Drivers often spend 15–25 minutes searching for parking, which increases traffic congestion, fuel wastage, and daily stress. At the same time, many parking spaces remain underutilized because there is no unified digital system connecting drivers with available parking providers.

Park Conscious makes parking easier by helping users quickly find nearby parking spaces, view pricing and details, and move toward digital booking and payments. For parking owners, it simplifies operations by providing tools to digitally manage spaces, track usage, and monitor revenue instead of relying on manual registers or cash handling.

In the long term, the platform aims to make parking safer and smarter using technologies like automated vehicle entry/exit logging, data-driven insights, and integration with smart city systems.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was handling location-based data and map integration reliably. While building the “Find Nearby Parking” feature, I had to work with Google Maps APIs, browser geolocation, and large JSON datasets of parking locations. Initially, issues like inconsistent coordinate formats, slow data loading, and map marker performance caused bugs and incorrect results.

I solved this by cleaning and standardising parking data using Python (BeautifulSoup + Pandas), converting fields like latitude, longitude, and pricing into consistent numeric formats, and optimising how parking data is loaded and filtered on the frontend.

**Open Innovation**

Park Conscious fits into Open Innovation because it solves a real-world urban problem that spans multiple sectors, including mobility, smart cities, infrastructure, and digital payments. The solution is not limited to a single industry; it can be integrated with government smart city initiatives, private parking operators, commercial buildings, EV infrastructure providers, and urban mobility platforms.

**The problem it solves**

# Bharat Mat  
### A Secure, Verifiable & Interactive Platform for Voter Awareness and Misinformation Control

**Bharat Mat** is a next-generation civic technology platform designed to combat political misinformation, improve voter awareness, and help citizens clearly understand complex democratic reforms such as **One Nation One Election (ONOE)** through interactive simulations, AI-powered fact-checking, and official-source verification.

Built by **Team Tensor Troops**, Bharat Mat bridges the gap between voters and trustworthy political information in an era of deepfakes, AI-generated propaganda, and fragmented civic knowledge.

---

## Problem Statement

Modern democracies face a growing crisis of trust and information overload:

- Political misinformation spreads faster than verified truth  
- AI-generated deepfakes mislead voters at scale  
- Reforms like **ONOE** are poorly understood due to lack of visual and interactive explanation  
- Existing tools are fragmented, text-heavy, and non-interactive  
- Voters lack a single, trusted source to verify claims and understand real-world impact  

**Bharat Mat** addresses these challenges by combining **AI, visualization, verification, and privacy-preserving identity systems** into one unified platform.

---

## Purpose & Vision

The goal of Bharat Mat is to:

- Empower voters with **clear, verifiable, and explainable information**
- Reduce the spread and impact of political misinformation
- Make democratic reforms understandable through **visual simulations**
- Provide a **single source of truth** backed by official documents
- Restore trust using **transparent AI + human verification**

---

## Key Features

### AI-Powered Misinformation Detection
- Detects **text, image, audio, and video** misinformation
- Classifies content as **Fake / Manipulated / Misleading**
- Displays **deepfake forensic heatmaps** as visual proof
- Links directly to **original documents or raw footage**
- Blockchain-logged verdicts ensure immutability

---

### Democracy & ONOE Impact Simulator
- Interactive **India Map–based Digital Twin**
- Visualizes state-wise tenure extension 🟢 and curtailment 🔴
- Sliders simulate governance efficiency vs accountability
- Shows required constitutional amendments
- Clear pros & cons instead of political narratives

---

### ECI Situation Room
- Real-time fetching of **official Election Commission of India (ECI)** circulars
- AI-generated summaries grounded only in official sources
- Interactive election timelines
- One-tap access to original ECI PDFs
- Calendar sync for critical election dates

---

### Campaign & Policy Intelligence Hub
- Source-backed verification of party claims
- Downloadable manifestos and policy documents
- PM / CM candidate comparisons
- No opinionated ranking — only verified data

---

### Secure & Private Voter Access
- DigiLocker / Aadhaar-based voter login
- **Zero-Knowledge Proofs** for privacy protection
- Prevents bots, fake users, and coordinated manipulation
- No tracking or profiling of voter behavior

---

### Smart Voter Assistance
- Interactive polling booth mapping
- Automated voter support center
- Real-time alerts and personalized reminders
- Works on mobile-first, low-bandwidth environments

---

### WhatsApp & SMS Verification (Planned)
- Forward suspicious messages to a national WhatsApp number
- Instant reply with:
  - Fake / Real verdict
  - Official source link
  - Simple explanation
- Designed for rural users and senior citizens

---

## Technical Architecture

- **Frontend:** React Native (Expo), TypeScript  
- **Backend:** FastAPI / Node.js (Express)  
- **AI Stack:**  
  - LLaMA-3, Mixtral  
  - Sentence Transformers  
  - LangChain + FAISS (RAG)  
  - Vision-Language Models (VLMs)  
- **Databases:** PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Pinecone  
- **Messaging & Alerts:** Twilio (SMS & WhatsApp APIs)  
- **Security:** Blockchain-based verdict logging, Zero-Knowledge Proofs  
- **Architecture:** Modular microservices + agentic AI  

Scalable from **1 citizen to 1 million citizens**.

---

## Impact

- Reduced misinformation exposure  
- Improved civic understanding  
- Higher informed voter participation  
- Transparent, proof-based political awareness  
- Stronger trust between citizens and democratic institutions  

---

## Future Scope

- Regional language expansion (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, etc.)
- Integration with India’s Digital Public Infrastructure:
  - DigiLocker
  - UMANG
- State-wise journalist & fact-checker verification network
- Nationwide WhatsApp & SMS misinformation gateway
- Deeper government and civil society partnerships

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I ran into

Building trust in AI fact-checks was difficult, as simple true/false labels felt unreliable for political content.  
We solved this by adding explainable evidence like deepfake heatmaps and direct links to official ECI sources.

Handling misinformation across text, images, and videos increased complexity.  
This was addressed using a modular AI pipeline with NLP, vision-language models, and RAG grounded in verified data.

Real-time performance and voter privacy were critical concerns.  
We improved scalability using async microservices and ensured privacy through DigiLocker-based verification with Zero-Knowledge Proofs.

Explaining ONOE clearly was challenging, so we built an interactive map-based simulator instead of long text.

**Open Innovation**

This project addresses a real-world civic problem: misinformation and voter awareness using emerging technologies like AI, blockchain, and interactive simulations.  

It combines public data, official government sources, and modern AI systems in a novel, user-facing way.  

The platform is designed to be extensible, allowing integration with existing digital public infrastructure and third-party services.  

By enabling transparency, explainability, and citizen participation, it creates a scalable foundation others can build upon.  

The solution is not limited to elections and can be adapted to multiple governance and public-information use cases.

### AquaRisk
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aquarisk-532c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/codemuggle09/AquaRisk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Predicting Safety for 60M Indians.

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Folium](https://img.shields.io/badge/Folium-333333?style=flat-square) ![Plotly](https://img.shields.io/badge/Plotly-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Fluoride contamination is a 'silent killer' affecting over 60 million people in India. Because it is colorless and odorless, rural communities often realize their water is toxic only after developing irreversible dental or skeletal fluorosis.

AquaRisk bridges this critical information gap by:

Predicting Risk at Scale: Using chemical markers like pH and Calcium to predict fluoride levels where laboratory testing is unavailable.

Human-Centric Communication: Translating complex hydrogeochemical data into intuitive Fuzzy Risk Labels (Low, Medium, High) for non-technical users.

Community Connectivity: Automatically linking high-risk Pincodes to the nearest safe water sources and mapped NGOs like WaterAid India for immediate intervention.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major hurdle was Data Imbalance. Our dataset of 16,776 samples was heavily skewed toward 'Safe' readings, which caused initial ML models to overlook high-risk 'Red Zones'.

The Solution: We implemented SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) to balance our classes, ensuring our Random Forest Classifier achieved 93% accuracy even for the rarest, most dangerous contamination levels.

Technically, we also faced a 'Cluttered UI' challenge. Judges initially found the raw data overwhelming. We overcame this by redesigning the interface using a Two-Stage Workflow: a simple community safety portal for citizens and a Technical Dashboard for experts, separating noise from insight.

**Sustainable Development Goals**

AquaRisk is a system designed to provide climate and health resilience through advanced monitoring and governance of freshwater resources. It specifically aligns with the following goals:
+3


SDG 6.3 (Water Quality & Pollution): Our platform addresses the critical need for detecting geogenic pollution like fluoride, which poses a severe ecological and health risk. By using a 93% accurate Random Forest model, we provide a scalable alternative to expensive lab testing, enabling immediate intervention in "data-dark" rural areas.
+4


SDG 6.B (Community Participation): AquaRisk democratizes water intelligence. By translating complex hydrogeochemical data into an intuitive Fuzzy Risk Score, we empower local communities and non-technical health workers to make informed decisions about water safety.
+4


SDG 11.5 & 11.B (Disaster Resilience): Since groundwater quality is under growing stress due to climate change, our Regional Trends map acts as an early-warning system. It identifies contamination corridors before long-term health damage occurs, allowing governments to prioritize infrastructure like defluoridation plants.

Team **Arch** -- [Monisha Badugu](https://github.com/codemuggle09)

> Bridging people in need with NGOs that care

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Finding help during times of need is often harder than it should be.

People facing issues like food insecurity, medical needs, shelter, or safety usually don’t know:

Which NGOs operate near them

What kind of help those NGOs actually provide

How to contact them quickly and safely

Existing information is:

scattered across different websites

outdated or hard to verify

not location-specific

overwhelming during stressful moments

As a result, people either delay seeking help or give up entirely.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building this project, I faced issues with state management and data flow across pages. Category selection worked visually, but selected data was not being passed correctly during navigation, causing NGO results not to display.

I resolved this by restructuring how state was handled, explicitly passing selected filters between pages and maintaining a clear separation between original and filtered NGO data. I also avoided over-engineering early by focusing on a frontend-first MVP, which helped me stabilize the core user flow before adding polish.

Through this, I learned the importance of clear data flow, proper state management, and debugging existing logic instead of continuously adding new code.

**Sustainable Development Goals**

This project supports multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals by improving access to nearby NGOs that provide essential services such as food, healthcare, education, and social support. By making local help easier to discover and contact, the platform contributes to No Poverty (SDG 1), Zero Hunger (SDG 2), Good Health and Well-being (SDG 3), Quality Education (SDG 4), and Reduced Inequalities (SDG 10). Overall, it strengthens community-level support systems, aligning with Sustainable Cities and Communities (SDG 11).

### Civic-saarthi
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/civicsaarthi-fcfe) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://GitHub.com/jagritiuppal158/civic-saarthii) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> 3R's Report Resolve Rewards

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Urban civic issues like garbage overflow, potholes, water leakage, and broken streetlights are common in cities, but the process to report them is complicated and inefficient. Citizens often do not know which department to contact, and government portals are fragmented across multiple platforms with confusing procedures.
Because of this:
Complaints get misrouted or ignored
Citizens lose trust and stop reporting issues
Authorities receive unstructured data, making prioritization difficult
Small issues escalate into larger environmental and infrastructure problems
There is no intelligent system that helps citizens identify the correct authority, understand issue urgency, or get guidance on whether the problem can be resolved locally. At the same time, governments lack real-time, structured civic data to make sustainable urban planning decisions.
Our project solves this gap by creating an AI-powered civic intelligence platform that simplifies reporting for citizens while converting complaints into actionable insights for authorities.
It makes existing tasks:
Easier — single platform, voice/text/image reporting
Faster — automatic issue classification and authority routing
Smarter — predictive analysis of recurring civic problems
More sustainable — tracks waste, water, and infrastructure stress trends
This transforms isolated complaints into a connected civic intelligence system that benefits both citizens and city administrations.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an AI-powered civic intelligence platform involved both technical and real-world challenges:
1. Multimodal Data Processing
Handling text, voice, and image inputs together was complex. We had to ensure accurate speech-to-text conversion and reliable image recognition for civic issues like potholes, garbage, and water leakage.
2. Issue Classification Accuracy
Civic complaints often use informal language. Training the system to correctly classify issues and detect urgency from varied descriptions required fine-tuning NLP models.
3. Authority Mapping
Different cities and regions have different departments and jurisdictions. Mapping issues to the correct authority dynamically was challenging due to lack of standardized public data.
4. Realistic Status Tracking
Government systems are not always integrated via APIs, making automated status updates difficult. We designed a hybrid tracking approach to handle this limitation.
5. Balancing AI Guidance vs. Misinformation
Providing citizen self-resolution guidance needed careful validation to avoid unsafe or incorrect suggestions.
6. Scalability & Real-Time Processing
Ensuring the system remains fast and responsive while processing AI models and storing large civic datasets required backend optimization.
7. Data Privacy & Security
Handling location-based civic complaints required secure authentication, user data protection, and safe data storage practices.
