[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/gujjusense-3938) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ThatNocturnalCoder/GujjuSense) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Bridging Silence, Connecting Gujarat

![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mediapipe](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mediapipe-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Bridging the Regional Accessibility Gap

While assistive technology has advanced rapidly, a significant void remains for regional Indian languages. Most sign language tools today focus heavily on American Sign Language (ASL) or standardized Indian Sign Language (ISL), often overlooking the nuances of regional contexts. In Gujarat, the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (DHH) community faces a "double barrier": the general communication gap with the hearing world, and a specific lack of digital tools that support Gujarati-contextualized communication.

This isolation creates friction in education, healthcare, and daily social life. Hearing individuals often lack the means to communicate even basic ideas to DHH neighbors, while DHH individuals lack accessible, interactive, and regionally relevant resources to learn and express themselves. GujjuSense solves this by leveraging AI to create a localized, accessible, and intelligent communication ecosystem.

What People Can Use It For
GujjuSense is designed as a dual-purpose platform: an educational tool for learners and a utility tool for daily communication.

1. Interactive, AI-Powered Learning
Gamified Skill Acquisition: Unlike static videos, the app uses Computer Vision (MediaPipe) to "watch" the learner. Users can practice Gujarati Sign Language (GSL) alphabets and numbers, receiving real-time validation (e.g., "Correct! 🎉" or guidance on finger placement).

Infinite AI Tutor: Powered by Google Gemini, the "AI Tutor" breaks the limits of pre-recorded content. Users can ask for lessons on any custom topic—from "Medical emergency signs" to "Family relationships"—and the AI instantly generates a structured lesson plan with quizzes and explanations in English and Hindi.

2. Real-Time Communication Bridge ("Setu")
Text-to-Sign Translation: A hearing person can type a phrase in Gujarati (e.g., "કેમ છો" - How are you?), and the app instantly retrieves and plays the corresponding sign language animation. This is vital for interactions in shops, banks, or government offices.

Voice-to-Sign Accessibility: To make interaction even more natural, the Voice-to-Sign feature allows users to speak directly into the app. It converts spoken Gujarati audio into sign language animations in real-time, facilitating smoother conversations without the need to type.

3. Self-Correction & Practice
Live Sign Detector: The app serves as a "digital mirror" for DHH individuals and learners. By visualizing the hand skeleton and recognizing gestures on the fly, it provides a safe, judgment-free environment for users to refine their signing accuracy before engaging in real-world conversations.

How It Makes Tasks Easier & Safer
Removing Geographical Barriers: Quality sign language education is often restricted to specialized institutes in major cities. GujjuSense democratizes this, putting a personal tutor in the pocket of anyone with a smartphone, regardless of their location in Gujarat.

Empowering Emergency Communication: In medical or legal situations, clarity is critical. The instant translation features ensure that specific, urgent messages can be conveyed visually and accurately, reducing the risks associated with misinterpretation.

Building Confidence: For hearing individuals, the fear of "doing it wrong" often prevents engagement. The app’s feedback loop builds confidence, encouraging hearing people to initiate conversations and integrating the DHH community more fully into society.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
Building GujjuSense was not just about connecting APIs; it was a battle against concurrency, resource management, and the architectural complexities of running real-time AI on a mobile device. Every feature that looks seamless now—the live tracking, the instant translation—was forged through hours of debugging "invisible" errors.

Here are the most significant hurdles I overcame:

1. The "Ghost Image" Race Condition (Concurrency Nightmare)
The most grueling challenge was a catastrophic crash (java.lang.IllegalStateException: Image is already closed) that would randomly kill the app during live detection.

The Struggle: This wasn't a logic error I could see. It was a race condition deep within the GPU pipeline. The CameraX analyzer runs at 30+ frames per second, while the MediaPipe AI (running on a background thread) takes a few milliseconds to process each frame. The camera was "closing" and deleting the image frame from memory before the AI had finished looking at it. The AI would wake up to process a "ghost" image that no longer existed, causing a fatal crash.

The Fix: I had to fundamentally re-architect the image processing pipeline. Instead of passing the live reference, I implemented a defensive "Copy-First" strategy. I forced the app to convert the raw YUV camera feed into a persistent Bitmap copy on the main thread before dispatching it to the background executor. This effectively decoupled the camera's lifecycle from the AI's processing speed, stabilizing the tracking without dropping frames.

2. Dependency Hell & The "Zombie" Classes
Integrating the cutting-edge Gemini 1.5 Flash model alongside MediaPipe created a massive dependency conflict that rendered the app unbuildable for days.

The Struggle: The app compiled fine but crashed instantly upon launching the "AI Tutor" with a cryptic NoClassDefFoundError: HttpTimeout. It turned out that the Google AI SDK and Firebase libraries were fighting over different versions of the Ktor networking client. Android Studio's automated dependency resolution failed, leaving the app with missing networking classes at runtime. It felt like trying to solve a puzzle where the pieces kept changing shape.

The Fix: I had to perform a "nuclear" clean of the project and manually override Gradle's dependency tree. I explicitly forced the inclusion of specific Ktor serialization and OkHttp libraries (okhttp:4.12.0), strictly managing the transitive dependencies to ensure the AI brain could finally talk to the internet without crashing the networking layer.

3. The "Silent Corruption" of the Neural Network
Early in development, the app would crash immediately upon opening the camera with zero meaningful logs.

The Struggle: The logs pointed to generic initialization errors. I spent hours auditing the permission flows and camera hardware access. The breakthrough came when I manually audited the binary assets.

The Fix: I discovered that the hand_landmarker.task file (the "brain" of the vision system) was corrupted. It was a 4KB HTML placeholder instead of the actual 3MB binary model. This taught me a valuable lesson: never trust the download. I now have strict validation checks that verify the integrity of AI models before the app even attempts to load them.

4. Balancing Real-Time Latency vs. Accuracy
Running a Vision Model (MediaPipe) and a Large Language Model (Gemini) simultaneously on a mobile CPU is resource-intensive.

The Struggle: Initially, the UI would freeze every time the hand detector ran, dropping the app to a sluggish 5 frames per second. The "Main Thread" was choked by heavy mathematical calculations.

The Fix: I implemented a strict Threading Architecture. The "Eyes" (Vision) were moved to a dedicated SingleThreadExecutor, while the "Brain" (Gemini) was confined to Coroutine Dispatchers.IO. This ensured that the UI remained buttery smooth (60 FPS) for the user, even while the phone was performing heavy matrix calculations and network requests in the background.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/woc-2f68) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1P_ivz7dDQKAu7dR74VB3eBp-2lJlQ8iIa0Fd3dn_aUk/edit?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Making the Ak-dskit Data Science library crash-pro

![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# Making Ak-dskit "Crash-Proof" for Beginners

Currently, the **Ak-dskit** library has a high barrier to entry for new developers. The demonstration scripts—which are supposed to teach users how to use the library—frequently crash due to missing dependencies, unhandled logic errors, and strict type requirements.

My project solves these critical stability issues across three key modules:

## 1. Solves "Dependency Hell" in Data IO & Modeling
* **The Problem:** Previously, if a user tried to run the standard demos without having *every* optional library installed (like PyArrow, CatBoost, or Optuna), the scripts would crash immediately.
* **The Solution:** I implemented **"Safe Mode"** patterns using defensive `try-except` blocks. Now, if an optional library is missing, the code detects it and gracefully skips that specific feature with a friendly warning instead of crashing the entire program.

## 2. Fixes Critical Logic Bugs in EDA
* **The Problem:** The Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) module contained a logic flaw where it expected a Dictionary return type. In certain environments where the library returned a simple health score (Float), the script crashed with an `AttributeError`.
* **The Solution:** I implemented dynamic type checking (`isinstance`). The code now intelligently handles both return types, ensuring the "Health Check" report works in all environments.

## 3. Enforces Type Safety for Machine Learning
* **The Problem:** The Modeling demo was broken for classification tasks, throwing `ValueError: Unknown label type: continuous` because target variables were being treated as floats.
* **The Solution:** I refactored the data preparation pipeline to strictly enforce integer casting (`.astype(int)`), allowing Scikit-Learn classifiers to run successfully "out of the box."

### Impact
This project transforms Ak-dskit from a fragile library into a **robust, beginner-friendly tool**, ensuring that new contributors can run all 15 demos successfully on their first try.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. Simulating "Broken" Environments
The biggest challenge was testing the "Safe Mode" features. Since my development machine had all libraries (CatBoost, Optuna, PyArrow) installed, the code always worked for me.
* **The Hurdle:** I couldn't reproduce the crashes new users were seeing.
* **The Fix:** I had to create multiple virtual environments and intentionally uninstall specific packages to trigger the `ImportError` and verify that my `try-except` blocks successfully caught the failures without crashing the script.

## 2. Debugging "Invisible" Return Types
The logic error in the EDA module (`03_eda_demo.py`) was difficult to trace because the crash was inconsistent.
* **The Hurdle:** The `demo_health_check` function would sometimes return a Dictionary (causing the script to pass) and other times a Float (causing it to fail). It wasn't immediately obvious *why* the return type was changing.
* **The Fix:** I used print-debugging to inspect the `type(report)` at runtime in different scenarios. This revealed that the core library has a fallback mechanism that returns a simple score when generation fails. I implemented `isinstance()` checks to handle this polymorphism dynamically.

## 3. Deciphering Scikit-Learn Errors
The "Unknown label type: continuous" error in the modeling demo was cryptic.
* **The Hurdle:** The data looked correct visually, but Scikit-Learn's classifiers are extremely strict about data types.
* **The Fix:** I realized that even though the numbers were whole (0, 1), they were stored as `floats` (0.0, 1.0). Explicitly casting the target variable using `.astype(int)` solved the issue instantly, teaching me the importance of strict type enforcement in ML pipelines.

> Explaining market signals using price & sentiment

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![GRAPHVIZ](https://img.shields.io/badge/GRAPHVIZ-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rule-based Analysis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rule--based%20Analysis-333333?style=flat-square) ![Log File Analysis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Log%20File%20Analysis-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves

Retail investors often rely on isolated indicators such as price trends or basic technical signals when analyzing stocks. These indicators provide limited context and do not explain why certain movements may be happening. At the same time, qualitative signals like news sentiment are usually analyzed separately, if at all.

This project explores how price-based indicators and simple sentiment signals can be combined in a transparent and explainable way. By analysing historical price data alongside sampled news sentiment, the tool helps users understand how different signals interact rather than treating them as independent sources of information.

The goal is not prediction or profit generation, but improved interpretability. It makes market analysis easier by bringing multiple signals into a single, clearly explained workflow that can be inspected, modified, and extended.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into

One of the main challenges was keeping the analysis realistic without relying on live or paid market data sources. Many existing tools assume continuous API access, which can hide complexity and make results difficult to verify.

To address this, I designed the system to work entirely with local, well-structured datasets. This required extra care in defining clear data formats and separating real analysis logic from simulated inputs. While this reduced scope, it improved transparency and made every output reproducible.

Another challenge was combining qualitative sentiment signals with quantitative price indicators in a way that remained explainable. Instead of using complex models, I relied on simple, rule-based combinations and clearly documented how each signal influenced the final output.

**AOPS**

This project fits the AOPS track because it focuses on clear, structured reasoning rather than prediction or automation. Instead of treating market analysis as a black box, the system breaks it down into simple, well-defined steps such as numerical indicators, rule-based sentiment interpretation, and transparent decision logic.

Each part of the analysis is explicit and traceable, similar to how mathematical problems are solved step by step. This makes it easier to see how different inputs affect the outcome and to reproduce the results. The overall focus is on understanding and explanation, which aligns closely with the AOPS approach to problem solving and logical thinking.

**The problem it solves**

****🧩 The Problem It Solves****

Open-source contribution has a steep and intimidating entry barrier for beginners. Repositories assume contributors already know how to explore complex codebases, set up environments, choose suitable issues, and create professional pull requests. In reality, beginners often struggle with:

**Not knowing where to start in large projects**

- Difficulty picking issues that match their experience
- Fear of making mistakes in branching, commits, and PRs
- Repeated setup failures due to unclear instructions
- Giving up before making their first contribution

Tutorials, documentation, and AI tools exist, but they deliver isolated information instead of context-aware, repository-specific guidance. This leads to analysis paralysis and prevents beginners from transitioning into active contributors.

🤔 ****How OnboardHub Solves This****

OnboardHub converts a confusing GitHub repository into a guided, beginner-friendly onboarding journey — taking users from exploration to their first merged PR.

✨ ****Key capabilities:****

Beginner Readiness Score
Evaluates documentation quality, setup clarity, and repo hygiene.

- **Issue Skill Mapping**
Classifies issues into Beginner, Intermediate, and Advanced so contributors don’t have to guess.

- **Suggested First Actions**
Tells beginners exactly what to do first (run locally, read key files, pick issues).

- **Setup Automation & Support**
Auto-generates setup commands to reduce trial-and-error with environments and build steps.

- **First PR Assistant**
Provides step-by-step guidance for:

- Branch creation
- Commit message formatting
- PR description drafting
- Pre-flight checks

****🎯 Impact****

By reducing confusion and setup pain, OnboardHub helps beginners:

- Contribute faster
- Build confidence
- Avoid common mistakes
- Successfully ship their first open-source PR

**OnboardHub** doesn’t just explain open source — it helps you start contributing.

**Challenges we ran into**

****⚠️ Challenges I Ran Into****

Building OnboardHub presented several interesting challenges because the goal wasn’t just to fetch GitHub data, but to interpret it into actionable guidance for beginners. This required balancing technical feasibility, UX clarity, and education value.

1️⃣ ****Classifying Issue Difficulty Without Trusting Labels****

**Problem**:
Most repositories either lack proper issue labels or misuse tags like good first issue, making difficulty inference unreliable.

**Solution:**
I created a lightweight difficulty classifier that combines multiple signals:

- Issue labels (when present)
- Description length and clarity
- Comment activity and discussion tone
- Keywords related to docs, UI, config, refactor, etc.

This allowed issues to be grouped into 
**Beginner / Intermediate / Advanced** without depending solely on labels.

2️⃣ ****Measuring “Beginner-Friendliness” of a Repository****

**Problem**:
GitHub metrics (stars, forks) don’t indicate whether a repo is approachable for first-time contributors.

**Solution:**
I introduced a Beginner Readiness Score based on factors like:

- Availability of README, CONTRIBUTING, setup docs
- Installation and run instructions
- Test/config presence
- Clarity and structure of repository scaffolding

The challenge was balancing signal strength without overcomplicating the scoring logic.

3️⃣ ****Auto-Generating Setup Commands Across Tech Stacks****

**Problem:**
Repositories vary wildly in tooling — Node, Python, Go, Rust, etc. There’s no universal way to detect “run this project”.

**Solution:**
I implemented a heuristic-based detection layer that:

- Scans for config files (package.json, requirements.txt, etc.)
- Infers package managers and run scripts
- Falls back gracefully if detection fails

This helped beginners reduce environment-confusion without over-promising automation.

4️⃣ ****Designing Guidance Without Taking Away Learning****

**Problem:**
Suggesting how to approach issues risked becoming “just solve it for me”, which removes educational value and ethical clarity.

**Solution:**
I structured suggestions to:

- Point contributors to relevant files/directories
- Highlight skills required
- Suggest safe starting points
- Avoid code generation or direct fixes
- This kept users in control while reducing ambiguity.

5️⃣ ****Preventing UI Overload From Multiple Features****

**Problem:**
The platform includes evaluation, issue filtering, setup detection, and PR guidance. Showing everything at once was overwhelming.

**Solution:**
I designed a journey-based UI flow:

****Evaluate → Understand → Act → PR****

****Beginner Readiness → Suggested First Action → Issue Selection → First PR Assistant****

Progressive disclosure made the experience smoother and more intuitive.

6️⃣ ****Handling GitHub API Limits & Latency****

**Problem:**
GitHub rate limits and slow network responses initially resulted in partial analyses and timeouts.

**Solution:**
I implemented:

- Batched API calls
- Local caching for repeated fetches
- Loading states and graceful degradation for missing data
- This made the experience reliable even under constraints.

****🧠 Key Takeaway****

The hardest part wasn’t fetching data — it was transforming raw repository information into meaningful, beginner-friendly guidance without overwhelming users or automating away the learning process.

**OnboardHub** ultimately works by guiding contributors through their first PR, not replacing their thinking.

**AOPS**

**OnboardHub** fits into the AOPS (Automation of Processes & Systems) track by automating and simplifying the open-source onboarding workflow for beginners.

Contributing to open source is currently a highly manual and fragmented process — users have to read long documentation, figure out setup steps, search for suitable issues, and understand Git workflows on their own. This often leads to confusion, setup failures, and contributor drop-off.

OnboardHub automates this entire process by:
- Analyzing a GitHub repository to evaluate beginner readiness
- Automatically categorizing issues by difficulty (Beginner / Intermediate / Pro)
- Generating clear setup commands to run projects locally
- Providing a guided, step-by-step First PR Assistant for branching, committing, and opening pull requests

By converting a complex, error-prone manual workflow into a structured and guided system, OnboardHub reduces friction, saves time, and helps users confidently complete their first open-source contribution.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/benchmark-cleanup-0509) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15uNpclMojLs94hysHD5oODeM-pakRYii/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=100462587352934131192&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> also maybe clean up the benchmarks

![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![ONNX](https://img.shields.io/badge/ONNX-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This project solves the critical "production gap" that currently restricts Kornia to research environments by eliminating the technical barriers that prevent high-performance deployment. Specifically, it addresses:

 (1) Performance Bottlenecks, where legacy Python control flow and .item() calls create "Graph Breaks" that force slow CPU execution and block PyTorch 2.0 optimizations like kernel fusion;

 (2) Deployment Deadends, where these dynamic structures fail to translate to static graphs, making it impossible to export models to ONNX, TensorRT, or edge devices;

 (3) Reliability Risks, by replacing the current lack of safeguards with a strict verification suite that prevents "silent failures" (such as crashes with dynamic batch sizes) from reaching production pipelines.

**The problem it solves**

Many learners struggle with unorganized study resources, scattered content, and inefficient learning flows across different platforms. Switching between multiple websites and tools for different subjects creates confusion, reduces focus, and wastes time.

Vocab Voyage solves this by providing a single, structured e-learning platform where users can access multiple study courses in one place. It simplifies learning by:

-  Organizing courses in a clear and structured format

-  Making navigation simple and intuitive

-  Saving time by reducing platform switching

-  Improving focus with centralized learning resources

-  Making learning more accessible through a clean web interface

People can use Vocab Voyage to:

- Study different subjects from one platform

- Follow organized learning paths
 
- Learn more efficiently without distractions

- Manage their study resources in a structured way

- Build consistent study habits

**Challenges we ran into**

While building Vocab Voyage, I faced several challenges:

UI structuring issues: Organizing multiple courses in a clean and user-friendly layout was difficult at first. I solved this by redesigning the layout structure and using reusable components to maintain consistency.

Navigation flow: Managing smooth navigation between different sections and courses required careful planning. I fixed this by restructuring the routing and improving component hierarchy.

Responsiveness: Making the website responsive across different screen sizes was challenging. I overcame this by using responsive design principles and flexible layouts.

Content organization: Managing and displaying different course contents efficiently required better data structuring, which I solved by modularizing the content and separating logic from UI.

These challenges helped me improve my understanding of frontend architecture, UI/UX design, and project structuring.

> World holiday Calendar

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/pytest-333333?style=flat-square) ![WordPress](https://img.shields.io/badge/WordPress-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Proposal 1:
This proposal extends the Open World Holidays Framework’s financial and bank holiday module to include major global economies—starting with China, Japan, and the UK. It involves integrating official market and bank holiday calendars, standardizing holiday metadata (names, dates, affected exchanges, and closure reasons), and building a scalable architecture to support future additions.

The enhancement maintains consistency with existing US, India, and ECB data while making the framework more globally relevant. It enables investors to track major market closures in one place, reduces reliance on multiple external calendars, and adds long-term value for trading, investing, and analytics tools by providing a foundation to easily onboard more economies.

Proposal 2:
This proposal strengthens OpenPrinting’s security and reliability by extending fuzz testing to its Go and Python-based projects using OSS-Fuzz. It focuses on integrating key components such as ipp-usb, goipp, pycups, and pyppd, developing fuzzing harnesses, and creating structured seed corpora to continuously test critical input surfaces like network data, printer descriptions, and protocol messages.

The enhancement builds upon existing C/C++ fuzzing infrastructure while bringing language parity across the ecosystem. It enables early detection of crashes and security vulnerabilities, reduces long-term stability risks, and provides a reusable, scalable fuzzing framework that future contributors can easily extend to additional OpenPrinting projects.

Proposal 3:
This proposal improves the Keploy blog website by fixing existing UI, UX, and performance issues while introducing modern blog features such as dark/light mode, likes and comments, sticky social share buttons, and built-in search. It focuses on enhancing layout consistency, responsiveness, readability, and overall site performance to deliver a smoother and more engaging reading experience.

The enhancement builds on Keploy’s existing blog architecture and resolves known repository issues while aligning the platform with modern developer blog standards. It improves content discoverability, increases user engagement, reduces load times, and provides a scalable foundation for future UI and feature enhancements that support Keploy’s growing community.

**Challenges we ran into**

Proposal 1 (challenges):
One of the main challenges was finding reliable and authentic sources for holiday data across different countries. To address this, I sought help from my sister, who works in HR at Ciena and regularly tracks holiday calendars for employees based in multiple countries. She shared some of the trusted sources she uses for official holiday data. I then cross-verified this information with my own research and publicly available sources to ensure accuracy and build a dependable holiday calendar dataset.

Proposal 2 (challenges):
Understanding and mapping complex, multi-language codebases (Go, Python, C/C++),
Identifying the most critical and fuzz-worthy input surfaces,
Writing effective fuzzing harnesses for stateful protocols like IPP,Integrating Go and Python projects cleanly into OSS-Fuzz

Proposal 3 (challenges):
Understanding and refactoring an existing codebase without breaking current layouts or content flow,
Ensuring cross-browser compatibility and full mobile responsiveness for new UI features,
Implementing interactive features (likes, comments, search) without hurting performance or security,
Balancing feature scope and performance optimization within a tight program timeline

2. Overstock locks cash

**What NexVyapaar Does:**

**What NexVyapaar Does:**

1. Supports 8 Indian languages
2. Designed for noisy shop environments

🖼️ Language selection UI or voice confirmation screen

🛡️ How It Makes Work Safer & More Reliable
🔒 End-to-end encrypted data
🧾 No data loss from paper
👤 Shopkeeper owns their data
📤 Export or delete anytime

*Trust is built into the system.*

**🧠 In One Line**

NexVyapaar turns everyday shop chaos into clear, actionable business intelligence - without forcing shopkeepers to learn software.

**Challenges we ran into**

**🧱 Challenges I Ran Into (and How I Solved Them)**

Building NexVyapaar for real Indian shops meant dealing with messy reality, not controlled demo data. Here are the key challenges we faced — and how we overcame them.

1️⃣ **Voice Recognition in Noisy Indian Shops**

**The Challenge:**
Shops are loud - traffic, customers, fans, regional accents.
Early voice input had:

1. Misheard product names
2. Wrong quantities
3. Low confidence in crowded environments

**Why This Was Hard:**
Most speech models are trained on clean, studio-like audio, not kirana chaos.

**How We Solved It:**

1. Designed confirmation-based input
2. “I heard: Add 5 Maggi. Is this correct?”
3. Allowed instant correction (voice or tap)
4. Treated voice as convenience, not compulsion
5. Combined voice with POS & image inputs for cross-checking

**Result:**

1. Initial accuracy: ~85%
2. After learning a shop’s accent & vocabulary: ~95% in 2–3 months
3. More importantly: high trust, even when accuracy isn’t perfect

2️⃣ **Extracting Data from Handwritten Notes**

**The Challenge:**
Shopkeepers write:

1. Fast
2. In mixed languages
3. With inconsistent formats
4. Standard OCR failed badly on real handwritten rush-hour notes.

**How We Solved It:**

1. Built a hybrid OCR + context model
2. Didn’t try to read everything — only:
3. Product name
4. Quantity

Used inventory context to validate guesses
(If “Parle-G” exists in stock, the model prefers it over random words)

**Result:**

1. Fewer errors than generic OCR
2. High usability even with messy handwriting

3️⃣ **Getting Value on Day One** (Cold Start Problem)

**The Challenge:**
AI needs data.
But users won’t stay unless they see value immediately.

**How We Solved It:**
We separated the system into two layers:

*Layer 1: Rule-Based Intelligence* (Day One)

1. Dead stock alerts
2. Margin checks
3. Simple visibility dashboards

*Layer 2: Predictive AI* (After 2–3 weeks)

1. Demand forecasting
2. Expiry prediction
3. Customer behavior insights

**Result:**

1. Immediate usefulness
2. No “wait 30 days to see value” problem
3. Strong early retention

4️⃣ **Resistance to “Yet Another App”**

The Challenge:
Many shopkeepers have already tried apps - and abandoned them.

**Root Issue:**
1. They don’t hate technology.
2. They hate tools that increase effort.

**How We Solved It:**

1. Zero mandatory typing
2. Multiple input modes (voice, photo, POS)
3. Minimal setup - usable within one business day
4. Positioned the product as a helper, not software

**Result:**

1. Lower adoption friction
2. 65% paid conversion after pilot trials

5️⃣ **Balancing AI Power with Human Control**

**The Challenge:**
1. Auto-executing decisions scared users:

“What if it makes a mistake?”
“I want control.”

**How We Solved It:**

1. *AI only suggests, never acts*
2. *Every insight comes with a reason*
3. *Shopkeeper remains final decision-maker*

**Result:**

1. Higher trust
2. Better long-term adoption

**🔑 Key Learning**

The hardest part wasn’t building AI.
It was designing intelligence that respects human habits.

*Solving for real-world behavior made the system stronger and harder to copy.*

**The problem it solves**

Many students and beginners struggle to understand how real-world websites handle backend logic, database interaction, authentication, and deployment. Most learning resources focus on theory or isolated features, making it difficult to connect concepts into a complete, working system.

This project addresses that gap by providing a practical, end-to-end implementation of a real-world web application. It helps users learn how to design, develop, and debug a scalable website while following proper software engineering practices. By working on this project, users gain hands-on experience with problem-solving, debugging, collaboration, and industry-relevant workflows, making them better prepared for internships, hackathons, and open-source contributions.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges I faced was understanding how different parts of the project—frontend, backend logic, and data handling—connect and communicate with each other. Initially, this led to issues such as broken flows, unexpected errors, and difficulty debugging when something didn’t work as expected.

Another challenge was debugging errors that did not clearly indicate the root cause, especially during integration and deployment. Small mistakes in configuration or file structure sometimes caused the application to fail silently.

I overcame these challenges by breaking the project into smaller modules, testing each component individually, and using proper logging and debugging tools. Reading official documentation, analyzing error messages carefully, and learning from community discussions helped me resolve issues efficiently. Through this process, I improved my problem-solving skills and gained a better understanding of real-world development workflows.

### REGIME AWARE ML STRATEGY FOR BITCOIN TRADING
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/regime-aware-ml-strategy-for-bitcoin-trading-d1a3) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AyushPallod/ooc_ps04_btc_pred_backtest) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Out%20Of%20Context'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://out-of-context-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> With you in bear and bull

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Emotional & 24/7 Trading Constraints: The cryptocurrency market operates 24/7 and is highly volatile. Manual trading is prone to emotional errors (FOMO, panic selling) and physical fatigue. This system automates the entire process, executing disciplined, math-based trades without emotion or sleep.

Adaptability to Changing Markets: Most static models fail when market conditions shift (e.g., from a Bull run to a Bear crash). This project solves this by using a Rolling Walk-Forward Retraining framework. It re-learns the market patterns every month, ensuring the model stays relevant to the most recent data.

Risk Management Optimization: Instead of a "one size fits all" approach, the system dynamically adjusts its risk. It identifies the "Market Regime" (Bull vs. Bear) to switch strategies—using leverage for growth during Bull markets and tight stops/shorting for protection during Bear markets.

**Challenges we ran into**

Data Stationarity (The "Unbounded Price" Issue)
Challenge: raw Bitcoin prices are "non-stationary" (they trend upwards over time). Machine Learning models struggle with this because they can't predict values they haven't seen before (e.g., predicting $60k when the training data only goes to $20k).
Solution: Instead of predicting price directly, the model predicts Log Returns and uses differencing. This normalizes the data, making it stationary and learnable, which is then reconstructed back into price levels for evaluation.

Data Leakage (Look-Ahead Bias)
Challenge: In time-series data, it is very easy to accidentally use future information in training (e.g., scaling data using the min/max of the whole dataset). This creates a "perfect" backtest that fails in real life.
Solution: Implemented a strict Walk-Forward Validation pipeline. The Scaler and Model are fitted only on the training window available at that specific point in time. No future data ever touches the training set.

Market Regimes & Feature Irrelevance
Challenge: Indicators like "Golden Crosses" work great in Bull markets but destroy capital in Bear markets. A single model trained on 5 years of data gets confused by these conflicting signals.
Solution: Integrated a Regime Filter (200-day EMA). The strategy logic checks the long-term trend first. If Price < 200 EMA, it completely shuts off aggressive buying and enables Shorting logic, effectively splitting the problem into two distinct trading modes.

Team **NullPointers** -- Chinmay Nagda, AYUSH PALLOD

Existing apps show numbers but don’t explain what they mean or why they matter. This leads to confusion, panic during volatility, and poor financial decisions.

**Challenges we ran into**

Problems i faced:

PDF Parsing: Demat statements had inconsistent formats, columns, and date styles, making extraction unreliable.

Backend Debugging: Small data issues caused full pipeline crashes, requiring defensive coding and step-wise debugging.

Health Score Logic: Designing an explainable, safe, non–black-box score without giving buy/sell advice was challenging.

Frontend–Backend Sync: Data existed in backend but didn’t reflect in UI due to response and storage mismatches.

CORS & Auth: Authentication worked on backend but failed in browser due to CORS and credential handling.
State Management: Maintaining upload progress, report persistence, and page navigation without reload issues was tricky.

News Integration: APIs worked but had limited stock coverage, requiring careful market and data-source decisions.

Single Source of Truth: Ensuring dashboard, chatbot, and reports used the same consistent data required redesign.

Chatbot Context: Handling follow-up questions needed context memory instead of stateless responses.

Environment Setup: Dependency, path, and runtime issues across systems slowed development and testing

### ClarifyAI

> Clear answers from complex policies

![Natural language processing (NLP)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20language%20processing%20(NLP)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20Language%20Toolkit%20(NLTK)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Geofencing API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Geofencing%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![langchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/langchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![FAISS](https://img.shields.io/badge/FAISS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Retrieval-Augmented Generation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Retrieval--Augmented%20Generation-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## Problem Statement

Organizations rely on internal policies—such as leave, expense, conduct, and compliance guidelines—to ensure consistent and fair decision-making. However, these policies are often lengthy, complex, and written in legal or formal language, making them difficult for employees to understand and apply in real-world situations.

As a result:
- Employees struggle to find accurate answers to policy-related questions.
- HR and compliance teams are repeatedly asked the same questions.
- Misinterpretation of policies leads to unintentional violations, disputes, or compliance risks.
- Existing solutions rely on keyword search or static FAQs, which fail to capture intent, context, or nuance.

There is no easy, reliable way for employees to *understand* policies—only to search them.

---

## What ClarifyAI Solves

**ClarifyAI** bridges the gap between complex policy documents and everyday questions by providing an AI-powered assistant that *explains*, *cites*, and *reasons over* internal company policies.

Instead of forcing users to read entire documents or guess the right keywords, ClarifyAI allows users to ask questions in natural language and receive clear, context-aware explanations grounded in actual policy text.

---

## Who Can Use ClarifyAI

- **Employees** – Quickly understand leave rules, expense claims, remote work policies, and conduct guidelines.
- **HR Teams** – Reduce repetitive queries and ensure consistent policy interpretation.
- **Compliance & Legal Teams** – Minimize risk by promoting accurate, explainable policy understanding.
- **Managers** – Make informed decisions without misinterpreting policy clauses.

---

## How ClarifyAI Makes Tasks Easier

### Natural Language Understanding
Users can ask questions the way they naturally think:
> “Can I carry forward unused leaves?”  
> “What happens if I submit an expense late?”

No need to know policy titles or keywords.

---

### Policy-Backed Answers (No Guessing)
Every response:
- Is generated **only** from relevant policy sections
- Includes **explicit citations** to the source text
- Explains *how* the policy applies to the question

This builds trust and transparency.

---

### Context-Aware Conversations
ClarifyAI maintains conversational context, enabling:
- Follow-up questions
- Clarifications without restating the full problem
- More natural, human-like interactions

---

### Ambiguity & Conflict Awareness
If policies are:
- Ambiguous
- Conflicting
- Potentially outdated

ClarifyAI clearly communicates uncertainty instead of making assumptions, encouraging responsible decision-making.

---

### Safer Responses for Sensitive Topics
For high-risk topics (e.g., disciplinary action, harassment, termination):
- Uses cautious, guidance-oriented language
- Avoids definitive or legal advice
- Encourages proper escalation when needed

This reduces organizational and legal risk.

---

## Why ClarifyAI Is Safer Than Traditional Chatbots

Unlike generic AI chatbots, ClarifyAI:
- Does **not** rely on general knowledge or assumptions
- Does **not** hallucinate policy rules
- Does **not** give definitive legal or HR advice

Instead, it acts as a **policy interpretation assistant**, not a decision-maker.

---

## Impact

By turning static policy documents into an interactive, explainable system, ClarifyAI:
- Saves time for employees and HR teams
- Reduces misinterpretation and compliance risk
- Improves policy accessibility and understanding
- Enables safer, more confident decision-making across the organization

---

**ClarifyAI transforms policies from documents people avoid into guidance people trust.**

**Challenges we ran into**

##  Challenges We Ran Into (and How We Solved Them)

Building PolicyLens within a tight hackathon timeline surfaced several technical and design challenges. Each challenge shaped the final architecture and made the system more robust, safer, and more explainable.

---

###  The AI Was Giving Confident but Incorrect Answers

**The Problem:**  
Early versions of the system answered policy questions confidently even when the policy text was unclear or incomplete. This was risky—especially for HR and compliance-related topics—because confident answers can be mistaken for authoritative guidance.

**Why It Happened:**  
Large language models are trained to be helpful and fluent. When asked a question directly, they tend to “fill in the gaps” using general knowledge rather than admitting uncertainty.

**How We Solved It:**  
We restructured the system to ensure the AI never answered in isolation:
- Introduced a **retrieval-first (RAG) pipeline** so the model only sees relevant policy excerpts.
- Added **explicit prompt rules** requiring the model to acknowledge ambiguity or missing information.
- Enforced a **structured response format** that includes an “Uncertainty” section.

This shifted the model from *answering* to *reasoning over provided evidence*.

---

###  Keyword Search Failed for Real User Questions

**The Problem:**  
Users often asked questions that didn’t share keywords with the policy text (e.g., “unused leave next year” vs. “leave carry forward”). Keyword-based search failed to retrieve the right sections.

**Why It Happened:**  
Traditional search relies on exact word matches and does not capture semantic meaning.

**How We Solved It:**  
We replaced keyword search with **semantic retrieval using embeddings and cosine similarity**:
- Policy sections and user questions are converted into embeddings.
- Cosine similarity is used to retrieve meaningfully related policy chunks.
- LangChain handles the retrieval layer, ensuring only relevant content reaches the model.

This dramatically improved answer relevance and user experience.

---

###  Conflicting Policy Sections Created Confusion

**The Problem:**  
Some policies contained sections that appeared to contradict each other (e.g., leave carry-forward vs. leave expiry rules). Early versions of the system picked one and ignored the other.

**Why It Happened:**  
Naively returning the top matching chunk hides important context and can mislead users.

**How We Solved It:**  
We added an **ambiguity detection step** before invoking the language model:
- Multiple retrieved sections are analyzed together.
- If potential conflicts or differing update dates are detected, the system flags ambiguity.
- The AI is explicitly instructed to communicate uncertainty instead of resolving it on its own.

This made the system safer and more transparent.

---

###  Handling Sensitive Topics Responsibly

**The Problem:**  
Questions related to disciplinary action, termination, or harassment require careful wording. A direct or definitive response could be harmful or misleading.

**Why It Happened:**  
LLMs don’t inherently know which topics are high-risk in an organizational context.

**How We Solved It:**  
We introduced a **sensitive-topic detection layer**:
- High-risk queries are identified before the AI is called.
- The prompt dynamically enforces **cautious, non-definitive language**.
- Responses are framed as guidance rather than decisions, encouraging appropriate escalation.

This aligned the system with real-world compliance expectations.

---

###  Maintaining Context Across Follow-Up Questions

**The Problem:**  
Follow-up questions like “What about interns?” lacked context and led to incomplete or irrelevant answers.

**Why It Happened:**  
Each query was initially treated as an isolated request.

**How We Solved It:**  
We implemented **lightweight conversational memory**:
- The system tracks the current policy and topic within a session.
- Follow-up questions reuse prior context unless the topic clearly changes.

This made conversations feel natural and significantly reduced friction.

---

###  Balancing Speed with Explainability Under Time Constraints

**The Problem:**  
Hackathon time limits made it tempting to optimize for speed over clarity and safety.

**Why It Mattered:**  
Fast but opaque answers undermine trust—especially for policy interpretation.

**How We Solved It:**  
We prioritized:
- Explainability over raw response speed
- Clear citations over generic summaries
- Safety over overconfidence

This design choice resonated strongly with the problem statement and target users.

---

##  Key Takeaway

Most challenges stemmed from the same root issue: **AI models are powerful but must be constrained**.  
By introducing retrieval, explicit reasoning boundaries, and safety-aware orchestration, we transformed a generic chatbot into a trustworthy policy reasoning assistant.

These challenges ultimately shaped PolicyLens into a

**AI**

##  How ClarifyAI Fits into the AI Track

ClarifyAI is an AI-first system designed to help users understand, interpret, and reason about internal company policies using natural language. The project demonstrates how modern AI techniques can be applied responsibly to solve a real-world problem involving complex, high-stakes documents.

Rather than using AI as a simple chatbot layer, ClarifyAI is built as a **controlled AI reasoning system** that combines semantic retrieval, language models, and safety-aware orchestration.

---

##  Semantic Intelligence at the Core

ClarifyAI leverages **text embeddings and cosine similarity** to understand the *meaning* of user questions rather than relying on keyword matching. Policy documents are converted into embeddings and stored in a vector database, allowing the system to retrieve the most relevant policy sections even when user queries are phrased differently from the original text.

This semantic understanding is a core application of modern NLP and aligns directly with the goals of the AI track.

---

##  LangChain-Orchestrated AI Workflow

The project uses **LangChain** to structure the end-to-end AI workflow:
- Policy ingestion and chunking
- Embedding-based semantic retrieval
- Prompt construction and LLM interaction
- Conversational context handling

LangChain enables modular, explainable AI pipelines and allows ClarifyAI to scale beyond a simple prompt-based chatbot.

---

##  Responsible and Explainable AI Design

ClarifyAI explicitly addresses common AI risks:
- **Hallucination reduction** via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
- **Uncertainty awareness** when policies are ambiguous or conflicting
- **Cautious, guidance-oriented responses** for sensitive HR and compliance topics
- **Explainability** through direct citation of policy excerpts

These design choices reflect key AI track themes such as trust, accountability, and alignment.

---

##  Context-Aware Reasoning

ClarifyAI maintains conversational context to support follow-up questions and adapts explanation depth based on inferred user intent. This demonstrates AI not just as a static model, but as a **context-aware reasoning assistant**.

---

##  Why ClarifyAI Belongs in the AI Track

ClarifyAI showcases:
- Practical application of NLP and LLMs
- Semantic search using cosine similarity
- Structured AI orchestration with LangChain
- Responsible AI behavior in real-world scenarios

By combining these techniques, ClarifyAI illustrates how AI can augment human understanding rather than replace human judgment.

---

##  Summary

ClarifyAI is a strong AI track project because it demonstrates **how to build AI systems that are accurate, explainable, and safe**, while solving a meaningful, real-world problem involving policy interpretation and compliance.

Team **Crusaders** -- Mitanshu Sarkar, Ishan Taranekar, Tanmay Joshi, Ojas Sahu

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem FinSight solves:

Lack of clarity in loan & investment eligibility – Users apply for loans or funding without knowing whether they qualify, leading to rejections and wasted time.
One-size-fits-all scoring systems – Existing platforms rely heavily on generic credit scores and ignore context like education, medical emergencies, business stage, or startup traction.
Hidden decision logic (black-box lending) – Applicants are rarely told why they were rejected or what exactly needs improvement.
High risk of financial stress – Blind approvals or high-interest loans push users into poor financial decisions.
No guidance to improve eligibility – Most tools stop at “approved / rejected” and offer no actionable next steps.




How FinSight helps:

Uses AI-driven, category-specific scoring models (education, personal, medical, business, startup investment) instead of generic checks.
Converts complex financial data into a clear eligibility score with confidence bands.
Provides explainable insights showing issues, their impact, and exact steps to boost the score.
Recommends real-world, score-matched loan and investment options to reduce rejection risk.
Helps users make safer, informed financial decisions before applying, protecting both time and credit health.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we ran into during development:


1.Designing fair, real-world scoring logic
Different loan types (education, medical, business, personal, startup investment) require completely different risk parameters.
Balancing realism with hackathon-time simplicity without oversimplifying the financial logic was challenging.

2.Avoiding black-box AI decisions
We didn’t want to just output a score; we needed explainable insights (issues, impact, improvements).
Translating backend risk factors into clear, human-readable insights required multiple iterations.

3.Frontend–backend synchronization

Managing multi-step question flows, conditional questions, and ensuring the correct payload reached the backend consistently was tricky.
Handling edge cases like skipped questions and incomplete inputs required extra validation logic.

3.CORS, local setup & environment issues- Setting up Flask APIs, CORS handling, and consistent local environments across different systems caused debugging delays.

4.Mapping scores to real financial products-Categorizing real-world loan and investment schemes accurately by score range while keeping data reliable and UI-friendly was non-trivial.

5.Time constraints of a hackathon- Balancing UI polish, backend logic, explainability, and stability within limited time meant prioritizing impact-heavy features over secondary enhancements.

**AI**

How FinSight fits into the AI track:

FinSight uses an AI-inspired decision intelligence system to evaluate loan and investment eligibility across multiple financial categories. Instead of relying on opaque black-box approvals, the system applies structured risk modeling, rule-based scoring, and explainable logic that mirrors how real financial institutions assess applicants.

The platform dynamically adapts its evaluation based on user context (education, medical emergencies, business cash flow, personal finance, or startup traction) and generates transparent insights explaining why a score was assigned and how it can be improved. This approach aligns with applied and explainable AI, focusing on decision intelligence, user trust, and actionable outcomes rather than raw prediction alone.

By combining structured financial heuristics, contextual analysis, and AI-style reasoning, FinSight delivers intelligent, transparent, and human-centric financial decision support.

> RAG-Powered Compliance Engine.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

***Problem (The "Why")***
Corporate policy documents (HR, InfoSec, Travel) are often hundreds of pages long. Employees never read them, and HR teams are overwhelmed answering the same questions repeatedly.

This creates a massive "Compliance Gap":

Employees unknowingly violate rules (e.g., booking expensive flights, using unsafe Wi-Fi).

Critical information remains buried in PDF attachments.

Auditing specific scenarios takes hours of manual reading.

***Solution (The "What")***

PolicyGuard is not just a chatbot; it is a Forensic Compliance Auditor.

Ingestion: Users upload raw PDF policies.

Vectorization: The system indexes the text using FAISS and Sentence-Transformers.

Audit: Users ask specific scenarios (e.g., "Can I expense a client dinner in London?").

Verdict: The AI consults only the document (preventing hallucinations) and issues a verdict: COMPLIANT, PROHIBITED, or CONDITIONAL, complete with specific citations (e.g., [Page 12, Section 4.1]).

Technologies Used (Select these tags or list them)

- Python 
- FastAPI 
- Streamlit 
- Llama-3 (via Groq API) 
- FAISS (Vector DB) 
- LangChain / RAG 
- Render (Cloud Hosting)

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **The "Hallucination" Problem**: Initial AI models wanted to use outside knowledge (like general labor laws) instead of sticking to the uploaded PDF. We solved this by implementing a "Four Walls Doctrine" system prompt that forces the AI to have "total amnesia" about the outside world.

2. **Handling Cloud Limits**: Deploying a sophisticated RAG pipeline on free-tier hosting (Render) meant dealing with "cold starts" and memory limits. We optimized our vector chunking strategy to keep the memory footprint low while maintaining high accuracy.


Also please note that since I am using Render's free tier there can be a delay of 50-60s for the result of your query.

**AI**

PolicyGuard is a native Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) application. It uses Sentence-Transformers to convert unstructured PDF text into high-dimensional vector embeddings stored in FAISS.

When a query is received, we perform a Semantic Similarity Search to retrieve relevant context, which is then fed into Llama 3.1 (via Groq). We heavily utilized Prompt Engineering to enforce a "Four Walls Doctrine," ensuring the AI only answers based on the provided evidence, effectively eliminating hallucinations in high-stakes compliance scenarios.

By utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs) and potentially Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), the system doesn't just fetch documents; it actively interprets user intent, synthesizes answers from disjointed policy text, and maintains conversational context to handle ambiguity. This transforms static compliance documentation into a dynamic, risk-aware intelligence layer that can "reason" about conflicts and adapt to user feedback, showcasing the practical power of AI in automating high-stakes cognitive tasks.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/compact-autonomous-warehouse-robot-1f12) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ABHIN0VB/code_kalari.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/wY6eDbmIVzE?si=17_i0aixf283v90n) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Code%20Kalari-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://code-kalari.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Smart path planning and obstacle avoidance

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fusion 360](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fusion%20360-333333?style=flat-square) ![Webots](https://img.shields.io/badge/Webots-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This robot system,  WarehouseBot, transforms a warehouse robot from a rigid, fixed-path machine into a flexible, intelligent assistant that plans its own routes using A* on a grid map. Workers can easily assign tasks by simply clicking a source and destination on a GUI, and the robot autonomously travels between shelves while dynamically avoiding obstacles (pallets, people, or forklifts) using sensors and turning 45° instead of stopping. This reduces operator walking distance, speeds up order picking and replenishment, and makes the warehouse safer by gracefully giving way to humans instead of blindly pushing forward. It also makes layout changes easier (no need for tape or QR codes) and supports scaling to multiple robots with a central dispatch interface, serving as both a practical tool for warehouse tasks and a flexible platform for learning and optimization. And the plan included having a scissor lift which is electrically controlled instead of hydraulics reduce the maintenance such as oil replacement and other things.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/ae6d3677ffd14a48a49e3bd7082be114/93212fc5-a4b3-4c7c-ba53-fa17233572ec.jpeg)  

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/ae6d3677ffd14a48a49e3bd7082be114/34690460-96b5-48c6-b8ba-1fd01021f406.jpeg)

**Challenges we ran into**

One major hurdle was that the robot in Webots could not receive the path from the PC GUI, even though the GUI ran correctly and created `path_request.json` as expected. Initially, the robot controller kept logging that the file was not found, which made the entire system useless even though A* and obstacle avoidance were working in isolation. After debugging, the root cause turned out to be a path mismatch: the Python script used an absolute path on the PC, but the Webots robot controller (running in a different working directory) was looking for path_request.json relative to its own controllers/ folder, so it never saw the file created by the GUI. To fix this, I first replaced the relative path in the robot code with an absolute path that matched exactly where the GUI placed the file, ensuring both sides agreed on the file location. Later, I improved it by adding strong debug prints in both the GUI and the robot controller to show the exact path being used and the JSON content, which made it easy to spot when a typo or wrong directory was in use. Once the file was reliably read, the next issue was that the robot followed the waypoints poorly because it didn’t correctly convert its world position to grid cell coordinates; this was solved by adding a `get_robot_cell()` function that uses the robot’s translation in Webots to map continuously to the 38×38 grid, allowing it to move step by step from one cell to the next in the A* path. The project need to be continued by adding the lift part and simulating it.

**The problem it solves**

Brand: ChargeEase

🚩 Problem

Smart homes are becoming common, but the way we control them is still not smart. Users face:

Fragmented control across multiple apps/devices

Too many steps for simple actions

No visualization of the home while controlling devices

Slow response in urgent moments

Low engagement with traditional 2D interfaces

✅ Solution

HomeVerse is a VR-based smart home control interface that allows users to control and monitor IoT devices inside an immersive virtual environment. Instead of switching between multiple apps, users can manage devices in one unified VR experience with real-time feedback.

🛠️ What it does

Controls appliances like Light / Fan from the VR interface

Provides real-time ON/OFF control

Sends commands instantly and receives live status feedback

⚙️ How it works (Architecture)

User → Unity VR App → WebSocket → NodeMCU → Relay Module → Devices → Status Feedback → Unity VR App

💡 Innovation / Uniqueness

Smart Control Beyond Screens (VR instead of 2D menus)

Immersive and intuitive interaction

Real-time control loop using WebSocket + IoT integration

💰 Business Model (Revenue)

B2C Premium Subscription — advanced VR features

B2B Licensing — smart home builders & office workspaces integration

🧰 Tech Stack

Unity (VR Interface)

C#

WebSocket (Real-time communication)

NodeMCU (ESP8266/ESP32)

Relay Module

Wi-Fi

🚀 Future Scope

Voice assistant integration

AI-based automation suggestions

Multi-user access & stronger security

Support for more devices and sensors

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
1) Real-time communication between VR and IoT devices

One of the biggest challenges was achieving instant response when controlling devices from the VR interface. Initially, commands were delayed or not received consistently by the IoT controller.

✅ How we solved it:
We implemented WebSocket-based communication to maintain a stable real-time connection between the Unity VR app and NodeMCU, ensuring low-latency command delivery and smoother device control.

2) Reliable device switching using NodeMCU + Relay Module

While testing the hardware setup, the relay sometimes behaved inconsistently (device not switching ON/OFF properly), especially during multiple rapid toggles.

✅ How we solved it:
We fixed wiring and control logic issues, added proper relay triggering conditions, and performed repeated testing to make the switching stable and predictable.

3) Syncing device status back into the VR interface

Even after successfully controlling devices, showing the correct ON/OFF status inside VR was difficult because feedback wasn’t updating properly in real time.

✅ How we solved it:
We created a feedback loop where the NodeMCU sends status updates back through WebSocket, allowing Unity to reflect real device status instantly in the UI.

4) Integrating hardware and software smoothly

Combining VR development with IoT hardware integration in a hackathon timeframe was challenging because debugging was required across both environments.

✅ How we solved it:
We tested each layer separately (Unity → WebSocket → NodeMCU → Relay) and then integrated step-by-step, which helped us isolate errors quickly and ensure end-to-end functionality.

### ECHO
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/echo-97db) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/PSonakshi/echo.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kRcUtwtTsUavh7ta9ynbMa34BltOUhxK/view?usp=drive_link) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/A6Don8qORBE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackNITR%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknitr7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Don't just watch the market! Listen to it

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cryptocurrency](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cryptocurrency-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Echo addresses the critical problem of cognitive overload and information asymmetry in the cryptocurrency market, where millions of unstructured social media signals create a chaotic environment that makes it nearly impossible for human traders to distinguish genuine market trends from bot-driven hype. Traders often suffer from "analysis paralysis" or fall victim to manipulative narratives (like "rug pulls") because they lack the ability to cross-reference rapidly shifting social sentiment with actual price behavior in real-time. Existing tools typically fail to solve this because they either analyze data in slow, historical batches or treat social metrics in isolation without verifying them against market reality. Echo solves this gap by automating the decoding of this high-velocity noise, instantly correlating linguistic intensity with price action to filter out deception and provide traders with a verified, actionable signal the moment a narrative begins to form

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Temporal Misalignment of Heterogeneous Data Streams
The Challenge: We had to merge two fundamentally different types of data streams. Social media data (tweets/messages) is event-based and irregular (bursty), while price data (CoinGecko) is time-series based and regular (ticks). Standard database joins failed because a tweet timestamp almost never perfectly matches a price tick timestamp.

The Solution: We implemented Pathway’s Temporal Windowing. Instead of joining on exact timestamps, we aggregated both streams into aligned 5-minute sliding windows. We used pw.temporal.sliding to create a common "bucket" for both streams, allowing us to mathematically correlate "Sentiment Velocity" with "Price Delta" without needing nanosecond-perfect synchronization.

2. Signal-to-Noise Ratio in Social Data
The Challenge: The crypto ecosystem is plagued by spam bots and low-quality engagement. Initial tests showed that raw volume of messages was a poor indicator of true momentum, as a bot farm could easily skew the "Pulse Score" by spamming generic positive messages.

The Solution: We developed a multi-layered filtering system. First, we built an Influence Calculator that weights messages based on the author's follower count and engagement, effectively "muting" low-quality accounts. Second, we moved from simple sentiment scoring to Sentiment Velocity—measuring the rate of change rather than just the average, which filters out the static background noise of constant shilling.

3. Latency Management in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
The Challenge: Large Language Models (LLMs) are inherently slow compared to high-frequency trading data. We needed to provide "real-time" explanations without blocking the high-speed ingestion pipeline. A delay in the ETL process would mean the "Pulse Score" was lagging behind the market.

The Solution: We decoupled the systems. The Pulse Score calculation runs on a highly optimized, low-latency path for immediate alerts. The RAG System operates asynchronously; it continuously indexes the stream into the VectorStoreServer in the background. This ensures that the quantitative signal (the score) is instant, while the qualitative explanation (the "why") is available on-demand via the Telegram bot without slowing down the core engine.

4. Detecting Genuine Market Divergences
The Challenge: Defining "Divergence" mathematically was difficult. A simple comparison (Price Down, Sentiment Up) produced too many false positives during normal market volatility, leading to "Alert Fatigue" for the user.

The Solution: We refined the logic to be threshold-based rather than binary. We introduced a "Divergence Penalty" that only triggers when sentiment and price move in opposite directions beyond a specific standard deviation (e.g., Sentiment > 0.5 AND Price Drop > 2%). This significantly reduced false alarms and increased the reliability of the "Bearish Divergence" alerts.

5. Orchestrating Real-Time State in a Stateless Container Environment
The Challenge: We needed the system to "remember" the last 5 minutes of context (for windowing) and the current "Pulse Score" state for the dashboard, but we wanted to avoid the complexity of managing an external database like Redis or PostgreSQL to keep the architecture minimalist.

The Solution: We leveraged Pathway’s Internal State Management. The pipeline itself holds the necessary state in memory (RAM). For the Dashboard, we created a lightweight shared state object that subscribes to the pipeline's output. This allowed Streamlit to read "live" data directly from the processing engine, eliminating the need for an intermediate database and reducing architectural complexity

**Real-Time AI Systems & Continuous Intelligence**

The Echo system delivers a multi-layered output centered around the Pulse Score, a real-time momentum metric (ranging from 1-10) that synthesizes sentiment velocity, viral narrative intensity, and price-sentiment correlation into a single actionable signal. This quantitative data is visualized on a live Streamlit dashboard, which features dynamic line charts for tracking momentum trends, real-time word clouds that surface emerging linguistic clusters (such as "buy the dip" or "rug pull"), and leaderboards distinguishing high-impact influencer activity from crowd noise. Beyond passive visualization, the system operates as an active sentinel by generating Telegram alerts the instant critical thresholds are breached (e.g., a "Strong Buy" signal > 7) or when potentially profitable "divergences" are detected between price and sentiment. Finally, the output layer includes interactive intelligence via a RAG-powered query interface, which provides natural language explanations that contextualize the hard metrics with specific, retrieved social media evidence to explain why a market move is occurring.

Team **SSA** -- [Sonakshi Pradhan](https://github.com/PSonakshi), [Srinibas Das](https://github.com/SSRINIBASS), [Anurag Mahapatra](https://github.com/IAnuragMahapatra)

**Challenges we ran into**

**🚧 Challenges I Ran Into
🏋️‍♂️ 1. Deploying a “Heavy” AI Platform**
Challenge:
Running multiple local ML models (BERT, RoBERTa, custom classifiers) alongside FastAPI caused memory spikes, slow responses, and crashes due to models reloading per request.

Solution:

- Used FastAPI lifespan events to load all heavy models once at startup via a global loader.
- Impact: Stable memory usage, faster inference, and reliable handling of concurrent requests.

**⚡ 2. Balancing RAG Speed with High-Quality Retrieval
Challenge:**
Delivering real-time, conversational RAG responses while running a 7-domain analysis introduced latency from repeated embeddings and multiple LLM calls.

Solution:

- LRU caching for embeddings to avoid recomputation
- Single-shot structured prompting to generate all 7 domains in one LLM call
- Hybrid retrieval using Pinecone (fast vectors) + SerpApi (live web data)
- Impact: ~80% reduction in response time with no loss in answer quality.


**🌍 3. Training on Real-World, Not Synthetic, Data
Challenge:**
I wanted Founders Fuel to reflect real startup and investor behavior, not toy or synthetic datasets. Collecting and normalizing high-quality, real-world data was the hardest part.

Solution:
I aggregated data from Y Combinator, Crunchbase, and Airtable-based startup datasets, then:

- Cleaned and deduplicated records
- Normalized industries, stages, and geographies
- Preprocessed text for ML and RAG pipelines
- Impact:
- Built a dataset of 300K+ global startups and 3K+ active investors, making predictions, matching, and analysis grounded in real market dynamics.

✨ **In short:** Founders Fuel uses GenAI to *think, reason, and explain* like a venture capitalist making it a true decision-making system, not a chatbot.

### ARC- Agentic Research and Contact
