> Bringing history alive. Anytime. Anywhere.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AR](https://img.shields.io/badge/AR-333333?style=flat-square) ![API3](https://img.shields.io/badge/API3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Visitors at heritage sites often struggle to truly understand what they are looking at. Information is scattered, guides aren’t always available, and traditional boards don’t offer an engaging experience. Many sites—especially lesser-known ones—receive little visibility, and travelers have no simple way to plan, learn, or explore culturally important places.

What People Can Use It For

Instant AR explanations of monuments and sculptures

Audio guides without hiring a guide or joining a tour

Learning history interactively through quizzes and facts

Discovering nearby heritage spots using location-based suggestions

Planning visits with integrated ticket links and recommendations

Exploring safely from home when travel isn’t possible

How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer

No need for physical guides → safer, independent, and accessible for everyone

No app installation required → anyone can use it instantly

Everything in one place → AR, timeline, facts, audio, and suggestions

Real-time distance & navigation help → reduces confusion and saves time

Clear, engaging content replaces confusing, outdated information boards

Reduced crowding around signboards or guide groups → safer visitor experience

Promotes lesser-known sites → boosts tourism and supports local culture

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Heavy 3D Models Causing Slow Loading

In the beginning, the 3D heritage models were too heavy, which caused slow loading and lag on mid-range devices.
How I solved it:
I implemented Draco compression and Basis texture compression, which reduced the model size drastically and improved loading speed without losing quality.

2. AR Not Working Consistently Across Devices

Different Android phones had very different AR support, and some browsers wouldn’t open WebXR mode.
How I solved it:
I added fallback AR modes like Scene Viewer and Quick Look, and tested using <model-viewer> for better compatibility across fragmented devices.

3. Geolocation Accuracy & “Near Me” Feature

The “Near Me” feature sometimes returned inaccurate distances because raw GPS readings varied a lot.
How I solved it:
I implemented the Haversine formula for accurate distance calculation and added user-permission handling to make the process smoother.

4. Chatbot API Quotas & Errors

The Gemini chatbot sometimes failed due to API quota limits, causing the app to break.
How I solved it:
I created a Node.js proxy server, added proper error handling, and added UI feedback like “Thinking…” and fallback responses so the app remains stable even when the API rate limits.

5. Managing State Across Multiple Screens

Since the app had login, site details, quizzes, suggestions, and AR—all in one page—managing the state was challenging.
How I solved it:
I structured the logic into clear functions, used localStorage for user data (favorites, progress, recent visits), and modularized features to keep the code clean and maintainable.

6. Missing Assets & Broken Links

Some posters, thumbnails, and models didn’t load because of incorrect path names.
How I solved it:
I built a diagnostic script that logs “OK” or “MISSING” assets in the console so I could quickly fix incorrect paths.

**The problem it solves**

Caring for elderly parents is often difficult, especially when adult children live far away. Important tasks like taking medicines on time, tracking health updates, and handling emergencies can easily be missed. This app solves that by giving elders a simple dashboard for daily medicines, tasks, and appointments, while the adult child manages all important details in the background. Handling navigation flow between different sections and ensuring the app remained smooth and error-free was another hurdle. Balancing features without overwhelming the user, especially elderly users, required multiple redesigns.

Overall, this project pushed us to learn about UI/UX for different age groups, database design, and proper screen flow management.

**The problem it solves**

MediBridge is a MERN stack–based healthcare platform that helps doctors, patients, and caregivers manage prescriptions, medicines, appointments, and communication in one secure place. It replaces error-prone manual processes with digital prescriptions, smart medicine reminders, and real-time caregiver alerts, ensuring no dose or emergency is missed. Optimizing the Node.js event handling.
Improving API response chaining,
Revalidating database triggers for missed doses,
After testing multiple edge cases, the alerts became instant and reliable.

This challenge helped us strengthen our backend logic, API integration skills, and real-time automation handling, making MediBridge more robust and production-ready.

**Best AWS Hack**

MediBridge is a cloud-ready MERN stack healthcare platform that naturally aligns with the AWS track due to its need for scalability, reliability, security, and real-time data processing. The platform handles sensitive medical data such as prescriptions, dosage schedules, appointments, and caregiver alerts, which require secure storage, high availability, and fast API performance—all core strengths of AWS.

> Smarter than an app. Friendlier than a bank.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The rise of the gig economy has created a crisis of income volatility for millions of workers. Traditional financial tools are designed for the predictable 9-to-5 paycheck, leaving freelancers and irregular earners underserved. Current solutions offer only static, backward looking data not advice trapping users in a cycle of financial fragility where a single unexpected expense, like a bike repair, can lead to a debt spiral.

"FinBud" functions as the intelligent financial nervous system for the modern workforce. We move beyond passive tracking to offer predictive, context-aware intervention acting as an always on CFO for those with irregular income. By analyzing real-time data to forecast cash flow gaps before they occur, FinBud provides the dynamic guardrails necessary to navigate volatility transforming financial anxiety into calculated, long term resilience.

Why this works:
"Intelligent financial nervous system": This implies the app is alive, reactive, and essential to the user's survival (like a biological system).

"Predictive, context-aware intervention": This is the "intelligence" angle. It doesn't just know things; it understands the context (e.g., your bike repair) and intervenes to save you.

"Dynamic guardrails": This keeps the safety aspect. A guardrail keeps you on the road; a dynamic one moves based on how fast you are driving (spending).

"Calculated resilience": Sounds far more professional and secure than just "saving money."

**Challenges we ran into**

- During the development of the Chat Interface, the text input field would lose focus after every single keystroke, forcing the user to click it again to type. This made the chat unusable.We refactored the architecture by extracting sub-components (ChatInterface, SummaryCard) outside the main App scope and utilizing React.memo to prevent unnecessary re-renders.

- Intalling dependencies caused a lot of problem along with tailwind versions and node.

- Existing chart libraries were either too heavy (bloating the app) or difficult to style to match the specific "Mustard Yellow" aesthetic and "Connected Scatter Plot" requirement. We built a Custom SVG Rendering Engine from scratch. It mathematically calculates coordinates based on the user's transaction history, automatically scales the Y-axis based on spending limits, and dynamically plots points for Weekly, Monthly, or Yearly views.

- A generic AI chatbot would hallucinate financial advice because it didn't know the user's actual bank balance or upcoming bills. We implemented a "Context Injection" system. Before every user message is sent to the LLM, the backend silently injects a hidden system prompt containing the real-time Firestore data (e.g., "Current Balance: ₹514, Upcoming: Bike Repair"). This ensures the AI gives mathematically accurate advice.

### IRIS-Intelligence Risk Insight System
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/irisintelligence-risk-insight-system-3793) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/akritithap07/IRIS--Intelligent-Risk-Insight-System) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/K6Xbb66NebQ) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Technocrats%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://technocrats-hackathon.devfolio.co)

> AI early warning for crime and unrest across India

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![GeoJSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/GeoJSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![Leaflet.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Leaflet.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Emerging public-safety risks in India—such as unrest, crime spikes, and misinformation-driven tensions—often go undetected until they escalate. Early warning signals exist across news, social media, and local reports, but the information is fragmented, unstructured, and not easy to interpret in real time. Without a unified view of evolving threats, authorities, analysts, and citizens struggle to recognize patterns early, respond proactively, or make informed decisions.

**Key gaps IRIS addresses:**

* Critical signals are scattered across multiple platforms and are difficult to monitor consistently.
* Existing tools are largely reactive, offering insights only after incidents occur.
* There is no centralized dashboard that visualizes real-time state-wise risk levels.
* Manual data collection slows down analysis and reduces accuracy.
* Citizens lack accessible tools to understand safety trends in their region.
* The absence of early-warning intelligence leads to delayed responses and preventable escalation.

IRIS bridges these gaps by unifying fragmented data into a single, real-time risk insight system that highlights emerging threats clearly and enables faster, more informed decision-making.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

While building IRIS, I encountered several technical hurdles that required rethinking my implementation and debugging approach:

* **GeoJSON map integration issues:**
  The India state boundaries did not initially load correctly due to mismatched property names and inconsistent identifiers. I resolved this by standardizing the dataset fields and updating my mapping logic to handle the GeoJSON structure reliably.

* **State details not appearing on hover or click:**
  Event listeners were not being applied correctly to each GeoJSON layer, causing the map to show “unknown” labels. Rebuilding the layer initialization and attaching listeners within the `onEachFeature` function fixed the issue.

* **Left-side trend panel not rendering:**
  The panel remained empty because asynchronous fetch calls returned before the UI was ready. I restructured the data-loading sequence to ensure the panel only rendered after the required data was fully retrieved.

* **Risk color coding not updating:**
  Risk levels were stuck on a default color because the color function lacked a proper return path. Debugging the logic and verifying thresholds solved this.

* **PDF report showing only the heading:**
  The export function wasn't capturing dynamic content, so I revised the rendering workflow to ensure the DOM element was fully generated before creating the PDF.

* **Deployment paths returning 404 errors:**
  Initial deployments failed because the hosting platform couldn’t detect the correct output directory. Switching to Netlify with a simple drag-and-drop deployment solved the problem immediately.

Each challenge improved the project’s structure, pushed me to optimize my code, and helped build a more reliable and polished final system.

### Zshield
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zshield-ed70) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/collinsville22/zshield) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1WtS4NEFB6hmFvFyBAKbGJ1wvfUT2NJst) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co)

> Shield your transparent ZEC

![WebAssembly](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebAssembly-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Bitcoin-derived hardware wallets (Ledger, Trezor) can only hold transparent Zcash. They cannot create shielded transactions because
  they lack Zcash-specific cryptography (Sapling/Orchard proofs). Millions of ZEC sit unshielded because users can't access privacy
  features with their existing wallets.

  ZShield bridges this gap - it lets any Bitcoin-compatible wallet sign the transparent input, then ZShield adds the shielded output
  and generates the proofs.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. halo2_proofs multicore WASM incompatibility
    - Zcash's proof system requires threading, which WASM doesn't support
    - Solution: Created lightweight WASM module without heavy crypto, proofs run server-side
  2. Shell escaping issues on Windows
    - Heredocs and special characters failed when writing files
    - Solution: Used Python scripts and Task agents to write files
  3. zcash_address::Converter API
    - Needed Container trait import for items() method
    - Solution: Correct imports from zcash_address::unified
  4. WASM file serving in Vite
    - "Outside of Vite serving allow list" error
    - Solution: Added server.fs.allow config for parent directories
  5. Missing WASM method exports
    - PcztBuilder had constructor but no methods
    - Solution: Added full API with #[wasm_bindgen] annotations

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![nextjs](https://img.shields.io/badge/nextjs-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zcashsdk](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zcashsdk-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. Skill-Based Gaming vs. Pure Speculation
   - Problem: Most Web3 games rely heavily on financial mechanisms rather than
     actual skill, making them more like investment vehicles than engaging games
   - Solution: PIR8 introduces a 70% strategic skill, 30% tactical luck model,
     where player decisions directly impact outcomes, making it genuinely
     engaging gameplay rather than just token speculation

  2. Complexity Barriers in Blockchain Gaming
   - Problem: Many blockchain games have steep learning curves and complex wallet
     interactions that deter mainstream players
   - Solution: PIR8 simplifies blockchain integration with intuitive UI/UX while
     maintaining the security and ownership benefits of Web3, making it
     accessible to both crypto-native and traditional gamers

  3. Lack of Real-time Strategy in Web3
   - Problem: There's a dearth of real-time strategy games that leverage
     blockchain technology effectively
   - Solution: PIR8 offers turn-based strategic naval combat with
     blockchain-verified game states, combining classic strategy gameplay with
     transparent, decentralized mechanics

  4. Incentivized Engagement Without Exploitation
   - Problem: Many Play-to-Earn games become "Play-to-Earn" systems that exploit
     players rather than provide entertainment
   - Solution: PIR8 creates genuine entertainment value first, with blockchain
     rewards as an enhancement rather than the core motivation, ensuring
     sustainable long-term engagement

  5. Cross-Chain Integration & Privacy
   - Problem: Limited interoperability between different blockchain ecosystems
     and privacy concerns in on-chain gaming
   - Solution: PIR8 integrates Zcash for privacy-focused transactions and
     explores multi-chain compatibility, enabling private gaming experiences
     with transparent results

  6. Tactical Decision Making with Real Consequences
   - Problem: Many games lack meaningful tactical decisions where timing and
     strategy matter
   - Solution: PIR8 incorporates decision time pressure, scan charges
     management, and resource control mechanics that reward skillful play and
     strategic thinking

  PIR8 transforms blockchain gaming from a financial experiment into a
  genuinely entertaining strategic experience where player skill and tactical
  decisions determine success.

**Challenges we ran into**

"fs in the browser" Error - The Anchor Client Import Issue

  One of the most significant challenges was the "fs in the browser" error that
   occurred when trying to use Solana client-side functionality. The issue was
  in the import structure where solanaClient.ts (used in client components) was
   importing from anchorClient.ts, which contained Node.js-specific code like
  fs and path for reading keypair files.

  The Problem:
   - anchorClient.ts had Node.js imports (fs, path) for loading wallet keypairs
     and program IDLs
   - solanaClient.ts (used in client components) imported functions from
     anchorClient.ts
   - This caused the Node.js fs module to be bundled into client-side code,
     leading to runtime errors in browsers

  How I Solved It:
   1. Created a separate utility file called anchorUtils.ts for pure-logic
      functions that don't require Node.js dependencies
   2. Moved shared functions like getGlobalGamePDA to the utility file
   3. Maintained anchorClient.ts for server-side functionality with Node.js
      dependencies
   4. Updated solanaClient.ts to import from anchorUtils.ts instead of
      anchorClient.ts
   5. Updated server/anchorActions.ts to import from anchorUtils.ts for shared
      logic
   6. Updated other files like tests/zcash-memo-watcher.ts to use the appropriate
      server-side imports

  IDL and Program Deployment Challenges

  Another significant hurdle was managing the IDL (Interface Definition
  Language) and program deployment workflow:

  The Problem:
   - The IDL file needed to be accessible both server-side and client-side for
     transaction building
   - Different deployment environments required different IDL paths
   - Program ID mismatches between local, devnet, and mainnet deployments
   - IDL file changes during development weren't being properly synchronized

  How I Solved It:
   1. Implemented environment-specific IDL loading with fallback paths
   2. Created centralized PROGRAM_ID constants to ensure consistency across the
      codebase
   3. Set up automated IDL generation as part of the build process
   4. Implemented error handling for missing or mismatched IDL files
   5. Used environment variables to manage different program IDs for different
      deployment targets

  Anchor Program Integration Complexity

  Working with Anchor framework for Solana program integration presented
  several challenges:

  The Problem:
   - Complex state management between on-chain and off-chain components
   - Transaction building inconsistencies between client-side and server-side
   - Account PDA (Program Derived Address) calculations needed to be identical
     across multiple files
   - Wallet integration with Anchor provider required different approaches for
     different contexts

  How I Solved It:
   1. Standardized PDA calculation functions in shared utility files
   2. Created separate client and server Anchor provider configurations
   3. Implemented robust error handling for transaction failures
   4. Established a consistent pattern for program initialization across
      different contexts
   5. Created dedicated server actions for complex on-chain operations while
      keeping simple read operations on the client side

  These challenges required careful separation of concerns between client-side
  and server-side code, proper dependency management, and consistent state
  handling between the frontend and the blockchain.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

Solana Components:
   - Game state is stored and managed on Solana blockchain
   - Real-time game mechanics (ship movements, attacks, claiming territories)
   - Player turn management, resource collection, and battle logic
   - Uses Solana's high-performance capabilities for fast, real-time gameplay

  Zcash Components:
   - Private transactions for in-game purchases and payments
   - Shielded memos for private communication between players
   - Confidential financial transactions to protect player financial privacy
   - Integration via Zcash SDK for private payment processing

  Cross-Chain Bridge Architecture:
   - PIR8 implements a dual-chain design where game state remains transparent on
     Solana for real-time gameplay (necessary for a strategy game)
   - Financial transactions and private payments are handled via Zcash for user
     privacy
   - The game bridges both ecosystems: Solana for performance and transparency of
     gameplay, Zcash for financial privacy
   - Players can interact with both blockchains seamlessly within the game

  Exact Match with Helius Criteria:
   - The track specifically calls for "Solana ↔ Zec focused solutions that
     enable cross-chain privacy and interoperability"
   - PIR8 creates a practical implementation of this by having game mechanics on
     Solana and private transactions on Zcash
   - The project enables users to benefit from both ecosystems: Solana's speed
     for gameplay, Zcash's privacy for financial interactions
   - It demonstrates real-world cross-chain privacy use case in the gaming domain

> Turning Traffic Chaos into AI-Controlled Harmony.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![YOLOv3 Algorithm](https://img.shields.io/badge/YOLOv3%20Algorithm-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🧠 The Problem It Solves

Traffic congestion and poor signal management are major challenges in urban India, leading to wasted time, increased fuel consumption, pollution, and even delayed emergency responses. Traditional traffic control systems operate on fixed signal timers that fail to adapt to dynamic and unpredictable traffic conditions — especially during peak hours, events, or accidents.

Netra aims to solve this by introducing an AI-powered, adaptive traffic management system that uses real-time data and reinforcement learning to optimize traffic signal timings intelligently.

By analyzing live video feeds, vehicle density, and traffic flow patterns, Netra can:

🕐 Dynamically adjust signal durations to reduce congestion and wait times.

🚑 Prioritize emergency vehicles for smoother and faster movement.

🌱 Reduce idle-time emissions, helping cities move toward sustainability goals.

🛣️ Provide traffic authorities with actionable insights for better urban planning.


In short, Netra makes city traffic management smarter, safer, and more efficient — using AI as the brain behind the road network.

Would you like me to write the next part in the same format — “What it does” (project overview / features) — next?

**Challenges we ran into**

⚙️ Challenges I Ran Into

Building Netra came with several real-world and technical challenges that pushed our limits and helped us grow as developers:

🧩 Real-time Data Processing:
Handling continuous traffic video streams in real time was one of the toughest parts. We had to optimize our model pipeline to process frames efficiently without losing accuracy. Using a combination of OpenCV and YOLO-based object detection, we managed to balance performance and speed by applying frame skipping and asynchronous data handling.

🤖 Training the Reinforcement Learning Model:
Designing an environment that mimics real-world traffic conditions was complex. We created a custom simulation setup to train the model safely before deploying it in live conditions. Fine-tuning reward functions took time, but eventually, the model learned to optimize signal timing adaptively.

🌐 Integration and Synchronization Issues:
Integrating the AI model with our backend and frontend dashboard initially caused data lags and mismatched updates. We resolved this by implementing WebSocket-based real-time communication and caching mechanisms to ensure smooth, synchronized updates across the system.

🧠 Scalability & Deployment:
Making the system scalable for multiple intersections required modularization. We used Docker containers to make each signal node independently deployable, ensuring the system could handle expansion seamlessly.

Each challenge taught us how to balance AI efficiency, system reliability, and real-world practicality, making Netra more robust and ready for large-scale implementation.

### Yatharth
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/crisisconnect-7404) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Bhakti-e/Yatharth) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20This%20Fall%202025%20--%20Milestone%20Edition-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackthisfall.devfolio.co)

> Verify global claims instantly

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today, information spreads faster than its verification.
False news, manipulated posts, edited screenshots and unverified claims can cause real-world panic, political tension, financial instability and social confusion.

**Yatharth solves this by acting as a real-time global monitoring station.**
It continuously collects posts, news headlines, and public claims from multiple open web sources and compares them with trusted global news channels, government feeds, and verified public records

**The system automatically:**

- Detects breaking claims from multiple sources
- Cross-checks them with reliable and authenticated publishers
- Flags suspicious or contradictory information
- Gives the user a clear Verified / Unverified / False verdict
- Displays the original source, explanation and credibility trail

This makes fact-checking instant, reliable and accessible, especially in situations where misinformation can cause damage — floods, conflicts, elections, public safety alerts, etc.

**How It Works**

Yatharth runs on a multi-layer verification pipeline:

1. **Real-Time Data Collection**: The system fetches global news, trending topics, social media posts and open-source intelligence signals.
2. **Claim Extraction**: The platform automatically detects key claims, headlines and statements from incoming data.
3. **Cross-Verification Against Trusted Sources**: Each claim is checked against multiple authenticated sources such as:
- BBC
- Reuters
- AP News
- NDTV / Indian Express
- Government disaster & safety portals
- Verified public records
4. **Credibility Scoring**: The system assigns a confidence score based on:
- Source reliability
- Number of matches across trusted channels
- Contradictions or lack of evidence
5. **Final Verdict: Each item is classified as**:
- Verified
- Unverified
- False / Misleading
6.**Live Monitoring Dashboards**: The platform provides three live streams:
- Recent Flagged Posts
- Global Scan Results
- Live Satellite-style News Feed

**Challenges we ran into**

- Integrating multiple external data sources with inconsistent formats.
- Handling rate limits and throttling from global news APIs.
- Extracting clean and meaningful claims from raw text and noisy data.
- Avoiding duplicate headlines from different news agencies.
- Designing a real-time verification pipeline that checks accuracy quickly.
- Keeping the UI fast even when large amounts of live data were loading.
- Ensuring the verdict system stays consistent and explainable.

### ReFactor Arcade
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/jobsphere-b555) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20This%20Fall%202025%20--%20Milestone%20Edition-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackthisfall.devfolio.co)

> Turn Every Bug Into a Boss Battle.

![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Refactor Arcade turns code quality and debugging practice into an interactive, gamified experience. Developers upload or write code, and CodeRabbit instantly analyzes it using multiple personas and MCP tools. Instead of dry review comments, the analysis becomes game objectives: fix a bug, reduce complexity, eliminate security risks, improve readability, or write better documentation. Each improvement increases your score and unlocks achievements.

Refactor Arcade solves the biggest learning gap for new developers:
how to understand, prioritize, and fix real review feedback.
It creates a safe playground to practice debugging, refactoring, and secure coding — guided by CodeRabbit as your live “AI game master.”

Perfect for teaching code quality, improving review skills, and making debugging actually fun.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the first challenges I hit was getting CodeRabbit to feel “live” inside the arcade environment. Since reviews take a bit of time to generate, the editor would freeze or feel sluggish whenever I triggered a new analysis. It completely broke the arcade-like flow I wanted. I eventually fixed this by sending review requests in the background and using a debounced trigger so the UI never paused even if CodeRabbit was still crunching the previous version.

Another big hurdle was converting CodeRabbit’s review comments into game-style objectives. The feedback isn’t designed to be “gamified” out of the box, so I kept ending up with too many suggestions or overlapping issues that confused the scoring system. To solve this, I built a small classification layer that grouped similar findings and translated them into clearer tasks like “Reduce complexity” or “Fix unsafe input handling,” making the challenges feel structured and fair.

Finally, integrating multiple analysis tools at once—linters, complexity checks, and security scans—initially slowed everything down. Running them together made the game feel more like waiting for CI logs than actually playing. I optimized this by caching results and only running certain tools on changed code sections. It made the overall experience much smoother and helped the gameplay feel fast and responsive, which was exactly what I was aiming for.

**Best Use of CodeRabbit**

Refactor Arcade was built specifically to showcase deep, practical, and creative use of CodeRabbit, not just as a reviewer but as the core engine of the entire experience. Every challenge, objective, score, and improvement inside the game comes directly from CodeRabbit’s analysis. Instead of treating CodeRabbit as a background tool, the project turns its reviews into something interactive and visual — which is exactly what this track is encouraging.

I used multiple CodeRabbit features together: multi-persona reviews, inline suggestions, severity rules, auto-actions, and rich configuration through the .coderabbit.yml. The findings produced by CodeRabbit are converted into game objectives, XP rewards, hints, and auto-fix patches, so the tool directly influences gameplay. This allowed me to explore and apply CodeRabbit’s capabilities far beyond a standard PR-review setup.

The project also integrates several MCP servers (linting, security checks, complexity analysis), and all their outputs are fed back into CodeRabbit as context. This makes the reviews more complete and shows how CodeRabbit can act as the center of a larger toolchain. Overall, Refactor Arcade uses the highest number of CodeRabbit features in a meaningful way, demonstrates complex configuration, and presents a very different and innovative way to apply AI-driven code reviews — which is exactly what the “Best Use of CodeRabbit” track aims to reward.

**The problem it solves**

Manually auditing a large website for these subtle errors is slow, expensive, and nearly impossible. This drift dilutes brand identity and creates a disjointed user experience.

### Global Translator
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/global-translator-5bf8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/shivamyadav-dev/A-Journey-Of-Data-Science/tree/main/Artificial%20Intelligence/Global%20Translator) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20This%20Fall%202025%20--%20Milestone%20Edition-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackthisfall.devfolio.co)

> "Translate text, hear the world."

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Translate API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Translate%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![gTTS](https://img.shields.io/badge/gTTS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### 🧩 The Problem It Solves

In an increasingly globalized world, **language barriers** remain a primary obstacle to connection. While simple text translators exist, they often leave a critical gap: **Pronunciation.**

Reading a translation is one thing; knowing how to say it—or understanding it when it is spoken to you—is another. Users often have to switch between a translation app and a separate text-to-speech tool, which is inefficient and disrupts the flow of communication or learning.

**Global Translator** solves this by unifying **accurate text translation** with **instant audio synthesis**, creating a complete bridge between understanding meaning and mastering speech.

---

### 🚀 Use Cases & Benefits

Here is how Global Translator makes specific tasks easier, faster, and more accessible:

#### 1. 🎓 Enhanced Language Learning
* **The Challenge:** Students often struggle to pronounce new words correctly just by reading phonetic spellings.
* **The Solution:** Users can type a phrase in their target language (or translate into it) and immediately hit "Listen."
* **Benefit:** It acts as an instant pronunciation coach, reinforcing auditory memory alongside visual learning.

#### 2. 🌍 Seamless Travel Companion
* **The Challenge:** Travelers often need to communicate quickly (e.g., giving directions to a taxi driver) but may not feel confident speaking.
* **The Solution:** Type the destination or question in native language -> Translate -> Play Audio.
* **Benefit:** Removes the anxiety of mispronunciation. The app speaks for you, ensuring clearer and more polite communication.

#### 3. ♿ Improved Accessibility
* **The Challenge:** Text-only translators are often difficult to use for individuals with visual impairments or reading difficulties (like dyslexia).
* **The Solution:** The integrated **Text-to-Speech (gTTS)** feature reads the output aloud automatically or on demand.
* **Benefit:** It transforms visual information into auditory information, making cross-language communication inclusive for everyone.

#### 4. ⚡ Workflow Efficiency
* **The Challenge:** Professionals or content creators working with multi-lingual content often need to verify how a translated script sounds before recording or publishing.
* **The Solution:** A single interface to generate the text and download the corresponding `.mp3` file.
* **Benefit:** Saves time by eliminating the need to copy-paste text between different software tools.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 🛠️ Challenges I Ran Into

Building **Global Translator** involved overcoming several technical hurdles, particularly regarding how Streamlit handles user interaction and file management.

#### 1. 🔄 Managing App State (Streamlit Reruns)
* **The Challenge:** Streamlit re-runs the entire Python script every time a user interacts with a widget (like clicking "Translate"). Initially, my translated text and audio would disappear immediately after the page refreshed.
* **The Solution:** I implemented `st.session_state` to persist the translation output and audio data across re-runs. This ensures the result stays on screen until the user enters a new input.
* **Key Takeaway:** Understanding state management is crucial for creating interactive, persistent web apps in Python.

#### 2. 🔊 Audio File Handling & Playback
* **The Challenge:** Integrating the `gTTS` (Google Text-to-Speech) library required saving an audio file to the server locally, but Streamlit's audio player reads byte data. Additionally, I needed a way for users to download this file.
* **The Solution:** I wrote a function to generate a temporary `translation.mp3` file, read it back as binary data (`rb`), and then pass those bytes to both the `st.audio` player and a custom HTML download link.
* **Key Takeaway:** bridging file-based libraries with web-based byte streams requires careful file I/O operations.

#### 3. 🎨 Customizing the UI Limits
* **The Challenge:** Streamlit's default UI is very rigid. I wanted to remove standard clutter (like the "Deploy" button) and add a custom footer, which isn't supported natively.
* **The Solution:** I utilized `st.markdown` with `unsafe_allow_html=True` to inject custom CSS. This allowed me to hide the main menu, style the footer, and adjust padding for a cleaner look.
* **Key Takeaway:** A little CSS knowledge goes a long way in transforming a basic data script into a polished web application.

### Fraudshield AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mediscan-f351) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/uzman2406/fraudshield-ai-demo) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://uzman2406.github.io/fraudshield-ai-demo/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/cCOu27RW80A) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20This%20Fall%202025%20--%20Milestone%20Edition-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackthisfall.devfolio.co)

> Smarter detection. Safer transactions

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Al-Based Financial Fraud Detector is a smart system that helps identify and prevent fraudulent financial transactions.
It uses artificial intelligence and Cyber Security to find unusual patterns in real time, alerting institutions before any major loss occurs.
The system uses predictive models and anomaly detection algorithms to flag potentially fraudulent transactions before they cause harm. It helps banks, NBFCs, and fintech organizations reduce financial losses, ensure compliance, and protect customer trust.
This solution improves security, builds customer trust, and supports safer digital banking.
**Key Features**
Real-time fraud detection and monitoring.
Behavioral and transaction pattern analysis.
Secure, scalable, and compliant architecture.
Easy integration with existing financial systems.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/fe9632bff3d247ba9c9f5ee859c23237/2497d193-f593-4402-bb2a-898038e8b765.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/fe9632bff3d247ba9c9f5ee859c23237/929e6ed4-974a-4d48-8d6d-78e0b1fa3f6b.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

Inconsistencies and noise in raw transaction data were major roadblocks when it came to creating the best training for the ML system. The data (raw transactions) used to train an ML model greatly impacts the model's performance.

I removed duplicates and addressed any missing fields in the raw transaction data to clean up and prepare it for the ML system. I then normalised numeric fields (through adding or removing zeros) in order to better balance them between transactions, and I anonymised sensitive information while retaining all the key signature patterns that would allow the model to detect fraudulent transactions (digital fingerprints).


Selecting the best ML features (i.e. factors/challenges) used to determine if a transaction is "faux" was a complicated process. The system did not perform well initially because the selected features were "basic." 

In addition to this, I studied real-world fraud and created or engineered advanced features based on how fraud is typically performed.


I implemented and established techniques for detecting rapidly changed devices used to conduct transactions, abnormal time for transaction completion, and sudden spikes in transaction amounts.

These advanced features led to improved performance by allowing the model to "map" the behaviour of users conducting legitimate transactions versus those participating in fraudulent activity. By doing this, I was able to significantly enhance the model's accuracy.


Initially, there was a significant volume of "false positive" results generated by the model when flagging fraudulent transactions. The volume of false positives presented significant opportunity for inconvenience for actual users and increased workload for investigators involved in investigating fraudulent activity.

I reduced the volume of false positives generated by fine-tuning the hyperparameters of the model and utilising adaptive learning techniques in order to enhance the model's discriminative ability to correctly identify fraudulent activity and legitimate transaction behaviour. 

By taking measures to improve the balance of data used for the model, the number of false positives decreased significantly.

**Best Use of GitHub**

The GitHub track appealed to me because it was important for the development of my AI-Based Financial Fraud Detector to utilize collaborative, version-controlled, and open-source practices. In addition to the artificial intelligence algorithm used for predicting financial fraud, our project also included other modules that were related to this software, including data processing, model training, and dashboard development. Each module functioned independently, so that in order to manage the project effectively, each module had to be managed in a structured manner for change management, project tracking, and collaboration with team members.


Using GitHub provided me with the following:


A clean, documented codebase that is easy to read and understand


The ability for my team members to work on their modules simultaneously without causing conflicts


Ability to track the addition of new features, fixes for bugs and enhancements through commits and branches


Ability to publicly showcase the technical implementation of our project


Because our project addresses a real-world issue (financial fraud), being able to share our solution and receive feedback will allow us to help others, plus it will allow us to contribute to the larger cybersecurity and AI/ML community.


The fact that I chose to go with the GitHub track reflects my commitment to writing maintainable code that supports team collaboration, as well as building projects that will continue to grow and be enhanced through open collaboration.

### AI-Based Electric Cable Fault Finder
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aidriven-fault-prediction-and-localization-system-for-electric-cable-infrastructure-using-iot-data-streams-a026) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://cableguard-ai.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1141558038) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20This%20Fall%202025%20--%20Milestone%20Edition-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackthisfall.devfolio.co)

> Smart detection for safer power lines

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Arduino IDE](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arduino%20IDE-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chart.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chart.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The solution addresses the major challenge of detecting and locating electric cable faults, which often cause prolonged power outages, safety risks, and high maintenance costs. Traditional methods rely heavily on manual inspection and trial-and-error, making fault identification slow, inefficient, and sometimes dangerous. By providing fast and accurate fault detection, the solution significantly improves the reliability and safety of the power network.

People and utility teams can use this system for:

1. Real-time monitoring of electric cables

2. Immediate identification of abnormal voltage or current patterns

3. Accurate fault localization to know exactly where a cable has failed

4. Predictive maintenance by identifying weak or failing sections early

5. Faster repair and restoration of electricity

6. Improved infrastructure management for utilities, industries, and smart cities


This solution makes existing tasks easier and safer in several ways:

1. Technicians no longer need to manually trace faults along long cable routes

2. Repairs become targeted rather than broad, reducing time, cost, and disruption

3. Faults are detected before they escalate into hazardous failures

4. Outages are minimized, improving continuity for homes, hospitals, industries, and essential services

5. Utilities gain a reliable and efficient method for maintaining critical infrastructure

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was unstable sensor readings, especially when simulating faults. The current sensor produced noisy values, which caused incorrect fault detection. I solved this by adding filtering, improving grounding, and calibrating the sensor under different loads.

Another issue was communication delays between the Arduino and ESP8266, which led to missing or partial data. I fixed this by optimizing the baud rate, restructuring data packets, and adding basic error checking.

Fault localization was also difficult in the beginning because small variations in readings made sections hard to distinguish. Collecting more simulated data and refining the logic helped improve accuracy.

These challenges were overcome through repeated testing, calibration, and incremental improvements.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyCharm](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyCharm-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![The Graph](https://img.shields.io/badge/The%20Graph-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Our cities behave like living beings — they show signs when danger is growing.
But today, those signs are scattered across different systems:
pollution sensors, traffic reports, industrial logs, weather alerts, and more.

Because nothing brings these signals together, risks rise quietly.
People realize the danger only after it affects their health, safety, or environment.

Cities try to warn us, but we don’t have a way to listen, understand, or prepare.
There is no real-time clarity, no future prediction, and no simple guidance on what to do.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. “I had to learn many languages…”

Every data source spoke differently — pollution, traffic, weather, industries.
Understanding them and combining their voices was a real struggle.

2. “Seeing the world in real-time wasn’t easy…”

Updating the map with live hotspots felt like trying to track a heartbeat that kept changing every second.

3. “Cities wouldn’t reveal their details easily…”

Connecting states → cities → domains smoothly took patience; one missing API and everything broke.

4. “Predicting the future is hard for anyone…”

Teaching the system to look 5 years ahead — and still stay accurate — pushed our limits.

5. “I had to survive even when the internet didn’t…”

Building an offline brain (mock data mode) so the platform never stops working was a big challenge.

6. “I wanted to look beautiful and move smoothly…”

Starfields, animations, charts, maps — all had to feel alive without slowing down.

7. “I had to stay fast while thinking a lot…”

Processing data, predicting trends, and updating visuals all at once was tough on performance.

### MitanVani
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mitanvani-067c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackBIOS%202K25-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackbios2k25.devfolio.co)

> Ai chhattisgarhi to hindi translator

![Speech Recognition](https://img.shields.io/badge/Speech%20Recognition-333333?style=flat-square) ![Text-to-Speech](https://img.shields.io/badge/Text--to--Speech-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural Language Processing](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20Language%20Processing-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In many parts of Chhattisgarh, people speak local dialects like Chhattisgarhi, Surgujia, Halbi and others. But most health workers, government officials, teachers, and emergency staff mainly speak Hindi. Because of this, they often cannot understand each other.

This creates a serious communication barrier in daily life:

1. Patients cannot explain their health problems clearly

A villager tries to tell the nurse about chest pain or dizziness, but she can’t understand the dialect well.
The patient repeats again and again. The nurse guesses.
This wastes time—and sometimes affects the person’s treatment.

2. Citizens struggle to understand government instructions

When people go for:

ration cards

pension

Aadhaar

vaccination

bank work

…they often don’t understand what the officer is saying in Hindi.
Many feel embarrassed or afraid to speak up.

3. Emergencies become even more stressful

During floods, accidents, or medical emergencies, every second matters.
If the responder and the local person don’t share a common language, information gets lost—
Who is hurt? Where did it happen? What exactly happened?
Miscommunication slows down help.

4. Both sides feel frustrated

Citizens feel they aren’t being heard.
Officials feel helpless because they cannot understand what is being said.
Simple tasks take too long and often need a third person to translate.

5. No existing tool solves this

Most apps and AI systems don’t understand Chhattisgarhi properly.
They misinterpret words, or they simply don’t support the dialect.
There is no tool that can listen to Chhattisgarhi and instantly convert it into clear Hindi speech.

Our Solution Fills This Gap

Your system gives people a way to talk freely without worrying about language.

It listens to the local Chhattisgarhi speech, understands it, translates it into Hindi instantly, and can even speak it out loud.
This removes stress and confusion for everyone involved.

It helps:

doctors understand villagers

officers guide citizens correctly

families communicate during emergencies

anyone feel confident while speaking in their own mother tongue

In short:
We are solving the communication gap between locals and officials by removing the language barrier completely.

If you want, I can rewrite this as:
✔ A short “Problem Statement”
✔ A 1-page introduction
✔ Highly polished version for a report or pitch

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Faced

- Chhattisgarhi is a spoken dialect, not a standardized language, which makes consistent data collection and labeling difficult.

- No existing Chhattisgarhi datasets for training or benchmarking, forcing us to build everything from scratch.

- No pre-trained models available for Chhattisgarhi translation or speech recognition, requiring custom model development and fine-tuning.
 
- Lack of offline/low-connectivity solutions, especially important for rural areas, meant we had to optimize models to run locally without cloud dependence.

### AI Powered Command Centre for Indian Farmer
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ai-powered-command-centre-for-indian-farmer-71b9) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackBIOS%202K25-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackbios2k25.devfolio.co)

> AI Market placed and intelligent

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AgriFinAi addresses the systemic fragmentation in Indian agriculture that traps farmers in a cycle of debt and low income. Currently, farmers struggle with opaque and scattered loan processes, exploitation by middlemen in the marketplace, and a lack of real-time, actionable crop advisory. Our platform solves this by consolidating a transparent Loan Comparison Engine, a Direct-to-Buyer Marketplace, and an AI-powered Crop Doctor into a single unified super-app. This ecosystem approach eliminates information asymmetry, empowering farmers to secure affordable formal credit, maximize profits by bypassing intermediaries, and mitigate crop risks through hyper-local intelligence

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of AgriFinAi, we tackled several critical technical hurdles. Our biggest challenge was the AI model initially generating false positives on non-crop images, which we resolved by implementing a strict 70% confidence threshold to ensure accuracy. We also navigated breaking changes in Next.js 15, requiring us to refactor our dynamic routing logic to handle asynchronous parameters effectively. Additionally, we fixed persistent Frontend-Backend connectivity issues (CORS) by standardizing our API endpoints and port configurations. Finally, we optimized the User Experience by shifting from an automatic trigger to a Manual Analysis Flow, giving farmers full control over the diagnosis process rather than overwhelming them with instant results

### AID-X
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aidx-39e3) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/haiideralyy01/AID-X) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/0MFyn-a-oQM?si=bqTLZNujjvzoARhL) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacknauts-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknauts.devfolio.co)

> Smart giving , timely living

![PHP](https://img.shields.io/badge/PHP-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem Statement (Clean & Concise)

Delays in rescue and relief occur because the needs of affected people are not verified quickly enough.

There is no accurate, real-time system to show where help is needed the most.

Resources often get misallocated — some areas receive excess aid while urgent zones are ignored.

Current verification methods (like Aadhaar/biometrics) are slow, unreliable, or inaccessible for many people.

Solution (Short & Clear)

AID-X provides a real-time coordination platform that connects victims, volunteers, NGOs, and donors in one place.

A map-based interface shows live locations of needs, volunteers, and deliveries to prioritize critical areas.

Smart AI + location-based verification quickly validates genuine requests and reduces fake appeals.

A transparent system that logs all donations and aid deliveries, improving trust and accountability.

**Challenges we ran into**

Real-time verification was harder than expected — balancing speed with accuracy required multiple iterations of our logic and data checks.

Map integration wasn’t smooth at first — syncing live locations of volunteers, donors, and recipients took time to stabilize.

Handling fake or duplicate requests was a major hurdle; we had to redesign our filters and scoring system several times.

Data consistency issues popped up in the backend due to simultaneous updates from multiple users.

Design alignment across the team was tricky — turning rough ideas into a clean, usable interface took extra coordination.

Deployment challenges occurred when managing responsiveness across different devices and screen sizes.

### xGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/xguard-0f54) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/md2004sameer/guard) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://guard-0lbi.onrender.com) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-KodeKalesh%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://kodekalesh-2025.devfolio.co)

> say no to fraud

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today, businesses deal with massive data streams, unpredictable user behavior, and evolving attack patterns. Traditional rule-based systems fail because they can’t adapt, detect unknown patterns, or respond in real time. This leads to financial losses, security breaches, and trust issues. X Guard eliminates this gap by providing an intelligent, adaptive, and real-time detection engine that continuously monitors activity, identifies anomalies, predicts risks, and blocks suspicious behavior instantly. It ensures accuracy, speed, and scalability—making digital platforms safer without adding heavy engineering overhead.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Handling messy and unpredictable data — the data wasn’t clean or consistent, so detecting patterns became harder.
2. Building accurate detection logic — balancing false positives and false negatives was challenging.
3. Real-time processing — making the system fast enough to detect issues instantly was tough.
4. Integrating multiple components — connecting backend, models, and alerts smoothly needed careful design.
5. Testing with real scenarios — creating realistic fraud/threat cases to validate the system was difficult.

**FinTech for Bharat**

X Guard is an intelligent fraud and threat detection system designed to keep digital platforms secure with real-time monitoring and adaptive analytics. It identifies unusual behavior, flags risky patterns, and prevents potential attacks before they cause damage. Built for modern applications, X Guard learns from live data, reducing false alerts while improving accuracy over time. It gives businesses a simple, fast, and reliable way to protect transactions, users, and sensitive information—making security easy without adding extra load on developers.

### FireGuard AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/fireguard-ai-5e9d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Arvind-Singh00/Backend) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://firefree-three.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/xo9hS7tlZb8?si=msWsZplBQKoKir_M) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-KodeKalesh%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://kodekalesh-2025.devfolio.co)

> Predicting Fires Before They Spread

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

FireGuard AI helps authorities monitor wildfire risk in real time by combining live weather (Open‑Meteo), satellite hotspots (NASA FIRMS), and Algerian Forest Fires training data to run a Random‑Forest ensemble (97% test accuracy). Users click a map cell, the app fetches weather, builds the payload, calls the Render-hosted ML API, colors the grid by risk, and shows details in the sidebar—plus alerts, reports, PDF exports, and safety tips—so they can plan patrols, evacuations, and resource deployment earlier and more safely.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Front-end(Divya Ratna)**: Biggest hurdle was the cold-start latency from the hosted ML API (Render free tier). The first prediction requests timed out and left the UI stuck on “error.” I solved it by adding exponential retry logic, extending the timeout, and surfacing a toast plus fallback colors so the dashboard stays responsive even if the API wakes slowly.

**ML engineer (Abhijeet and Ayush)**: The ensemble Random Forest needed both historical Algerian data and live weather/FWI inputs, but FFMC/DMC/DC/ISI aren’t provided by Open‑Meteo. He built a feature-engineering layer inside the Flask service to recompute those indices each time, then re-ran the pipeline to reach 0.97 test accuracy. That bridge between live weather and legacy features was the key hurdle.
**
Backend engineer (Arvind)**: Aligning REST paths between Express (/risk/zones, /risk/fire-hotspots) and the React client was tricky—React still called the old URLs and threw 404s. He audited both sides, renamed the endpoints, and expanded the JSON schema (alerts, statistics, heatmap seeds) so the frontend could drop its placeholders and consume live data reliably.

**AgriTech & Rural Innovation**

**FireGuard AI** directly addresses sustainability by focusing on proactive environmental protection and resource management.

**Prevents Ecosystem Collapse:** By predicting fires before they start or spread, the tool helps prevent the destruction of forests, which are critical carbon sinks, biodiversity hotspots, and regulators of water cycles.
**Reduces Carbon Emissions:** Large-scale wildfires release massive amounts of CO2 into the atmosphere. Early detection and containment, enabled by our tool, directly mitigate this impact on climate change.
**Optimizes Resource Use:** It allows firefighting agencies to allocate limited resources—like water, personnel, and equipment—more efficiently by targeting high-risk zones, reducing waste and the environmental footprint of emergency responses.
**Promotes Community Resilience**: It safeguards communities and infrastructure from destruction, ensuring the long-term social and economic sustainability of regions prone to natural disasters.

**AgriTech & Rural Innovation**
FireGuard AI is a powerful tool for rural innovation, bringing advanced technology to protect agricultural assets and enhance community safety.

**Protects Agricultural Livelihoods**: Wildfires can devastate farms, destroying crops, livestock, and essential infrastructure. Our platform provides a crucial early warning system that gives farmers time to implement protective measures and evacuate livestock.
**Enhances Rural Safety**: Rural communities are often on the front lines of forest fires. FireGuard AI empowers these communities and local authorities with the data needed for timely evacuation alerts and effective preparedness strategies, making rural living safer.
**Brings AI to the Field**: It applies sophisticated AI and real-time data fusion to solve a problem that disproportionately affects rural areas, demonstrating a practical use of technology to innovate beyond urban centers.
**Supports Economic Stability**: By protecting agricultural assets and preventing widespread damage, the project helps maintain the economic stability and food security of rural regions.

Team **Farmfusion** -- [Ayush Singh](https://github.com/ayu-sh87), [ArvindKumar Singh](https://github.com/Arvind-Singh00), [Abhijeet Gupta](https://github.com/ag21o9), [Divya Ratna Gautam](https://github.com/vayu_gautam)

Key Local Changes Summary
AWS Version

EventBridge / Lambda
Manual run or Python schedule
S3 Buckets

**Challenges we ran into**

We faced three major technical challenges during this hackathon. Each one required a significant "pivot" to overcome, leading to our final hybrid "local-to-cloud" solution.

1. AWS Account & Service Permissions
Our biggest initial blocker was that our hackathon-provided AWS account (WSParticipantRole) was heavily locked down.

The Problem: We were denied permission to use core serverless services, including lambda:InvokeFunction (to test) and events:PutRule (to create a schedule).

Our Pivot: We completely abandoned the AWS Lambda/EventBridge plan and re-engineered the project as a local Python script that would still connect to cloud services.

2. AWS AI Service Permissions
After pivoting to a local script, we discovered our role also blocked the AI services we needed.

The Problem: Our script failed with an AccessDeniedException for comprehend:DetectSentiment. We weren't allowed to use Amazon's AI.

Our Pivot: We wrote our own simple, keyword-based sentiment analyzer from scratch directly in run_agent.py. This allowed us to fulfill the "intelligence" part of the prompt without any external AI service.

3. Local Environment & C++ Build Hell
Our biggest and most time-consuming challenge was a deep-rooted local environment conflict on macOS.

The Problem: pip3 install streamlit failed. We were using the brand-new Python 3.14, which didn't have pre-compiled libraries ("wheels") for pyarrow (a Streamlit dependency).

The Cascade: This forced pip to build pyarrow from source, which led to a cascade of C++ errors. We had to manually install cmake, then apache-arrow, and still ended up with a fatal ImportError (symbol not found in flat namespace...).

Our Solution: We solved this by creating a stable, isolated Python 3.12 virtual environment (venv). This allowed pip to download the correct, pre-compiled libraries, fixing all build errors instantly.

4. GitHub Authentication
As a final challenge, we had to navigate modern GitHub authentication.

The Problem: GitHub no longer accepts passwords for terminal commands.

Our Solution: We successfully created a Personal Access Token (PAT) with repo scopes and used it to authenticate and push our code.

### Anomaly Detection Agent
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/anomaly-detection-agent-e607) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vegadarsiwork/bits-anomaly-finder) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ll7eNVnfg4c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-IEEE%20ML%20presents:%20The%20Spark-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ieee-ml-presents-the-spark.devfolio.co)

> For the Spark Hackathon

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS Lambda](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS%20Lambda-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS Cloudwatch](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS%20Cloudwatch-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chart.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chart.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![DynamoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/DynamoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Real-time cryptocurrency anomaly detection for traders, exchanges, and risk management teams.

This autonomous agent solves the critical problem of detecting unusual price movements in real-time before they escalate into major financial events. Traditional monitoring requires constant human attention and suffers from alert fatigue with high false-positive rates.

Key benefits:

🎯 Reduces false positives - Multi-rule fusion (combining z-score, volatility, and velocity signals) provides 95%+ confidence before alerting, unlike single-metric systems that generate noise

⚡ Real-time detection - Identifies anomalies within 20 seconds of occurrence, giving traders and risk teams time to act before losses compound

🧠 Natural language explanations - Non-technical users get human-readable explanations like "BTC/INR spiked 8.2% to ₹94,50,000 (6.7σ above mean)" instead of raw statistics

🔧 Adaptive configuration - Tune detection sensitivity via REST API without code changes, adapting to different market conditions (bull/bear/volatile)

📊 Severity classification - 4-tier system (INFO→WARNING→CRITICAL→EMERGENCY) enables proportional responses instead of binary alerts

Use cases: Flash crash detection, market manipulation identification, exchange outage monitoring, automated trading risk management, compliance surveillance, portfolio protection

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **AWS Deployment Blocked by Workshop IAM Restrictions**

Challenge: Attempted to deploy the serverless architecture on AWS Lambda + DynamoDB but hit 5 permission blockers:
- iam:CreateRole denied – couldn't create Lambda execution roles
- iam:AttachRolePolicy denied – couldn't attach policies
- dynamodb:UpdateTimeToLive denied – couldn't enable TTL for data cleanup
- lambda:InvokeFunction denied – couldn't test functions
- Cognito service completely disabled

How I overcame it: Instead of abandoning AWS integration, I created a comprehensive 900-line AWS_ROADMAP.md that documents:
- Complete serverless architecture design (Lambda, DynamoDB, EventBridge, SNS)
- Exact permission requirements with JSON policies
- Step-by-step deployment guide
- Cost estimation (~₹140/month, ₹33 with free tier)
- Monitoring setup with CloudWatch

This turned a limitation into a demonstration of enterprise-level cloud architecture thinking.

---

2. **Numerical Stability in Rolling Statistics**

Challenge: Initial implementation using standard formula variance = E[X²] - E[X]² caused catastrophic cancellation errors when prices were large (₹94,00,000+) but changes were small (±0.5%).

How I overcame it: Implemented Welford's algorithm for one-pass variance calculation with O(1) memory and numerically stable updates. Added MAD (Median Absolute Deviation) as fallback for extreme outlier scenarios. This ensures accurate z-scores even with Bitcoin's high nominal prices.

---

3. **Alert Fatigue from False Positives**

Challenge: Single-signal detection (z-score alone) triggered 40+ alerts per hour during normal volatility, rendering the system useless.

How I overcame it: Designed multi-rule fusion combining three independent signals with weighted confidence:
- Z-score (50%) – statistical deviation
- Volatility (30%) – market condition
- Velocity (20%) – rate of change

Added persistence requirement (2 consecutive polls) and cooldown mechanism (5 minutes). This reduced false positives by 95% while maintaining 100% true positive detection.

---

4. **Making AI Decisions Explainable**

Challenge: Users couldn't understand why an alert fired – "z-score: 6.7" is meaningless to non-technical traders.

How I overcame it: Built natural language generation that contextualizes every anomaly:
- "BTC/INR spiked 8.2% to ₹94,50,000, marking a 6.7 standard deviation surge above the ₹87,00,000 mean"
- Shows exact price, percentage change, z-score in plain English
- Provides actionable context for decision-making

---

5. **Production-Ready Architecture from Day One**

Challenge: Many hackathon projects are "proof of concepts" that can't scale. I wanted production-grade code.

How I overcame it:
- Separated concerns: Poller, Detector, Storage, Server modules
- RESTful API with 7 endpoints for integration
- Comprehensive error handling and logging
- Export to CSV for offline analysis
- Designed for horizontal scaling (AWS Lambda functions can run in parallel)
- 3000+ lines of documentation for maintenance

The system is ready to deploy at scale, not just a demo.

Team **Growifyai** -- Sachin Vasu, Vega Darsi
