**The problem it solves**

Our app helps people find nearby hospitals, clinics, and ambulances easily. In normal situations, it saves time by showing trusted clinics, available doctors, and waiting times so people don’t have to run around in confusion. During emergencies, the app makes it safer by instantly sharing your location with the nearest ambulance or clinic, so help reaches faster. It is also useful for travelers, trekkers, or people in remote areas where medical services are hard to find. Overall, the app makes getting healthcare simpler, quicker, and more reliable, giving people peace of mind in both daily life and urgent situations.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major hurdle we faced was integrating real-time hospital/clinic availability and ambulance tracking. Many clinics do not have digital systems, so getting live data was difficult.

- We designed a manual update system where clinics can quickly update their status (open/closed, doctor available, wait time).

- For ambulances, we used GPS-based live location sharing so even if hospital data is missing, users can still get emergency help.

**The problem it solves**

Real-time Queue Updates:
Ensuring smooth synchronization between patients and clinic admins.
Handling potential network drops and stale queue data.

Map Integration:
Balancing cost vs features Google Maps,
Making sure maps load fast even in low-network conditions.

Database Design:
Designing queue management schema that supports triage, live updates, and history tracking.
Preventing duplicate or “ghost” tokens when users leave unexpectedly.

Multilingual & Accessibility:
Designing UI that supports multiple languages without clutter.
Making the web app usable for seniors with larger text and simple navigation.

Scalability Concerns:
Choosing lightweight hosting options (Supabase) to stay cost-effective yet scalable.
Keeping Redis pub/sub efficient for high peak loads.

User Adoption Challenge:
Clinics with minimal tech exposure may resist adopting new software.
Needed to keep admin dashboard simple, one-click friendly.

**Challenges we ran into**

Making real-time queue updates reliable .

Choosing between free vs paid map APIs while keeping performance good.

Designing a simple yet scalable database schema for queues and patients.

Ensuring the app is easy for clinics with low tech experience to adopt.

**The problem it solves**

For Patients: It Ends the Waiting Game
Imagine feeling unwell and all you want is to see a doctor. But instead, you're faced with a frustrating guessing game. You drive to a clinic with no idea how long you'll be stuck in the waiting room, surrounded by other sick people. You might spend your morning calling different clinics, just trying to find one that's open and can actually see you. If you're new to town, that feeling of being lost and unable to find trusted medical care is even more overwhelming. It's a draining cycle of wasted time, unnecessary travel, and growing anxiety when all you really need is care.

For Clinics: It Brings Calm to the Chaos
Now, picture it from the clinic's side. The staff is trying to juggle a constantly ringing phone while managing a waiting room that's overflowing with people. They're often relying on paper systems or clunky tools, making the daily rush feel chaotic and overwhelming. One moment the clinic is swamped, and the next it's empty, making it impossible to plan the day efficiently. They are essentially cut off, with no easy way to let the community know if they're at capacity or have openings. This constant stress leads to staff burnout and makes it harder to provide the quality care they want to give.

### PulsePoint
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/pulsepoint-3849) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QpatMyfFKjptv-d0x_QZRecqDG7KG1qR/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=106413902287866362696&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackBuild-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackbuild.devfolio.co)

> Because every minute matters in care

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mapbox](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mapbox-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most patients visiting small neighborhood clinics face uncertainty—they don’t know how long the wait will be, if the clinic is open, or if they’ll even be accepted. Receptionists struggle with managing calls, queues, and updates at the same time, leading to long waits and frustration.
Our project solves this by providing:

1. A map-first view of nearby clinics with real-time wait times and open/closed status.

2. Queue transparency so patients know when their turn is coming.

3. Direct chat with the clinic reception to avoid unnecessary phone calls.

4. Anonymous updates to keep wait times accurate, even if staff forget to update.

5. This saves time, reduces stress, and makes local healthcare more accessible and efficient.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Real-time updates: Getting queue data to refresh instantly was tough. We solved this by using WebSockets + Redis for fast live updates.

2. ETA accuracy: Initially, our wait time estimates were off. We introduced a simple formula with average service time per priority level (EMA smoothing) to improve accuracy.

3. Balancing priority vs fairness: We had to ensure emergency/urgent cases go first, but routine patients shouldn’t wait forever. We solved this by adding an “aging factor” so routine patients slowly gain priority.

4. User adoption concerns: Many patients may not want to create accounts. To fix this, we added an anonymous mode where they can still check in or confirm completion without logging in.

5. Multi-platform support: Making it work across both web and mobile required a PWA (Progressive Web App) approach so users can install it on Android/iOS without separate apps.

**The problem it solves**

QuickCare makes accessing local healthcare simpler and more efficient by giving patients real-time visibility into clinic queues, easy appointment booking, and AI-powered wait time predictions. Instead of spending hours in uncertainty, patients can plan visits more effectively, receive timely notifications, and manage bookings for the whole family. Features like multilingual support, emergency service integration, and secure document uploads reduce confusion and stress, ensuring that people from all backgrounds can navigate healthcare smoothly and confidently.

For clinics, QuickCare streamlines daily operations by replacing manual check-ins with a digital system, enabling dynamic queue management, and allowing direct communication with patients. Staff can announce delays, handle emergencies with priority, and access valuable analytics on patient flow to improve efficiency. At the community level, QuickCare helps distribute patient load across clinics, strengthens emergency response, and provides health networks with actionable data for better planning. Together, these benefits create a more transparent, reliable, and patient-friendly healthcare ecosystem.

**Challenges we ran into**

While developing QuickCare, one of the main challenges I encountered was integrating real-time queue management across clinics with varying levels of digital infrastructure. Ensuring data privacy and secure document handling required careful planning to meet compliance standards. Another hurdle was designing a user-friendly interface that worked seamlessly across multiple languages and devices, while still remaining lightweight for smaller clinics with limited technology resources. Balancing these technical, operational, and user-experience challenges was essential to creating a reliable and inclusive platform.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Maps API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Maps%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

****The Problem It Solves****
When someone feels sick or gets hurt, the last thing they want is confusion or long waits at a clinic. In many neighborhoods, especially around colleges or busy areas, people often don’t know:  
- Which clinic is open right now  
- How long the wait will be  
- Whether the clinic can actually help with their issue  
- If they’ll be stuck waiting for hours without updates  
This leads to frustration, wasted time, and sometimes even skipping care altogether.  

****What****  ****People****  ****Can**** ****Use**** ****CareQueue**** ****For**** 
CareQueue makes visiting a local clinic much easier and less stressful. Here’s how:  
- See nearby clinics on a map, so you don’t have to search randomly or ask around  
- Check live queue updates, knowing how many people are ahead of you before you go  
- Book your spot or request help without calling or filling out long forms  
- Get notified when it’s your turn, so you can wait comfortably or finish errands  
- Chat with clinic staff, asking questions like “Do you treat sprains?” or “Is there a female doctor today?”  
- Share feedback to help others choose the right clinic based on your experience  

****How**** ****It**** ****Makes**** ****Life**** ****Easier**** ****and**** ****Safer****  
- Less waiting, more certainty; you know what to expect before you even leave home  
- Faster help in emergencies, especially useful for students, parents, or elderly folks  
- No more guessing; you get real-time info, not outdated Google reviews  
- Clinics stay organized too; they can manage patient flow and reduce crowding  
In short, CareQueue turns a stressful, unpredictable clinic visit into a smoother, smarter experience for both patients and clinics.

**Challenges we ran into**

****Challenges We Ran Into (So Far)****  
Even in the planning and presentation phase, we faced some key challenges that influenced our approach:  
****1. Scoping the MVP for a 3-Day Hackathon****  
We had many ideas, from live queue tracking to appointment booking and clinic reviews. However, we had to be realistic about what we could build in just three days.  
**How we handled it:**  
We grouped features into logical phases and focused only on the core experience: helping users find clinics, check queue status, and get notified. This helped us stay focused and build something functional and impactful.  
****2. Designing for Two User Types****  
CareQueue needs to work for both patients and clinic staff, which means two very different user journeys.  
**How we handled it:**  
We created separate flows in our design, a simple map-first interface for patients and a control dashboard for clinics. This keeps things intuitive without overcomplicating the MVP.  
****3. Making It Useful Without Overengineering****  
We didn’t want to build a complex backend or real-time system that would slow us down.  
**How we handled it:**  
We planned lightweight solutions like manual queue updates and simple notifications—enough to show the concept clearly without getting stuck in technical depth.

**The problem it solves**

Uncertainty & Inefficiency in Queues

Patients: face long, unpredictable wait times & overcrowding.

Staff: spend too much time on manual queue management and handling disputes.

Poor Communication

Patients: don’t get timely updates on delays, appointments, or emergencies.

Staff: waste time answering repetitive queries, leading to frustration.

Emergency Handling Gaps

Patients: emergencies are not prioritized → delays in urgent care.

Staff: lack of advance notice for emergencies → chaos in managing flow.

Accessibility & Trust Issues

Patients: struggle to find genuine clinics (risk of fake degree providers, no reviews).

Staff: face credibility challenges due to lack of transparent rating/feedback system.

Fragmented Medical History

Patients: repeat tests due to lost/incomplete records.

Staff: no centralized patient history → inefficient diagnosis & treatment.

### FINOVA
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/finova-0c12) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Karan-Shyam-Sundar/devfolio-Saas-.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20The%20Horizon%202.0%20(VIT--Chennai)-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-the-horizon-2.devfolio.co)

> SMART FINANCE, SIMPLE  SOLUTIONS

![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![NoSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/NoSQL-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This project solves the financial management challenges faced by small and medium-sized businesses that lack access to a full-time CFO. It addresses issues like fragmented financial data spread across multiple sources, poor real-time visibility into cash flow and expenses, difficulty in forecasting future performance, missed anomalies, and low financial literacy. By integrating multi-source financial data into a single AI-powered, real-time dashboard, it centralizes insights, detects risks early, forecasts cash flow accurately, and explains complex metrics in plain language. The gamified financial health score makes performance easy to track and improve, while automation removes tedious manual work, enabling business owners to make faster, smarter, data-driven decisions without the cost of an in-house finance team.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was integrating multiple financial data sources, as each API had different authentication methods, data structures, and rate limits. Standardizing and cleaning the imported data to ensure accuracy across various formats was time-consuming. Designing a multi-tenant database structure that maintained strict financial data privacy while allowing for easy scaling required careful planning. Developing accurate AI-powered forecasting and anomaly detection models was challenging, especially in making the insights understandable for non-financial users. On the frontend, building a modern, mobile-responsive UI/UX that complied with WCAG accessibility guidelines while still looking visually appealing for a hackathon was demanding. Finally, ensuring smooth performance during the demo meant thorough testing, robust error handling, and preparing realistic sample data that highlighted the platform’s capabilities.

**SaaS**

It’s part of SaaS because it’s a cloud-hosted, on-demand software platform that users can access from anywhere via a browser or mobile device without installing or maintaining anything locally. All the heavy lifting—data processing, AI insights, API integrations, and dashboard updates—happens on the server side, so every user always gets the latest version automatically. It supports multi-tenant architecture, meaning many businesses can securely use the same system, and it’s easily scalable without redeploying for each customer. Its subscription-friendly structure, continuous delivery of features, and integration with external financial services make it a textbook example of a SaaS product

Team **Howamihere** -- [Nishka Pinnamaraju](https://github.com/Nishka-06), Karan Shyamsundar, Aniruth VS, JACOB MATHEW
